Relative paths resolve against the effective working directory and an explicitly supplied absolute path is accepted. Non-image files are decoded as strict UTF-8 without an extension allowlist and split on UTF-8 boundaries into the existing server-sized `AttachedFileDto` chunks. Staged text and stdin share 1-MiB-per-part and 32-MiB aggregate allocation authority without a file/part-count ceiling; the stdin reader's 10 MiB ceiling is not imposed on each `--with` file. Existing path and byte checks remain authoritative. Recognized images pass through `ScryingFocusStager` and its configured MIME/size policy. Text diagnostics report UTF-8 bytes, part count, and lowercase SHA-256; image diagnostics report decoded bytes and lowercase SHA-256. Stdin is materialized as the labeled `stdin.txt` source. Only typed content and a relative display label cross the API boundary. On live routes, the server performs normal current-turn materialization and model-policy checks. With Attachments enabled, it persists and Session-binds those text/image values before inference; with Attachments disabled, it keeps them in memory for the current turn. The client path itself grants no server filesystem authority, and a dry-run never persists staged content.

With no route option, dispatch enters the standard Agent Loop. `--research` calls the sole server-owned multi-hop research workflow, preserving effective context, current-turn files/images, and supported synthesis controls. `--spell <name>` resolves an exact case-insensitive name or a unique case-insensitive name prefix through the shared Spell catalog, then sets the production `OverrideSpellName`; forced selection does not replace normal Spell loading, dependency, attunement, Ward recording, or Sanctum policy. `--research` plus `--spell` is the only route conflict. Route selection does not add capability restrictions: ordinary and forced-Spell turns retain the production tool policy, while research synthesis keeps its pre-existing server-owned `DisableAllTools` untrusted-source boundary.

`--dry-run` carries the resolved prompt, context, forced Spell, preview-only files/images, output reserve, sampling options, and research-only system/tool policy into `POST /api/intelligence/context/inspect`. It always disables retrieval and automatic semantic Spell routing, while still resolving an explicitly named Spell. The result is a spend-free static pre-inference payload/context plan: it never searches, embeds, calls a provider model, executes a tool, reserves turn spend, persists an assistant Entry, or persists staged content. It is not an identity-equal copy of the later live `PingRequest`; live Agent dispatch may still add local `PatternSnapshot` and `ChronosyncDelta` context at handoff. `--show-content` is the explicit authenticated content reveal. Common route flags (`--new`, `--unattended`, model, context, temperature, top-p, max tokens, seed, stops, and response format (`json` aliases `json_object`), plus penalties) and research bounds remain available on the unified surface. `--new` simply clears the continuation Session, including when `--session` is also present, rather than adding a second option conflict. Recursive `--plain`, `--json`, and `--no-context` retain the process-wide contracts below.

**Command authority:** [`Arcanum.Command.Reference.md`](Arcanum.Command.Reference.md) is the complete user-facing reference for CLI syntax, arguments, options, aliases, interactive slash commands, output modes, and exit behavior. This design document retains ownership of composition, selection/context architecture, security boundaries, and process lifetime.

**Live-observation architecture:** The unified watch client consumes the existing independent authenticated Session, Apprentice, log, MCP, and daemon SSE routes plus the authenticated health endpoint; it does not merge those streams or add another backend channel. The shared transport preserves source events, reports keep-alives and reconnect gaps only as diagnostics, uses a Session Entry cursor when available without claiming replay guarantees, and keeps authentication, validation, not-found, and connection-cap denials terminal. A stream the host ends for a maintenance window arrives as an ordinary `[DONE]`, so a watcher exits cleanly rather than reporting a disconnect it did not have; the window itself is visible as the `503` a reconnect attempt receives while it lasts. Invocation syntax and per-command filters are documented in the command reference.

**Composition:** `ArcanumApiClient`, System.CommandLine command tree (`CliApplicationFactory` builds it from `CliCommandTree`), theme/Spectre UX, Command Center (`Cli/CommandCenter/`), `IArcanumServeLauncher`. Discover verbs in `Cli/Commands/`. Guided setup (§3.4.2) lives in `Cli/Services/Setup/` — `SetupStateMachine`, `SetupPlanner`, `SetupCommitter`, `SetupProviderProbe`, and `ISetupPrompt` — with `SetupCommand` as the thin driver over them.

**Command Center session changes:** bound attachment references and pending fork intent are cleared when the bound session changes; staged local file paths remain. The footer reports dropped reference counts. Clear, resume, fork, branch navigation, and archiving the active session are denied while a turn generates. A reasoning event whose log anchor was removed appends safely. Session/transcript page loads and post-turn session refresh share the session-action gate. Chat admission briefly holds that gate while claiming the turn and publishing its cancellation source; a busy gate refuses the submit without clearing composer text or staged attachments. The gate is released before inference so cancellation and human answers remain available. Completion clears only its owned source by identity, disposes it before reopening turn admission, and refreshes without moving focus from another pane or overlay; the focus decision uses current state when the UI callback runs. Submit completion, duplicate-submit refusal and error refreshes use best-effort writes after UI shutdown; invocation cancellation during post-turn refresh is ordinary cleanup, and turn/source ownership is still released.

**Command Center transcript paging:** the window retains one 200-entry page. Resume and fork request 201 newest entries, using the extra row only as the older-history continuation signal. Older reads use the existing Session entries endpoint's exclusive `(beforeCreatedAt, beforeId)` cursor at the oldest loaded entry, never a moving offset or a total captured at resume. Newer navigation reloads the latest page. Every applied page retains persisted Entry identities and rebuilds Incantations; live-only reasoning and status remain ephemeral until the operator navigates to another history page. The stream does not supply persisted Entry identities, so live answers acquire history selection identities when their page is reloaded.

**Human prompts:** the hard modal renders the complete sanitized question in a scrollable ListView, independently of the argument-preview row cap. Page keys scroll the question without moving focus or changing the answer. The streamed question is also appended to the bounded in-memory transcript as Status; this adds no application log or persistence sink. Auxiliary actions, including Quit, cannot preempt the prompt; Enter submits its answer and Ctrl+C retains ownership of turn cancellation.

**Application launch and deep links:** `center` and `open center` enter the existing `ICommandCenterHost` in-process; they do not spawn a second CLI. `open theforge`, `open compendium`, and the resource-specific `open` commands use Core's AOT-safe `IApplicationLauncher` and platform `IApplicationDiscoveryService`. A resource selector must finish before discovery or process start. The versioned `ApplicationDeepLink` envelope contains only the target application, resource kind, canonical server resource identifier, optional opaque Workspace scope ID, optional initial view, and reserved connection-profile ID. It never carries an API key, endpoint, prompt/file content, attachment, or server path. Compact source-generated JSON is passed as one value after `--arcanum-deep-link` through `ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList`; no shell parses resource text. When the target is Command Center, the CLI consumes and removes that private argument before normal command parsing. A target-only link opens the current host, while a Session link resumes its canonical GUID after the host connects; malformed, wrong-target, and unsupported-resource links fail with fixed diagnostics that never echo the private payload.

Discovery reports ordered candidates with a typed kind, launch path used only by the starter, and a safe display path used by diagnostics. It checks installed platform locations and a repository project discovered by walking up from the executable's own `AppContext.BaseDirectory` only; the current working directory is never consulted, because a hostile clone carrying the `RetroDownfall.Arcanum.slnx` marker would otherwise choose the project that `dotnet run --project` executes. No process offers that project as a launch candidate unless `ARCANUM_DEV_LAUNCHER=1` opts in (it is still listed as a non-existent candidate so the display-only fallback prints). The gate does not depend on the runtime: The Forge and Compendium ship as self-contained JIT images, so treating a JIT runtime as a development build would leave it open on every installed copy of them. The legacy `CompendiumLauncher` behind `arcanum config open` and The Forge applies the same gate to its own repository-project step, and its upward walk accepts the project only from an ancestor that also holds the `RetroDownfall.Arcanum.slnx` marker, so no launcher runs `dotnet run --project` from an unopted image or from a bare project path planted in a writable ancestor such as a folder at a drive root. Windows/Linux discovery also recognizes the exact sibling folders produced by the release packaging scripts; Linux selects only the current process architecture's `x64` or `arm64` folder. A development fallback is always rendered repository-relative. Failed candidates do not stop later attempts. In `ApplicationLauncher`, a start, discovery, or deep-link encoding step that throws is reported by exception type name only; the legacy `CompendiumLauncher` wraps only its process-start step the same way (its fixed settings deep link and local candidate enumeration are not wrapped). Neither reports message text, which can carry paths and secrets. When no candidate starts, the CLI prints every attempted safe candidate, the copyable development command, and the equivalent resource/config CLI command. Displayed command arguments use PowerShell quoting on Windows and POSIX-shell quoting on macOS/Linux; this has no effect on the shell-free `ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList` launch path. The baseline starts a new instance and reports `Started`; reuse/focus may be reported only by a platform activator that actually supports it.


### 4.4.1 Auto-launch serve lifecycle

Interactive `run` and **Command Center** call `IArcanumServeLauncher.EnsureRunningAsync` before context resolution, Session creation, or inference (Command Center: after UI host entry, before its first server-backed refresh):

1. Gate: `ICliEnvironment.IsInteractive` and `ARCANUM_NO_AUTO_SERVE` unset. `NO_COLOR` does **not** disable auto-serve (it only gates color + live layout / Command Center theme).
2. Each observation sends a fresh random 32-byte nonce to anonymous, bodyless `GET /api/presence`, with a two-second network budget. Before producing any proof, the endpoint requires both the raw transport peer and the post-forwarding effective peer to be loopback. Forwarded and `Host` headers cannot substitute for the raw peer, and a loopback reverse proxy cannot relay a capability for a remote effective peer. The endpoint also refuses to sign caller-controlled `Host` or request-scheme data: it derives the authority from the raw server-side listener's actual local port and TLS feature, fixes the client-facing name to `localhost`, and fails closed when that listener identity is absent or invalid. A same-host process therefore cannot relay a challenge from Arcanum on one port as proof for a different port. A ready host returns only the protocol version, that canonical loopback authority, a nonce/authority-bound HMAC proof, and one encrypted short-lived process capability. The server captures one UTC/timestamp pair when its capability service starts and advances that UTC authority only by monotonic elapsed time; later wall-clock corrections can neither lengthen nor prematurely expire a bearer, while the signed UTC issue/expiry fields remain portable diagnostics. After proof verification, the client bounds its own renewal and expiry windows by the signed lifetime and measures them from no later than the start of that challenge with its monotonic clock, so its cache is conservative and wall-clock changes cannot reopen or extend it. The client validates the complete response before opening secure storage and never sends a credential on this route. Initial resolution decrypts the owner-only `security.dat` mirror first and accepts it only when its key digest verifies the proof and decrypts the capability; while no digest has yet been retained, only a missing, corrupt, or mismatched mirror permits one OS-store read, which must prove the same challenge. Once a digest is retained, restart refresh and proactive renewal never reopen the OS store. A retained-digest mismatch may inspect the encrypted mirror against that same fresh challenge and adopt a different digest only when it validates the proof and capability, which permits legitimate key rotation without turning an unproved responder into another Keychain prompt. The process-wide `ArcanumApiCredentialLease` retains only the short-lived capability and fixed-size key digest, never the reusable master API key. Initial resolution, refresh after `401`, and proactive renewal shortly before expiry share a single-flight resolution. Caller cancellation detaches only that caller's wait. It does not abandon the one physical OS credential-store read: the macOS-owned password dialog is synchronous and cannot be cancelled reliably, so the flight finishes once and retains its proved result for the next caller instead of opening a second prompt. Lease shutdown cancels every waiter and requests cancellation of the flight, although an already displayed operating-system dialog may still finish independently. A proactive transient failure keeps a still-unexpired capability. A proactive `429` does the same and adds one bounded, clamped retry window measured with monotonic elapsed time, while a `401` evicts the rejected capability before refresh and never falls back to it. Every local CLI API transport passes through `ArcanumAuthenticatedHttpSender`: it sends only the process capability, binds both relative and absolute request URIs to the exact authority that passed the presence proof, refuses request, content, or client-default credential headers, refreshes after at most one `401`, and rebuilds and replays a request at most once only when that body is explicitly replayable. If that replay also returns `401`, the lease evicts only the exact rejected capability before returning; the failed call performs no third presence exchange or secure-storage read, and the next caller renews through the normal single-flight path. The two named local clients disable redirects and proxy use, so a handler cannot carry the capability beyond that verified authority. The only raw HTTP exceptions are the anonymous presence exchange itself and the guarded external-provider probe used by setup; a generator-complete semantic whole-CLI inventory resolves the compiled symbols rather than trusting syntax or text and closes that set. Typed client failures distinguish a missing key, unreadable secure storage, a readable-but-mismatched key, transient host reachability, and an answering endpoint that failed presence verification. Transient network/readiness failures are not cached as credential failures. Map: valid proof + matching local key → already running; 503 → retry the existing host for three seconds; malformed, replayed, wrong-authority, wrong-key, TLS, timeout, or other answering responder → fail without spawning; connection refused / network unreachable / DNS → definite no-listener → proceed. Thus the normal fast path performs one initial small unauthenticated loopback exchange, tries the local mirror once and the operating-system store at most once per client process, and then sends a constant-size process capability; a foreign listener can neither receive the API key nor trick the launcher into spawning onto its port.

The transient-failure rule has one bounded throttling exception: a `429 Retry-After` outcome is shared only until its clamped monotonic retry window closes, so concurrent callers honor one throttle response instead of hammering the proof endpoint. It does not turn the response into a stable credential failure or extend a retained capability beyond its signed expiry.

3. If effective ListenAny needs interactive acknowledgement → failed with guidance (do not auto-ack).
4. Probe-and-spawn is one step across processes. After a probe that finds no listener, the launcher takes an owner-only, `FileShare.None` retained lock (`.arcanum-serve-{name}.lock` in the parent of `ArcanumPaths.GrimoireDirectory`, the same hardened primitive and the same sibling placement as the maintenance and client-mutation locks: the lock is held for a whole launch, and a restore or installation reset replaces the Grimoire directory wholesale, which Windows refuses to rename while it holds an open handle) and holds it until its launch has finished. A client that had to wait for the lock probes again before spawning and adopts the host the other client started; a lock held for the whole 20-second poll window fails the launch with `Timed out waiting for another arcanum process that is starting the host`, and a lock that cannot be created safely only logs a warning and proceeds, because the host's own PID-file claim (item 5) is still what admits exactly one host. Before a fresh-install spawn, the foreground CLI explains that the host will read or create its private server-authentication key in the operating-system credential store and that any password dialog belongs to the operating system; Arcanum never receives the login password. Spawn via `IServeProcessLauncher` with `ARCANUM_AUTO_LAUNCHED=1` (direct `ProcessStartInfo`, no shell), then poll the same credential lease for up to 20 seconds. The presence timeout applies only to the loopback exchange and never cancels a slower local password dialog. Cancellation removes one caller's wait without abandoning an already-started physical credential-store read; that one flight is allowed to finish and its result is reused, which prevents a retry from opening another password prompt. Lease shutdown cancels the waiters and requests cancellation of the shared resolution. Missing/corrupt/mismatched credentials stop immediately with fixed repair guidance rather than reopening Keychain. These foreground budgets never terminate the spawned host or redefine its initialization lifetime.
5. Canonical PID file remains owned by `PidFileService` under `{ArcanumPaths.GrimoireDirectory}/arcanum.pid`. The launcher never deletes it on health failure. The claim is written to a unique owner-only sibling (`FileMode.CreateNew`, `FileShare.None`), flushed durably and closed, then published to the exact PID path with `File.Move(..., overwrite: false)` while holding the existing retained replacement gate. Every fresh claim and stale replacement shares that gate, so the destination absence check and publication cannot race between starters, including on Unix where the move API can check then rename. Two starters cannot both publish it, and readers see a complete claim even on Unix, where advisory share locks are acquired after creation. Every enabled claim attempt checks caller cancellation before taking the gate. Cleanup removes only a successfully opened sibling still owned by that attempt and stops owning its name after publication. Failed construction or a crash may leave private `.claim` residue, which is never treated as an owner. A competing claim that is still being written is waited for rather than deleted as malformed. An existing file blocks the start only when its PID names a live process that could have written it: a process that started after the file's last write is a recycled id and counts as stale, a start time the OS will not report, or a process the caller is not allowed to open at all (on Windows a protected or other-session process answers "Access is denied" even to the exit check), counts as live and is refused with the remedy rather than surfacing as an access error that stops the host, and a malformed, empty-and-old or dead-owner file is removed and the claim retried (a bounded number of times). **Replacing a stale file is serialised.** Two starters can read the same stale file as replaceable; if each then deleted it and claimed, the slower one would delete the faster one's fresh claim and both would run. The delete and the re-claim therefore happen only while holding an exclusive, owner-only `FileShare.None` gate beside the PID file (`arcanum.pid.replace.lock`, retained and never deleted so a waiter cannot hold a handle to an unlinked file), and only after the file is read again under the gate: a starter that waited finds the winner's claim, no longer stale, and refuses with the live-owner message. A stale file that cannot be removed fails with `Could not remove the stale PID file ... <reason>`, a file this account may not read (or, on Windows, a create over a delete that has not completed and does not clear) fails with an access-denied message, and only a lost race reports that another process is starting at the same time. Ownership is judged by start time against the file's last write and not by process name: the host runs as `arcanum`, under `dotnet`, or under a test host, so a name comparison would read a legitimate host as a recycled id and let a second one start over it, which is the worse mistake. The refusal names the PID file path and says to remove it if no Arcanum process owns that PID. `arcanum doctor` (`runtime.pid_file`) applies the same ownership rule through `PidFileOwnership`, so it never reports live a file a starting host would replace.

On a readiness failure, retry the invoking command, run `arcanum doctor`, confirm the local key with `arcanum key show`, and inspect the owner-only `logs/auto-serve-bootstrap.log` for host startup detail.

Direct interactive `arcanum serve` prints the same pre-bootstrap explanation itself. The auto-launched child suppresses it because its foreground launcher already owns the user interaction. A successful `arcanum setup` also explains what the first later server start will do; setup does not create the server key early or make secure storage part of configuration rollback. Only a successful host start publishes the owner-only, non-secret `secure-storage-bootstrap-v1` lifecycle marker; failed starts do not suppress the next explanation, and the marker replaces unreliable guesses based on whether one particular secret file exists. The file-encryption key is deliberately lazy: startup only proves whether existing ciphertext requires it, and a new key is created on the first attachment/upload/batch write so any later operating-system prompt arrives in that context.

Auto-launched processes do not expose `arcanum serve stop` or `daemon stop`.

**Host lifetime.** An auto-launched host is not a detached service, and it is not tied to its terminal beyond the launching command's own run either. `ServeProcessLauncher` spawns it directly from the invoking process with no `setsid`, process-group, or `DETACHED_PROCESS` step, so on macOS it starts in that process's session and process group with the same controlling terminal, and the terminal signals it only while that process group is the terminal's foreground job. While the launching command is still running as the foreground job (Command Center, or `run` and `ask` in the middle of a turn), Ctrl+C or closing the terminal reaches the host as well, and `ServeCommand` shuts it down gracefully on the interrupt. Once the launching command has exited, which is what `run` and `ask` do when they finish, the shell owns the terminal again and that process group is no longer its foreground job: Ctrl+C at the prompt does not reach the host, and closing the terminal does not end it either, because the terminal's hangup goes to its foreground process group and to the shell, and the shell no longer lists the finished command as a job to forward it to (this is the job-control rule, not something the repository tests: no probe of it ships here, so a shell configured to hang up every process it ever started could behave differently). The host then keeps listening until it is stopped with `arcanum serve quit`. Windows console-attach semantics differ and the launcher asks for no console window there, so no stop-with-the-terminal behavior is promised on Windows at all. `ServeOwnershipPolicy.OwnsHost` is true only when this launch reported `Started`: Command Center asks the host it started to quit on every exit path (including the terminal-too-small gate), a host that was already running is never stopped by a client, and `run` and `ask` leave the host they started running. Command Center gives that best-effort quit request its own five-second cancellation budget across credential preparation, response headers and response body. It uses a fresh token because normal UI cleanup has already cancelled the run token. Expiry logs a fixed warning and leaves the chosen CLI exit code unchanged; it does not kill a process or change the general API client headers deadline. Successful and failed completion dispose the cleanup timer. An operator who wants no resident listener sets `ARCANUM_NO_AUTO_SERVE=1`; one who wants a host that outlives the terminal deliberately starts `arcanum serve` under their own supervisor or installs the background daemon (`arcanum daemon install`; on Windows that is a service under an account the operator names, §11.29). No document promises survival or stop-on-hangup to an auto-launched host.

**MSBuild:** an explicit RID selects `PublishAot=true`, `SelfContained=true`, and `PublishSingleFile=false`; `IsAotCompatible` and `EnableConfigurationBindingGenerator` remain enabled. `ARC0001` rejects attempts to disable Native AOT and also rejects a `publish` with no runtime identifier, which would otherwise write a framework-dependent, non-AOT build that looks like the product (`-p:ArcanumDevPublish=true` is the deliberate escape hatch for a local framework-dependent publish with no runtime identifier; it never relaxes the rule for a RID-qualified publish, which stays an `ARC0001` error whenever Native AOT is turned off). On macOS, the linker is selected by the Native AOT runtime-pack version: .NET 10.0.12+ emits relocation anchors that repair Apple's large-object `ld-prime` limitation and therefore uses Apple's linker, while the isolated pre-10.0.12 compatibility path uses LLVM `ld64.lld` and fails with `ARCAOT008` if it is unavailable. The root `global.json` keeps the serviced SDK floor at `10.0.401` and selects the highest installed stable SDK (`rollForward: latestMajor`, `allowPrerelease: false`). CI and release resolve the latest supported stable SDK once per workflow run from Microsoft release metadata and install that exact version in every compiler lane. The currently verified SDK 10.0.402 carries runtime and ILCompiler 10.0.13. On `osx-arm64`, official SDK installations retain their own matching portable Native AOT runtime pack. When an installed bundled pack bears .NET's `nonportable.txt` marker, as Homebrew source builds do, `Directory.Build.targets` activates an isolated compatibility bridge that substitutes the matching repository-audited Microsoft portable pack instead; an SDK servicing update can therefore use its own matching pack without colliding with a stale `PackageDownload`. `PackageDownload` does not participate in `packages.lock.json`, so the bridge maps the SDK's bundled version to an audited `10.0.11`, `10.0.12` or `10.0.13` SHA-512 pin, keeps the version/hash pins, activation decision, linker selection, and every derived package, staging, SDK-search, and ILC-native path local so command-line global properties cannot replace them, and fails before downloading or compiling when the SDK requires an unaudited package. It verifies both NuGet's recorded SHA-512 and the actual `.nupkg` bytes against the repository-pinned content hash and fails before ILC on any mismatch. NuGet's separately expanded global-cache files are never linker inputs: the target copies the verified `.nupkg` into a clean build-owned intermediate tree, re-verifies that copy, extracts it there, validates its static Brotli/zlib inputs, and stages only those extracted bytes before .NET constructs the ordered native-link arguments. The staged Apple cryptography archive has only its compiler-module debug metadata removed; the signed NuGet cache remains untouched and all code/global symbols remain available. The shipping gate additionally rejects any macOS dependency outside system and app-relative locations, so a Homebrew path cannot silently enter the release. `System.CommandLine 2.0.10` and `System.CommandLine 2.0.10.Abstractions` are analyzer/source-generator packages with no runtime DLL reference, so no `TrimmerRootAssembly`, `[DynamicDependency]`, or IL-warning suppression is needed for CLI parsing. **Terminal.Gui** is referenced only from `Cli`; first-party AOT IL for the Command Center bootstrap is gated by `./scripts/verify-aot-il-warnings.sh` (method-level suppressions on `CommandCenterApp` only, with no project-level blanket suppress). Transitive vulnerable packages: `dotnet list package --vulnerable --include-transitive` on the Cli project.

### 4.4.2 Subsystem diagnostics and safe repairs (`arcanum doctor`)

`arcanum doctor` is a registry, not a switchboard. Two contracts in `Core/Cli/DoctorDiagnostics.cs` carry the whole surface:

- **`IDoctorCheck`** — `Id`, `Name`, `Subsystem`, `RequiresNetwork`, and `InspectAsync` returning a `DoctorFinding(DoctorOutcome, Detail, Remedies)`. Implementations must be **strictly read-only**: not creating a directory, not taking a lock, not opening a database for write. The one place this is subtle is the maintenance lock — `ArcanumMaintenanceLock.CannotAcquireSafely` answers by *acquiring*, which creates the file and tightens its parent, so `runtime.maintenance_lock` opens the existing path with a *shared* mode (`FileShare.ReadWrite`) instead and treats a sharing violation as held. A missing lock file is reported healthy before the parent's posture is judged: the parent is often a shared directory (`~/.config`) that only the first acquisition tightens, and with no file there is nothing anyone can hold. The probe therefore claims nothing exclusive: it fails against a holder, whose exclusive open refuses every other open, but two diagnostics never report each other as the holder. Holding is only knowable by attempting an open, so the probe's instantaneous open can still collide with a concurrent acquisition; `ArcanumMaintenanceLock.AcquireDetailed` therefore retries a verified-contended attempt three times (5, 10 and 20 ms) before it reports contention. The retry is deliberately in every exclusive acquirer — host startup, a restore, an installation reset and the CLI's exclusive operations — because the probe can land on any of them, so a diagnostic never fails a real acquisition while a genuine holder still reports contention after about 35 ms. The probe opens for write, the access real acquisition needs, so it reports a lock file the acquirer could not open. On Unix that has one known blind spot: .NET skips the shared `flock` for a write-access open on NFS, SMB and CIFS, so on a home directory on those filesystems the probe cannot see a holder and reports the file as unheld. Only the diagnostic is affected — acquirers still take `LOCK_EX` and exclude each other.
- **`IDoctorRepair`** — `Id`, `Subsystem`, `DetectorIds`, `Description`, and a side-effect-free `PlanAsync` separate from `ApplyAsync`. Diagnosis, repair planning, and repair application are three distinct steps; only an explicit `--apply` reaches the third.

**Outcome vocabulary.** `Skipped < Healthy < Unavailable < Degraded < Unhealthy`, ordered so aggregation is a plain maximum. `Skipped` sorts below `Healthy` because a check whose precondition is absent is not evidence of a fault. The original `ok`/`warn`/`fail` string survives as `DoctorCheck.Status`, now *derived* from the outcome by `DoctorOutcomes.ToLegacyStatus`, so the published `--json` shape is extended rather than replaced and existing consumers are unaffected.

**`grimoire.key_material` reads the committed sidecar.** An encryption secret that exists but cannot be read (`SecretStoreReadStatus.Unreadable`) is reported with fix-the-permissions guidance and no restore remedy, and the database checks that open the Grimoire themselves (`GrimoireProbe`) keep that status as their own `UnreadableKey` state with the same guidance rather than folding it into the missing-key restore. Beyond the encryption-secret status and a stranded pending upgrade, the check calls `GrimoireKdfSidecarFile.Read` on an existing committed `.kdf` sidecar instead of trusting that a file of that name exists. A torn, truncated, non-base64, wrong-salt-length or unsupported-version sidecar (`InvalidDataException` / `NotSupportedException`) is `Unhealthy` with its own `grimoire.restore_kdf_sidecar` remedy (restore the sidecar from the backup that holds the database), because the key salt is then unknown and the database cannot be opened; it is never reported as "current". A read that fails for I/O or permission reasons is `Unavailable` with no restore remedy, and the sidecar is never modified. That includes an open the operating system refuses or fails: `GrimoireKdfSidecarFile.Read` maps a denied open to `UnauthorizedAccessException` and any other failed open to `IOException`, and keeps `InvalidDataException` for what the file itself shows (a link, a hard-linked alias, a non-regular file, an oversize or unparseable body). An unreadable sidecar (mode 000, wrong owner, an I/O error) therefore says "unknown, fix the permissions", never "damaged, restore it".

**Id namespace.** Every id is `subsystem.snake_case`, and `DoctorDiagnosticRunner` enforces that the prefix matches the declared `DoctorSubsystem` at construction, alongside id uniqueness and the rule that every repair's `DetectorIds` name registered checks. A miswired registration therefore fails on the first `arcanum doctor` rather than silently omitting a subsystem from the report. The same namespace is what `--only`/`--skip` resolve against, so `--only grimoire` and `--only grimoire.integrity` share one vocabulary.

**Containment.** A check registered on the runner that throws becomes an `Unavailable` finding naming only the exception *type*. Both halves matter: doctor is the command an operator runs because the installation is already broken, so one failing probe must not take down the other twenty-odd; and an exception message is an uncontrolled string that may carry a path, a response body, or a credential. Operator cancellation is the sole exception and always propagates. The twelve original checks are composed by `DoctorCommand` outside the runner and still catch their own exceptions individually, as they always did — several of them put the exception *message* into their detail, which is why new checks belong on the runner.

**Repair contract.** Every repair is narrow, has a matching read-only detector, produces a no-change dry-run plan, and converges — a second successful apply reports `AlreadyConverged` with no steps. Repairs only ever narrow permissions, create a missing managed directory, or delete verified crash residue. Nothing regenerates a key over existing ciphertext, deletes user rows, or rewrites a corrupt encrypted database; those states fail closed with restore guidance (§5.4.6, §5.4.9). Safety preconditions are re-evaluated at apply time, not trusted from the plan: `runtime.remove_stale_pid` re-reads the PID file and refuses while any process holds that id, because `Process.GetProcessById` proves liveness but cannot prove identity against a recycled id.

**Non-billable network.** `providers.reachability` reuses `SetupProviderProbe` — one guarded `GET {endpoint}/models` per provider, never a completion — and is the only check that leaves the machine, so it is gated behind `--include-network`. Perplexity has no non-billable endpoint, so web research is diagnosed by credential status only. Endpoint URLs are never printed.

**Host relay over re-implementation.** `host.health_components` surfaces the full `HealthComponentDto[]` from `GET /api/health` rather than re-deriving Grimoire, MCP, provider, embedding, sandbox, workspace, and Conclave verdicts CLI-side, where several of those services are not even registered. An unreachable host is `Unavailable`, never a failure.

**Placement.** Contracts, the runner, the outcome algebra, and the remediation-command catalog live in `Core/Cli`; filesystem, configuration, credential, Grimoire, and operation checks and every repair live in `Infrastructure/Diagnostics`; the checks that need CLI-owned services (`ISetupProviderProbe`, `ArcanumHealthProbe`) live in `Cli/Diagnostics`. The `Core` and `Infrastructure` parts are inside the aggregate coverage denominator; the `Cli/Diagnostics` checks are outside it. The Include filter in `coverage.runsettings` instruments the `Cli` assembly so they appear in the report, but `Cli` is a reported assembly held to its own line floor and removed from the aggregate (§13.1) — they are scenario-tested, not part of the aggregate line gate.

The twelve original checks are a second case: they remain inline in `DoctorCommand`, which lives in `Cli` and is also `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`, so nothing in it is counted either way. They were left in place because rewriting a published `--json` surface and expanding it in one change would make any regression impossible to attribute; `LegacyDoctorChecks` gives them an id, subsystem, outcome, and remedy without touching their behavior. They resolve `--only`/`--skip` themselves rather than being filtered after the fact, because several of them probe the network, load the tokenizer, or scan encrypted blob storage — filtering results after paying for them is not filtering. Migrating them onto `IDoctorCheck` is the natural follow-up.

**Outcome derivation runs in both directions.** A registry check reports a `DoctorOutcome` and the runner derives `Status` from it. A legacy check reports the `ok`/`warn`/`fail` string and `LegacyDoctorChecks.Enrich` back-derives the outcome, which cannot recover `Unavailable` or `Skipped` — both collapse into the legacy vocabulary. One case is corrected explicitly: an optional `arcanum.json` or `mcp.json` that simply is not there reports `warn`, and projecting that onto `Degraded` would make `--strict` fail every default installation, so it is mapped to `Skipped` and its status restated as `ok`.

**Remediation commands are contract-tested.** `DoctorRemedyCommands` holds every command a `DoctorRemedy` may name, and `DoctorRemedyCommandContractTests` parses each against the real command tree. This exists because the earlier guidance pointed at `arcanum config set-key`, a verb this tree has never had; a renamed or removed verb is now a build failure rather than shipped bad advice. The legacy checks' *prose* detail still embeds a few command names inline (`arcanum setup`, `arcanum key show`) that the catalog does not cover — those move under it when those checks migrate.

### 4.5 `RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Api.DevHost` (console executable, debug-only)

Thin host for F5 debugging the HTTP stack without Spectre. References `Api`, `Core`, and `Infrastructure`; mirrors `ServeCommand` wiring. Not the production entrypoint. The project sets `IsAotCompatible` and `EnableConfigurationBindingGenerator` as unconditional **analysis signals** so F5 catches source-level AOT and binding defects, but it does not set `PublishAot` or import EF NativeAOT query generation. Its ordinary managed runtime therefore matches `arcanum serve` for dynamic EF behavior instead of stamping NativeAOT feature switches into a debug runtimeconfig. On first run generates an API key and prints it to stdout, which is why it **refuses to start** (a message on stderr and exit code `2`) in any environment other than `Development` or `Testing`; production hosting is `arcanum serve`.

### 4.6 `RetroDownfall.Compendium.Ux` (.NET 10 Avalonia desktop configuration editor)

Visual editor for §3.4 — ordinary pages read/write `arcanum.json` and do not run inference, daemon, Grimoire, or MCP operations. The polished Presets page consumes the same Core `IConfigurationPresetService` as the CLI for catalog, inspection, diff, apply, and reset; it does not duplicate overlay or persistence logic. Compendium edits credential environment-variable references, never provider/PFX values. Its local certificate generator writes an owner-only PEM pair, avoiding a generated password. `SettingDescriptor` drives controls/clamps; preset, parity, and coverage tests guard drift. It launches from `arcanum open compendium`, the compatibility `arcanum config open`, existing configuration actions, and the macOS application-menu **Settings...** item. A valid settings deep link selects the configuration surface; an absent, malformed, wrong-target, or future-schema link safely retains the default Edition section. See [`Compendium.README.md`](Compendium.README.md).

Descriptor-driven views cache only completed builds. They observe replacement field collections so an asynchronous configuration load rebuilds controls even when the view was created first; view construction and rebuilds perform no diagnostic file I/O.


---

## 5. Hybrid hosting model

### 5.1 Process roles

One binary; the CLI verb selects the process role (per-command detail in [`Arcanum.Command.Reference.md`](Arcanum.Command.Reference.md)). The defining axis is process lifetime:

- **No arguments** — opens Command Center on an interactive TTY; prints standard usage when noninteractive or `ARCANUM_NO_COMMAND_CENTER=1`.
- **`center` / `open center`** — explicitly enter that same in-process Command Center host; `ARCANUM_NO_COMMAND_CENTER` suppresses only the automatic no-argument entry.
- **`open`** — resolve an optional server resource, then launch The Forge or Compendium through the safe versioned deep-link contract; unavailable applications retain copyable development and CLI fallbacks.
- **`serve`** — the long-running HTTP host: builds `WebApplication` with slim defaults and blocks until shutdown.
- **`run`** — composes positional/piped/interactive input and bounded current-turn files, resolves active context, then dispatches one Agent, research, named-Spell, or context-preview run. The preview runs no model turn, but with retrieval on it still writes embedding run and ledger rows (§22.2). It is the only one-shot turn entry; `-p/--print` marks it explicitly headless so a scripted invocation never blocks on a picker or prompt even when attached to a terminal.
- **`completion` / `help`** — pure projections of the command tree. `completion` writes a shell script and touches no state; `help <topic>` explains a task in plain language. Neither reaches the host, except the hidden `completion resolve` helper, which is bounded and silent by design.
- Short-lived verbs — `look` / `doctor` run local checks (no HTTP for path checks); `lore`, `daemon jobs|initiative|alert` call the running host's `/api` (Unseen Servant interval control via `/api/unseen-servant/*`, §5.5.2; Comm Link smoke tests via `POST /api/commlink/send`); `daemon install|uninstall|status` drives OS service lifecycle (the daemon runs as the invoking user: Windows `install` creates a service only under an account the operator names at a prompt and refuses a `LocalSystem` one, directing to a per-user Task Scheduler task, §11.29). Bare interactive `arcanum` opens the Command Center (long-lived TUI) until `/exit`. A terminal that cannot host it — redirected stdin/stdout, `ARCANUM_NO_COMMAND_CENTER=1`, or a window under 80×12 — gets usage naming `arcanum run` rather than a degraded second REPL.

### 5.2 Why System.CommandLine 2.0.10

Source-generated parsing (AOT-clean, no reflection). Spectre remains for rendering. A repeated flag accumulates into its array-valued option (`run --with a --with b` and `watch --event-type`), and `AllowMultipleArgumentsPerToken` additionally lets one flag take several values where a verb documents it. There is no alias layer: exactly one spelling resolves each action, and a removed spelling fails to parse with a diagnostic naming its replacement.

Every direct command inherits these recursive root options, accepted before or after the verb:

- `--output-format text|json` selects the output shape, and `--json` is its shorthand. `json` forces one valid JSON document on stdout. Commands with typed structured output write that type through `IConsoleDispatcher.WriteJson` and an explicit source-generated `JsonTypeInfo`; legacy text commands are captured at the process boundary and returned as `CliTextPayload { output, exitCode }`. ANSI is disabled while JSON is active, so terminal control sequences cannot corrupt a pipe such as `arcanum budget --json | jq`. Combining `--json` with `--output-format text` is a contradiction and exits `2` rather than resolving a precedence.
- `--plain` disables ANSI color and terminal animation for that invocation. It does not persist or replace `Arcanum:Cli:Theme`. The guarantee holds inside CI environments whose detectors would otherwise force ANSI on (§16.5, "Opting out of ANSI is final").
- `--yes` is the only global auto-approval signal. `IConfirmationPrompt` returns immediately when it is present; otherwise a redirected-output invocation fails closed with `NonInteractiveConfirmationException` before reading stdin or writing a prompt. Command Center modals and inference `ask_human` are separate interactive protocols.
- `--no-context` bypasses owner-local saved CLI context for one invocation while retaining independent current-directory Campaign and Workspace detection.
- `-p`/`--print` is the explicit headless marker. It makes a real TTY behave like a redirected one through `ICliEnvironment.IsInteractive`, so a scripted invocation never blocks on a picker or a prompt merely because it happens to be attached to a terminal. Headless was previously implicit from non-TTY detection alone, which a script could not assert. `--print` also rebuilds the global stdout console without ANSI, colour or interactivity, exactly as `--plain` and `--json` do (`CliApplicationFactory.CreateInvocationConsoleSettings`), so a real TTY behaves like a redirected one for rendering as well as for prompts: no escape sequence reaches stdout, and a prompt such as the listen-any confirmation of `serve` refuses with exit `2` instead of blocking.
- `-v`/`--verbose` enables `IConsoleDispatcher.WriteVerbose`, which writes additional operator detail to stderr only. It never changes payload content or the exit code.

**Short-option contract.** A short flag means exactly one thing across the entire tree, verified by test. Claude parity does not justify ambiguous parsing, so `-c` is `--continue` everywhere and `--campaign` takes `-C`. `--output-format` is deliberately long-only because `-o` already means `--output`.

**Surface projection.** `CliSurfaceBuilder` walks the live `RootCommand` object graph — no assembly scanning, AOT-clean — into a `CliSurfaceMap`. Help examples, shell completion, "did you mean", topic help, and the committed `docs/Arcanum.CommandMap.json` are all readers of that one projection, so none of them can describe a tree the parser does not have. The command map is regenerated and compared by test, which makes an unintended diff in it an unintended change to the public surface.

`IConsoleDispatcher` owns the process stream contract: requested text/JSON payloads go to stdout; diagnostics, warnings, progress, and confirmation copy go to stderr. `CliInvocationContext` carries the immutable per-invocation option snapshot without process-wide environment mutation. New command code must use these services rather than writing directly to `Console` or serializing with a reflection overload.

Direct local writers use `IArcanumClientMutationBoundary`. The retained client-mutation mutex and its durable reset/replace-restore blocker are distinct from the installation maintenance lock; any owner needing both takes maintenance first, then client. Startup synthesizes a blocker from authenticated active evidence when needed and holds the client mutex through safe bootstrap. A reset or replacement restore publishes the blocker before its first durable maintenance effect and removes it last only after the authoritative evidence has converged. Publication is itself a point of no return: once the blocker file has been moved into place, the store's flush and verification read run on `CancellationToken.None`, and neither the maintenance acquire nor the host-startup acquire checks the caller's token again, so a cancellation that lands during or just after the publish returns the lease that owns the blocker instead of throwing and leaving one no operation holds. That removal is bookkeeping after the point of no return, so it runs on `CancellationToken.None`: a completed replacement restore retires its blocker even when the caller's token is cancelled as it returns, and a replacement restore cancelled while the installation is provably back in its prior state (nothing displaced, or a verified reversal with its secrets reinstated, and no staging retained) retires it before the cancellation propagates. That state is evidence an exit has to establish: it starts unproven, so an exit nobody anticipated keeps the blocker, and a cancellation during the restore's preparation — before the phase loop, with nothing displaced — first removes the staging root it had just created, whose journal would otherwise be the very restore evidence that refuses the retirement. Neither path bypasses `RemoveBlockerIfSafeAsync`'s reset- and restore-evidence checks, and a retirement those checks refuse on the cancellation path is logged with the restore's operation id and the refusal; any other exit leaves the blocker for the next start to resolve. CLI context/session/recency, Compendium configuration/preset/certificate work, and The Forge managed stores/exports admit the entire logical mutation through this boundary; host-derived values are revalidated inside admission, and stale pre-reset payloads cannot be written into the replacement generation. Ambiguous blocker, reset, restore, topology, permission, or identity evidence returns `Blocked` or `Unsafe` without running the callback. Client-local legacy projections are read-only fallbacks, not mirrors.

`CliExitCode` is the closed process contract: `0` success, `1` generic/runtime failure, `2` configuration or command-line failure, `3` network failure, and `130` cancellation. Arbitrary handler return values normalize to `1`. `CliApplicationFactory.RunAsync` disables System.CommandLine's default exception printer and is the global exception boundary: `CliFailureMapper` maps only exception categories to fixed public messages, never exception messages, paths, PII, API keys, or stack traces. JSON invocations receive a source-generated `CliErrorPayload`; the same fixed diagnostic goes to stderr.

### 5.3 `ServeCommand` lifecycle

1. Cancellation token check on the injected `CancellationToken` (System.CommandLine 2.0.10 wires SIGINT/SIGTERM to it automatically because the method declares a `CancellationToken` parameter).
2. `WebApplication.CreateSlimBuilder()` (§6).
3. `UseWindowsService` / `UseSystemd` (cross-platform no-ops on other OSes).
4. Kestrel: `ListenLocalhost(port)` unless `ARCANUM_HOST_ANY` is set (§7).
5. `ClearProviders()` so Serilog replaces default logging.
6. `AddArcanumConfiguration()` loads `arcanum.json` (JSON file only). Explicit environment overrides `ARCANUM_EDITION` and `ARCANUM_HOST_ANY`, plus secret references (`ARCANUM_PROVIDER_*`, `ARCANUM_HTTPS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD`, `ARCANUM_COMMLINK_WEBHOOK_URL`, `ARCANUM_GRIMOIRE_DEV_KEY`, `ARCANUM_HTTPS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD`) remain environment-backed.
7. `AddArcanumApiServices(configuration)` registers all services (API §8.3), including `AddArcanumDaemonServices` for the Unseen Servant (§5.5).
8. `Build()` → `MapArcanumEndpoints()`. Registration and provider materialization keep `HostLockSerilogFileSink` inert and create neither the guarded root nor a log file.
9. `StartAsync()` starts `GrimoireDatabaseHostedService` first. It acquires and publishes the exact installation maintenance lock, acquires the client-mutation mutex in maintenance-before-client order, authenticates reset/restore evidence, converges restore topology, and revalidates the guarded root. Only its post-topology callback may then activate the rolling file sink, persist the listen-any acknowledgement or auto-launch console lease, and run `ArcanumMasterKeyBootstrapper.EnsureMasterApiKeyExistsAsync`. Database bootstrap and the post-schema expected-installation-UUID check follow under the same serialized lifecycle. The generated master key is released to `ServeCommand` only after successful start. `PidFileService` starts after the verified Grimoire host (API §8.19). `Log.CloseAndFlush()` remains in `finally`.

`LoggingBootstrapper` installs a standard-error-only bootstrap logger during registration so failures before the rolling sink is admissible are still visible. The DI graph contains a deferred `HostLockSerilogFileSink`: registration, `Build()`, and an early log event do not create the guarded root or `logs/`. Activation is allowed only after the exact host lock is attached and restore topology has converged; deactivation and disposal occur before detach/release. This keeps one file writer and prevents logging, key generation, listen-any acknowledgement, or auto-console redirection from occupying an absent live-root name that recovery still needs.

Outbound request URIs never reach a log sink. Every named `HttpClient` Arcanum registers chains `.RemoveAllLoggers()` (the MCP Streamable HTTP transport, the Campaign rollup provider client and the Long Rest provider client are not named clients: each builds an owned `HttpClient` from an explicit handler chain that has no logging handler), because `IHttpClientFactory`'s default handlers write `Start processing HTTP request {HttpMethod} {Uri}` at Information and .NET redacts only the query — scheme, authority, and path survive verbatim, and a hosted MCP or A2A endpoint routinely carries its bearer token in a path segment. `LoggingBootstrapper` additionally sets `MinimumLevel.Override("System.Net.Http", Warning)` so the same guarantee holds for any client that is added later without the call. Provider- and dispatcher-owned diagnostics report host and outcome code only (§11.9).

### 5.4 Grimoire persistence (Infrastructure + Api)

**Role:** Local-first session history in an SQLCipher-encrypted SQLite file under `~/.config/arcanum/`.

**Composition:**

- **`GrimoireDatabaseHostedService`** — initializes SQLCipher, resolves the DB passphrase from a dedicated Grimoire encryption secret (the Data Protection–sealed `grimoire-key.dat`, which has no OS-store copy and is same-user-confidential rather than protected against a disk-level reader, §11.2) using PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (600,000 iterations) with a unique 16-byte salt stored in a `{grimoire.db}.kdf` sidecar, falls back to legacy API-key HKDF for databases without a sidecar, and installs the complete embedded schema via **`GrimoireDatabaseBootstrapper`** → **`GrimoireSchemaInstaller`** (raw SQLite, three transaction tiers with independent failure domains, no migration chain and no `__EFMigrationsHistory`; AOT-safe; no `MigrateAsync` on the host), publishes Covenant tier health through `ICovenantAvailability`, then `IGrimoireDbReadiness.MarkReady()` — a Covenant tier failure is published but never delays readiness (§5.4.5a, §5.4.5b). When erasure fingerprints exist, bootstrap resolves the erasure key once before readiness (a keychain read that can raise a macOS prompt), so Covenant agent writes are not withheld until an operator call; an installation with no fingerprints reads no erasure key at startup. A key mismatch or unreadable dedicated secret throws the sanitized `GrimoireDatabaseUnavailableException`, so startup fails closed while host/test cleanup can unwind normally; it never terminates the embedding process with `Environment.FailFast`. Bootstrapping always happens under the installation maintenance lock: both production entry points (the host's start-up and the CLI's exclusive operations) pass the lock they hold to `GrimoireDatabaseBootstrapper.EnsureInitializedAsync`, whose every non-private overload takes it as a non-nullable parameter and throws `ArgumentNullException` for a null, because topology recovery and Covenant authority preparation need exclusive ownership and a null lock silently skips them. The one implementation is a **private** core that accepts a null lock so tests can exercise the schema and key paths without one, reachable only through `EnsureInitializedWithoutInstallationLockForTestsAsync`; the compiler's nullable analysis (warnings are errors) therefore refuses any `src/` call that passes a null literal or a variable that may be null, `GrimoireBootstrapLockCallSiteTests.Every_non_private_bootstrap_entry_point_requires_a_non_null_lock_by_type` pins that every non-private entry point declares the lock non-nullable, and the same class's Roslyn scan stays as a second check that fails if any `src/` call site passes a literal null or `default` lock or calls that seam. The key probe distinguishes what it saw: only SQLite "not a database" (26) and "corrupt" (11) are a verdict on the key or the file and produce the "key verification failed" refusal; a database that is busy, locked or unreadable (busy, I/O, cannot-open) is reported as unreadable without calling it tampering, and the legacy-key candidate probe throws that same unavailability instead of answering "no candidate opened it"; a host shutdown that lands during the probe propagates as cancellation rather than as a key failure. Legacy databases are transparently re-encrypted to the new KDF on unlock; the new salt is durably staged to `{grimoire.db}.kdf.pending` before the irreversible `PRAGMA rekey` and promoted by atomic rename after it commits, so either side of that crash window is recoverable on the next start (§16.3). **The KDF is a frozen persisted-format contract.** `GrimoireKeyDerivation` is PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 600,000 iterations and a 32-byte output over the UTF-8 (no BOM) key material, base64-encoded; the legacy path is HKDF-SHA256 with salt `Arcanum.Grimoire.SQLCipher.salt.v1` and info `Arcanum.Grimoire.SQLCipher.hkdf.v1` (API key) or `…hkdf.v2` (dedicated secret). Every existing database was keyed through exactly these functions, so a changed constant would make them unopenable while every round-trip test stayed green. `GrimoireKeyDerivationTests` therefore pins each variant with a hard-coded known-answer vector computed once by independent implementations (Python `hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac` cross-checked with `openssl kdf`, and RFC 5869 HKDF cross-checked with the `cryptography` package) and asserts the iteration count. Changing the KDF requires a new declared KDF version with a rekey path, never an edit to these constants. The same bootstrapper runs from the CLI (`run` and Command Center) so host and CLI share one schema-install path (§10.5).
- **`CampaignLoggerQueue` / `Loremaster`** — bounded `Channel<Guid>` (capacity 100 **session IDs**, not Entry rows) with **non-blocking `TryQueue`**: duplicate session ids coalesce via a pending-marker map; a full channel rejects with a warning log and clears the marker so the session remains eligible for a later sweep (internal sweeps fail-open). Reading no longer releases that marker. Only the consumer's explicit terminal `Conclude` does, after success, a genuine skip, or a genuine failure. Maintenance deferral therefore keeps the exact session identity and uses a dedicated priority re-signal lane after admission reopens; normal intake cannot suppress or fill that lane. The lane is unbounded at the channel primitive but logically holds at most the one session owned by the sole consumer, so reopening creates neither a queue allocation on the ordinary path nor a backlog rush. Explicit `POST /api/sessions/{id}/rest` returns **202** when accepted/coalesced and **503** + `Session.RestQueueFull` when rejected. Background service `Loremaster` (formerly `CampaignLoggerBackgroundService`) runs hybrid sweeps using **`Session.UnsummarizedEntryCount`** (incremented on every entry append — both the inference path and The Forge `POST /api/sessions/{id}/entries` path, each serialized per-session via **`SessionEntryPersistence`** / **`SessionWriteLock`** + **`SqliteBusyRetry`** so concurrent appends never lose an increment; reset on summarize) instead of full-table `Entries` aggregation. The consume path loads session headers via **`GetSessionHeaderAsync`** (no entry hydration). Headless summarization uses a stateless `PingRequest` with `SkipSpellRouting`, `DisableMcpTools`, `DisableAllTools` (the transcript it reads can carry hostile text, so no tool is advertised, §22.2), `UnattendedMode`, optional `Arcanum:FastModel` (else `DefaultModel`); on success, `UpdateSessionCampaignRollupAsync` atomically sets `Session.Summary`, `LastSummarizedMessageAt`, and the remaining unsummarized count. The discovery sweep takes a DB-only `LoremasterSummarization` lease before its scope. Each queued session takes the same work lease before its scope and one external-effect group immediately before inference; that group remains held through the rollup write, then disposes before the scope and lease. A refused lease or group waits without any held scope or admission lease and changes no marker, provider state, rollup, or watermark. On genuine inference failure, the watermark is **not** advanced.
- **`ArcanumDbContext`** — compiled model; SQLCipher passphrase from hosted service.
- **`SessionRepository`** — implements **`ISessionRepository`** for Session CRUD, entry append, export, and analytics. Entry writes delegate shared invariants (lock, retry, per-entry validation, counter, UpdatedAt) to internal **`SessionEntryPersistence`**. **`AddEntryAsync`** returns **`Result<Entry>`** for expected domain outcomes (not found, archived, invalid or oversized entry); there is no total persisted-entry ceiling. **`PatchSessionAsync`** writes only the header fields a `SessionHeaderPatch` supplies (Title, Status) in one statement, so neither a concurrent change to the other field nor a Grimoire-owned counter or rollup is overwritten from a stale read; there is no whole-row header update. **`GetEntriesAsync`** refuses a keyset cursor with only one of `beforeCreatedAt` / `beforeId` (`ArgumentException`) rather than paging by offset.
- **`GrimoireRepository`** — implements `IGrimoireRepository` (the interface is the authoritative reference). Entry append/finalize/discard paths delegate the same **`SessionEntryPersistence`** invariants. `GetSessionAsync` loads the session header (no eager `Include`) and a code-owned bounded, chronologically ordered window of the most recent 1,000 `Entry` rows so very long threads do not exhaust host RAM. The window is pushed down server-side as parameterized SQL (`ORDER BY "Sequence" DESC LIMIT n`) and is widened to at least the number of entries after `LastSummarizedMessageAt`, guaranteeing read-time compression sees every unsummarized message. Campaign Logger reads one cancellable checkpoint page strictly after `LastSummarizedMessageAt` and widens it through the complete `CreatedAt` group containing the boundary row, so a timestamp-only watermark can never split a tool call/result pair. A successful summary commits that boundary as the next watermark; later passes continue until the durable unsummarized history is exhausted. Older entries remain in SQL — Campaign Logger summaries (API §8.7), pageable session reads/exports, and FTS5 `search_archives` cover the long tail.
- **Native transcript search** — `SearchArchivesAsync` returns `Result<string>` and `ISessionRepository.QueryAsync` returns `Result<SessionQueryResult>`. Both trim outer whitespace and bind the complete FTS5 expression as a SQL parameter on the admitted scoped connection. SQLite owns parsing and tokenization; no operator sanitizer or partial grammar sits in this path. A separate `SELECT rowid ... MATCH ... LIMIT 1` probe forces parsing even on an empty corpus or a title-only match, reads no transcript content, and does not scan a second full result set. Recognized native syntax diagnostics become `Validation.InvalidQuery` without exposing or logging the diagnostic or query. The exact native parser-stack-overflow diagnostic also maps to that code, with guidance to reduce nesting; other resource failures retain their infrastructure semantics. Native `unknown special query` refusals from raw leading-star expressions map narrowly to the same validation code with suffix-wildcard or literal-quoting guidance. Missing tables, corruption, admission failures and cancellation retain their infrastructure semantics. Empty/whitespace or overlong expressions fail validation rather than being truncated or mistaken for no hits. Valid tokenless quoted expressions such as `""` or `"***"` simply have no transcript hits. Only `Content` is indexed; `Id`, `SessionId` and `Role` remain `UNINDEXED`. Session search additionally matches the complete expression as a literal title substring and retains its existing date/identity paging. Internal Lexicon-generated literal terms keep `FtsMatchQuerySanitizer`, including dropping underscore-only or unattached-combining-mark terms, so they cannot poison a joined FTS query.
- **`CampaignRepository`** — `ICampaignRepository.AddAsync` returns `Result<Campaign>`. It attaches EF to a SQLite **immediate** transaction and wraps the insert in `SqliteBusyRetry`, preserving unique and relational integrity across concurrent writers without an incidental total-campaign count query or `Campaign.MaxReached` rejection. Large registries use paged reads; `CampaignBackedWorkspaceRegistry.GetAllAsync` follows every advancing page until exhaustion and treats a non-advancing offset as deterministic repository no-progress. Unrelated write/lock failures remain infrastructure exceptions. `GetByPathAsync` answers the row holding exactly the given spelling, otherwise the row that names the same path under another spelling (a trailing separator, or the case or Unicode normalisation form of a name on a platform whose file systems fold them), and registration refuses that same directory spelled another way inside the immediate transaction that would write it as `Campaign.DuplicatePath`, because the byte-comparing unique index on `Path` cannot see it. Two spellings that differ only by case or normalisation are one registration unless the file system shows them to be two directories: on a case-sensitive volume `proj` and `Proj` are two directories and can be registered side by side. `GetByContainedPathAsync` answers the registered Campaign whose root is the directory or one of its ancestors (the deepest wins; when several rows name the same directory, the strictest Sanctum wins, a Sanctum that cannot be read ranking above the rest, then the identifier). `GetBySpelledPathAsync` answers the same question for the path as it is written: no link in the path is followed, so a link that stands inside a root is a name inside that root whatever it points at and a path written through a link to a root is not written inside it (the roots' own spellings are still compared with every form of the root, the links of the root resolved, and the path is compared as text, but a case or normalisation fold between the two is judged per volume like any other: each directory the path's own spelling names is asked for its identity without following the last component, and a fold that equates one of them with a root is dropped when the root reaches a different directory, so on a case-sensitive volume a case-sibling registration is neither taken for the Campaign a path is really inside nor able to outrank it; the text still over-matches only where the file system cannot be asked, a root that is not on disk or a prefix that does not exist or is itself a link). `ICampaignRepository` gives `GetByContainedPathAsync` and `GetBySpelledPathAsync` no default body: a store that fell back to the exact match would silently stop applying a Campaign's Sanctum to every directory below its root or spelled differently, so each implementer, production repository or test double, answers both itself (a double either answers containment over the Campaigns it holds, delegates to its exact match when it holds no rows or its scenarios ask only about the exact roots it registered, or refuses path lookups when only identifier lookups are expected; a decorator forwards to the store it wraps), and a reflection test pins that both members stay without a body. `CampaignRootContainment` decides containment over the registered roots, by whole components so it never confuses `/work/app` with `/work/app-legacy`, and with no limit on how many components deep the directory is. The file system answers whenever it can: the physical identity (volume and file identifier) of the directory the registered root reaches, followed through every link with one query per root, is compared with the identity of every existing directory above the working directory, read when asked and never stored, so a repointed link cannot leave a stale answer. That comparison does not depend on any spelling and is exact on every volume: a root registered through a symlinked spelling (a temporary directory behind `/var`, a symlinked projects directory) is found from the physical path `getcwd` reports, a case or normalisation variant is found on a volume that folds them, and on a volume that does not, a case sibling is a different directory with a different identity, so it is neither contained by the root nor able to outrank the real parent. Only when the file system cannot answer for a pair (the root is not on disk, or the working directory is longer than any file system can hold) is the text of both compared, with trailing separators dropped, in Unicode normalisation form C, without regard to case on Windows and macOS, over the spelling as given and over the symlink-resolved spelling of each side; that comparison errs toward containment and is never consulted once the file system has answered. The normal form is fixed by the product's own Unicode 17 composition (`UnicodeNfc`, the tables the Covenant's NFC runs on) and never by `string.Normalize`, which asks the globalization library: the shipping executable, host and command-line client alike, runs with invariant globalization, where that method returns a non-ASCII string unchanged and throws nothing, so a registration under the decomposed spelling of an accented name would not be a duplicate of the composed one, the text fallback would miss a normalisation variant, and a path spelled through a link out of a root registered under the other spelling would not find its Campaign. A name that is not well-formed UTF-16 has no normal form and is compared as it is spelled. `PathKeyGlobalizationTests` refuses a use of the globalization library's normalisation in the sources that fix a path's identity (those named for a Campaign root or a Sanctum, the workspace path policy and the two Unicode helpers), and the published-executable smoke registers a directory under both spellings of its name against the real Native AOT binary. Because the answer costs one query per registered root and not a walk of each root's path, a lookup for a directory no root contains stays at milliseconds with thousands of registrations. `GetBySpelledPathAsync` costs the same one query per root, plus one no-follow query for each directory the path's own spelling names, made once per lookup; a root's own components are walked to find its resolved spelling only for a root whose directory is one of those or that is not on disk, so it stays at milliseconds too. The same identity comparison serves the guard's path boundary (`CampaignRootContainment.RebaseOntoRoot`, §11.15). A path longer than any file system can hold names no directory that exists and is compared as text only (§11.15 "Which Campaign governs a turn").
- **`ChronosyncEngine`** — implements `IChronosyncEngine`: compares the current `PatternSnapshot` to the latest `WorkspaceContext` row for that path, persists a new baseline row, and returns a `ChronosyncReport` (headless; no HTTP or Spectre).

**Outcome-model policy:** Repository and service boundaries return **`Result` / `Result<T>`** with wire-stable **`Error.Code`** values from **`ErrorCodes`** for expected, recoverable domain outcomes (not found, validation, limits, state conflicts). Reserve thrown exceptions for unrecoverable infrastructure faults, programmer errors, and transport layers where a catch-and-fallback is intentional (for example cooperative cancel on SSE). HTTP endpoints map **`Result.Error.Code`** to status codes exclusively via **`ArcanumErrorMapper`** — never by parsing exception messages.

#### 5.4.1 Grimoire data model

| Entity | Table | Primary key | Notable |
|--------|-------|-------------|---------|
| `Session` | `Sessions` | `Id` (Guid) | Optional `CampaignId`, `Status` (default `active`), `Title` (nullable), `CreatedAt`, `UpdatedAt`, nullable `Summary`, nullable `LastSummarizedMessageAt`, **`TotalTokensUsed`**, **`TotalCostUsd`** (decimal `TEXT`, matching EF's exact provider mapping; never SQLite `REAL` arithmetic), **`ForkedFromSessionId`**, **`UnsummarizedEntryCount`** (entries after watermark; default `0`; `-1` reserved for lazy backfill if ever needed); indexes on `CreatedAt`, `Status`, `UpdatedAt`, `(CampaignId, Status, UpdatedAt)`, `ForkedFromSessionId`, `UnsummarizedEntryCount`; cascade-deletes entries. |
| `Entry` | `Entries` | `Id` (Guid) | FK to `Session`; composite index on `(SessionId, CreatedAt)`; **unique** index on `(SessionId, Sequence)`; index on `Role`; `Role` (enum → int); `ModelUsed` (non-null); `Sequence` (`INTEGER NOT NULL`, application-assigned); optional tool columns; FTS5 virtual table `Entries_fts` + triggers for `search_archives` — the triggers key each index row by the entry's `rowid`, because FTS5 resolves only MATCH/rowid/rank constraints and an equality on the `UNINDEXED` `Id` column scans the whole index once per row. |
| `MageSetting` | `MageSettings` | `Key` (string) | `Value`, `UpdatedAt`; operator key-value surface (`/api/lore`, `arcanum lore`). No longer model-directed memory — the Lore MCP tools are removed; agent memory is The Lexicon (§10.6). |
| `WorkspaceContext` | `WorkspaceContexts` | `Id` (Guid) | `CreatedAt` (`DateTimeOffset`), `WorkspacePath` (mapped column `RootPath`, max 4096), `SerializedSnapshot` (JSON `PatternSnapshot` via `GrimoireJsonContext`). **Chronosync reporting** appends a row after each analysis; “latest” for a path is `ORDER BY CreatedAt DESC`. Composite index on `(RootPath, CreatedAt)`. |

**Supporting DTOs (Core):** `GrimoireEntryDto`, `LoreDto`, `UpsertLoreRequest`, `ChronosyncReport`, `ArcanumPaths`, `ChatCompletionUsage` (OpenAI-shaped `usage` for NDJSON and `/v1` responses), `PromptTurnResult` (buffered inference text + usage). The Session DTOs live under **`Core.Tower`** (`SessionDetailDto`, `EntryDto`, etc.), because a Session is an authored resource rather than a feature of any one client.

**Entry ordering authority (`Entries.Sequence`).** `Sequence` is a strictly increasing per-session append position and **the** intra-session chronological order. `CreatedAt` is not sufficient and must never be the sole sort key: one turn writes its prompt and its answer under a single identical `CreatedAt`, as does a tool call with its result, and `Id` is a random Guid that cannot break that tie in append order — a `(CreatedAt, Id)` sort inverts those pairs for roughly half of all turns. `CreatedAt` remains the wall-clock fact and the basis of the Campaign Logger watermark (`Session.LastSummarizedMessageAt`), so watermark reads still *filter* on `CreatedAt` while *ordering* by `Sequence`.

Repositories allocate sequences through `SessionEntryPersistence.ReserveSequenceRangeAsync`, which reserves a consecutive range while holding the per-session write lock that already serializes every entry append; a batch assigns its reserved values in append order. Gaps are permitted (a rolled-back transaction burns its range), reuse is not: the **unique** `(SessionId, Sequence)` index turns a lost allocation into a write failure instead of a silently reordered transcript. `Sequence` is application-assigned (`ValueGeneratedNever`), so EF always writes the value the repository supplied. It is deliberately absent from `ToolInteractionReceipt` identity comparison (§10.2.1) because it is an ordering fact, not part of receipt identity. Fork copies carry the source sequence forward, preserving order without renumbering.

Consequently `EntryTemporalQueries` orders and pages on `Sequence`: newest-first windows, offset pages, ascending export/fork batches, and the SSE replay cursor (`ISessionRepository.GetEntriesAfterAsync` takes an exclusive `Sequence`). The `GET /api/sessions/{id}/entries` wire contract still accepts a `(beforeCreatedAt, beforeId)` cursor; the repository resolves that entry's sequence and falls back to the timestamp/id predicate only when the cursor entry has since been deleted.

#### 5.4.2 Temporal context: Session-Based Consolidation and Chronosync

**Campaign continuity (`features.campaignRollups`, default `false`).** The Campaign Logger also maintains a separate, immutable native contribution for each Campaign-bound Session and a Campaign aggregate over those contributions. A short completed Session contributes without first reaching the compression threshold. `campaign_contribution_artifacts` / `campaign_contribution_state` own that Session's contribution; `campaign_rollup_artifacts` / `campaign_rollup_state` own the Campaign Summary; `campaign_rollup_sources` retains legacy exact consumed contribution revisions; Core25 shared segments and revision roots retain new provenance without copying every previous source (see Campaign continuity closure below). `campaign_fork_frontiers` excludes copied fork prefixes, including nested and cross-Campaign forks. A legacy copied prefix without durable proof remains ineligible for contribution; no ancestor or frontier is invented. These objects are declared under `Data/Schema` and installed through the resumable version-16 raw-SQL transition; the immutable version-15 fingerprint remains unchanged.

Pages contain at most 32 KiB of input and publish at most 8 KiB of summary, with 2,048 output tokens. These allocation bounds do not cap Campaign lifetime or the number of contributors. An Entry larger than the remaining page budget is represented by a deterministic `[omitted: N bytes]` marker as the first Entry on a page.
