The endpoint calls `ToolExecutionPipeline.RefreshSessionAttachmentAsync`, which shares selector ownership, source resolver, Sanctum, MIME/kind/size policy, version gates, encrypted persistence, and indexing enqueue with `refresh_session_file`; because no model turn is active, it neither checks an unrelated default model's vision capability nor queues content injection. Session attachment projections are cleared whenever the bound Session ID changes, while a metadata update for the same Session preserves its projection. Successful sidebar and confirmed resumes explicitly request a backend refresh before refreshing the unrelated Session list; a failed resume keeps the prior binding and rows. Every monitor request captures the Session ID and a monotonic in-process binding revision. Snapshot admission, notice generation and binding changes share a short synchronous lock, so a delayed response from a previous visit cannot overwrite the current projection, including a switch away and back to the same Session. No provider or filesystem work occurs under that lock.

**Standalone CLI projection:** The attachment CLI delegates to the same authenticated listing, snapshot, live-reference, secure refresh, version-selection, pin, export, and reveal services as the host and Command Center; it does not duplicate persistence or source policy. Complete invocation, selector, privacy, overwrite, and output behavior belongs to [`Arcanum.Command.Reference.md`](Arcanum.Command.Reference.md).

Direct inference attachment references remain opaque Bound attachment IDs owned by the effective Session. They enter the explicit-first materialization ledger without an incidental count ceiling. Metadata validation does not load their aggregate bytes: after provider/model resolution, each snapshot is streamed, admitted against the current candidate context, and appended in request order before the next reference is opened. Failed or cancelled chat attempts retain staged IDs; only a completed turn consumes them.

**Metadata invariants:** `SessionAttachments` is installed by the embedded `20260719180000_AddSessionAttachments` script and accessed through scoped `ArcanumDbContext` raw SQL + `SqliteBusyRetry`, not an EF `DbSet`.

| Column group | Bound attachment | Pending attachment |
|--------------|------------------|--------------------|
| `Id` | set | set |
| `SessionId` | non-null | null |
| `EntryId` | set when the user Entry is known; otherwise nullable | null |
| `PendingTurnId` | null | non-null |
| `State` | `Bound` | `Pending` |
| `LogicalKey`, `OriginalFileName`, `Version`, `RelativePath`, `ContentSha256`, `MimeType`, `ByteLength`, `Kind`, `CreatedAt` | populated | populated |
| `SourceKind`, `SourceStatus` | `SnapshotOnly`/`NotApplicable` unless host-verified | same |
| `SourceWorkspaceIdentity`, `SourceRelativePath`, `SourceCanonicalPath`, `SourceContentSha256`, `SourceFileIdentity`, `SourceLastWriteAt`, `SourceByteLength`, `SourceDiagnosticReason` | optional encrypted provenance | optional encrypted provenance |
| `EncryptionVersion`, `EncryptionKeyId` | current envelope version/key id | current envelope version/key id |

**Source provenance and refreshability:** attachment bytes always remain a durable snapshot; the existing attachment-store `RelativePath` always points to that snapshot and is never reinterpreted as an original file locator. A host-trusted caller may supply an `AttachmentSourceClaim` to `PersistNewFromSourceAsync`. The scoped `IAttachmentSourceResolver` accepts it only when the active configured workspace exists and the source passes lexical containment, canonical/symlink containment, pre-open path identity, post-open handle identity, and immediate pre-I/O revalidation. The handle must be a regular file with exactly one hard link: a second name for bytes that may live outside the workspace passes every path-containment test, so a link count other than one is `Unsafe` on every read path (persistence, reference, and refresh). A claim that names its own workspace root is accepted only when the `IWorkspaceRegistry` knows that root. The registry is a required constructor dependency of the resolver (no optional parameter, so no composition can leave the resolver with nothing to prove a claim against): the host composes the Campaign-backed registry, and the offline CLI maintenance composition (`AddArcanumGrimoireForCli`, which registers the resolver because the session store and the Grimoire repository depend on it) registers an empty `InMemoryWorkspaceRegistry`, so a claimed root there is `Unsafe` as unregistered rather than trusted. An unregistered claim can only refuse and never widen containment. A claim with no root still resolves against the active configured workspace. It hashes the bytes read from the verified handle. Matching bytes produce `Refreshable`; differing bytes are retained as a safe `PriorVersion` snapshot. Ordinary native/API `AttachedFileDto` paths are untrusted labels and always persist as `SnapshotOnly`; remote clients cannot nominate a live host path.

Public `SessionAttachmentDto` exposes only source kind/status, refreshability, opaque workspace identity, sanitized workspace-relative path, safe hash/time/length observations, and a bounded diagnostic reason. `SourceCanonicalPath` and file identity remain encrypted raw-SQL metadata and are never returned by the API. On restart reconciliation revalidates workspace identity, containment, file identity, availability, and observed content. Missing, moved, inaccessible, unsafe, changed-workspace, or corrupt metadata changes source status without deleting the row or snapshot bytes. Forks copy source metadata with the snapshot and revalidation applies in the fork. Watcher-based rename repair is an optional future optimization; correctness never depends on a watcher.

The complete per-round ordering is maintained in [Arcanum.CHAT-LOOP.md](Arcanum.CHAT-LOOP.md): a tool result cannot alter the provider request that produced it, so refreshed content is appended only to the next request in the same logical turn and only after the round's complete tool transcript.

The source columns are part of the canonical hand-authored `20260719180000_AddSessionAttachments.sql` table definition and remain outside the compiled EF model. This release intentionally does not ship an upgrade migration: installations with an older Grimoire schema must recreate the database when installing the latest version.

**Lifecycle and consistency:**

- New attachment publication captures the encrypted blob's no-follow filesystem identity, acquires SQLite writer ownership, revalidates that exact artifact, and inserts its metadata before releasing the same transaction. Fork row publication performs the same validation after acquiring the writer lock inside the ambient fork transaction. If reset/deletion wins first or the path is replaced, no attachment row is published and identity-bound cleanup preserves the replacement.
- Before session binding, bytes and rows live under `_pending/{turnId}` with `State=Pending`. `SessionBound` / the first persisted user Entry promotes by copying bytes into the Session tree, then updates the rows to Bound in a DB transaction. This is not an atomic filesystem move.
- Persistence completes before model inference; failure closes the turn before the model sees bytes.
- Bound attachment metadata is read through stable `(LogicalKey, Version)` SQL keyset pages. The all-version list API still iterates every page to preserve its established response contract, while turn/tool hot paths request only SQL-selected latest rows. Prompt index construction applies its logical-key `LIMIT` in SQL and pages only version integers for the selected keys; it never loads every full attachment record merely to group and discard most of them in managed memory.
- Fork pre-copies ciphertext, authenticates every chunk, and verifies the decrypted plaintext hash, then inserts the new Session, Entries, and attachment rows in one EF ambient transaction with raw SQL enlisted. A disposable fork scope retains only captured file identities across copy pages and completes immediately after the ambient transaction commits. Failure cleans those exact owned artifacts from every completed page, preserving occupied destinations, unrelated files and replacements; it never recursively deletes the fork directory. Compensation is best effort and cannot replace the original fork failure. The source metadata remains paged, and commit releases cleanup ownership before post-commit indexing.
- Hard purge deletes attachment rows with Session/Entry rows in one DB transaction, then best-effort removes the Session attachment tree under an independent cleanup token. A failed filesystem delete is logged and left for reconcile.
- Hard-deleting an Entry sets matching `SessionAttachments.EntryId` to null in the same transaction; the Bound row and bytes remain owned by the Session.

`SessionAttachmentPendingGcHostedService` reconciles once at startup. It removes stale Pending rows and matching pending directories after a code-owned retention window; removes Bound rows whose Session no longer exists before best-effort directory cleanup; deletes rows for missing/escaping files; and deletes unreferenced files under the attachment tree. Filename suffixes such as `.tmp` or `.tmp.csv` never override row ownership: staging files and ordinary blobs pass the same snapshot and live-row claim checks before orphan removal.

Both of those last two sweeps run while the host is serving — at startup Kestrel is already accepting requests, and `POST /api/operations/reconcile` can drive reconciliation at any time — so each carries an explicit concurrency boundary rather than serializing attachment writes behind the sweep. A row deletion is conditional on the persisted row still naming the exact `State` and `RelativePath` the sweep observed, so an attachment promoted concurrently is an atomic no-op for the sweep and is never destroyed. "Unreferenced" is likewise evaluated against a moving target: nothing modified at or after the moment of the sweep's own path snapshot is touched, because an attachment write lands its ciphertext *before* it inserts its row (which also spares `EncryptedBlobStore`'s staging temporaries); every candidate is re-checked against the live table immediately before unlinking, so a row committed since the snapshot keeps its bytes; and uploads and promotion copies in flight are skipped, because their ciphertext can predate the snapshot and still have no committed row. Each upload and promotion registers its destination in a process-wide in-flight set before the first byte lands and unregisters it only after its rows commit or publication fails; encrypted-writer and copy staging files have the same protection. Pending directory aliases are compared by physical directory identity, and the sweep consults that set before its live-table re-read. For a Session-owned candidate it first attempts the existing Session gate without waiting, skips a held gate, and retains a successful acquisition through the destructive checks and identity-owned unlink. A new fork cannot acquire ownership between a gate observation and deletion; the sweep never waits behind an active publication or reverses the Session-then-pending lock order. The promotion also revalidates every copy's captured file identity inside its commit transaction, so a copy that is unlinked anyway aborts the promotion with the original intact instead of publishing a row for missing bytes. A production fork holds its Session gate from before the first copy through its ambient transaction commit, so its unpublished copies remain protected even before or after attachment rows are inserted into that uncommitted transaction. Commit-time identity revalidation remains an independent defense against external deletion or replacement. The sweep snapshots the no-follow physical identities of claimed files as well as their stored path spellings. A legacy candidate with no exact live SQL claim is compared against fresh claimed identities before identity-owned deletion; this honors the actual volume's case and normalization behavior without globally ignoring case. An unresolved claim conservatively prevents orphan removal for that pass. This legacy fallback can scan the live claims per unmatched legacy candidate; it is not a constant-time full-tree sweep. Invalid `_pending` child names are warned and left untouched rather than passed to an identity-unsafe delete. The code-owned per-Session byte boundary rejects only measured storage overflow; there is no per-logical-key version-count cap. Bound files are not background-pruned. Reconciliation also fails closed when source metadata is malformed or no longer resolves, updating only its availability/status fields and preserving an otherwise valid attachment snapshot. Encrypted-file validation authenticates every referenced snapshot; legacy plaintext is surfaced for migration by health/doctor and remains readable through the explicit compatibility lane; corrupt envelopes and snapshot digest mismatches fail reads.

**Privacy:**

| Layer | Protection |
|-------|------------|
| Grimoire metadata (`SessionAttachments`) | SQLCipher-encrypted (same as other Grimoire tables) |
| Attachment **bytes** on disk | Chunk-authenticated AES-256-GCM `ARCABLOB` envelope plus owner-only permissions under `~/.config/arcanum/attachments` |
| File-encryption master key | OS credential store `arcanum/file-encryption-master-key`; DP-sealed recovery mirror in `file-encryption-key.dat` |
| OS disk encryption / backup | Operator responsibility |
| Full conversation continuity | Create and verify one encrypted `.arcbackup` containing the database, attachment ciphertext, and filtered portable recovery keys from one generation (§5.4.8) |

Deleting or reinstalling only `arcanum.db` leaves orphan encrypted attachment bytes. A portable backup uses §5.4.8 rather than manually copying a live database and blob tree, and `arcanum backup restore` (§5.4.9) moves that whole ownership set — `~/.config/arcanum/attachments`, the database, and matching recovery keys — as one generation or not at all; a reset or uninstall must respect the same set. This tree is distinct from `/v1/files`, whose encrypted envelopes use `files/{guid}`. Configuration authority remains the Compendium reference linked from §3.4.

### 10.2.6 Structured mentions and durable context pins

`SessionContextPinKind` is the closed structured-mention vocabulary: `File`, `DirectorySnapshot`, `SymbolRange`, `SessionEntry`, `Attachment`, `Url`, and `Diagnostic`. The existing free-text `@path` staging contract remains backward compatible and turn-scoped; pins are an additive, explicit session facility. Command Center exposes the vocabulary in `/help` and provides `/pins`, `/pin <kind> <target>`, and `/unpin <pin-id>`. A `File` pin runs from the Terminal.Gui key handler, so it takes the attachment paths' guard: `AttachableFile.TryConfirmRegularFile` refuses anything but a regular file, `AttachableFile.OpenWorkspaceFileForRead` opens without ever waiting on the path (a FIFO swapped in after the check is refused by its handle), then admits that handle through `WorkspacePathPolicy.TryGetOpenedHandleRelativePath`. The kernel-relative result becomes the pin target and the same admitted handle supplies the streamed SHA-256; filesystem case and contained aliases work without weakening physical containment, and an outward symlink is refused before content is hashed. Invalid paths are normal command refusals. The dispatcher gains no Infrastructure dependency. `/attach` and `/pin` retain internal whitespace in their original argument tails, avoiding selection of a different file whose name has fewer spaces. A registered but incomplete slash command receives its registered usage. Branch-child navigation requires a current Session before matching parent ids. `/config` reads the configuration service’s local path property without opening or writing the configuration file and labels it local, independently of host routing. Bare `/context` is the token readout; the removed `/context list|pin|unpin` spellings are denied by the parser with a message naming those replacements rather than silently executing the readout.

The raw-SQL `SessionContextPins` table stores the session id, kind, stable target identifier, display label, optional content hash/version, and created/updated timestamps. The unique key is `(SessionId, Kind, TargetIdentifier)`, so pinning an existing target updates metadata without duplicating it. The foreign key cascades on session deletion. This table is intentionally absent from the compiled EF model and is installed by `20260730010000_AddSessionContextPins.sql`; `ISessionContextPinStore` owns access.

Materialization happens afresh before every bound inference turn:

- File, directory, and symbol/range paths are resolved relative to `PingRequest.WorkingDirectory`. Containment fails closed in two steps: the lexical prefix check, then the canonical-path rule of `WorkspacePathPolicy` (the root and the candidate are each resolved through every symbolic link they traverse and compared), which also admits a link that stays inside a workspace root that is itself reached through a link and rejects an intermediate directory link that leaves the workspace. File and symbol/range content is opened once through `SecureFileReader` with link following disabled and is accepted only when the opened handle is a single-link regular file. The no-follow open guards only the final path component, so an intermediate directory link swapped in after the path check would be followed; the kernel's own path for the open handle (`WorkspacePathPolicy.IsOpenedHandleUnderWorkspace`) must therefore be inside the workspace root both before and after the read, and a handle that is not (a link retargeted, or a directory moved out of the workspace while the file was open) reports `Unsafe` with no content. Missing sources produce a labeled `Missing` block. Total file length is not an admission gate: an accepted file up to the 8 MiB hash cap is hashed incrementally across the complete handle while retaining at most the pin output ceiling; a hash differing from the optional pinned version produces `Modified` and injects only the current bytes with the new hash disclosed. A larger file is previewed without reading past the preview (a seekable handle that declares more than the cap is never read beyond the pin output ceiling), and its `size=<bytes>;mtime=<ticks>` token (read from the open handle, never re-resolved by path) replaces the hash as the freshness value; a pinned version in that form that no longer matches reports `Modified`, while a pinned content hash cannot be verified above the cap and is not reported as a change. Old bytes are never cached in the pin row.
- Directory snapshots are deterministic ordinal breadth-first path/size listings, never full recursive content. They do not descend into `.git`, `node_modules`, `bin` or `obj` below the pinned directory (a pin rooted at one of them still lists it), so version-control and dependency trees cannot spend the byte budget before the source does. A `.gitignore` in the workspace root, in any directory between it and the pinned directory, or in a directory the walk enters is honoured too: comments, negation, anchoring, directory-only rules, `*`, `?`, bracket classes and `**`, with the nearest file that has a rule for an entry deciding it. Each file is opened through the no-follow regular-file open (a link, pipe or device of that name contributes nothing), read to at most 64 KiB ending at a whole line, and limited to 1,000 rules of at most 512 characters; whatever is dropped or unreadable lists more files, never fewer. `.git/info/exclude` and the user's global ignore file are not consulted, and the fixed list above is never re-included by a negation. A snapshot stops at the pin byte ceiling or after visiting 2,048 directories, whichever comes first, and reports `Truncated` with the reason. Symbol ranges require `path:start-end`, have no line-count ceiling, scan the opened handle incrementally, retain only the byte cap, and normalize CRLF output without loading every source line.
- Entry targets must parse as an entry id belonging to the same session. Attachment targets accept an attachment id or logical key and must resolve to a bound text attachment in the same session. Diagnostic text is stored as the stable target itself. URL metadata may be pinned and listed, but implicit materialization reports `Unsupported`; URL retrieval must enter through guarded web browsing and never an unrestricted `HttpClient`.
- Each pin is limited to 64 KiB and each turn to 256 KiB of materialized pin data. The existing `sessions.maxPinnedEntries` durable-pin admission setting is out of scope and remains unchanged; materialization adds no separate pins-per-turn count ceiling and considers every already-accepted pin. Truncation and byte-budget-deferred pin counts are explicit. These appended `TextContent` parts flow through the normal model-aware context/mana estimator, so their tokens are visible without a parallel estimate.

Every materialized item is surrounded by an adaptive backtick fence and explicit source kind, label, stable id, freshness status, and diagnostic fields inside an `UNTRUSTED SESSION CONTEXT DATA` envelope. Models must treat these bytes as data, never instructions. Each header value is rendered on one line with line breaks, control characters, backslashes and backticks escaped, and the cap of 256 characters is on that rendered text (an escape is kept whole or left out, and an ellipsis marks the cut), so a pin label or id cannot open a line that reads as the end marker or a fence nor grow past about a fifth of a kilobyte through escaping; a `Diagnostic` pin's stable id is the pin id rather than its body, which appears only inside the fence. The per-turn budget is applied to the framed block: when a block does not fit, the closing fence, a `[TRUNCATED BY PER-TURN CONTEXT BUDGET]` line and the end marker are reserved first and only the content is cut, so every emitted block is balanced and ends with the end marker; a pin that cannot fit even an empty frame is counted as deferred instead, and it is deferred before its source is opened, hashed or walked. The identity hash a materialized item carries into the context ledger is the source's own hash when the store supplies one (an attachment's content hash) and otherwise the SHA-256 of the framed block exactly as injected, so a block cut by the per-turn budget never claims the bytes the model did not see. A single source failure, including attachment lookup, corrupt or unreadable bytes, decryption failure, or source-local cancellation, becomes an error/status block whose diagnostic is a constant per exception type (never the exception message); later healthy pins continue and the failure cannot mutate or corrupt the session. Caller cancellation propagates instead of becoming a pin error. Listing the pin collection remains outside this per-source recovery boundary. `Entries.IsPinned` remains the independent transcript-compression contract: context pins neither set it nor change which historical entries compression retains.

### 10.3 Registration lifetimes

`IArcanumIntelligenceProvider` / `WizardIntelligenceProvider` are **scoped** (one instance per request scope). `IChatClientFactory` is **singleton**; each call to **`ResolveClientAsync`** returns a **`ChatClientLease`** that owns a fresh `IChatClient` for that inference turn — over the named OpenAI-compatible `HttpClient` pipeline for an HTTP provider, or over one short-lived child process for a Familiar. The lease lifetime is the process lifetime, so there is no long-lived CLI to leak or wedge between turns.

### 10.4 Telemetry and observability

Telemetry is the set of `System.Diagnostics.Metrics` instruments on `ArcanumMetrics` (one process-wide `Meter`), emitted at the point each event happens and observed by whatever listener or exporter the host attaches. The product keeps no in-process roll-up of them: an earlier `TelemetryService` aggregated every measurement into snapshots that nothing read, and it was removed together with its snapshot types and the subagent run sink (a child run's tokens, cost, and outcome are on its `SubagentRunResult` and its long-running-operation record; raw child turns are not telemetry events). Command Center's non-focusable `TelemetryPane` consumes the native per-call `context` frames instead: it performs one immutable text replacement per update and shows chat-history, explicit-attachment, refreshed-file, attachment-RAG, and workspace-RAG tokens plus an estimated or provider-billed input total. Ledger-recorded semantic pressure produces a dropped-RAG warning. On wide layouts the pane shares the left rail with Sessions; `Ctrl+T` toggles `CommandCenterState.ShowTelemetryPane` without taking focus. Attachment DTO indexing states are aggregated separately in the footer as running/pending, completed, or failed; while any row is Pending (including snapshot-only rows), the drift monitor schedules another authenticated projection read after about one second, subject to coalescing and the logical-operation spacing above, until it reaches a terminal state. A transient failed GET does not strand that known pending projection; its next poll remains paced and cancellation stops self-polling. Rendering never exposes chunk text, vectors, hashes, or raw ledger labels.

### 10.4.1 Grimoire integration

The provider persists through `IGrimoireRepository`. When `sessionId` is set, prior turns are loaded for `IChatClient`. A dynamic `ChatRole.System` message from `SystemPromptBuilder` is prepended in memory (not persisted to Grimoire). Tool rounds are persisted as bracket-formatted `Entry` rows. Assistant entries contain **answer text only**: raw, visible, protected, and summarized reasoning are never written to Grimoire. After every successful buffered or streamed turn with a bound session, the code-owned tracking policy makes **`IncrementSessionTokensAsync`** atomically add the provider-authoritative reported **`total_tokens`** to **`Session.TotalTokensUsed`**. Persistence failures on the buffered path are logged as warnings only.

### 10.5 Spatial context on inference

**Problem:** the API host's cwd is not the operator's shell cwd.

**Solution:** `PingRequest` carries `WorkingDirectory`, `ContextSnapshot` (`PatternSnapshot`), optional `SessionId`, optional `StatelessMessages` (`CoreChatMessage[]` transcript for stateless callers), optional `AttachedFiles`, optional `ChronosyncDelta` (`ChronosyncReport`), and optional `DataStreams` (reserved for future real-time JSON injection). For live `run` Agent/Spell inference and Command Center turns, the CLI resolves `Environment.CurrentDirectory`, runs Eye of the World, runs `IChronosyncEngine` inside a DI scope against the local Grimoire, and populates these fields before the inference HTTP call; `run --dry-run` deliberately remains a static server preview and may omit the locally produced snapshot/delta until live handoff. CLI bootstrap (`run` and Command Center) reuses `IGrimoireCliInitialization` once per process so SQLCipher setup and first-run migrations match the host (`GrimoireDatabaseBootstrapper`, shared with `GrimoireDatabaseHostedService`).

**`SystemPromptBuilder.Build` ordering (DCI blocks):**

| Position | Block | Produced by |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | **Preamble** (base persona + the "INSTRUCTIONS override conflicting DATA" rule) | static content |
| 1 | **DATA** (`[None]` when empty): `### The Covenant, Proposed` → `### Lexicon (Known Context)` → `### Chronosync Report (Temporal Delta)` → `### Attached Files for this Turn` → `### Retrieved Session Attachment Context` → `### Session Attachments Index` → `### Semantic Context (Retrieved Codebase)` → `### Saga (Associative Memory)` → `### Hierarchical Context (The Tapestry)` → `### Data Stream: {StreamId}` | agent-authored Covenant admission (§10.13), Lexicon retrieval (§10.6), `ChronosyncDelta`, explicit attachments, ledger-filtered attachment/workspace RAG, Saga retrieval, Tapestry retrieval (§10.4 §21.4 §21.8 §21.11) |
| 2 | **CONTEXT**: `### Workspace Context` / `### Table of Contents` → `### The Covenant, Global Confirmed` → `### The Covenant, Campaign Confirmed` → `### Master Codex (CODEX.md)` → `### Campaign Summary (cross-session context)` (when enabled and present) → `### Session Summary (compressed context)` (only on compression; legacy `### Campaign Summary (compressed context)` when the feature is off) | `ContextSnapshot`, operator-authored Covenant admission (§10.13), `CodexReader`, read-time compression (§10.2.3) |
| 3 | **INSTRUCTIONS**: `### Active Operational Spell ({Name})` (omitted when `SkipSpellRouting`) → `### Available Spell Scripts` (when present) → `### Output Formatting Directive` (when `CliTerminalFormatting`) | `SemanticRouter`/`SemanticSpellRouter` (§10.2.2 §21.10), scripts scan, CLI flag |

**Ordered prompt document and cache planning.** `SystemPromptBuilder.BuildDocument` emits immutable ordered `PromptSegment` values and `Build` delegates to `Render()`. Regression tests require byte-for-byte equality with the established DCI text, including whitespace, adaptive fences, Unicode, and `[None]`. Preamble, Codex, primary/resonant Spell text, stable script instructions, and request-invariant terminal formatting are stable candidates. Lexicon, Chronosync, attachments/index/images, semantic retrieval, Saga, Tapestry, streams, workspace/session summaries, and per-request instructions are volatile. For cumulative-prefix contracts, planning stops at the first volatile segment; later stable Codex/Spell segments are not falsely counted as independently cacheable. The shipped root-only key/retention dialect does not split content or add messages.

**Covenant placement and attribution (§10.13).** Both Covenant sections are optional and absent by default. When absent, `BuildDocument` emits the exact pre-Covenant segments, the same `[None]` placeholder, and an unchanged cache plan; a golden-digest test pins those bytes. When Proposed content is present the DATA region is emitted as `DataHeader` / `CovenantProposed` / `Data` segments instead of one `Data` segment, because `PromptCachePlanner` hashes segment kind and text and places its boundary by segment index — splitting DATA unconditionally would move every existing cache key on a turn that injects no Covenant bytes at all. Covenant segments are `Volatile`, sensitivity-marked, and never boundary-eligible, so no provider-retained cache prefix can ever contain profile bytes. `BuildResult()` renders once and returns the string, per-segment cache descriptors, and the Core-owned `SystemPromptAttributionMap`; every later consumer reads spans over that one string.

**Workspace Context (CONTEXT, hardened):** `PatternSnapshot.RootPath` and every Table of Contents thread are workspace-derived paths, and a POSIX filename may legally contain a newline. `AppendContextSegments` runs both through `SystemPromptBuilder.HardenWorkspacePathLine`, which replaces every control character with `_` so a filename cannot open a fresh line and forge a second `## INSTRUCTIONS` header inside CONTEXT. Unlike `HardenAttachmentIndexName` it deliberately preserves `#`, which is legal in both POSIX and Windows paths and which the model needs verbatim to address files; `#` cannot start a heading here because `RootPath: ` and `- ` already occupy the start of every rendered line. A thread that hardens to nothing is dropped alongside the whitespace-only ones.

**Data Streams (DATA, hardened):** `PingRequest.DataStreams` are externally supplied and treated as untrusted DATA. `AppendDataStreams` sanitizes each `StreamId` as a label (collapse whitespace, strip control chars and `#` heading markers, cap length) so the `### Data Stream: {id}` heading cannot break DCI structure; the payload is preceded by an explicit “untrusted data / not instructions” warning and wrapped in an adaptive markdown fence (`ComputeFenceBacktickLength`) so embedded triple-backticks cannot break out.

The sterile `[None]` (never an empty block, never chatty copy) prevents smaller models from hallucinating about missing sections. Segment builders use chained `.Append()`/`.AppendLine()` calls, and `SystemPromptDocument.Render` pre-sizes the final `StringBuilder`; large content blocks (Master Codex, Attached Files, Campaign Summary) are passed as raw strings rather than `$"..."`-interpolated. The same `WorkingDirectory` scopes `McpConnectionManager`, `CodexReader`, and `SpellScanner`.

### 10.6 The Lexicon — agent-directed entity memory

**Role:** structured, model-writable memory that replaces the legacy key-value Lore MCP tools for agent use. Entities are typed (Person, Project, API, DaemonState, …) with a fact array; the inference pipeline retrieves them by subject and injects them into the Master system prompt under DATA as `### Lexicon (Known Context)`. The legacy `MageSettings` Lore surface (`/api/lore`, `arcanum lore`) remains as an operator-only key-value store; it is no longer model-directed. Keys remain nonempty trimmed strings up to 256 characters. CLI and Forge get/delete use `GET`/`DELETE /api/lore/entries/by-key?key=` so every accepted key, including existing slash and dot keys, is addressable without path normalization. Legacy single-segment routes remain compatible, and `GET /api/lore` retains its paginated list envelope. Query routes share the legacy normalization, typed errors and cancellation path and reuse the existing source-generated Lore and Boolean envelopes.

**Persistence (raw SQL, no EF):** `lexicon_entries` (Id, Name, NameNormalized, ScopeCampaignId, Type, FactsJson, FactsText, UpdatedAt, RetiredAtUtc, PinnedAtUtc, CurationGeneration) + an FTS5 external-content virtual table `lexicon_fts` (Name, Type, FactsText; `content='lexicon_entries'`, `content_rowid='rowid'`) with `lexicon_entries_ai`/`_ad`/`_au` triggers syncing the index on insert/delete/update. Neither table is part of the compiled EF model — they are declared in `Data/Schema/` (`Tables/lexicon_entries.sql`, `Tables/lexicon_fact_attachment_provenance.sql`, `FullTextSearch/lexicon_fts.sql`, and one file per sync trigger) and installed with the rest of the schema at Grimoire bootstrap, then accessed via `LexiconService` over the scoped `ArcanumDbContext` connection + `SqliteBusyRetry` + `DbCommand.CreateParameter()`, mirroring `SagaMemoryStore` / `SanctumBreachRepository`. No EF migration, no compiled-model regeneration.

Lexicon schema belongs to the Core tier: installation and version-transition failures fail closed with that tier (§5.4.5a). The FTS triggers copy `Name`, `Type`, and the newline-joined `FactsText` projection (using the FTS5 delete command for the old row); SQLite never parses `FactsJson`, which remains the source-generated durable fact array. Existing operator `MageSettings` Lore rows are not migrated into the net-new Lexicon.

**Scope (optional, per Campaign).** `ScopeCampaignId` is `NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`, and the empty string is the global tier: SQLite treats NULLs as distinct in a UNIQUE index, so a nullable scope column would let one global name be inserted any number of times and quietly undo the uniqueness this table has always had. It also means the upgrade needs no sweep — every existing row is global the moment the column exists, which is the behaviour preservation this change promises. The unique index moves from `NameNormalized` alone to `(ScopeCampaignId, NameNormalized)`, so two Campaigns may each hold an entity called `config` with different facts while a global name stays unique among global names. `LexiconScope` is the tier a read or a write names; `LexiconScope.Global` is the struct's default value, because every caller with no Campaign to state is asking about that tier. A `scribe_lexicon` or `delete_lexicon` call takes its tier from the Session the client send boundary bound to that call, which the turn publishes before each tool call (§10.7.4). With `Arcanum:Features:CampaignScopedMemory` on and no Session bound, the tool refuses and reads or writes nothing rather than falling to the global tier every Campaign reads: a call with no Session is one whose turn binding was lost, and the global tier is exactly where a lost Campaign-bound write would leak to every other Campaign. With the gate off the global tier is the only one, and the call proceeds as before. The refusal is only for a call with no Session at all: a call that carries a Session id whose Session has no `session_campaign_bindings` row (or a Global-only or legacy-unresolved binding) is not refused, and resolves through `MemoryScopeResolver` to the installation-scoped memories alone, which for the Lexicon is the global tier.

**Write path (`scribe_lexicon` / `delete_lexicon` MCP tools):** upsert by `NameNormalized` (trim + invariant) under `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` so concurrent appends cannot lose facts; append every non-empty non-duplicate fact at its complete length. The former silent 32-fact input total, 1,024-character truncation, and latest-256 eviction are removed. `FactsJson` is serialized via the source-generated `LexiconJsonContext` (AOT), `FactsText` is newline-joined for FTS. Name/type identity fields retain their explicit control-column bounds; request/body, SQLite, and provider-visible context boundaries own concrete resources instead of deleting durable facts. Type semantics: new + blank → `General`; existing + blank → keep; non-empty → refresh. Both tools follow `Arcanum:Features:Lexicon` and the record-only `ungated` Ward path. When a request selects `ToolPolicy.NoForbiddenArts`, an operator-configured `delete_lexicon` name may be omitted from advertisement; when advertised, Lexicon availability, scope, provenance, and validation remain the live boundaries. `LexiconService.UpsertCoreAsync` is the Lexicon erasure chokepoint: inside its `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, after the exact-scope read and whether or not a row still holds the name, a scribe whose `Name.Trim().ToUpperInvariant()` identity carries an erasure fingerprint in exactly that scope is refused as `Lexicon.SuppressedNameRefused` (409) and records nothing, while the evidence probe that may read the OS credential store runs before the transaction and a key that cannot verify the evidence withholds every scribe. `scribe_lexicon` reports that refusal with the operator-managed text it shares with the pinned-delete refusal ("This Lexicon entry is managed by the operator in this scope, so nothing was recorded."), and because a pin never blocks an agent scribe that text comes only from a fingerprint on this tool, an accepted and bounded oracle: the agent already holds the name it tried and learns only that the operator withheld that name in this scope, never anything about content. `delete_lexicon` removes only an active, unpinned entry: a tool-level pre-check refuses a retired entry with the retired-deletion text and a pinned one with the operator-managed text before any purge runs, and returns only a tool result string, which carries no error code or status; on the ordinary delete path the agent-origin `DeleteByNameAsync` (any origin other than the operator's) repeats that check inside its own transaction, refusing as `Lexicon.RetiredMutationRefused` / `Lexicon.PinnedMutationRefused` (409), so an entry the operator curates after the pre-check is still refused; the purge path, which skips that delete, has only the pre-check, and an agent never reaches it, because a tool call carries no sensitivity-purge authority and a labelled target is refused as `Covenant.ForbiddenAuthority`, while the operator's delete is unchanged.

**Read path (preflight + retrieval):** `SemanticRouter` now returns `SemanticSpellRoutingResult(Spell, Entities)` — the JSON contract is `{ "spellName": "...", "entities": [...] }`. When the router ran but supplied no entities (or routing was bypassed: `OverrideSpellName`, pure embedding `DirectResonance`, no-spell user-facing turns), `WizardIntelligenceProvider` first probes whether the resolved Lexicon tiers contain an eligible active entry. The probe uses parameterized SQL on the admitted scoped connection and the same Core-schema snapshot as its retirement predicate; pre-curation schemas remain readable. Global reads only Global, while a Campaign includes its own tier and Global. An empty eligible scope skips both fast-client resolution and the extraction call. A failed probe is logged without content and skips optional Lexicon context; it does not assert that storage is empty, and caller cancellation propagates. A populated scope runs `LexiconEntityExtractor` — a 128-output-token JSON preflight on the fast model (`{ "entities": [...] }`) — so memory retrieval stays available even when spell selection avoided an LLM call. Router-supplied entities proceed directly to matching, and the final match still rechecks current active rows; the probe grants no disclosure authority. Every distinct non-empty entity returned within that provider response is preserved; the former post-response eight-entity truncation is removed. The `ShouldUseLexiconForTurn` gate skips only true internal headless tasks (`SkipSpellRouting && DisableMcpTools && UnattendedMode` — Campaign Logger, Saga extraction). `MatchEntitiesAsync` is tiered: exact `NameNormalized IN (...)` hits first, then column-weighted FTS5 `MATCH 'Term' ORDER BY bm25(lexicon_fts, 3.0, 2.0, 1.0) ASC` (3.0 Name, 2.0 Type, 1.0 FactsText — no Lucene caret boosting inside MATCH), deduplicated by Id, exact hits before FTS hits. FTS failure degrades to a bounded `LIKE` fallback or empty matches. With `Arcanum:Features:CampaignScopedMemory` on and a Campaign-bound turn, that whole exact-then-FTS pass runs against the Campaign's tier first and then against the global one, and a name the Campaign answered is never answered again from the global tier — a Campaign entity **shadows** the global entity of the same name rather than merging with it, so the model is never handed two contradictory answers to one term and left to choose. Shadowing is recorded by the entity's own normalized name rather than by the term that found it, because an FTS hit may be reached by a word appearing in its facts. With the gate off, or on a turn that resolved no Campaign, the global tier is read alone, which is exactly what every match saw before scopes existed. Every operational exact, FTS, and LIKE query requires `RetiredAtUtc IS NULL`. `GetByNameAsync` resolves active Campaign then active Global; `GetByNameInScopeAsync` reads only the active exact tier. A retired Campaign entry therefore stops shadowing Global. Conditional deletion instead uses the content-free, exact-scope `FindAllLifecycleIdentityForDeletionAsync`, which includes retired rows.

**Injection (DATA, hardened):** `SystemPromptBuilder.Build` accepts `IReadOnlyList<LexiconEntryDto>? lexiconEntries` (default null) and renders `### Lexicon (Known Context)` at the top of the DATA block. Lexicon is model-writable and potentially stale/adversarial, so it is treated strictly as DATA — never instructions; the preamble already states DATA may be stale and never overrides INSTRUCTIONS. Facts are hardened: whitespace collapsed, newlines/control chars stripped, exactly one plain markdown bullet per entity (`- **Name** (Type): "Fact 1"; "Fact 2"`), so facts cannot create headings or break DCI structure. Total rendered bytes are capped by `LexiconMaxInjectedBytes`; entry count by `LexiconMaxMatchedEntries`. Retrieval/injection failures are logged and swallowed — Lexicon never fails an inference turn. Lexicon contents are not persisted into audit logs or exposed on `/v1` tool surfaces.

**Operator contract:** authenticated `/api/memory/lexicon*` routes expose inspection, exact-target curation, and item-scoped hard deletion. Invalid input maps to 400, an absent exact subject to 404, stale targets and retired correction to 409, protected mutation refusal to 403, and integrity/publication failures to 500 (API §8.33). MCP converts expected failures to tool-result strings.

#### 10.6.1 Attachment-derived memory promotion and privacy policy

Attachment bytes are untrusted DATA; neither a file nor instructions inside it can authorize durable memory. A successful materialization publishes a turn-scoped `AttachmentMemoryProvenance` containing Session ID, Attachment ID, logical key, version, content hash, materialized-at timestamp, and source type. Failed, stale, cross-session, or merely indexed content publishes no promotion authority.

| Destination | Default attachment policy |
|-------------|---------------------------|
| Current-turn context | Explicit files and bounded retrieved chunks are allowed as untrusted DATA. |
| Session attachment RAG | Eligible textual chunks remain session-scoped; historical versions are explicit-only. |
| Session Entry RAG | Attachment chunks are not copied into Entries; the normal assistant conclusion alone may be persisted. |
| Campaign Summary / Session Summary | Record consulted logical key/version and useful decisions; never send all attachments or raw content. |
| Lexicon | No automatic promotion. `scribe_lexicon` requires `attachment_id` whenever attachment content was materialized, validates that id against the current turn, and stores per-fact provenance in `lexicon_fact_attachment_provenance`. |
| Saga | No raw automatic ingestion. Extraction receives only the conversation plus a metadata allowlist, accepts concise conclusions, and rejects any claimed attachment id absent from the source turn. Typed provenance is stored in `saga_memory_attachment_provenance`. |
| The Annals | No promotion authority of its own. A claim inherits whatever promotion decision its subject row already passed, and records only an identity, an origin, a scope, a sensitivity, two timelines, and a content binding — never attachment bytes or host paths. The content-free Lexicon version-provenance ledger retains attachment coordinates and attachment hashes, but no superseded fact text or per-fact hashes. A file cannot cause itself to be claimed, because nothing writes a claim except the store that wrote the row. |
| The Tapestry | No promotion. Attachment-derived nodes stay session-scoped exactly like attachment RAG, are injected as turn-local untrusted DATA, and never become Lexicon or Saga content. A tree is derived data rebuilt from its corpus, so deleting an attachment removes its leaves on the next sweep (§21.11). |
| Prompt cache | Attachment metadata, paths, hashes, and bytes are volatile DATA. They are excluded from stable prefixes and shared cache keys. |
| Audit log | Metadata-only inference accounting; no attachment bytes, raw paths, content, or provenance hash payloads. |
| Subagents | Only explicit file values whose attachment ids intersect the parent materialized allowlist; no inherited index or enumeration. |

Deleting an attachment does not silently delete unrelated conclusions. Lexicon/Saga provenance rows remain and resolve `Availability=Unavailable` when no Bound source row exists, so downstream users are never told that an unavailable source is verifiable. This metadata is a typed side table, not opaque text concatenated into the fact or memory.

#### 10.6.2 Unified memory inspection without unified storage

`MemoryEndpoints` is a read model over the existing stores, not a new memory database. `status` counts Session Entries, pins, Session Summary presence, logical attachments, indexed attachment chunks, Lexicon entities, Saga memories, and workspace chunks. A selected session narrows owned session/attachment/Saga data and its Campaign-backed workspace; omission intentionally reports the global persisted inventory. Feature flags are reported alongside counts, so a disabled retrieval gate never masquerades as deletion.

`POST /api/memory/search` performs case-insensitive lexical inspection of persisted content and does not require an embedding provider. Scope defaults to `all` and is echoed in every response. Each hit has one source scope, source id, retention category, and sanitized provenance. Saga and Lexicon hits additionally carry a typed exact-inspection target; the server never emits a shell command. Session, attachment, and workspace hits have no action target. Attachment hits name session/attachment/logical-key/version/hash but never raw bytes or host paths. They are read from the stored attachment index chunks and carry no Comprehension gate: turning `Arcanum:Features:Comprehension` off removes document text from model context and retrieval, not from this operator inspection surface, so text extracted from a document while the gate was on stays searchable here until its attachment or the attachment index is removed or reset. Workspace hits expose registered labels and relative paths, never absolute host roots. When the search includes workspace scope, a supplied nonblank selector resolves against Campaigns on the same admitted connection before any result budget is consumed: GUIDs in any accepted format bind the canonical stored GUID, and other selectors match the registered name case-insensitively. Unknown selectors return `Workspace.NotFound` rather than a complete empty page, even when earlier scopes would exhaust the row or byte budget. Omitted or blank selectors keep the unfiltered workspace inspection; selectors do not affect scopes that exclude workspace. Lexicon attachment-derived facts retain their typed provenance summary. Lexicon hits carry their lifecycle and retrieval eligibility, and Saga hits carry theirs the same way: the lifecycle stamps and the eligibility `SagaRetrievalEligibilityClassifier` assigns are read in the same statement as the row, so a retired memory, which the listing reads like any other row, still matches and says whether a turn could recall it. Covenant stays outside this generic search and is queried only through its protected inspection route. One request is bounded twice, by row count (10,000, `limit` narrows it) and by an aggregate 8 MiB of returned hit content shared across every scope. The native session, attachment, and workspace readers first bound their selected-ID windows and examined-field bytes before exact matching/hydration, then honor the returned-content budget per hit, so response limits never stand in for examined-work limits. The Saga and Lexicon scopes take their row slice (at most the rows the budget has left, plus one) from their own stores before the byte check trims it, so for those two the byte budget bounds what is returned, not what is read; the row slice still bounds the read. The byte check follows each row, so the answer can exceed the budget by the one row that crossed it, and a scope that stopped on it reports `hasMore` because it cannot know it left nothing behind. Search is read-only: no hit is injected, pinned, summarized, or promoted.

**Literal search and Core28.** Native operator inspection preserves `instr(lower(field),lower(query))` independently for Entries.Content, Sessions.Summary, attachment Content/OriginalFileName/LogicalKey, and workspace Content/RelativePath. SQLite's fold is ASCII-only; this is separate from existing full native FTS5 expression APIs. Core28 adds one corpus-discriminated normalized projection owning an external-content FTS5 trigram index (`case_sensitive 1`, `detail=none`). Only source AFTER INSERT/UPDATE effects replace projection rows, explicitly deleting old/new identities and every secondary uniqueness conflict before insertion; AFTER DELETE removes them. This preserves INSERT/UPDATE OR IGNORE and REPLACE with recursive triggers off. Projection BEFORE DELETE removes old tokens while normalized values still exist, and AFTER INSERT adds current tokens. Secure-delete is set and verified during schema initialization; the projection and closed native shadow shapes belong to Core and factory cleanup. Physical erasure follows the authoritative source owners and the existing secure SQLite/WAL protocol, not merely a no-hit assertion.

The old Core27 catalog/fingerprint is frozen in full. Core28's transition creates the projection, maintenance triggers and global/ownership-prefixed seek indexes and extends the instant inventory/view. Its bounded journaled sweep copies at most 200 source rows per batch; projection changes and cursor advancement share the coordinator's transaction. Committed Core remains below 28 until the sweep finishes. Search refuses pending/unhealthy native projection state with `MemorySearch.IndexUnavailable`; it never performs an opportunistic rebuild during a read or treats a partial projection as complete.

Sparse candidates use at most three deduplicated scalar-aligned first/middle/last seeds of exactly three Unicode scalars, each safely quoted and bound, after native `lower(query)`. Each query collects cap+1 (257) IDs before source ownership filtering, full predicate hydration or recency sort. The first complete set of at most 256 is a superset; final original predicates remove seed/wrong-field false positives. Truncated lists are never intersected. Short/NUL queries and dense seeds use ordered source windows. Stored NUL text remains covered by native parity tests. Bounded SQL materialization sorts sparse candidates with SQLite collations; .NET Ordinal does not reproduce BINARY ordering for non-BMP paths.

Native phases share at most 512 examined rows and 2 MiB of searched-field bytes per request, charged before full matching including nonmatches, with an explicit one-row overshoot. Seed and statement budgets are shared too. Metadata windows precede predicates; hydration starts from a MATERIALIZED selected-ID relation and forced primary-key lookups, because a bare rowid IN query can choose a full ownership-index scan. Disjoint equality-prefix/range seeks preserve mixed direction order without rescanning deep timestamp/path/chunk ties. Source IDs break remaining ties. The global Summary recency index excludes NULL summaries, so they cannot cause an unbounded scan before a selected summary window. Result limits and the existing 8 MiB returned-content budget remain distinct; a trimmed matching lookahead is not advanced past. VM/plan regressions use actual shipping SQLCipher and production statements; VM counts do not claim strict tokenizer/IO/wall-clock bounds.

Every unfinished page has a versioned bounded continuation and closed truncation reason, including empty work-limited pages. It binds the trimmed query, requested/resolved selectors, effective memory/Campaign policy and order version; limit may change. Tokens contain exact native/Saga stored order keys and source identity, never a raw absolute workspace root, live object/lease, or protected canonical payload. Lexicon tokens contain only row ID/scope; the owning store resolves its current name after complete current authority/structural verification, in the same snapshot. A deleted/moved/no-longer-matching boundary returns safe restart guidance. A concurrent rename uses current boundary order. No snapshot is held across requests; static-store pages are complete without omissions/duplicates, while concurrent changes can affect later pages. Phase order stays entries then summaries, attachments, workspace, Saga, Lexicon; later phases are not consulted after native work exhaustion. Per-scope counts/hasMore describe this page and distinguish exhausted earlier phases from unvisited later phases.

Saga's narrow owning-store overload seeks its existing CreatedAt DESC/Id DESC order and retains ranking/lifecycle/provenance/ownership checks. Lexicon's overload uses native Name NOCASE/scope/Id order and retains its whole-store evidence and structural checks before boundary/selection, protected snapshot/export lease, canonical digest checks, lifecycle and fact boundaries. Neither tail lane acquires the four-corpus performance claim. The CLI exposes explicit `--continuation`/`--limit`, prints unfinished reasons/tokens in normal/plain mode and preserves typed JSON; it never loops automatically.


`explain` reports candidates for the next turn rather than promising inclusion: transcript and pins need a selected session, Summary needs a stored rollup and context-pressure policy, attachment chunks need the owning session plus prompt retrieval, and Lexicon/Saga/workspace material requires its existing gate and prompt match. Lexicon additionally requires `Eligibility == Eligible`; retired-only persisted inventory cannot make it a next-turn candidate. Saga likewise requires at least one memory a turn in the resolved scope could rank — not retired, still embedded, and owned by that scope (`ISagaMemoryStore.AnyRetrievableAsync`) — while status keeps counting every stored row. Disabling or deleting one store never claims to affect another. Mutation remains deliberately narrow and always names one store and one item: `/api/memory/lexicon/{name}` deletes one named Lexicon entity and six static Lexicon POSTs perform exact inspection/curation (§10.6.3), `/api/memory/covenant/*` carries the Covenant's own prepare-and-commit curation (§10.26), and `/api/memory/saga/{id}` reads one Saga memory whole while its five `POST` siblings correct, retire, reinstate, pin, and unpin it (§21.13). There is no ambiguous generic memory delete and no verb that reaches across stores.

#### 10.6.3 Immutable Lexicon curation

**Served-state compatibility.** While a resumable Core transition has recorded a version below 11, ordinary Lexicon reads, scribe writes, deletion, unlabeled inspection, Annals inspection, and retention retain their legacy SQL shapes. This includes a journaled v2-to-v3 transition whose Annals tables already exist while the committed version remains 2. Legacy projections preserve reader ordinals with null lifecycle instants, generation 1, format-1 Annals versions, and empty historical fact provenance. Ordinary legacy scribe binds `LegacyStoreDigest` with the existing type/facts digest; disabled capture leaves a claimless row claimless but still corrects an existing head. Only correct/retire/reinstate/pin/unpin require v11 and return retryable `Lexicon.CurationUnavailable` (HTTP 503) until it is committed. The noncached Core-version read and dependent SQL run in the same SQLite snapshot; read paths use a deferred snapshot, and retention apply selects its shape inside the deletion transaction. An unchanged exact target measured before upgrade remains valid afterward. Protected endpoint authority remains first: denied/stale authority wins, and an authorized request observes the temporary curation refusal. Legacy protected labels with no established digest grammar remain unreadable even with valid authority; no text-digest fallback is accepted.

**Version-aware erasure.** Saga erasure never names `lexicon_annal_fact_provenance`. Lexicon's shared Annals erasure step is required from committed Core v11, not generically optional: direct deletion, live Covenant purge, and staged backup/restore purge skip it only before v11, then delete it before its owning versions. A missing declared v11 table fails closed and rolls back rather than silently leaving evidence behind. Legacy retention reports zero pinned inventory and uses the legacy age predicate; after upgrade, apply rechecks current pin state within its transaction so an older plan cannot delete a newly pinned row.

The operator can inspect, correct, retire, reinstate, pin, and unpin one exact Global or Campaign entry through six static authenticated POST routes and `memory lexicon` commands (API §8.33; Command Reference, `arcanum memory`). These operations remain available independently of prompt-time Lexicon and ordinary Annals capture flags. Correction replaces the type and the complete ordered facts array; it never renames or moves the entry. Retirement keeps the row inspectable but removes it from matching, daemon context, and prompt construction. Reinstatement restores eligibility and Campaign shadowing. Plain deletion still removes an active or retired entry and records nothing, so a later scribe may write the name again. `memory lexicon erase` is the separate, confirmed verb that removes the entry and records an erasure fingerprint, after which a scribe of that name in that scope is refused until the operator releases it (§21.15).

**Core schema v11.** `RetiredAtUtc` and `PinnedAtUtc` are nullable fixed-width UTC instants. `CurationGeneration` is a positive SQLite integer, default 1 for inherited and new rows. `annal_versions.ContentHashFormatCode` defaults to 1 and accepts only 1 or 2. The transition pins the exact v10 source fingerprint `B484778B9288D99C4337FA3C95BEB56B95FDAE6B1D149C6A9A2A822591BBE951`, adds the columns without an eager content backfill, and explicitly replaces all three Lexicon FTS triggers. Insert publishes only active rows; delete removes only previously active rows; update removes the old active row and publishes the new active row. Fresh and evolved catalogs converge, including SQLite's added-column declaration shape and the UTC inventory containing both lifecycle instants and historical provenance's `MaterializedAt`.

**Core schema v13 and the full-text index.** FTS5 `secure-delete` is what makes a delete scrub the tokens it removes. Without it a deleted or replaced entry leaves its tokens in the index's segments until a later merge happens to reach them, so an erased entry would stay legible in `lexicon_fts_data`. Version 13 turns it on for `lexicon_fts` and runs `optimize` once, which merges every segment and drops the tokens that scribe merges, corrections, retirements and deletes had already left behind. The step declares no sweep, because one merge is bounded work inside its own transaction. `CoreGrimoireSchemaDataInitializer` converges and reads back the same setting on every install, so a fresh installation has it before its first write and an installation that lost it gets it back; it never runs the merge. An erase asks anyway, at the start of its own transaction: found off, the setting is enabled, the index merged, and the setting read back before anything is deleted, and a setting that still does not read as on is recorded as `FullTextSecureDeleteUnverified`, a reason that never clears. A retired entry has no index row to scrub, because its tokens were scrubbed at retirement or merged away by version 13, and the proof that a live entry's tokens are gone is that its `lexicon_fts_docsize` row is absent.

**Canonical content and format 2.** One normalizer trims name/type/facts, drops empty facts, removes exact ordinal duplicates while retaining the first occurrence, and requires at least one fact. Correction requires a nonempty type. Stored fact bytes are not whitespace-collapsed or control-stripped; DATA rendering still sanitizes them. The snapshot preimage is strict UTF-8 `Arcanum.Lexicon.Snapshot.v2\0`, byte `0x02`, a uint32 big-endian type byte length and the type bytes, a uint32 big-endian fact count, then each fact's uint32 big-endian byte length and bytes in order. Unpaired UTF-16 surrogates and lengths/counts outside uint32 are refused. SHA-256 of that preimage is the snapshot digest. `LegacyStoreDigest` (1) retains the historical store-specific bytes; `LexiconStructuredSnapshot` (2) binds this grammar. Equality compares format and digest together; a retirement tombstone has no content digest. New content-bearing Lexicon versions use format 2; Saga stays format 1.

**Exact inspection and compare-and-swap.** `ILexiconCurationService.ShowExactAsync` reads the row, current attachment provenance, Annals head/history, historical source coordinates, and sensitivity label in one deferred SQLite snapshot, without Campaign fallback. Its target binds scope, normalized name, stable entry id, curation generation, format-2 snapshot digest, exact lifecycle, an explicit present/absent Annals head, and an explicit present/absent label. A mutation opens `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and checks every target component against that same transaction's live evidence. It independently verifies canonical content, head operation/format/digest/scope/sensitivity, and label owner/revision/derived-artifact digest. Contradictory evidence fails closed. A stale target fails even if the requested state has already been reached; there is no durable mutation replay receipt. With a current target, `Unchanged`, `AlreadyRetired`, `NotRetired`, `AlreadyPinned`, and `NotPinned` write nothing.

**Atomic publication.** Correction replaces canonical type/facts, current provenance, FTS, Annals, and any protected label in one transaction. Unchanged facts retain their source; new operator facts inherit no removed source. A claimless row first receives its exact `AgentAsserted` baseline; a legacy head receives a format-2 `SystemBackfilled` restatement before curation. Correction appends `OperatorStated` `Correct`, retirement appends a content-free `Retire`, and reinstatement appends a content-bearing successor. These state-changing curation revisions are ungated. Ordinary scribe remains capture-gated for claimless rows, but keeps an existing head consistent even when capture is disabled. Scribe refuses retired rows and refuses content changes to protected rows. Pin/unpin never open history. Every semantic content or lifecycle write increments the generation with overflow refused; only content changes advance `UpdatedAt`. Every write that records an Annals version, whether scribe, correction, or any lifecycle change, takes its instant from the service's one injected `TimeProvider` through a single helper that clamps it strictly past the entry's last update and the head it follows, so a retirement never records a zero-length belief for the version it supersedes; a baseline restatement and the operation that follows it share one instant, because they are one write.

`lexicon_annal_fact_provenance` is keyed by `(AnnalVersionId, FactOrdinal)` and owned by that Annals version. It retains only source Session/attachment identity, logical key, attachment version/hash, materialization instant, and source type. It stores no fact text, fact hash, `FactsJson`, or `FactsText`. Each format-2 content revision snapshots current source coordinates by canonical fact ordinal. Superseded plaintext exists nowhere in the history; there is no old-content restore command.

**Authority and read boundaries.** Operational `ILexiconService` reads are active-only. Operator list/search can include retired rows with lifecycle/eligibility; status and sources describe persisted inventory, while explain counts only `Eligible` rows as next-turn candidates. Exact Global/Campaign inspection uses its scoped `CovenantReadLease`; effective Campaign lookup, arbitrary-scope list/search/sources/explain use `CovenantInstallationReadLease`. Protected mutations require the exact owner's `CovenantWriteLease` before reading and retain it through commit and response serialization. The protected result revalidates before serialization and holds sole lease ownership through the last byte, emitting the private no-store header tuple. Label replacement CAS-checks the complete old label, keeps the same artifact id and owner, issues a new label id at checked revision n+1, and preserves sensitivity/generation provenance. The label binds `DerivedArtifactContentDigest.ForBytes` of the canonical snapshot bytes, a distinct domain from the snapshot/Annals digest. Session sensitivity maxima stay monotonic, its projection revision advances, and replacing one artifact does not increase its tainted-artifact count.

**Retention and ownership.** Pins exempt entries from automatic age pruning; they do not block operator correction, lifecycle changes, hard deletion, resets, or permitted active scribe writes. The plan's `lexiconCuration` inventory reports total pinned rows and pins otherwise old enough for the enabled retention rule. Apply rechecks pin state inside the deletion transaction and reports `Data.PinnedAfterPlanning` if a planned candidate was pinned meanwhile. Retirement does not refresh age. Hard erase, Campaign memory reset, whole-store reset, protected purge, retention, and factory reset use the shared Annals erasure plan for historical coordinates, edges, heads, versions, and claims; current provenance and canonical lifecycle follow the entry. Workspace reset preserves durable Lexicon state, including its owning Campaign's entries. Physical database backup already carries these columns, tables, and trigger definitions; no separate backup format or ownership list is introduced.

**Inspection projections.** List and search use constant-statement bulk reads within one admitted deferred snapshot. Content-free identity, lifecycle, label, and current-head preflight precedes canonical content: protected heads cannot masquerade as unlabeled rows, orphan Lexicon labels fail closed, and other artifact kinds may legitimately reuse the same GUID. Search applies a parameterized, deterministic ordinal-case-insensitive predicate to deserialized fact values, preserving Unicode and fact boundaries; unified search projects at most its slice limit plus one sentinel. Current provenance retains insertion order. Sources/explain use a dedicated count projection that streams metadata without retaining an identity or DTO corpus and reads canonical content only for protected rows whose label/content digest must be verified. Retained and eligible counts stay distinct; the endpoint retains the existing lease through protected serialization.

**Verification.** Digest golden vectors, fresh/evolved schema equivalence and scalar constraints, UTC diagnostics, exact-target/integrity/authority negatives, publication rollback, deterministic lifecycle races, active-only exact/FTS/LIKE paths, protected final-byte lease lifetime, apply-time pin races, and lifecycle-bearing reset survivors are executable tests. SQL statement and canonical-materialization budgets, malformed-evidence zero-read controls, Unicode matching, and multi-fact provenance-order regressions cover the bulk inspection boundary. `LexiconCurationArchitectureTests` closes ordered SQL projections against reader ordinals and classifies operational versus inspection consumers. Endpoint/security, source-generation, Grimoire acquisition, and EF Native AOT inventories remain closed; no EF entity or compiled-model change is needed. Canonical route/command documentation is checked against the mapped host and generated command surface.

### 10.7 End-to-end turn lifecycle and chat loop

This section is the canonical ordered workflow for every Master inference turn. It describes the shared logical run, buffered/streaming differences, fallback and correction loops, persistence, cost/context admission, cancellation, and terminal event behavior.

#### 10.7.1 Ownership, projections, and entry points

```text
WizardIntelligenceProvider          thin IArcanumIntelligenceProvider facade
        ↓
TurnExecutionCoordinator            sole semantic consumer; one projection per request
        ↓
TurnEngine                          logical run: preflight → attempts → loop → finalization
        ↓
TurnEventEmitter                    ordered internal Channel<TurnEvent>
        ↓
Exactly one projection
  ├── BufferedTurnProjection        → Result<PromptTurnResult>
  └── IntelligenceEventProjection   → Channel<IntelligenceEvent>
        ↓
HTTP writer
  ├── native NDJSON
  └── production /v1 IntelligenceEvent → OpenAI SSE mapping
```

`ExecutePromptAsync` and `StreamPromptAsync` create an internal `TurnExecutionRequest`. Idempotency ownership reaches a turn only through `TurnIdempotencyAmbient`, which the HTTP idempotency filter sets; it is never accepted from a public `PingRequest` body. The coordinator consumes semantic events and selects exactly one projection; it does not serialize HTTP. Native routes serialize `IntelligenceEvent` as NDJSON. Production `/v1/chat/completions` receives those same native events and reshapes them in `OpenAiV1Endpoints`, whose mapper owns terminal usage and tool-argument fragmentation. SSE keep-alives are transport-only, and exact-byte replay capture stays in the HTTP writer/idempotency layer.

Three invariants bind every SSE writer. The first two exist because `IAsyncEnumerator<T>` is neither concurrent-safe nor disposable mid-move. First, only one `MoveNextAsync` may be outstanding at a time: a heartbeat races the *same* pending move task through `WhenAny` and never starts a second one. Second, a writer must never dispose a streaming enumerator while a `MoveNextAsync` is outstanding — a compiler-generated async iterator throws `NotSupportedException` from `DisposeAsync` in that state, which would surface an ordinary client disconnect as an unhandled streaming error instead of a clean abort. Both the native writer and the `/v1` writer therefore tear down through the shared `SseStreamWriter.QuiesceAndDisposeAsync`: cancel the stream CTS so the producer unwinds, observe the pending move, then dispose. Both also cancel the per-iteration heartbeat delay when a frame wins the race, so no heartbeat timer outlives its iteration.

**Third, a maintenance revocation may only be honoured between frames, and it reaches the producer token alone.** A frame is a `data:` prefix, a serialized payload, a terminating blank line and a flush; cancelling the token those writes run on aborts the sequence part way and leaves bytes no client can parse and no later frame can repair. The bytes cannot be withdrawn, so the only safe place to stop is between frames. `GrimoireStreamQuiescence` is what keeps the two tokens apart: it publishes the admission lease's `MaintenanceRevocation` for a request that holds a `QuiesceableStream` lease and a permanently uncancellable token for every other, and `LinkProducer` is the only way that token reaches anything. `SseStreamWriter.StreamAsync` links it into the enumerator's token, tests it before starting each `MoveNextAsync` and again after each frame returns, and passes the *unrevoked* request token to `writeFrameAsync` and to the keep-alive. A revoked stream therefore finishes the frame in hand, starts no next frame and writes no further keep-alive, cancels and observes the producer through the same `QuiesceAndDisposeAsync` teardown as a disconnect, and ends with the terminal `data: [DONE]\n\n` frame — the one both first-party parsers already read as a deliberate end. The parameter is required rather than defaulted, because a writer that silently inherited "never quiesces" is exactly the one that holds a transition open until stage one times out. An ordinary end of stream still writes no terminal frame; that case belongs to each route's own cancellation arm. The `/v1` SSE mapper and the NDJSON `InferenceExecuteWriter` are separate writers and are deliberately untouched, which is what keeps a billable stream out of this path structurally rather than by a runtime check.

Semantic events are internal and non-durable. Every writer, including Ward and human-input observers, uses the bounded `TurnEventEmitter` channel; sequence numbers are strictly monotonic, request events are emitted before waiting, and the terminal guard suppresses everything after the first terminal event. The current event vocabulary is:

```text
RunStarted, TurnStatusChanged, SessionBound, ContextCompressed, ContextAccounted,
ProviderAttemptStarted, ProviderSelected, ProviderAttemptCommitted,
ProviderAttemptCompleted, ProviderAttemptFailed,
ModelCallStarted, TextDelta, ReasoningDelta, ModelCallCompleted, ModelCallFailed,
ToolCallProposed, ApprovalRequested, ApprovalResolved,
HumanInputRequested, HumanInputReceived,
ToolInvocationStarted, ToolInvocationCompleted,
OutputValidated, RunCompleted, RunFailed, RunAbandoned
```

The logical-run invariants are:

- exactly one `RunStarted` and exactly one terminal `RunCompleted`, `RunFailed`, or `RunAbandoned`;
- every provider attempt starts once and ends completed or failed; at most one attempt commits, and commitment precedes provider-derived client-visible events;
- every model call starts once and ends completed or failed;
- approval, human-input, and tool-invocation pairs complete unless terminal cancellation interrupts them;
- answer and reasoning remain distinct through execution, events, projections, validation, and persistence; provider `ProtectedData` never becomes an event;
- tool calls remain sequential within a round, call/result groups remain paired, and attachment injection occurs only after all exchanges in that round;
- client-forwarded calls bypass server authorization and invocation; and
- run, Grimoire, reservation, accounting, idempotency, finalization, and provider-lease ownership execute at most once.

`RunCompleted` is the authoritative buffered result: final answer, ordered client-safe reasoning, usage, observed tool calls, finish reason, warnings, Session id, and structured-output warning state. Keep-alives and captured replay bytes remain transport concerns, never semantic events.

| Surface | Current route | Turn call |
|---------|---------------|-----------|
| Buffered native ping | `POST /api/intelligence/ping` | `ExecutePromptAsync` |
| Streaming native ping | `POST /api/intelligence/ping-stream` | `StreamPromptAsync` through `InferenceExecuteWriter` (NDJSON) |
| Spell execution | `POST /api/spells/{name}/execute` | `ExecutePromptAsync` |
| Streaming Spell execution | `POST /api/spells/{name}/execute-stream` | `StreamPromptAsync` through `InferenceExecuteWriter` |
| Prompt execution | `POST /api/prompts/{id}/execute` and `.../execute-stream` | buffered or streaming |
| Buffered OpenAI compatibility | `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `stream:false` | mapped stateless `PingRequest` → `ExecutePromptAsync` |
| Streaming OpenAI compatibility | `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `stream:true` | mapped stateless `PingRequest` → `StreamPromptAsync` → OpenAI SSE mapper |

The OpenAI mapper sets `SessionId=null`, `UnattendedMode=true`, and populates `StatelessMessages`. `InferenceExecuteWriter` writes each native event as one `application/x-ndjson` line.

All provider chat I/O in this pipeline goes through Core `IModelCallExecutor` (`ExecuteBufferedAsync` / `ExecuteStreamingAsync`): initial inference, tool continuation, structured-output correction, Spell routing, and Lexicon extraction. Tool invocation failures use the same code-owned tolerant policy in buffered and streaming modes.

#### 10.7.2 Shared preflight, provider attempts, and context seed

Before any inference provider call, both response modes execute these gates in order:

1. `GuardrailsPipeline.FilterInputAsync`: PII, toxicity, and authored topic policy on the current user group; disabled guardrails pass through. For stateless transcripts, anchor at the last case-insensitive `user` role and include preceding user messages back to the prior `assistant` boundary. Ignore intervening system/tool text and any assistant/tool suffix after the last user. Scan fallback content plus textual content parts; exclude historical turns. Stateful input is the incoming prompt. PII has default-true per-detector controls under the `DetectPii` master switch: email patterns, digit-bounded hyphenated SSNs, whole 13–19 digit Luhn-valid card candidates (excluding identical digits), and formatted US or explicit international phone candidates. Bare epochs/IDs are not phone evidence; Luhn-valid card-shaped IDs remain ambiguous. Fixed category/remedy messages and fixed audit masks contain no matched text. Output toxicity/topic checks remain in force; PII remains input-only.
2. Attached-file validation.
3. `PingRequestBoundsValidator`.
