The production `GrimoireOfflineTransitionHandlerRegistry` is closed over exactly `(CovenantReset, 1)` and `(HealthyCatalogFactoryErasure, 1)`; duplicate registrations, zero/undefined/unregistered keys, unsupported versions, handler/payload disagreement, and changed bindings all fail through that same refusal. A registry assembled only in tests accepts a test-only codec/handler, proving that a future kind can extend dispatch without adding a speculative production migration discriminator today.

**Every durable window of a closed period is opened by the component that owns connection policy.** Ordinary admission is shut, so the erasure opens the operation store's own connection itself under a scoped permit — and a bare open on that object runs none of this installation's policy, because Entity Framework's connection interceptors fire for connections Entity Framework opens. What that silently loses is not a nicety: `secure_delete` and `foreign_keys` are applied and read back in exactly one place, and without them an erasure's own deletions leave the erased bytes readable in the freed pages and leave every cascade-only child row behind, while reporting a proven erasure. Opening is therefore a method on the ledger rather than something a caller does to it, in the ordinary read-write mode every other connection to the database uses, and re-applied on each window because the window is opened and closed around each durable step.

**A closing proof is two publications, and a resumed run finishes the one that is missing.** Every edge out of `Closing` except the closing advance itself requires a complete proof, so a run that died between entering `Closing` and recording the close leaves a journal with exactly one legal move — and a resume that read the state as evidence the proof had been made would leave a transition that can never be advanced, rolled back, parked, or retired. The mirror-image rule governs the verification publication: the graph admits it only when it changes something, so a resumed run republishes it only when it is not already complete, because a refusal there is answered by parking straight back into the state being resumed from.

**An uncommitted closure setup failure reopens admission, including caller cancellation.** While the exact closing owner still proves the gate is only `Closing`, the coordinator spends the no-effect abort on an uncancellable unwind, burns the successor generation, and only then permits the Covenant rollback and journal retirement. Stage two commits the gate to `Closed` on a burned generation before it drains, so a cancellation, returned refusal, or exception at or after that commitment may already be past the point of no return. That path parks the active journal, spends the Covenant disposition as `KeepClosed`, and retains the exact closing owner for authenticated retry; it never reconciles or retires evidence as though both gates had reopened. Once a closed lease has been issued, a failure to take the maintenance lane, the ledger connection, or the scoped permit completes that lease with a rollback disposition instead of merely releasing it — releasing leaves the gate closed, and for a closure that never ran a phase that is an installation nobody can open over a setup step that touched nothing. The whole region from the lease being issued to the closure being handed back runs inside a catch that reopens and rethrows, because until the closure exists nothing holds the lease on the caller's behalf — and the lane acquisition inside that region honours the run's cancellation token, so an ordinary shutdown would otherwise leave a live lease nobody can reach and refuse even the retry the gate offers.

**A journal whose only remaining step was retirement is swept rather than left holding the slot.** Retirement is the last thing a transition does and the operation row is terminalized several publications before it, so a run that died in between leaves a spent journal that nothing can adopt — recovery does not resume a terminal row — while it holds the profile's one active slot against every future reset and factory erasure. The phase authority retires such a journal on its way to opening a new one, and the condition is exactly retirement-pending: the one state whose remaining act is retirement itself, so sweeping it asserts nothing that did not happen. The wider reading — anything whose row is already terminal — names more of the window, and reaching retirement from there would mean publishing a reconciliation suffix the transition never performed, recording a lane it did not close and a disposition it did not spend. A journal that lies about what happened is worse than one that is merely in the way. The earlier windows therefore still hold the slot and an operator has to clear it by hand; closing them needs a retirement edge meaning "abandoned because its operation is terminal", which the lifecycle graph does not have.

A parent-bound journal is read no differently here and is admitted no more easily. Retirement-pending requires a complete reconciliation suffix, and for a bound journal that suffix is complete only when it carries a receipt digest equal to its own binding — a value that exists only because the completion receipt was already published into the outer record and read back. So the sweep takes nothing away: what the journal proved is already in the record that outlives it, which is the arm the pair matrix reads as a nested transition already retired. A bound journal that never got that far is not retirement-pending at all and stays where it is.

**A second closed table over the same key space says what each kind is allowed to be, and what it owes.** The payload table above decides how a journal of a given kind and version is read and written; `GrimoireOfflineTransitionEffectHandlerRegistry` decides which durable operation a transition of that kind may be and whether it owes the installation ordinary database work the phase ladder does not describe. Keeping them apart keeps a decoding concern out of an erasure concern; keeping the key identical is what lets a suite assert that neither table knows a kind the other has never heard of, which is the failure a second table would otherwise introduce — a journal that decodes perfectly and cannot be run, or an effect that runs under a payload nothing can read back. The coordinator resolves the effect handler from the journal rather than from the checkpoint and refuses when the operation the table names is not the one the run claims, so the durable record settles which exclusive scope a run adopts rather than an entry point checking its own caller. It is one handler class registered twice, because the two kinds differ in what they are configured with rather than in what they do, and it is composed per scope rather than held as a process-wide constant: decoding depends on nothing but the bytes, but an effect is reached through the same scope its journal session and operation store are, and a shared instance would invite one to capture a scope it outlives. The progress record it mutates is handed in rather than returned, because most of what it records is decided on paths that go on to fail and whether admission may reopen turns entirely on it.

`GrimoireOfflineTransitionLifecycleStore` is the typed facade over this lifecycle foundation. Raw begin allocates the slot epoch and invokes a bound-payload factory before publishing an active anchor; a typed epoch mismatch therefore leaves no active journal. Typed publication state carries no handler. Advance re-decodes the current authenticated publication and uses only the registry-resolved handler before raw CAS, so caller-carried same-key policy cannot weaken validation. Recovery decodes and validates before returning a value, and retirement requires exact typed `RetirementPending` suffix readiness. Handler observations are the exhaustive `NotApplied`, `AppliedAndVerified`, `ReconciliationPending`, and `KeepClosed` outcomes; there is no boolean success channel. The authenticated raw journal store otherwise remains concerned only with authenticated bytes, envelope revisions, anchor/file security, and raw CAS.

**Process-local admission primitive.** The singleton `IGrimoireConnectionAdmissionGate` is a generation-bound state machine for request, work, native-open, and exclusive-owner capabilities. Only the exact owner may begin, resume, disposition, or reopen the gate. Stage 1 refuses new request/work capabilities and drains the existing request and work lifetimes. Stage 2 resolves every outstanding native-open attempt only after an explicit opened, failed, or refused-after-open terminal outcome; disposing a ticket cannot manufacture terminality. Each work capability owns one atomic provider-effect frontier: if maintenance revocation wins, the provider I/O group does not begin; if the effect wins, maintenance waits through that group and its durable disposition without delivering maintenance cancellation to it. The exact initiating request may be promoted only for its exact `DbConnection` and generation, and promotion grants no general database authority. Capabilities minted before a reopen are rejected during every later closing generation.

**Authored hosted-producer inventory (24 services).** `HostedGrimoireProducerInventory` is the bidirectional source contract for every application-owned `IHostedService`: `GrimoireDatabaseHostedService`, `CovenantFeatureConfigurationPublisher`, `PidFileService`, `LongRunningOperationStartupHostedService`, `SessionAttachmentPendingGcHostedService`, `CovenantMaintenanceHostedService`, `GrimoireSchemaTransitionHostedService`, `EntryWeavingService`, `SessionAttachmentIndexingService`, `WorkspaceIndexingService`, `SagaExtractionService`, `TapestryWeavingService`, `ArcanumSettingsClampStartupLogger`, `ArcanumSecurityStartupChecks`, `FileEncryptionKeyBootstrapHostedService`, `DataRetentionSweepHostedService`, `A2ASendingLeaseRenewer`, `Loremaster`, `LongRestSweepHostedService`, `ApprenticeService`, `McpServerBootstrapHostedService`, `ProviderHealthProbeService`, `UnseenServantService`, and `BatchProcessingService`. Each catalogued operation is classified as ordinary hosted work with an exact closed `GrimoireWorkKind`, awaited pre-readiness startup, stopped-host work, or effect-free work. The Roslyn discovery fails in both directions when a registration or a reachable scope, ordinary connection, provider call, filesystem access, or effect frontier exists on only one side of the catalog. It also joins the non-hosted backup CLI, restore safety-backup, installation-reset, and offline startup-recovery chains into the same site bijection under their exact owner-bound or stopped-host proofs. No naming convention, descriptor name, class name, or optional dependency can manufacture authority. This is a bounded proof of authored source and exact reviewed external contracts, not an exhaustive inventory of runtime effects. Exact framework scalar operators follow the Structural Operand Rule: `System.Index.op_Implicit(Int32)`, the `System.Int128` implicit conversions from the integral types, `System.Int128` addition, subtraction, multiplication and division, and `System.Threading.CancellationToken` `==` and `!=` are classified as value operations when their assembly identities are the trusted CoreLib identities, the operator is not lifted, and no operand carries a user-defined conversion at the operator boundary. Only parentheses and exact framework value conversions are looked through at that boundary. Everything beneath it, including every authored conversion, call, getter and operator inside an operand, is traversed where it is written, so these operators grant no authority and hide no execution (`AuthoredPayloadConversionBeforeFrameworkInt128OperatorRemainsExecutableWork`, `AuthoredIndexLookalikeOperatorRemainsExecutableWork`, `AuthoredInt128LookalikeArithmeticRemainsExecutableWork`). `Type` `==` and `!=` are classified as Runtime Type Identity Comparison only when each operand is a `typeof` expression or an exact `System.Object.GetType()` call whose receiver passes the same boundary rule, because both sides are then `RuntimeType` values and the comparison is reference identity; any other `Type` value could be an authored subclass and stays unclassified. The closed float-vector contract recognizes only exact `float.IsFinite`, `double.IsFinite`, `Vector<float>.Count`, `Vector<float>(ReadOnlySpan<float>)`, and `Vector.Dot<float>` declarations whose containing type has the full trusted CoreLib or `System.Numerics.Vectors` identity; the callable members take the same argument-boundary rule (no ref or out argument and no user-defined conversion at the argument boundary), and their argument expressions are traversed independently. The name-keyed reviewed intrinsic set accepts a name that Roslyn binds as a special type (`System.Double`, `System.Int32`, `System.String`, and so on) only when the type is that special type, so a same-named type from another assembly stays unclassified (`FrameworkIntrinsicsFromAnUnreviewedAssemblyStayUnclassified`). A compiler-generated record or record-struct `==` or `!=` that exact-construction certification cannot close, including a lifted comparison of nullable operands, is certified by Closed-Value Equality when a recursive field walk, charged to the same per-site proof budget, shows that every instance field is a handle-incapable leaf or a nested closed-value record. Leaves are exact CoreLib scalars, `string`, `Guid`, `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset`, `TimeSpan`, `Int128`, `UInt128`, `Index`, `Range`, enumerations, `Nullable<>` of a leaf or closed record, one-dimensional arrays and `ImmutableArray<>` of leaves, and value tuples of leaves; an interface, `object`, delegate, type parameter, non-record class, unsealed or generic record, source-authored lookalike, authored `EqualityContract`, or static initialization (a static constructor, or a static field or property initializer, which nothing traverses) keeps the record outside the rule, and with it any nested record that has one (`ClosedValueEqualityRefusesARecordWithStaticInitializationAndNeverCertifiesItsEquals`). The operand expressions are still traversed where they are written. An authored typed `Equals` that the operator reaches is traversed by Canonical Equals Traversal: it is bound with no arguments, so the argument bindings and the recovery bindings of the traversal state are blank while the root, the recovery context, the Work, Effect and recovery-effect frontiers, the field publications, completion ownership and lifecycle stay the caller's (Full-Environment Identity), and its operation id is `<root operation>/equals@<type>`. Every comparison site under one root and frontier therefore reaches one state, and an effect inside `Equals` is still reported under each root and each recovery tuple that reaches it (`ClosedValueEquality` fixtures). A formal that feeds only such a comparison, only an exact framework scalar operator, a pure intrinsic argument or a primitive-queue argument does not ask its callers for the actual argument, so every caller of a comparison helper shares one evaluation environment; a record whose authored `Equals` can reach a producer site, and the Long Rest histogram arguments, keep that demand and with it the precision of an exactly constructed receiver (`AFormalThatFeedsOnlyAFrameworkRuleStatesDoNotGrowWithTheNumberOfCallers` counts the states). Constructor classification proves only exact local setup and storage of a typed transport. It neither certifies host activation nor waives factory, getter, conversion, callback or later physical-send effects; those remain separate authored execution obligations. Controlled SDK setup, the three owned tagless Long Rest histogram emissions and the three `ArcanumMetrics` `Histogram<long>` token-count emissions (`arcanum_estimated_input_tokens`, `arcanum_provider_reported_input_tokens`, `arcanum_input_token_estimation_variance`) are reviewed within that boundary; physical chat and embedding generation remain producer calls requiring their ordinary work and effect frontiers. The Long Rest frontier observation is the one whose value comes from a data-dependent list: the branch cursors of a hierarchy expansion are built from child ids that an authored static helper reads from storage and returns in a `List<Guid>`. Those ids are an opaque run of `Guid` values, and nothing else, only when the helper resolves exactly and returns the framework list it created empty itself, its call boundary uses only built-in conversions, the list reaches the local or argument that receives it through no cast and no user-defined conversion, and each id reaches its cursor as the `Guid` lambda parameter. A subclass, a list the helper does not create or replaces after creating it (by assignment, an `out` or `ref` argument, a deconstruction or a `ref` alias), an element type other than `Guid`, a helper that cannot be resolved, a boundary conversion, a cast or an authored conversion on the list, and an id that is passed through any other call (which is reviewed there) all keep the observation refused. The helper, its arguments and the ids are traversed where they are written, and the cursors are still enumerated so that their certified getters are proved (`HierarchyFrontierObservationRequiresReachedCompleteScalarOrigins`, the `children-*` rows). The token histograms are an exact reviewed contract: each is a `static readonly` field of `ArcanumMetrics`, created from the exact `Meter("Arcanum", "0.1.0")` by the exact `CreateHistogram<long>(string, string?, string?)` overload with constant arguments (the instrument-tags and advice overloads are refused), the recorded value takes the argument-boundary rule, and each tag must be an inline `new KeyValuePair<string, object?>(constantKey, value)` or a never-reassigned local initialized by one, whose value is statically `string` or a null or string constant. The first-party Prometheus exporter formats every tag value while `Record` runs, so a tag value of any other type could run an authored `ToString` or `IFormattable` that no traversal of the call site reaches (`ArcanumTokenHistogramsRefuseEveryLookalike`). The exact default-constructed primitive `PriorityQueue<TElement, (double, ulong, ulong)>` takes only the argument-boundary rule for the arguments of `Enqueue`, which are traversed where they are written, while its receiver keeps the exact default-origin demand. Histogram listeners run synchronously and may perform work or throw, and that limit applies to every histogram contract above. Source-authored observer registrations, callbacks, arguments, getters and wrappers remain analyzed or explicitly refused. Ambient SDK telemetry switches, static initialization and shared HTTP client observer timing, framework reflection/loader/native behavior, and arbitrary third-party runtime observers are unproved limits; recognizing setup or observation confers no producer authority.

The virtual metadata `SqliteConnection.CreateCommand()` slot requires a closed receiver at each source call. An exact provider allocation or nonvirtual metadata base call retains its reviewed external contract. A sealed authored allocation with a compiler-selected override enters that actual source body with its constructor bindings. Stable locals, by-value argument bindings and private readonly current-instance fields may supply that allocation only while every followed wrapper has built-in conversions; unknown receivers, opaque factories, authored conversions and incomplete provenance remain unclassified. A compiler-selected static async source method may supply the receiver through the exact framework `Task<SqliteConnection>.ConfigureAwait(false)` shape only when its complete return scan has one successful expression. The walk retains original caller arguments and the same proof budget. Any followed local or by-value formal referenced by a nested callable is refused before its initializer or argument can hide that capture, including constructor-stored callbacks. Nominal provider type alone does not hide an override or certify a later call with a different receiver. This contract grants no work or effect authority.

**Provider Dispatch Closure.** The reviewed database support members and the database sites name framework members by identity, and almost every one is virtual or abstract, or is a non-virtual wrapper over a virtual slot, of a type authored code can extend: `DbConnection.CreateCommand` calls `CreateDbCommand`, `DbCommand.CreateParameter` calls `CreateDbParameter`, `DbCommand.ExecuteReader` calls `ExecuteDbDataReader`, `DbDataReader.Get*`, `DbParameter.Value`, `DbTransaction.Connection` and `DbParameterCollection.Add` are abstract, and `DbContext.Set`, `DbSet<T>.Add` and `ChangeTracker.Entries` are virtual. A grant by name states what the framework body does and nothing about an override an authored subclass put behind it, which is how `DbConnection c = new EvilDb(); c.CreateCommand()` with an effectful `CreateDbCommand` produced neither a site nor a diagnostic. A grant is therefore valid only for a closed receiver; any other receiver leaves a reviewed support member `HOSTED_SITE_UNCLASSIFIED` and, for a database site (`DbCommand.Execute*`, `DbConnection.Open` and `BeginTransaction`, `DbDataReader.Read`, `DbTransaction.Commit`, ...), keeps the site and adds `HOSTED_CALL_TARGET_UNRESOLVED` beside it, because the access is real whatever the receiver holds. The audited surface is the instance members of the ADO.NET provider bases (`DbConnection`, `DbCommand`, `DbTransaction`, `DbDataReader`, `DbParameter`, `DbParameterCollection`, `DbConnectionStringBuilder`) and of the Sqlite types authored code can derive from (`SqliteConnection`, `SqliteCommand`, `SqliteParameter`, `SqliteConnectionStringBuilder`), and of the extensible Entity Framework types the grants name (`DbContext`, `DbSet<T>`, `ChangeTracker`, `EntityEntry`, `DatabaseFacade`, `IDbContextTransaction`); statics and constructors have no receiver to dispatch on. For the ADO.NET and Sqlite wrappers a receiver is closed when its static type is a framework class no authored code can derive from (`SqliteDataReader`, `SqliteTransaction` and `SqliteParameterCollection` have no accessible constructor), when `SqliteSealedByUse` holds and its static type is exactly `SqliteConnection`, `SqliteCommand` or `SqliteTransaction`, when its provenance proves an exact framework runtime type (an allocation, or the final-provider factory chain), or when it is the `Parameters` of a closed command. An exact authored runtime type is never closed, because the wrapper hides its overrides. For the virtual Entity Framework types the compiler already bound the most-derived override of the static type it saw, so a sealed static type is closed, an exact runtime type is closed when it overrides nothing the member could reach, and the `Database`, `ChangeTracker`, `Set<T>()` and set properties that a closed context hands out are the framework's own (a set property counts only on a sealed context, and only when its body is exactly `Set<T>()` or nothing authored assigns it). A local holds what was assigned to it in its declaring member, and only by plain assignment: a local that is written by a deconstruction, a `ref`, `out` or `in` argument, a `ref` alias, a compound assignment or an increment, or that a nested function mentions, holds nothing the analysis can name, and the local's own writes are consulted only where the provenance could not follow the value (a provenance that named every source and found one that is not closed is the answer, never overridden by the local). A value handed to a reviewed member, as an argument or as the value assigned to a property, is judged by what it is and not by what it is declared as: an authored subclass of a provider type refuses the grant even for a receiver no one can extend, because the framework member calls that argument's virtual members, and so does a value declared as anything an authored subclass converts to (the type itself, one of its bases, an interface it implements, `object`, a type parameter) unless its provenance proves an exact framework runtime type (an allocation, or a parameter a closed command created) (`AnAuthoredProviderSubclassHandedToAReviewedMemberThroughATypedLocalIsRefused`, `AFrameworkProviderValueHandedToAReviewedMemberStaysClassifiedWhileAnAuthoredSubclassExists`, `ALocalWrittenByAnythingButAReadablePlainAssignmentIsNotAClosedReceiver`). A `Dispose` or `DisposeAsync` written as a call is judged like any other member, while a disposal that cleanup resolution reaches names the exact candidate it proved. A member read or assigned through a conditional access (`value?.Member`, and the C# 14 `value?.Member = x`) is judged exactly as the same member through a plain access: the name a conditional access binds has no operation of its own, so the judgement reads the operation of the binding that holds it, whose receiver is the expression the access guards. A closed receiver stays classified, a receiver that can hold an authored subclass is refused, and a member of a type no authored code can derive from (`SqliteTransaction.Connection`, `SqliteDataReader.FieldCount`) is closed whatever the receiver is (`AReviewedDatabaseMemberReadThroughAConditionalAccessIsJudgedLikeAPlainRead`, `FrameworkAccessorIsJudgedByItsClassificationWhateverTheReceiverIsProvedToBe`). `DbProviderTypesClosedByUse` (below) is the verified closed-world premise that grants the whole audited surface for a receiver of any provenance, which is what lets the shipped code keep its abstract `Db*` types and its `DbSet` properties. The `DbProviderDispatch` fixtures pin the rule: every audited family refused on an opaque receiver and classified on a closed one, an authored subclass or an unsealed context behind the same member refused, the reviewer's `EvilDb` probe, disposal, and an authored argument.

**Explicit stream cleanup dispatch.** An explicit call to the exact framework `Stream.DisposeAsync()` virtual slot follows the existing effective-cleanup proof used for `IAsyncDisposable` and `await using`. The receiver must have a complete, compiler-effective origin; a private readonly wrapper field carries only its proven constructor argument. Authored overrides are traversed under the Work and effect frontiers live at disposal, and asynchronous cleanup must be joined before those frontiers end. A read-only file origin retains its filesystem-read classification, including disposal; a writable file or an authored cleanup effect still needs the matching effect group. Unknown or mixed implementations stay refused. A nonvirtual `base.DisposeAsync()` call retains the conservative framework-effect classification rather than redispatching to the overriding method. Synchronous `Stream.Dispose()` also retains its conservative classification because its framework body can call protected virtual cleanup. No general stream cleanup is mechanical or exempt from authority. `ExplicitStreamCleanupFollowsWrapperInnerOwnership`, the incomplete-origin and expired-lifetime controls, the synchronous/interface parity controls, and `ProductionAttachmentExtractionRetainsItsExactAdmittedLifetime` pin this boundary. The real attachment root proves both the encrypted reader and legacy read-only file disposal hold Work through final use without acquiring a write effect group; snapshot read/hash validation, parser quarantine, worker effect admission and storage write/erasure authority retain their independent checks.

**Non-Owning Provider Observation.** A call on a disposable parameter makes the parameter's source part of its callee's environment, because the call could be the disposal itself or hand the parameter's ownership on. `DbCommand.CreateParameter` is neither: it returns a fresh parameter that belongs to no command until the caller adds it, and the framework body of the slot, `DbCommand`'s or `SqliteCommand`'s, neither disposes nor keeps its receiver. The call is therefore not a cleanup use of its receiver while `DbProviderTypesClosedByUse` holds, which proves that no authored or referenced type derives from a provider type and so that no override can do either. Without the premise, or with an authored `DbCommand` subclass, the call keeps its demand and the helper keeps one state per command it is handed. The `Add(DbCommand command, string name, object value)` helpers that nearly every store carries are one state per payload type, not one per command and call site.

**Implicit Enumeration.** A `foreach`, an `await foreach` and a collection-expression spread call `GetEnumerator` (or `GetAsyncEnumerator`), `MoveNext` (or `MoveNextAsync`), `Current` and `Dispose` (or `DisposeAsync`) of their operand, and an iteration variable of another type calls any user-defined element conversion, without one call being written. The traversal models those calls where the loop or the spread executes them. The members are the ones the compiler selected: the semantic model's foreach binding for a loop, and the same binding replayed on a synthetic loop over the operand, bound at the spread's position in the same model, for a spread (a binding depends on syntax and semantic model only, so it is cached per syntax node). The selected members are followed whatever the operand is classified as. An authored extension or static `GetEnumerator` or `GetAsyncEnumerator` is chosen by the operand's static type, so it runs for a closed framework collection, an iterator result, a `ConfigureAwait` wrapper, a default struct and a null receiver alike, and the enumerator it returns is proved from its return expressions so that its `MoveNext`, `Current` and `Dispose` are resolved too (`ExtensionGetEnumeratorSelectedForAnIteratorOperandIsTraversed`, `ExtensionGetEnumeratorSelectedForAConfiguredAsyncSequenceIsTraversed`, `ExtensionGetAsyncEnumeratorSelectedForAClosedListIsTraversed`, `NullReceiverReachesAnExtensionGetEnumeratorThatAcceptsIt`); an extension declared for another receiver is never selected for a closed operand and adds nothing (`ExtensionDeclaredForAnotherReceiverIsNotSelectedForAClosedOperand`).

An operand is classified before any instance member is followed. It is closed when its static type is an array, `string` or one of the reviewed closed framework collections, each with its trusted framework identity: `List<T>`, `Dictionary<TKey,TValue>` with its key and value collections, `HashSet<T>`, `Queue<T>`, `Stack<T>`, `ConcurrentDictionary<TKey,TValue>`, `ConcurrentQueue<T>`, `ImmutableArray<T>`, `Span<T>`, `ReadOnlySpan<T>`, the `JsonElement` array and object enumerators, the two rune enumerators and the regular-expression `MatchCollection`. Their enumeration members are non-virtual, so the static type fixes them whatever the runtime type is, and they call only framework code over in-memory storage; a type of another assembly that shares a name, and an authored subclass that hides `GetEnumerator`, are not closed (`ForeignTypeSharingAClosedCollectionNameIsNotClosed`, `AuthoredSubclassThatHidesGetEnumeratorIsTraversedNotClassifiedAsTheFrameworkList`). A few more framework types are trusted only for their exact runtime type, because the members they declare call abstract or virtual members of their subclasses: `SortedSet<T>` (a view calls its comparer), the sealed `ImmutableArray<T>.Builder`, and the access-control collections `RawAcl` and `AuthorizationRuleCollection`, whose members are declared by `GenericAcl`, `AceEnumerator` and `ReadOnlyCollectionBase`. An allocation or a sealed static type of one of them is accepted and a storage location typed as an unsealed one, such as a `SortedSet<T>` view, is not (`ExactTypeOnlyFrameworkCollectionsAreAcceptedOnlyForTheirExactType`). A framework implementation is accepted for a candidate only when the type that declares it is closed, or when the candidate is itself the exact framework type; the declaring type alone never decides, so an authored subclass of `GenericAcl` or `ReadOnlyCollectionBase` is not accepted through its base (`AuthoredGenericAclSubclassIsNotTheExactFrameworkAcl`, `AuthoredReadOnlyCollectionBaseSubclassIsNotTheExactFrameworkCollection`). The reviewed primitive priority queue's `UnorderedItems` is closed by its existing origin review. So is `AggregateException.InnerExceptions`, the read-only view over the array the exception copied from its constructor arguments, because that list is framework-owned and its elements are exceptions that are never enumerated as sequences; any other read-only view wraps whatever list it was given and is not closed (`AggregateExceptionInnerExceptionsIsAFrameworkOwnedSequence`, `AnyOtherReadOnlyViewIsNotAFrameworkOwnedSequence`).

Any other operand is proved value by value. A conditional, a coalesce or a switch arm is proved arm by arm. An allocation or a struct or sealed-class static type is an exact candidate runtime type. The `default` of a value type is an exact candidate of that type, and a `null` or `default` of a reference type is a null receiver, which has no instance member to run (the static or extension `GetEnumerator` it can still reach is the selected member above); the default of a type parameter is unproven (`DefaultOfAnAuthoredStructEnumerableIsTraversed`, `DefaultOfAClosedFrameworkStructStaysClassified`). Storage is followed through the existing reviewed value sources (locals, readonly fields without an authored write, properties, parameters whose caller value is bound), each judged with the semantic model of the tree that holds it, under a 256-unit work budget of its own whose exhaustion leaves the value unproven. A local or a field that a tuple deconstruction names is reassigned by it and is not followed to its declaration (`LocalReassignedByDeconstructionIsNotFollowedToItsDeclaration`, `ReadonlyFieldReassignedByDeconstructionInTheConstructorIsNotFollowedToItsInitializer`). A user-defined conversion hands the loop whatever the operator returns, not the value it converts, so a value to which the context applies one, a written cast or an implicit conversion at an initializer, a return or an argument binding, is unproven (`CastThroughAUserDefinedConversionIsNotFollowedToItsOperand`, `ImplicitUserDefinedConversionHidesTheRuntimeTypeAndIsRefused`; the twin with a built-in reference conversion is `BuiltInReferenceConversionKeepsTheRuntimeTypeAndIsTraversed`). An authored iterator is closed, because its body is the enumerator and is traversed where it is called with its lazy consumption proved by the lazy-sequence rule (below); any other authored method is the union of what it returns, evaluated in its bound context.

A framework or external call is followed only when it returns a framework sequence interface or the reviewed `ConfigureAwait` wrapper and is a reviewed sequence operator: a `System.Linq.Enumerable` operator that builds a new sequence out of the sequences and callback results it is given (`Select`, `SelectMany`, `Where`, `Concat`, `OrderBy`, `Take`, `Zip`, `Range`, `Empty` and the rest of the reviewed table), the `ImmutableArray` `Select`, `SelectMany` and `Where`, and `ConfigureAwait` of an asynchronous sequence. Every sequence it was given, receiver and arguments, must itself be proved, and so must the values the callback of `SelectMany`, the one family that enumerates a sequence its callback returns, returns, read from the lambda or anonymous method or through the authored method a method group names. The value the call returns enumerates those sequences through their own members inside framework code, so what they can be is judged on its own (a framework type must be closed, an authored one is the framework-member rule's concern at the call) and never through the slots of the operand (`LoopOverAFrameworkOperatorWrappingAnAuthoredSequenceIsJudgedAtTheOperatorCall`, `FrameworkOperatorsOverClosedInputsStayClosed`). A framework call that returns an element or a stored value of a sequence interface type is not a reviewed operator: `First`, `Single`, `ElementAt`, a service lookup and a volatile read can hand back a sequence the proof never saw, so the value is unproven (`FrameworkCallReturningAStoredSequenceIsNotClosedUnderStrictDiscovery`), and it is accepted only under the Authored Enumerables Absent premise, where no authored type can stand behind a framework collection interface (`StoredSequenceIsAcceptedOnlyUnderTheAuthoredEnumerablesAbsentPremise`). An explicit interface call such as `((IEnumerable<T>)this).GetEnumerator()` is not a reviewed operator either, and is unproven. A concrete type outside the closed set keeps its own members and is judged by its type, except that a stored framework value type, such as the `ConfigureAwait` wrapper kept in a local, is first followed to where it was built (`StoredConfigureAwaitWrapperIsFollowedToTheSequenceItWraps`). An operand that is neither closed nor proved to exact candidates is refused as `HOSTED_SITE_UNCLASSIFIED` at the loop or spread, naming the compiler-selected `GetEnumerator`: an interface-typed receiver, an abstract or unsealed one, a type parameter or a `dynamic` one is never assumed to be a framework collection (`UnprovenInterfaceTypedReceiverIsRefusedAsUnclassified`).

A candidate and a slot may come from different project compilations when the value was followed through a caller, and Roslyn does not equate symbols across compilations, so a slot is matched to its implementation by contract and member identity when the symbols themselves differ (`AuthoredSequenceHandedToALoopInAnotherCompilationIsStillTraversed`). For each exact candidate every statically bound slot is resolved to its implementation: the interface implementation, the most derived override of a virtual slot, or the non-virtual member itself, which an authored subclass cannot replace. An instance member is resolved only on a candidate that is its declaring type or derives from it, so a candidate that reached the loop through a conversion no proof modeled has no such member and is refused. An implementation without source is accepted as described above; an authored implementation is traversed. An authored `GetEnumerator`, instance or extension, that is not an iterator returns its enumerator through its return expressions, which are proved the same way, and the enumerator's `MoveNext`, `Current` and `Dispose` are then resolved on the exact enumerator types, a returned enumerator that cannot be followed or a framework enumerator outside the closed set being refused at the site; an authored `GetEnumerator` that is itself an iterator is the compiler-generated enumerator, so its body is the lazy work of the whole loop and is traversed once. A non-iterator `GetEnumerator` that returns a call to an authored iterator method which returns the enumerator (`GetEnumerator() => Iterate()`) does not run that body at the call but on the `MoveNext` calls that follow, so the body is owned by the provider's traversal only when the Work and effect frontier live at the operand is the one live at the end of the loop body and at the loop's end, and otherwise the call stays unowned: it is refused as `HOSTED_CALLBACK_OWNERSHIP_UNPROVEN` and traversed with no frontier, as is an iterator that returns an enumerator anywhere else (`GetEnumeratorReturningAnIteratorRunsItsBodyUnderTheLoopWideFrontier`, `ExplicitIteratorEnumeratorCalledAfterTheLeaseWasDisposedLosesTheWork`; a method that merely returns an enumerator runs at its call, `NonIteratorMethodReturningAnEnumeratorRunsAtTheCall`).

Each authored step is traversed as a call at the loop, under the Work and effect frontiers live where the compiler executes it, using the existing positional lifetime queries: `GetEnumerator` just past the operand; `MoveNext`, `Current` and an element conversion at the loop head, which a back-edge reaches after the whole body, so they keep a frontier only when the same one is live at the operand and at the end of the body; `Dispose`, which runs on every exit including a `break` or a fault anywhere in the body, only when the same one is live at the operand and at the loop's end; and a lazy iterator body across all three. Disposal is monotone in position, so comparing the two ends compares the whole span, and a lease disposed inside the body therefore ends the Work of every later enumerator call (`LeaseDisposedInsideTheLoopBodyEndsTheWorkOfTheLaterEnumeratorCalls`, `IteratorGetEnumeratorRunsItsBodyUnderTheLoopWideFrontier`). A spread executes its steps once, at the spread. Spread lowering sizes and fills a collection operand through `Count` and `CopyTo` and does not call the enumerator at all for one (a spread mixed with other elements calls `Count` and `GetEnumerator`), so a spread also traverses, for every exact authored candidate, the authored implementation of each member of the collection interfaces the candidate implements (`ICollection`, `IList`, `IDictionary`, `ICollection<T>`, `IList<T>`, `ISet<T>`, `IDictionary<TKey,TValue>`, `IReadOnlyCollection<T>`, `IReadOnlyList<T>`, `IReadOnlySet<T>` and `IReadOnlyDictionary<TKey,TValue>`) except the members that change the collection (`Add`, `Remove`, `RemoveAt`, `Clear`, `Insert`, `UnionWith`, `IntersectWith`, `ExceptWith`, `SymmetricExceptWith` and every setter), which no operator that only reads the collection calls (`SpreadOverAnAuthoredCollectionTraversesCountAndCopyTo`, `AuthoredCollectionMutatorsAreNotRunByEnumeratingOrSpreading`). The selected members of a spread come from a synthetic loop bound at its position, which Roslyn cannot place in a field or property initializer; such a spread is classified by what its operand is alone, so a closed operand passes and exact candidates are refused.

Asynchronous steps are join-owned. `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` results join `IEnumerable<T>` in the lazy-sequence ownership rule. A lazy sequence's body runs on every `MoveNext` of its consumer, so the Work and effect group it ran under must be live wherever the consumer resumes it: a consuming `foreach` or `await foreach` resumes it after its operand, after each pass of its body and when it ends, and an iterator method used as the operand, directly or through a local, keeps the frontier of its call only when the same one is live at all three, so a lease disposed inside the loop body ends its Work (`IteratorOperandKeepsItsWorkOnlyWhileTheLeaseOutlivesTheLoop`, `IteratorOperandKeepsItsWorkWhenTheLeaseIsDisposedAfterTheLoop`, `AuthoredAsyncIteratorEnumeratedAfterItsLeaseWasDisposedLosesTheWork`). The callbacks of a lazy `Enumerable` operator and a lazy filesystem sequence such as `Directory.EnumerateFiles` run on the same `MoveNext` calls and are judged at the same three points (`LazyCallbackOperandKeepsItsWorkOnlyWhileTheLeaseOutlivesTheLoop`, `LazyFilesystemSequenceKeepsItsWorkOnlyWhileTheLeaseOutlivesTheLoop`). A sequence handed to an authored consumer that loops over it keeps the frontier of the call only when nothing else the consumer receives, another argument or the receiver it is called on, carries the admission, because a consumer that holds the lease can end it between two `MoveNext` calls (`IteratorHandedToAConsumerThatAlsoReceivesTheLeaseDoesNotKeepItsWork`). A body reached by an explicit call is traversed there once and never again at the loop that consumes it. A lazy sequence consumed only through an enumerator that a `using` or `await using` declaration owns (`GetEnumerator` or `GetAsyncEnumerator` on the call, then nothing but `MoveNext`, `MoveNextAsync` and `Current` on the local, none of them inside a callable) runs its body between that declaration and the end of its scope, where the enumerator is disposed, so the Work live at the end of the scope is what the body ran under and a lease disposed inside the scope loses it (`AsyncIteratorConsumedThroughAUsingScopedEnumeratorKeepsItsWorkOnlyWhileTheScopeIsProven`); passing, storing, returning, capturing or disposing the enumerator by hand leaves the consumption unproven. When no consumption of an asynchronous sequence can be proven, its body is traversed with no frontier and the `HOSTED_CALLBACK_OWNERSHIP_UNPROVEN` refusal is owed only if that traversal finds a site, so a returned async iterator whose body reaches no site is not refused, whereas the synchronous rule refuses a returned lazy sequence whatever its body does (`ReturnedAsyncSequenceIsRefusedOnlyWhenItsBodyCanReachAProducerSite`, `ReturnedSynchronousSequenceIsStillRefusedWhateverItsBodyDoes`).

A framework member that enumerates a sequence it was given runs that sequence's enumeration itself, so the sequence parameters of a framework call (`IEnumerable`, `IEnumerable<T>`, `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` and the types that implement them, the extension receiver included) are followed to their exact runtime types. The member enumerates through the contract, not through the pattern a loop over the same value would bind, so for every exact authored candidate the implementations of `IEnumerable<T>.GetEnumerator`, `IEnumerable.GetEnumerator` or `IAsyncEnumerable<T>.GetAsyncEnumerator`, and of `MoveNext`, `Current` and `Dispose` (or the asynchronous members) of the enumerators they return, are followed as well as the pattern members, because an explicit implementation can have a body of its own (`ExplicitContractImplementationIsWhatAFrameworkMemberRuns`, `ExplicitContractImplementationIsNotWhatALoopRuns`); and the read members of the collection interfaces the candidate implements are followed too, because `ToList`, `ToArray`, `Count`, `Contains`, `ElementAt` and the `List<T>` constructor call `Count`, `CopyTo`, `Contains` and the indexer instead of the enumerator (`EnumeratingFrameworkMemberOverAnAuthoredCollectionIsRefusedWhenItsCollectionMembersHaveEffects`, `EnumeratingFrameworkMemberOverAnAuthoredListIsRefusedWhenItsIndexerHasAnEffect`). An authored enumerable whose enumeration or collection members can reach a producer site, by the same transitive scan an opaque callback body gets, is refused as `HOSTED_CALLBACK_OWNERSHIP_UNPROVEN` naming the framework member, while the same call over an effect-free authored enumerable or a closed framework collection is not (`AuthoredEnumerablePassedToAnEnumeratingFrameworkMemberIsRefusedWhenItsEnumeratorHasEffects`, `FrameworkCollectionsDoNotRunAuthoredCollectionMembers`). An exact candidate that is a framework type outside the reviewed set is judged the same way and refused when its enumeration members cannot be followed, because a read-only view or a collection wrapper forwards to whatever list it was given. The member needs positive evidence about what it enumerates: a sequence argument whose runtime type nothing proves, passed for a parameter the member declares as a sequence, is refused the same way, exactly as a loop over it is, and under the Authored Enumerables Absent premise an interface-typed one is accepted because no authored type can stand behind it (`UnprovenArgumentToAnEnumeratingFrameworkMemberIsRefusedUnderStrictDiscovery`, `UnprovenInterfaceArgumentIsAcceptedOnlyUnderTheAuthoredEnumerablesAbsentPremise`). The sequence a `SelectMany` callback returns is enumerated by the member and is judged the same way, an unproven one being refused (`SelectManyOverAnAuthoredSequenceIsRefused`, `SelectManyLambdaReturningAnAuthoredEnumerableIsRefusedAtTheCall`). That transitive scan follows the authored enumerators and collection members of every loop and spread in a scanned body, so an opaque callback that enumerates an authored sequence is judged by what that enumerator can do (`OpaqueCallbackBodyThatEnumeratesAnAuthoredSequenceIsJudgedByThatEnumerator`). The limits are exact: a parameter of an authored callee carries a runtime type only when its caller value is bound; and a framework member that enumerates through a contract other than the sequence and collection interfaces named above is not followed.

**Implicit Call Census.** C# runs user-written code in many places where no invocation is written, and each one that no lane models would be a silent soundness hole. The census closes them by construction instead of one shape at a time. For every member body the traversal analyses, it walks the body's `IOperation` tree, with the pruning of the syntax walk (a lambda or a local function written in the body is not entered, because its body is analysed where it is called, and the implicit lambdas of a query expression are; the argument of `nameof` is never evaluated), and lists every operation that binds a method, a property or an event on the compiler's behalf. Each listed operation is anchored at its syntax node, which the traversal's node loop visits once, so it is judged under the Work and effect frontiers live there, at the position where the compiler runs the member. An operation whose call an existing syntax lane already traverses at that site is left alone. The census recognizes those operations by their syntax (a written invocation, creation, event assignment, prefix unary or binary operator), confirms the user-defined conversion the conversion lane reaches from the conversion's own node, and confirms that a property reference is read at a node the property lane visits (a member access, an element access, an identifier other than the name of a member access, which includes the receiver of a member access, and the name of a member binding) and refuses it otherwise (`LaneVisitsPropertyReference`). Every other call is traversed under the live frontiers or refused as `HOSTED_SITE_UNCLASSIFIED` (`HOSTED_CALL_TARGET_UNRESOLVED` when the construct binds at run time) with the selected member as the detail. A construct the census cannot follow is refused, not admitted; the operations it leaves to a lane are exactly as sound as the lane, whose limits are listed with the limits of the census below. Roslyn gives an expression written as `checked(...)`, `unchecked(...)`, `(...)` or `expression!` no operation of its own, so a body that is one is walked from its operand, and a body Roslyn produces no tree for is refused (`ImplicitCallInAMemberWhoseWholeBodyIsAWrappedExpressionIsTraversed`). The census depends only on the syntax and the semantic model, so it is computed once per member body and shared by every state of it. An anchor the syntax walk would not visit is moved to the region itself.

Two tables pin the Roslyn surface the census classifies. `OperationKindCensus` gives every `OperationKind` the pinned Roslyn declares, the Visual Basic and flow-graph kinds included, a role (structure: no member of its own; lane: dispatched by a syntax lane; census: taken over here; refused: no exact target) and a reviewed reason. `OperationSymbolCarriers` lists every public property of a Roslyn operation interface that carries a symbol or a conversion (directly, as a sequence or a nullable of one, or in a Roslyn info object that holds one) with its disposition, and is compared with reflection over the interfaces. A kind or a carrier that a Roslyn upgrade adds fails `OperationKindCensusClassifiesEveryRoslynOperationKind` or `OperationSymbolCarriersMatchTheRoslynOperationInterfaces` until it is classified, and `EveryProductionMemberBodyHasAnOperationTree` pins that the walk has a tree for every region the traversal analyses (a method, constructor, operator, conversion or accessor body, the expression of an expression-bodied property or indexer, a lambda, a local function and the expression of a field, property or event initializer), and `ProductionMemberBodiesContainNoOperationTheCensusCannotFollow` that none of them holds a construct the census can only refuse. The operations whose pattern members Roslyn does not expose through any symbol property (`await`, `using`, `foreach`, `lock`, a deconstruction, a tuple comparison, an interpolation hole, a string concatenation, `fixed`, a query) are classified by kind and resolved from the semantic model's own queries: `GetAwaitExpressionInfo`, `GetDeconstructionInfo`, the foreach binding, and the member lookup at the construct's position.

The constructs, with the position at which each member is judged (the position just past the operands that precede it, so that a lease disposed in them has ended the Work):

- **Deconstruct.** A deconstruction assignment or declaration calls `Deconstruct` of the right operand, instance or extension, then the `Deconstruct` and the user-defined conversions of every nested element; a positional pattern (`x is (var a, var b)`, a switch arm) calls the `Deconstruct` of its matched type; a deconstructing `foreach` calls it per element at the loop head, with the element conversions (the corpus entry `deconstruct-foreach`). `KeyValuePair<TKey,TValue>.Deconstruct`, `DictionaryEntry.Deconstruct` and `TupleExtensions.Deconstruct` are the reviewed framework Deconstruct members.
- **Collection initializers and collection expressions.** Each `Add` of a collection initializer, written as an element, a braced element or a nested initializer, is an implicit invocation with the element as its syntax. A collection expression, and the `params` collection of a call, runs the target's constructor or `[CollectionBuilder]` method and, for a target built by constructor, every `Add` in scope found with `LookupSymbols`, extension methods included, that one element can call: the first parameter takes the element and every other parameter is optional or a `params` array, so an overload with an optional or `params` parameter is followed too (the corpus entries `collection-expression-add-optional-parameter`, `collection-expression-add-params-parameter` and `collection-expression-add-generic-extension-optional`; an overload that needs a second argument is not selected). Each overload that can be selected is a conservative addition. The framework targets run reviewed framework members, and a framework target handed a value its parameter type allows it to hash, compare or format is judged by the framework callback rule below.
- **Awaiters.** An `await` calls `GetAwaiter` (an instance or extension member), `IsCompleted`, `GetResult` and `UnsafeOnCompleted` or `OnCompleted` of the awaiter, found from `GetAwaitExpressionInfo`. The awaiters and awaitables of `Task`, `Task<T>`, `ValueTask`, `ValueTask<T>`, `ConfigureAwait` and `Task.Yield` are the reviewed framework identities; a dynamic await is refused. An `await foreach` awaits two values the loop never names, the one `MoveNextAsync` returns at the loop head and the one `DisposeAsync` returns at the exit, and Roslyn reports no awaiter for either, so the awaiter members of each are found by member lookup on the awaitable's type (every `GetAwaiter` the lookup finds, instance or extension, which is a superset of the one the compiler selects) and traversed under the frontiers of the loop head and of the exit (the corpus entries `await-foreach-movenext-*` and `await-foreach-dispose-*`).
- **Interpolated string handlers and implicit `ToString`.** A handler's constructor and every `AppendLiteral` and `AppendFormatted` are implicit calls at the literal or the hole. A hole of a string interpolation, an operand of a string concatenation or of `+=`, and a value a framework handler appends, format the value with `ToString`, `IFormattable.ToString` and `ISpanFormattable.TryFormat` of its runtime type. The intrinsic framework value types, enums and primitives format with no authored code; `System.Uri` is not among them, because it is not sealed and an authored subclass can override `ToString`, so a `Uri` is formatted through the reviewed framework members for the exact framework type and through every authored subclass (`uri-subclass-*`). An exact authored type (a struct or a sealed class) is resolved on its own members; a value the existing value-source proof follows to its construction is resolved on the types it proves; and a value whose runtime type nothing proves is followed to the authored types of the analysed source that format with code of their own (a `ToString` override, an `IFormattable` or `ISpanFormattable` implementation, a generated record member, and for an exception the virtual `Message`, `StackTrace`, `Data`, `Source` and `HelpLink`) and are assignable to its static type, which is exact because the source is closed. A type that formats with the framework's own code adds nothing, so a hole typed `object` is followed to every authored formatter, and a formatter that cannot reach a producer site is not traversed (`UnprovenFormattedValueIsFollowedToTheAuthoredTypesThatCanBeIt`: the twins show that a type which cannot be the value is not followed). A hole whose static type is a framework class also runs the framework implementation of that type, which is classified or refused as it is for a value whose type is proved (the `ToString` of the framework classes the printing of an authored record reaches for its printed members, which format state they store and call no supplied code, is reviewed by exact type and assembly: `Regex`, `Type`, `Component`, `X509Certificate2`, the command-line `Symbol`, `ChatResponse` and `ChatResponseUpdate`; a nullable member is formatted as the value it holds), so a hole typed `Lazy<T>` is refused whether or not the lazy's creation is in view (`lazy-unproven-interpolation`, `lazy-proven-interpolation`). `Exception.ToString` formats the inner exceptions too (every one of an `AggregateException`), and an inner exception can be any exception the analysed source declares, so formatting an exception also follows the formatting of every authored exception type (`exception-inner-interpolation`, `aggregate-exception-interpolation`). An interpolated string that is converted to `FormattableString` or `IFormattable` keeps its holes and formats them when the value is consumed (`ToString`, `Invariant`, `Format`, `GetArguments`), which can be after the lease ended, so its holes are traversed under no frontier at all and their sites are reported with the missing-frontier diagnostics (`formattable-string-deferred`, the `Detached` disposition of the corpus). The members of an authored formatter are followed wherever the formatting is written: `AddFormatterCandidates` follows only the formatters that implement the slot with code of their own.
- **`with`, records and anonymous types.** A with-expression calls the record's clone, which calls its copy constructor; the copy constructor of a record that declares none copies state and calls the base record's. The generated `Deconstruct`, `ToString` and `PrintMembers` of a record or an anonymous type run only the accessors the type declares itself, because positional and printed members are auto-properties unless declared, and format the type of every printed member the same way (`RecordGeneratedMembersAreAcceptedWhenTheRecordDeclaresNoAccessorBodies`, `RecordDeclaredAccessorsRunWhenAGeneratedMemberCallsThem`); the generated `Equals` and `GetHashCode` compare and hash every field the record holds (every property of an anonymous type) with the default comparer of the field's type, which calls the `Equals(object)`, `IEquatable<T>.Equals` and `GetHashCode` the field's type declares (an exact type on its own members, any other type on every authored type it can be). Roslyn does not expose the generated members of an anonymous type, so they are resolved from the `object` member they override. A call to one of these members that is written (`rec.ToString()`, `anon.Equals(other)`, `rec.Deconstruct(out var a)`) has no declaration for the invocation lane to follow, so the census takes it over (`ImplicitCallKind.SynthesizedMember`; the corpus entries `anonymous-type-*` and `record-written-*`), and so does a written call to a framework slot that dispatches on the runtime type of its receiver (`object.ToString`, `Equals` and `GetHashCode` and the members of the contracts a framework member calls on a value). An auto-property accessor, declared or generated, runs no code.
- **Patterns and indexing.** A positional pattern over a value that is not a tuple type and has no `Deconstruct` tests the value as an `ITuple` and reads its `Length` and its indexer, the members of the value's runtime type (`ituple-*`); a list pattern reads `Length` and the indexer of its input and a slice pattern calls `Slice`, on the runtime type of the expression the pattern tests when it is a top-level pattern; `x[^1]` reads the `Length` of `x` (the indexer or `Slice` it then calls is the element-access lane's); a range builds `System.Range` through a reviewed framework member.
- **Operators and conversions.** The compound assignment operator (`+=`) and its conversions of the target and the result, the increment and decrement operators, the `true` and `false` operators of a condition and a `?:`, the operator of every pair of elements of a tuple comparison (every user-defined equality operator an element type declares, which conservatively includes an operator the comparison does not select), and the user-defined value conversion of a `??`, a `switch` governing expression and a `foreach` are all calls with no operator syntax of their own. The lane keeps the written ones; the conversion lane keeps every conversion it reaches from the conversion's node.
- **Construction entry.** A constructor with a declaration runs, before its body, the instance field, property and event initializers of its type and its base constructor, unless it chains to another constructor of the type with `: this(...)`; an explicit `: base(...)` is a constructor-initializer invocation. A creation whose constructor has no declaration of its own (the implicit one, a primary constructor, a record's, of a class or of a struct) runs the same entry (`struct-primary-constructor-initializer`, `record-struct-primary-constructor-initializer`), with the base type's constructor taken from the primary constructor's base list when there is one. An initializer is a member whose body is the initializer expression, and one that cannot reach a producer site is not traversed (`ConstructionEntryRunsInitializersAndTheBaseConstructor`). A spread in an initializer has no statement position to replay the foreach binding at, so its exact candidates are followed through the foreach pattern and the enumeration contracts by member lookup, a superset of what the compiler selects, and an operand that nothing proves is refused (the corpus entry `field-initializer-spread` for the first, `UnprovenSpreadInAnInitializerIsRefused` for the second). The base constructor of an Entity Framework context keeps its options and runs no EF service code, because `OnConfiguring` and `OnModelCreating` run at the first use of the context, which the first-use hooks judge; the parameterless constructors of `System.Threading.Lock`, `AsyncLocal<T>` and `ConditionalWeakTable<TKey,TValue>` are reviewed, and the `AsyncLocal` constructor that takes a callback is not. The base constructor an authored stream chains to, written or implicit, is the framework stream constructor, a file-system site that is reported under the frontiers live where the creation runs it (`AuthoredStreamBaseConstructorIsAFileSystemSite`). Static initializers belong to the type, not to an instance construction, and are not part of the entry; they are judged by the static initialization rule below.
- **Queries, `fixed`, `lock`, and what has no target.** A query expression passes lazy callbacks to the framework query operators, so its clause expressions are scanned like an opaque callback and refused as `HOSTED_CALLBACK_OWNERSHIP_UNPROVEN` when they can reach a producer site, and are not refused when they cannot. A `fixed` statement calls the `GetPinnableReference` found at its position for a value that is not an array or a string; `stackalloc` and the pointer forms call nothing; any other operation Roslyn does not model is refused. `new T()` runs the constructor of the caller's type argument, a dynamic member access, creation or await binds at run time, an operator or a conversion over a dynamic operand selects its operator at run time, and a function pointer call has no target; each is refused. A `System.Threading.Lock` declared in source is authored code that `lock` would call and is refused.
- **Accessors and virtual methods the runtime type selects.** A property or event accessor, and a written call to a virtual or abstract method of a class declared in source, is resolved on the runtime type of its receiver, not on the slot the access names. A static, non-virtual or sealed member, and a base call, is its own body. Otherwise the receiver is the static type when that is a struct or sealed, the type an object initializer creates, the types the receiver expression is proved to have, and for a receiver nothing proves every authored class or struct assignable to its static type (to every constraint of a type parameter), that implements the accessor's interface if it is an interface member: the one body the universe holds is traversed (`interface-property-unproven-single`, `abstract-method-unproven-single`), several bodies are refused as `HOSTED_CALL_TARGET_UNRESOLVED` when any of them can reach a producer site and run nothing here otherwise, except for a slot whose complete set of overriding classes is reviewed (`ReviewedClosedOverrideSets`, the `CredentialMirror` read and write), where every override is traversed and a set that is not exactly the reviewed one (a class added or removed, or the same shape under a name that is not reviewed) is refused again; the delegates such an override keeps from its constructor are followed to every construction of the class, unless one member builds the class twice with callables that differ, which leaves the callback unproven (`CallbackKeptFromTheConstructorIsFollowedToEveryConstruction`, which is why `OsKeychainSecretStore` builds each of its two mirrors in a member of its own) (`interface-property-unproven-many`, `virtual-method-unproven-many`, `ReviewedClosedClassDispatchTraversesEveryOverrideOrIsRefused`; `OverrideOfATypeThatIsNotTheRuntimeTypeIsNotRun` pins that the body of a slot a runtime type overrides, and the override of a type that is not the runtime type, are not run). An accessor or method that the framework or generated code declares is judged by the classification of the access, and an authored override of one (a `Stream` or `TextWriter` member) is not followed (a limit, listed with the others below). An accessor binds the construction context of its receiver (the callables and values the receiver was constructed with) the way a written call to a method of it does (`BindReceiverContext`). The receiver of a property pattern is the expression the top-level pattern tests, and a property read as the receiver of a further member (`Service.Go()` with an implicit `this`) is read where it is written. An accessor declared without a body that is not an auto-property accessor (an abstract, extern or interface accessor, the definition part of a partial property) stands for no code of its own: like a bodiless method it is resolved to what the runtime type selects, or to the implementation part of a partial property (`interface-property-*`, `abstract-property-*`, `partial-property-*`, `interface-event-*`, `virtual-event-add`, `receiver-property-*`). The written call of a method an interface declares keeps the invocation lane's own contracts (the bound implementations, the closed internal interface), which refuse a contract with several implementers.
- **Values handed to framework members.** A framework member calls the `ToString`, `Equals`, `GetHashCode`, `CompareTo`, `GetFormat` and `Format` of the runtime type of a value it is handed: when it formats, compares, hashes or orders it, or asks a format provider for a formatter. Which of those it can call is fixed by the declared type of the parameter: a parameter of type `object`, a type parameter or a `params object[]` admits formatting, equality and ordering; a parameter whose type is a format provider admits `GetFormat`; a comparer admits `Compare`, `Equals` and `GetHashCode`. For each value handed to a parameter that admits them, every authored type the value can be (its static type, an array's element) is judged by the sites-only scan below, and the call is refused as `HOSTED_CALLBACK_OWNERSHIP_UNPROVEN` when one of them can reach a producer site (`framework-*` corpus entries: `string.Concat`, `string.Format`, `StringBuilder.Append(object)`, a hash set's initializer and collection expression, `List<T>.Contains`, a sorted set's comparer, `int.ToString(IFormatProvider)`, and the format provider of an interpolated string handler, which the census reads from the call that creates the handler). A parameter that admits none of them (an exception's inner exception, a span of key-value pairs) hands the value over unjudged, and so does anything the member does that is not one of these calls (a serializer reading a property, a logger, a stream override): those limits are listed below. The `AppendFormatted` of a framework handler formats the value itself and is modeled by the formatting of the hole, so the value is not handed over a second time. `ProductionAuthoredCallbackImplementersReachNoProducerSite` pins that no authored implementer of those slots in the production source can reach a site.
- **Static initialization and async method builders.** The runtime runs the static constructor and the static field, property and event initializers of a type at the first use of the type, which is neither a call nor a position, and an authored `[AsyncMethodBuilder]` runs its `Create`, `Start`, `AwaitOnCompleted`, `SetResult`, `SetException` and `Task` at points of the state machine; no operation binds either, so neither is traversed. Each is judged by the sites-only scan: a use of a type whose static initialization can reach a classified producer site (a static member of it, its creation, the creation of a type derived from it), from code of another type, is refused (`static-*` corpus entries), and so is a call to an async method whose authored builder can reach one (`async-method-builder-*`; `IAsyncStateMachine.MoveNext`, which a builder's `Start` calls, is the async method's own body and is reviewed). The production source declares neither, which `ProductionStaticInitializationReachesNoProducerSite` pins by name.
- **The sites-only scan.** What runs at a point nothing places (a callback, a static initializer, one of several bodies a receiver might select) is not traversed, so there is no diagnostic for an unreviewed framework member or an unfollowable construct in it to be the cause of; it is judged by whether it can reach a classified producer site. A second graph per set of analysed compilations answers that, with the scan of a body unchanged except that it does not ask about framework members nobody has reviewed, about constructs the traversal refuses, or about a method group that is passed and not called (the factory handed to a `Lazy<T>` runs at the first read of its value, which the lazy lane judges). The scan that prunes what the traversal follows (the next paragraph) keeps all of those questions.
- **Erroneous operations and the reviewed forms the production census reached.** An invocation that binds to no method is refused by the invocation lane at the invocation (`HOSTED_CALL_TARGET_UNRESOLVED`), so the census does not refuse the same site twice; every other erroneous operation has no lane and is refused as `HOSTED_SITE_UNCLASSIFIED` (`ErroneousOperationIsRefusedOnceByTheLaneThatOwnsIt`). Formatting an `object` that nothing proves reaches the formatting code of every authored type, so each framework call those bodies make is judged by an exact identity: `System.Text.SpanRuneEnumerator`, which the production reference pack declares in the `System.Memory` contract assembly and the runtime implements in `System.Private.CoreLib`, is a closed enumerator by name and contract identity, not by widening the contract mapping (`SpanRuneEnumerationIsClosedOnlyForTheFrameworkType`); `Base64Url.EncodeToUtf8` is a static transform of the caller's spans, and `UInt32.TryFormat` writes digits into the caller's span and is reviewed only when the caller passed no format provider, because a provider that was passed is asked for its number format and an authored one answers with code of its own (`InMemoryFrameworkFormattingMembersAreReviewedByExactIdentity`, `PassedFormatProviderKeepsUInt32FormattingRefused`); the indexer of `IReadOnlyList<T>` is the framework's own under the Authored Enumerables Absent premise and refused without it (`AuthoredEnumerablesAbsentClassifiesTheIndexerOfAnUnprovenReadOnlyList`); and `AITool.ToString`, whose body is a virtual call of `Name`, is reviewed for an implicit formatting call only, where the formatting resolution adds the `Name` implementation of the exact tool type (every authored tool type for a value nothing proves), while a written `ToString` call on a tool stays refused (`FormattingAnAiToolRunsItsNameOverride`, `WrittenToStringCallOnAnAiToolStaysRefused`).

A member is resolved on exact runtime types. A static member, a constructor and a non-virtual member are their own implementation. Any other slot is resolved on the static type when it is a struct or sealed, on the types the receiver is proved to have otherwise, and is unresolved when nothing proves them (`VirtualDeconstructRunsTheOverrideOfTheExactRuntimeType`, `UnprovenRuntimeTypeOfAVirtualImplicitMemberIsRefused`); the accessors and written method calls above follow the closed-world rule of the bullet that describes them, and a value formatted or compared by a framework slot follows every authored type that implements the slot; a call through a framework collection interface is the framework's own under the Authored Enumerables Absent premise. A resolved framework member is classified through the same exact reviewed identities as a written call, and one that is not reviewed is refused with its name. A source member with no body (abstract, extern, generated) that none of the rules above models is refused.

The transitive scan an opaque callback body gets, and that prunes what the traversal follows, follows every one of these: the census items of the scanned body, the dispatched accessors and virtual methods, the user-defined conversions, the cleanup of a `using` statement or declaration, the construction entry of a declared constructor, and every refusal the syntax lanes make at a node (a dynamic call or indexer, a framework member that enumerates an authored sequence or is handed a value it calls back into, a conditional logical operator, a lifted operator, a generated record operator the operator lane cannot certify, the first use of a type whose static initialization can reach a site, an async method with an authored builder). The scan has to say yes wherever the traversal would report a site or refuse, because the instance initializers a construction runs and the formatters of a value nothing proves are traversed only when it does; it may say yes where the traversal would not (`ImplicitCallInsideAnOpaqueCallbackIsJudgedByTheCallbackScan` runs every construct of the corpus, in every disposition, inside a callback, and requires the effect-free twin of a traversed construct not to be refused; `ImplicitCallInsideAPrunedMemberIsStillTraversedOrRefused` runs every construct inside a formatter reached through an unproven hole and inside an instance initializer, and requires the reported or refused outcome of the construct written in plain code; `FrameworkMemberEnumeratingAnAuthoredSequenceIsRefusedWhereverItIsWritten` pins the expression forms; `OpaqueCallbackThatCreatesATypeIsJudgedByItsConstructionEntry` does the same for a creation). A scan from a fresh path depends on the member and on the bindings it was bound with, so it is computed once per member and per set of bindings. A scan that is asked for again while it is being computed ends where it began, and a result cut that way is not cached (`SelfReferentialInitializersAndFormattersTerminate`). The `ImplicitCallCensus` self-check runs the corpus of one instance of every construct, each with its physical effect in the member the compiler calls: the effect is reported exactly once under the frontiers live at the construct inside an admitted region, is reported with the missing-frontier diagnostics outside one, is not reported when the member has no effect and not refused (`EveryImplicitCallConstructIsTraversedOrRefused`), follows the lease lifetime before and after the construct (`ImplicitCallFrontierFollowsTheLeaseLifetime`), and `TheCorpusExercisesEveryKindOfImplicitCall` pins that every kind of implicit call is produced by some construct. The limits are exact: a framework member can only be judged by what it is handed, so a value handed to one as `object` or an unconstrained type parameter is followed to the authored enumerables assignable to its static type, which the member may enumerate (`FrameworkMemberHandedAValueThatHidesAnAuthoredEnumerableIsJudgedByIt`; the Authored Enumerables Absent premise makes that set empty), and to the authored implementers of the slots its parameter admits, but what a serializer or a logger calls on the value besides those slots (a property read, a stream override, a handler) is not followed, a value handed to a parameter whose declared type admits none of the slots is not judged, and a framework collection of authored values (a `List<Key>` handed to a member that hashes its elements) is judged only through the parameters of the members that take an element; a virtual member that the framework declares (a `Stream` or `TextWriter` override) is not followed to its authored overrides, so an override that reaches a producer site is missed when the access is through the framework type; the scheduling context an awaiter captures is not followed; and an authored static initializer or async method builder is judged by whether it can reach a classified producer site, not traversed.

**Limit Pins.** A limit stated above is a claim about the shipped source only while something proves that the shipped source holds no instance of the shape the checker cannot see. `CheckerLimitPinTests` pins every one with a semantic scan of the production compilations (by type, call, registration, conversion and subscription, never by text) that is compared with an exact reviewed list, and runs the scan on a synthetic source that holds every shape it names, so that a scan which stopped matching cannot pass for ever. Its register ties each limit to the words of this document that state it and to its pin, and fails when either is gone. What the pins hold: (1) **EF model code.** The product declares no value converter, value generator, comparer, `IModelCustomizer`, convention or convention plug-in, supplies none to a model, replaces no EF service and overrides no `ConfigureConventions`; its two conversions are `HasConversion<int>()` of an enum, which runs framework code. (2) **Contexts the container owns.** The product has one authored context, registered twice: scoped in the offline command-line composition, and pooled in the host's. A pooled context is disposed with the root provider, after every hosted root has stopped, and the pool holds only idle contexts whose connections are closed, since the Grimoire opens a connection for one operation and closes it after; the registrations are exact, so a second pool, a singleton context or a context factory fails the pin. No authored context is converted to `object`, `IDisposable`, `IAsyncDisposable` or any other disposable type, so a disposable of unknown provenance is never a context. (3) **A disposable the container owns is disposed with the root provider** when the host is disposed, and the census does not follow that disposal.
