A disposal is the method a type runs for `IDisposable.Dispose` or `IAsyncDisposable.DisposeAsync` (an explicit implementation included) and every override of it, so a hosted service that overrides `BackgroundService.Dispose` is one. A registration owns the types it names and the authored types that its factories construct, found by following each factory (a lambda or a method group written at the registration) through every authored method it calls, every authored override and implementation of a virtual or interface member included; a type registered more than once keeps its longest lifetime. A factory whose product cannot be listed is refused unless it is reviewed: a delegate it invokes that could return an authored disposable, a delegate passed as a value, and a build by reflection from a type that is not a type argument. The one reviewed is a test seam of the secure file writer, a static delegate that only the tests assign. The authored disposals that reach a classified site by the sites-only scan and belong to a singleton registration are exactly `GrimoireDatabaseHostedService.Dispose`, which releases the installation maintenance lock the service holds; every other authored disposal that reaches a site is a lease or a handle that its owner disposes in a `using`, located where it is written. (4) **Framework virtual members.** The authored overrides of members the framework declares that reach a producer site are, outside the hosted roots (a hosted service's `StartAsync`, `ExecuteAsync` and `StopAsync`; its other overrides, `Dispose` included, are reviewed like any other) and the EF interceptors (followed by the Interceptor and Logger lane), the twenty-one types the pin lists: the provider and MCP HTTP handlers and the response streams they build, the AI tools the chat client's function-invocation loop calls inside the classified model call, the encrypted blob store's reader and writer (returned only by classified slots), the daemon runner's output cap (built inside a classified site), the request-pipeline streams, the command-line client's reader and writer, the A2A server object and the log file hook. The pin is exact on each type and on the members that construct it, so a new construction site is a review. The reviewed Tapestry SDK policy validates source/model currentness inside the existing classified attempt and is constructed only by the chat/embedding factories; the attachment digest reader wraps the already-open decrypted blob from its classified read slot. Neither starts independent provider work or creates effect authority. The encrypted blob writer is constructed by the private `CreateWriterCoreAsync` shared by its two classified public writer slots, so the exact constructor pin names that core rather than either forwarding method. (5) **Serializers and loggers.** No type implements a `System.Text.Json` callback contract, no message template destructures its argument (`{@`), and no destructuring is configured, so a logger reads no property. A template is judged by the values of the argument that a Serilog or Microsoft.Extensions.Logging call binds to its template parameter (a literal, a constant, a concatenation of constants, either branch of a conditional, and for a parameter of a private method the values every caller passes) and by the message of a `LoggerMessage` attribute, so the call through Microsoft.Extensions.Logging, whose provider is Serilog, counts; a template whose values cannot be listed is a finding of its own, and production has none; the seven converters are listed and none reaches a site; and the properties a source-generated serializer reads are those of the closure of the types its `JsonSerializable` attributes name, which holds no type whose getter reaches a site. The closure follows the public properties, every member marked `JsonInclude` whatever its accessibility, the public fields of the types a context reads when that context includes fields, the base types, the type arguments, the array elements and the subtypes a base type names with `JsonDerivedType`. (6) **The scheduling context an awaiter captures.** The product declares no `SynchronizationContext`, no `TaskScheduler`, no awaiter and no `AsyncLocal` with a change handler, installs no context, and subscribes to `UnobservedTaskException` once, in the host, with a handler that logs and marks the exception observed. (7) **Runtime observers.** The registrations of authored code that the runtime runs when something happens (a console interrupt, a termination signal, a file watcher event, a telemetry listener, a process exit, an ambient switch) are the twenty the pin lists with a reason each: the command-line clients' handlers, which run in a process that hosts no root; the workspace watcher's handlers, which hand a change to the indexing service's in-memory scheduler; and the metrics exporter's listener, whose callback reaches no producer site. (8) **The Authority Carrier Ban reads the source.** A compiler-generated state machine hoists the locals and parameters of an async or iterator method into fields the source does not show. The machine of a task-returning method is owned by its awaiter for the whole of the method, which is the lifetime of the lease it holds, so it is no carrier; an iterator's machine is the sequence, enumerated at the consumer's pace, and an `async void` method's machine is owned by nobody, so the pin refuses an iterator, an `async void` member or an async member that returns anything but a task, when any of them declares a parameter or a local that holds a lease or a group. Nothing in the source says what a reflective access does, so the pin lists every reflective read, write or invocation, every delegate built from a method object, every handler added through an event object, every call of an unsafe accessor (an `extern` method that the runtime binds to a field or member of another type) and every build of an object from an argument array (two constructions of authored tools by the container's activator), and refuses any that is handed a handle, reads one or returns one; the product loads no assembly, and loads a native library once, in the design-time context factory that only the EF tools allocate. The only unsafe accessors are the EF compiled model's, which read and write the backing fields of its seven entity types in the generated members that build the model (the ten accessor-class and member pairs the pin lists), and none of them touches a handle. (9) **The constant guard.** `EveryEnumerationOfAMembersValueBindingsIsGuardedAgainstAConstant` reads the compiled checker, so a `foreach`, a `.Values` read, a LINQ call, a copy of the dictionary, an alias and a lambda count alike; every method that enumerates the value-binding dictionary and reads a source's caller either calls the guard or is one of eleven reviewed readers that only name a source by its caller (an identity), compare two sources or copy them whole, and a method that enumerates the dictionary and never reads a caller cannot follow a source to it. A method reads a caller when it hands a source, a pair, a collection of sources or the dictionary to a checker method that reads one, so a walk that follows each source to its caller in a helper is found, and the keys copied out with every source then read through a lookup count as an enumeration. The scan follows calls and not values, so a method that copies the dictionary and, separately, hands one source it looked up by key to a comparing helper is listed too, and its row says what it hands over. (10) **A default body on a slot that takes a handle.** The lifetime walk resolves a call to the body it finds on the slot, and looks for the DI-bound override only when the slot has none, so a default interface body on a slot that is handed a lease or a group would be walked in place of an override that disposes it. `No_interface_slot_that_takes_an_authority_handle_has_a_default_body` reads every interface of the production compilations and lists each non-abstract, non-static slot (an accessor included) whose parameter or return type holds a lease, a group or a type that holds one; the list is empty, and a synthetic interface with a default body on each shape is the twin that proves the scan finds it. Reflection pins the gate and lease contracts beside it. One limit has no pin of its own, with the reason: the timing at which a shared HTTP client's observers see a request is not a shape in the source. The others in that sentence are held elsewhere: an ambient switch by the observers pin, static initialization by `ProductionStaticInitializationReachesNoProducerSite`, native imports by `ReviewedNativeImports`, reflection and loader behavior by the reflection pin (which also refuses a call that loads an assembly or a native library), and a provider's own state change by the connection-state fixture above.

**Production Discovery Entry and the Premise Ledger.** Production discovery runs through one entry, `DiscoverProductionSites(partition, rootSubset?)`, for the primary and the additional partition. An optional root subset narrows a scoped run to named hosted-service types, declared operation ids or non-hosted chain ids without touching any limit, scan or refusal, and a selector that names no declared root is an error, because a run that silently analysed zero roots would look green. The entry is the only production caller that requests closed-world premises, and fixtures cannot request them: `DiscoverProducerSites` has no premise parameter, so every fixture keeps `HostedProducerPremises.None` and the strict behavior above. Only `DiscoverProducerSitesUnderPremises` accepts a premise, and an architecture pin limits its callers to the entry and the `ClosedWorldPremises` fixtures. The ledger holds three premises. `SqliteSealedByUse`: no subclass of `SqliteConnection`, `SqliteCommand` or `SqliteTransaction` exists in any analysed source or in any reference an analysed compilation resolves. It is verified once per discovery, by an unbudgeted enumeration of every type of the analysed source assemblies and of every resolved reference assembly, not only those that name the provider (a subclass whose base is reached through a type-forwarding facade names only the facade in its own metadata, yet the compilation resolves that base to the provider type), and every isolated root worker shares that one verdict. A reference that is a module rather than an assembly, a reference that references a `Microsoft.Data.Sqlite` the compilation does not resolve, a base type that does not resolve, or a reference that binds no symbol and is not an exact duplicate of a loaded assembly (an image that cannot be read, or one whose name, version, culture and public key token are not those of a loaded assembly) means the premise is not granted; any subclass reports `HOSTED_PREMISE_VIOLATED` and the strict behavior stays. Granted, it makes a virtual `SqliteConnection.CreateCommand` on a receiver of any provenance (a parameter, a static property, a borrowed field) the reviewed provider contract, resolves the cleanup of a static `SqliteConnection`, `SqliteCommand` or `SqliteTransaction`, and lets a factory result whose receiver is statically one of those types take the exact provenance an allocation would. It never maps abstract `DbConnection`, `DbCommand`, `DbTransaction` or `DbDataReader` to Sqlite, never accepts an authored type that merely shares a name or namespace, and grants no work or effect authority. `Production_universe_satisfies_SqliteSealedByUse` pins that the shipped universe satisfies it. `AuthoredEnumerablesAbsentByUse` is the second: no type declared in an analysed source assembly implements `IEnumerable`, `IEnumerable<T>`, `IAsyncEnumerable<T>`, `IEnumerator`, `IEnumerator<T>` or `IAsyncEnumerator<T>`, directly or through a base type or an interface, and none declares a member whose name ends in `GetEnumerator` or `GetAsyncEnumerator` (an instance method, an explicit implementation, an interface default, or an extension, whether a static extension method or a member of a C# 14 extension block, which Roslyn exposes as a nested type of its own kind and as an implicitly declared method of the static class that holds it, so both are read: `AuthoredEnumerablesAbsentIsWithheldForAnExtensionBlockEnumerationMember`, with the twin `AuthoredEnumerablesAbsentIsGrantedForAnExtensionBlockWithoutAnEnumerationMember`). It is verified in the same once-per-discovery enumeration; an unresolved base type or interface of an authored type withholds it, and a violation reports `HOSTED_PREMISE_VIOLATED` naming the type and the contract. Granted, it lets the proof of an enumeration operand stop at any value it cannot follow, a storage location, a parameter or the result of a call, when the value is statically a framework collection interface of trusted framework identity (`IEnumerable<T>`, `IAsyncEnumerable<T>`, `IReadOnlyList<T>`, `IList<T>`, `ICollection<T>`, `IReadOnlyCollection<T>`, `ISet<T>`, `IReadOnlySet<T>`, `IDictionary<TKey,TValue>`, `IReadOnlyDictionary<TKey,TValue>`, `IOrderedEnumerable<T>`, `IGrouping<TKey,TElement>` and the non-generic `IEnumerable`, `ICollection`, `IList`, `IDictionary`), because no authored runtime type exists to dispatch to; compiler-generated iterators stay outside it, as their bodies are traversed and their consumption proved where they are produced. For the same reason the indexer of a value statically typed `IReadOnlyList<T>` is a framework member without a proof of where the list was built. It never covers a concrete framework type outside the closed set, an authored interface, or an interface of another assembly that shares a framework interface's name, and it grants no work or effect authority. `Production_universe_satisfies_AuthoredEnumerablesAbsentByUse` pins that the shipped universe satisfies it, and the strict behavior (an unproven interface-typed receiver refused) is exactly what every fixture without the premise sees. The premise stops a proof at a value of a sequence interface because no authored runtime type exists to dispatch to; it never covers an Entity Framework query, whose runtime type is a framework type whose enumeration is a database access. A query that flows into a sequence-typed parameter, return, field or capture is therefore refused where it is built (EF Queries below), so nothing the premise stops at can be a query (`AuthoredEnumerablesAbsentNeverHidesAnEfQueryBehindASequenceInterface`, with the twin `AuthoredEnumerablesAbsentStillCoversAnInMemorySequenceInterface`). `DbProviderTypesClosedByUse` is the third: every type in an analysed source or in any reference an analysed compilation resolves that derives from `DbConnection`, `DbCommand`, `DbTransaction`, `DbDataReader`, `DbParameter`, `DbParameterCollection`, `DbConnectionStringBuilder`, `DbSet<T>`, `ChangeTracker`, `EntityEntry` or `DatabaseFacade`, or that implements `IDbContextTransaction`, is declared by a trusted provider assembly (`Microsoft.Data.Sqlite`, `System.Data.Common`, `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore`, `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Relational` and `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite`, each by exact name, version, culture and public key token, so a lookalike assembly that shares a name is not trusted), and no authored `DbContext` overrides any member other than `OnConfiguring`, `OnModelCreating` and `ConfigureConventions`. It is verified in the same once-per-discovery enumeration of every type of every resolved assembly, shares the same unresolved-reference rules (a module, an unbound image that is not an exact duplicate, an assembly that references a trusted assembly the compilation does not resolve, an unresolved base type or interface withhold it), and reports `HOSTED_PREMISE_VIOLATED` naming the type and the family. Granted, it makes every audited member of the Provider Dispatch Closure valid for a receiver of any provenance, because every runtime type behind a provider-typed value is then a framework type (the shipped universe has the Sqlite types, `System.Data.DataTableReader`, EF's `BufferedDataReader`, `InternalDbSet<T>` and the sealed `ArcanumDbContext`). It grants no work or effect authority. `Production_universe_satisfies_DbProviderTypesClosedByUse` pins that the shipped universe satisfies it. The shipping CLI's two process-descriptor P/Invokes, `dup` in `libc` and `_get_osfhandle` in `msvcrt.dll`, are reviewed non-producers by an exact pin on assembly, declaring type, member, library, entry point, `SetLastError`, accessibility and signature; a lookalike differing in any one stays unclassified.

The widened `DbDataReader.this[int]` is a SQLite `DatabaseAccess` site only for a closed final provider. The receiver's cleanup provenance must still end in the exact `SqliteDataReader` chain, and the context behind it must be a container-resolved instance of a context whose registrations alone configure it. Every terminal value source of the context is an exact registered constructor dependency, or a `GetRequiredService`/`GetService` call on the container's own provider: a registration factory's provider parameter, an injected `IServiceProvider` or `IServiceScopeFactory` of an exactly activated owner, or the `ServiceProvider` of a scope created from one of those by the exact `CreateScope`/`CreateAsyncScope`. Each of those parameters, the context's own constructor parameter included, must be never written, whether it is named at the use or reached through storage that captured it: the check reads the operations the compiler binds, so a simple, compound, coalescing or deconstructing assignment (through any depth of target tuple), a `ref`, `out` or `in` argument, an increment, an address-of or a `ref` alias anywhere in the declaring type or factory body, a local function or a lambda included, leaves the value unproven. The value flow follows storage, not a write to a captured parameter, so this check cannot be left to it. A caller-created context, an authored or opaque provider, an `ActivatorUtilities`- or factory-built instance and a provider held in an authored property are not that provider. The certificate is a separate flavor of the cleanup provenance and never shares its stable cache, so cleanup and disposal tracking neither gain nor lose anything from it.

Each registration of that context may use its options builder only through the connection-string `UseSqlite` overload (a `DbConnection` argument can be any derived connection), a reviewed provider-neutral setting (`ConfigureWarnings`, `AddInterceptors`, `UseModel`, `EnableSensitiveDataLogging`, `EnableDetailedErrors`, `UseQueryTrackingBehavior`, `EnableThreadSafetyChecks`, `ConfigureLoggingCacheTime`), or an authored helper that takes the builder as a builder and satisfies the same rule. A builder value must be consumed by an analysed call, a property read, a discard or a named-method return, so an alias, array, `params`, tuple, lambda return or object/generic parameter is an escape. No other descriptor may name the context, `DbContextOptions`, `DbContextOptions<T>`, `IDbContextOptionsConfiguration<T>`, `IServiceProvider`, `IServiceScopeFactory`, `IKeyedServiceProvider`, `IServiceProviderIsService` or an `IInterceptor`. Every `IServiceCollection` mutation must be EF's exact registration method, an inspectable authored helper (a helper that only borrows the `AddDbContext` name is judged like any other helper), or a metadata helper from an assembly that is, by name, version, culture and Microsoft public key token, exactly the signed assembly the test host loaded; a simple name that starts with `Microsoft.` is not an identity. A body-less, extern or delegate mutator, a cast or `IList` view of the collection, an indexer write, an authored collection type or any carrier that bypasses the scan refuses. `SetDbConnection`, `SetConnectionString`, any member of `IRelationalConnection` or of a type implementing it, `IInfrastructure<T>.Instance`, `UseServiceProviderFactory`, `ConfigureContainer` and EF's accessor extensions refuse anywhere in the analysed graph; the one reviewed accessor read is `GetService<ILoggerFactory>`. The scan reads the bound symbol of every simple name in every syntax tree, so an invocation, a method-group conversion, a property assignment and a reference no root reaches all refuse alike. That verdict is a property of the analysed compilations alone, so it is computed at most once per discovery, by a scan that does not depend on which isolated root worker asks first, and every worker graph shares it (measured on 2026-10-15, the primary discovery runs it once and spends 2.9, 4.1 and 5.1 s in it under one, two and three root workers, and the additional discovery, whose roots never demand the certificate, never runs it; the scan and every worker graph read one shared semantic model per tree and so find bound what another already bound); a discovery whose roots never demand the closed-provider certificate never pays for it. `ConnectionReplacementIsScannedOncePerDiscoveryWhateverTheWorkerCount` and `ConnectionReplacementIsScannedAgainByTheNextDiscovery` pin the sharing, and `ConnectionReplacementVerdictIsTheSameForEveryWorkerCount` pins that the verdict, including a reference no root reaches, is the same for one, two and three workers. The context itself must also hand EF the options its registration configured: it has exactly one public instance constructor with exactly one `DbContextOptions<TContext>` parameter, that parameter is never written, and it is the whole argument (no wrapper, conversion or assignment) of the constructor initializer, which reaches EF's `DbContext(DbContextOptions)` directly or through authored constructors that each forward their own parameter the same way. A context that passes other options to its base class, falls back to the implicit parameterless base call, or offers the container a second constructor reads a provider its registration never chose. An authored `OnConfiguring` must be only discard assignments followed by `if (builder.IsConfigured) return;`. A refusal of any one of these leaves the indexer `HOSTED_SITE_UNCLASSIFIED`, never a grant.

**Inventory Facts.** A fact that depends on the analysed compilations alone, and not on any traversal state, binding environment or root, is computed at most once per discovery by a lazy scan and shared by every isolated root worker, so a discovery that never demands it never pays for it and the verdict cannot depend on which worker asks first. The facts are the connection-replacement scan above, the first authored type that implements a logger contract (`ILogger`, `ILoggerProvider`, `ILoggerFactory`), the first authored type that implements EF's identity-resolution interceptor contract, whether any analysed source spells an EF event-data type (`EventData` itself or any type Entity Framework ships that derives from it) anywhere but as a parameter's declared type, every allocation of an authored `DbContext` in analysed source, and every subscription to `DbConnection.StateChange`. Each reads the same trees the graph analyses (the product source, never generated build output), filters on a name before it binds anything, and treats a name that binds to nothing as a possible hit. The scans and every worker graph share one semantic model per tree, created on first use: a model binds lazily and is safe to read from several threads, so what one scan or worker binds the next finds bound, and the graph does not pay once per worker for the same binding. The model is shared across discoveries as well (**Shared Semantic Models** in the hosted-producer testing contract).

EF hands its events to authored interceptors and logger factories. The certificate claims provider identity and nothing about their effects, which belong to the Interceptor and Logger Lane below, and the interceptor shapes it tolerates are judged for identity alone. `UseLoggerFactory` is not a reviewed builder setting. An authored interceptor keeps the certificate only when it implements nothing but the connection-lifecycle callbacks of `IDbConnectionInterceptor` (opening, opened, closing, closed, failed, canceled, disposing, disposed and their asynchronous forms), found through interface mapping and through overrides of an inherited virtual, because those observe a connection EF already owns. Command, transaction, `SaveChanges`, materialization, query and identity-resolution interceptors, `ConnectionCreating`/`ConnectionCreated`, and a stored or returned interceptor value refuse. The serving `CovenantConnectionEnrolmentInterceptor` and `SqlitePragmaConnectionInterceptor` have exactly the reviewed shape, which is why refusing every authored interceptor was not an option. The Interceptor and Logger Lane below enters those callbacks at the operations that raise them, so this certificate does not stand in for their effects.

**Interceptor and Logger Lane.** EF hands its events to the interceptors registered on a context at the operations that raise them, and every authored callback is code nothing calls. The inventory therefore enters each authored callback at the EF operation that raises its contract, under the Work, effect and recovery frontiers live at that operation, as an ordinary traversal (the callback is completion-owned, because the operation does not return before EF has run it). The operations and the contracts they raise are `DbContext.SaveChanges*` (`IDbConnectionInterceptor`, `IDbCommandInterceptor`, `IDbTransactionInterceptor`, `ISaveChangesInterceptor`), `DatabaseFacade.BeginTransaction*` (connection and transaction), `OpenConnection*` and `CloseConnection*` (connection), `IDbContextTransaction.Commit*` and `Rollback*` (transaction), and every executed query (connection, command and the materialization and query-expression interceptors); the creation callbacks (`ConnectionCreating`, `ConnectionCreated`) are raised by every operation that needs the connection object. Within a contract every authored implementation of every slot is entered at every operation of that contract, found through interface mapping and through overrides of an inherited virtual; an operation never enters a contract it cannot raise (`AnAuthoredInterceptorCallbackIsTraversedOnlyAtTheEfOperationsThatRaiseItsContract`). The interceptors of a context are the set its configuration closes. For a container-built instance that is the union of what every `AddDbContext` and `AddDbContextPool` registration of the context adds through `AddInterceptors`, walked through authored helpers that receive the builder as a builder, with every argument an inline allocation of a type that implements EF's interceptor contract, or a static readonly field or get-only static property of such a type whose initializer is an allocation and whose declaring type has no static constructor (a static constructor could reassign it), read from the compilation that declares it, and no other descriptor able to hand EF an interceptor (a collection, an `IEnumerable<IInterceptor>` argument and any other value leaves the set open: `AnInterceptorSetBuiltFromAnythingButNamedInterceptorsIsRefusedAtTheEfOperation`, `AStaticSingletonNoStaticConstructorCanReassignStaysTrusted`, `ASingletonDeclaredInAnotherAnalysedCompilationIsReadFromItsOwnCompilation`); an `OnConfiguring` that is not the provider-complete guard adds what it hands the builder. For a context the analysis sees allocated, the set is what the options chain it was built from adds (a fluent chain over `new DbContextOptionsBuilder<T>()`, or over `new DbContextOptionsBuilder<T>(options)`, which carries everything the copied options carry and so follows them too and is not understood when they cannot be followed, or a local every value of which is one, with the model and the provider required of every value and the interceptors the union of them), with the `OnConfiguring` additions unless the guard returns for a chain that selected a provider. For a context that cannot be followed to either source, the set is the union over the Context Universe below. The set is only the one the options say when the context constructor hands its options, unchanged and unwritten, to the base context (`ContextOptionsForwarded`); a constructor that rewrites them proves nothing. The context an operation runs on is followed from a `Database` facade to the context it was read from and from a transaction to the facade that began it, through the values a local holds in its declaring member (`ALocalHoldingATransactionOrFacadeIsFollowedToTheContextThatBeganIt`). An interceptor that implements an EF interceptor contract the analysis does not enter is refused at the operation, naming the contract: `IInstantiationBindingInterceptor` and `IIdentityResolutionInterceptor`, whose triggers (building the model, starting to track an instance whose key is already tracked) are not operations of this lane, and any contract the table has not reviewed. `EfInterceptorContractVerdict` gives every contract a verdict (entered, marker or refused) and `EveryInterceptorContractEfShipsIsEitherEnteredOrRefused` reads the contracts from the assemblies, so a contract a later EF version adds fails there until it is reviewed (`AnInterceptorOfAContractTheAnalysisDoesNotEnterIsRefusedAtTheOperation`). The first use that builds the model raises the instantiation-binding interceptors too, so when no compiled model is supplied an interceptor of that contract is refused at the use (`AnInstantiationBindingInterceptorIsRefusedAtTheFirstUseThatBuildsTheModel`). The operations that start EF tracking an instance (`DbSet<T>.Add`, `Attach`, `Update`, `Remove` and their range and async forms, `ChangeTracker.Entries`, `DetectChanges` and `TrackGraph`, and the `EntityEntry.State` setter) can raise the identity-resolution contract, so while the analysed source authors an implementation of it none of them is a reviewed member and each is refused as an unreviewed framework member (`AnOperationThatStartsTrackingIsRefusedWhileAnIdentityResolutionInterceptorExists`). A context nobody can follow, an interceptor set that is not closed (an opaque value, an array element that is not an allocation, a registered `IInterceptor` descriptor, a registration that is not a lambda), and an authored type that implements `ILogger`, `ILoggerProvider` or `ILoggerFactory` anywhere in the analysed source (EF reports every operation to the application's loggers, so such a type could receive its events) are refused at the operation with `HOSTED_SITE_UNCLASSIFIED` rather than assumed empty. `UseLoggerFactory` stays outside the reviewed builder settings. The logger lane covers Microsoft's logger contracts; an authored Serilog sink that receives EF's log events is reached through the same reviewed logging boundary as any `LogInformation` call (logging is a reviewed non-producer, and a sink's effects are not producer sites of any root), and is not a gap of this lane. The data EF hands a callback is read through getters of EF's own event-data types (`DbContextEventData.Context`, `ConnectionErrorEventData.Exception`, `CommandEventData.Command`, ...) and of `StateChangeEventArgs`, which run no authored code; EF declares most of them virtual, so the read is reviewed only while no analysed source spells an event-data type (the Inventory Facts above), and an authored or lookalike type is not reviewed (`AGetterOfTheDataEfRaisedAnEventWithIsReviewedWhileNoSourceMakesEventData`, `AGetterOfALookalikeEventDataTypeFromAnotherAssemblyIsNotReviewed`). `AccessorExtensions.GetService<ILoggerFactory>` is the same kind of read while no authored logger exists. Calls made through `base` into EF's interceptor base classes, whose bodies only return the result they were handed, are reviewed non-producers; the serving `CovenantConnectionEnrolmentInterceptor` is entered at each operation, and the pins `Production_interceptor_set_is_closed_and_is_exactly_the_reviewed_enrolment_interceptor` and `Production_declares_no_authored_logger_and_never_selects_a_logger_factory` hold the shipped set and the absence of an authored logger. The lane covers the callbacks of the contracts above at the operations above. Disposal is its own operation. Disposing a context closes the connection if it is still open and then disposes it, which raises `ConnectionClosing`, `ConnectionClosed`, `ConnectionDisposing` and `ConnectionDisposed` (the synchronous slots for `Dispose`, the asynchronous slots for `DisposeAsync`) and the `StateChange` of the connection, and runs where the disposal is, under the frontiers live there, which can be after the work that used the context has ended. An operation therefore raises the rest of the connection contract but never the disposing and disposed slots. The disposal is located where it is written: an explicit `Dispose()` or `DisposeAsync()` on a value that is a context (its static type, or a disposable held as an interface or `object` whose every source is a context allocation), a `using` or `await using` declaration or statement over one, and the disposal of a container scope (`IServiceScope.Dispose`, `AsyncServiceScope.DisposeAsync`, or a `using` over one), which disposes the contexts the container built; the services of the scope are not followed, so every registered authored context is a candidate and its closed interceptor set is entered under the frontiers live at the scope's disposal (`ADisposedContextRaisesItsDisposalCallbacksUnderTheFrontiersLiveAtTheDisposal`, `AnOperationOnAContextRaisesNoDisposalCallbackBecauseNothingHasDisposedIt`, `AContainerScopeDisposalRaisesTheDisposalCallbacksOfTheContainerBuiltContexts`). A scope declared inside the block of the `await using` statement that holds a work lease is disposed before the lease, so its contexts' callbacks run under the lease; the lease handle forwarded to a call that returns a `Task` or `Task<T>` is not carried out by that task (a task is disposable but exposes no way to dispose what it was handed, and carries a handle only through the result it will produce), so the forward does not end the lease for what is disposed afterwards, while a task of the handle itself still does (`AContainerScopeDeclaredInsideAnAwaitUsingLeaseStatementIsDisposedInsideTheLease`, `AHandleCarriedOutThroughTheTaskItIsForwardedToStillEndsTheLeaseForWhatIsDisposedAfterwards`, `AResourceDisposedAtTheEndOfTheBlockOfAnAwaitUsingLeaseIsDisposedInsideTheLease`). A context the container disposes when the host's root provider is disposed is not disposed by any hosted root, and a disposable of unknown provenance is not assumed to be a context (every `Stream.Dispose` would otherwise be refused); both are stated limits. Value converters, value generators and comparers a model names, and `IModelCustomizer`/convention plug-ins, run authored code at points no operation of this lane names; they are stated limits, not claims. The same limit holds for the other authored context code EF runs on its own schedule, see Context Hooks below.

EF runs the authored `OnConfiguring` at the first use of a context's services, so the inventory enters the most-derived authored override at every such use, with no work, effect or recovery admission inherited. The use that really triggers it is not the read of a `DbSet` property or of `Database`: it can be a later consumer of a value read there (the `DbSet`, an `IQueryable` built from it, the `DatabaseFacade`), after the admission that held at the read has ended, and no position proves otherwise, so the override's effects are unadmitted wherever the hook fires. The serving context's override is the provider-complete guard and is skipped, and the stopped-host reset's fallback performs no producer site, so this hook alone changes no production site. A use is any non-static member of `DbContext`, or of an interface the framework context implements (`IDbContextDependencies`, `IDbSetCache`, ...), other than `Dispose`/`DisposeAsync`, whether the receiver is spelled out, reached through `?.`, or implied (`this` inside a derived context, including an implied property used as the receiver of a further member such as `Database.CanConnect()`), an authored instance member of a derived context called on a known receiver, a delegate to such a member, or one of EF's accessor extensions. A container-resolved instance whose override is the provider-complete guard skips it, because the registration configured that instance and the guard returns first; a caller-created or unproven instance runs the guard's fallback and is judged. An implied `this` cannot tell which instance it is, so inside a guard-closed context it is not assumed unconfigured and the fallback is judged at the call that has a receiver. A call through an interface into the context's own member is refused as an unresolved target rather than skipped.

**Context Hooks.** The same first use runs every other piece of authored context code EF runs on its own schedule, and the inventory enters each of them at the use, with no admission inherited. The receiver of a use is classified rather than skipped when its provenance cannot be followed. A value every source of which is an allocation is a created context; a container-resolved instance is a container context; any other value, whether its type is known from a sealed declaration or from a binding or only from its static type, is a context of the Context Universe below: a sealed or exactly known type is that type, and any other static type (a base context, `DbContext`, an interface the context implements, a type parameter's class constraint) is every concrete authored context assignable to it, enumerated from the analysed source assemblies, so an unfollowable receiver cannot hide an authored hook and a type nothing can make has no authored code to run (`AnOpaqueContextReceiverStillRunsTheAuthoredOnConfiguring`, `AnUnsealedContextReceiverRunsTheOnConfiguringOfEveryAuthoredSubclass`, `AnOpaqueReceiverOfAContextWithNoAuthoredHookRunsNothing`). For each candidate the use enters the most-derived `OnConfiguring` (unless the instance is container-built and the override is the provider-complete guard), the most-derived `OnModelCreating` and `ConfigureConventions` unless a compiled model is always supplied, and, for an instance not allocated in analysed code, the activation: the instance constructors with a body, the field and property initializers of the type and of every authored base, and the arguments of a primary constructor's base call. EF does not build a model it was given, so neither model hook can run when `UseModel` with a model is called on every path that configures the instance and the constructor hands those options to the base context unchanged: for a container-built instance, in every registration of the context (an unconditional call in the callback or in an authored helper that receives the builder; a conditional call, a null model and a second registration without it do not count), for an allocated instance, in the fluent options chain it was built from (a local holds its initializer and each assignment to it, all of which must supply the model, and a local that is captured, passed by reference or assigned from a value that cannot be followed holds nothing), and for any other instance, in every registration and every allocation of its type; otherwise the hooks are judged (`TheModelHooksRunAtTheFirstUseWhenNoCompiledModelIsSupplied`, `AModelSuppliedByTheRegistrationMeansTheModelHooksCannotRun`, `AModelThatIsNotAlwaysSuppliedStillRunsTheModelHooks`, `ACreatedContextWhoseOptionsSupplyTheModelRunsNoModelHook`, `ALocalHoldingTheOptionsOfACreatedContextIsFollowedThroughItsAssignments`, `AContextConstructorThatDoesNotForwardItsOptionsProvesNothingAboutTheModel`). The shipped registrations supply `ArcanumDbContextModel.Instance` through the shared configurator, so `OnModelCreating` cannot run for a container-built `ArcanumDbContext`, which `Production_registrations_supply_the_compiled_model_so_the_model_hooks_cannot_run` pins. An explicit allocation of an authored context traverses the constructor it names and the initializers, where it is written and under the frontiers live there (`ACreatedContextRunsItsInitializersAtTheCreationUnderTheFrontierLiveThere`). An implied `this` is judged at the call that has a receiver for everything except `OnConfiguring`'s unguarded fallback, so a context's own `Set<T>()` does not enter the hooks a second time. The `Context` of an EF event is the context EF was working for when it raised the event, whose first use, and the hooks it ran, were judged where that work was done, so reading it is not a first use; this holds only while no analysed source spells an event-data type, because an event-data value made in source could carry a context nothing has used (`TheContextOfAnEfEventIsNotAFirstUseWhenNoEventDataIsMadeByAnalysedSource`, `AnAnalysedSourceThatSpellsAnEventDataTypeMakesTheContextReadAFirstUseAgain`, `ALookalikeContextPropertyIsNotTheContextOfAnEfEvent`).

**Context Universe.** A context nobody can follow to its source is still an instance of a type the program can make, and authored code makes one in exactly two ways: the container builds it from the registrations of its type (`AddDbContext`, `AddDbContextPool`), and an allocation in analysed source builds it from options that source supplies. What EF is given (a compiled model, the interceptors) is therefore bounded by the union of the two, which is what a receiver of unknown provenance is judged by instead of being assumed to be anything: the compiled model is supplied only if every registration and every allocation of the type supplies it, the interceptor set is the union of what each adds and is closed only if each is, and the provider is configured only if each configures it. An allocation the analysis cannot follow (options from a parameter, an allocation in a field initializer, a constructor that rewrites its options) leaves nothing proven, a type with neither a registration nor an allocation has no instance the analysis can speak for, and a reflective or factory-built instance is a call to an unreviewed external member that is refused where it is reached. EF's design-time factory is the one allocation that is not a way the host makes the context: an `IDesignTimeDbContextFactory<T>.CreateDbContext` is instantiated by EF tooling in its own process, so its allocation is marked design-time only and left out of the union, but only while nothing in the analysed source names the factory type outside its own declaration, because a name is a way for analysed code to run the allocation (`AReceiverOfUnknownProvenanceIsJudgedByEveryWayItsTypeIsMade`, `AnAllocationInADesignTimeFactoryNothingNamesIsNotAWayTheHostMakesTheContext`, `AnAllocationInACreateDbContextThatIsNotTheFrameworkFactoryIsStillAWayTheHostMakesTheContext`, `AFactoryNothingNamesIsMarkedDesignTimeOnlyAndAFactoryTheSourceNamesIsNot`, `TheInterceptorsOfAnUnfollowableReceiverAreTheUnionOfTheRegistrationsAndTheAllocations`, `AnAllocationWhoseInterceptorsCannotBeNamedLeavesTheSetOfAnUnfollowableReceiverOpen`, `ADesignTimeOnlyAllocationAddsNoInterceptorToTheUniverse`). Following the value would have split a state per caller of every shared helper that takes a `DbContext`, so the universe is the bound that costs nothing per path. `Production_context_universe_is_the_registrations_and_the_installation_reset_allocation` pins that the shipped `ArcanumDbContext` universe is both registrations and the installation reset's stopped-host allocation, that all of them supply the compiled model, and that the only interceptor any of them adds is the reviewed enrolment interceptor; `Production_allocates_the_context_in_the_installation_reset_and_in_a_design_time_factory_only` pins the two allocations in the product source and that the factory is the design-time one.

**Connection State Handlers.** A handler subscribed to `DbConnection.StateChange` is authored code nothing calls: the connection raises the event when it opens, closes or changes state, so the handler runs inside that operation. The subscription itself runs no handler and holds no work, so it is reviewed wiring (and so is its removal) only while every handler in the analysed source can be named, a method group or a lambda that resolves to one authored member; an opaque delegate anywhere in the analysed source, reached or not, leaves the subscription refused as an external event whose handler is unknown, and every operation below refused with it, because that handler could be on this connection (`AHandlerThatCannotBeNamedRefusesTheSubscriptionAndEveryOperationThatChangesState`, `AnUnreachedOpaqueSubscriptionStillOpensTheRegistryForEveryReachedOperation`). The handlers are then entered, under the frontiers live there, at the operations that change a connection's state: an authored `Open`, `OpenAsync`, `Close` or `CloseAsync` on a `DbConnection`, and every EF operation that raises the connection contract (`AHandlerOfConnectionStateChangeIsEnteredWhereTheConnectionChangesState`, `AHandlerOfConnectionStateChangeRunsUnderTheFrontiersLiveAtTheOperation`, `AnEfOperationThatRaisesTheConnectionContractEntersTheHandlersToo`), while a call that changes no state enters none. An authored event that merely shares the name is its own event (`AnEventNamedStateChangeThatIsNotTheFrameworkEventIsNotAHandlerRegistry`). The disposal of a context closes its connection, so the handlers are entered at a context's disposal too (Interceptor and Logger Lane, Disposal); a state change the provider makes by itself is not an operation of this lane and is a stated limit. `Production_subscribes_exactly_one_named_handler_to_connection_state_changes` pins that the enrolment interceptor's `OnPhysicalStateChanged` is the only subscription in the product source.

**EF Queries.** Executing an Entity Framework query is a database access wherever it is written, and each of these is a `DatabaseAccess` site that requires the Work frontier live at it: enumerating a query (a `foreach`, an `await foreach` or a spread, whose frontier must hold at the operand, at the back edge and at the end, because the reader stays open between them), and every terminal operator over one. The operators are classified by exact framework identity and by a name table the assemblies check: `EfOperatorVerdict` gives every public operator of `Enumerable`, `Queryable`, `System.Linq.AsyncEnumerable`, `TaskAsyncEnumerableExtensions`, `EntityFrameworkQueryableExtensions` and `RelationalQueryableExtensions` a verdict (builder, terminal or refused), and `EveryPublicOperatorOfTheQueryClassesHasAReviewedVerdict` reads the operators from the assemblies, so a member a later framework version adds fails there until it is reviewed instead of being guessed at. A terminal runs the query before it returns: the eager LINQ operators (`ToList`, `ToArray`, `ToDictionary`, `ToHashSet`, `ToLookup`, `First*`, `Last*`, `Single*`, `ElementAt*`, `Count`, `LongCount`, `Any`, `All`, `Contains`, `Sum`, `Min*`, `Max*`, `Average`, `Aggregate`, `SequenceEqual`, and the `...Async` forms of `System.Linq.AsyncEnumerable`), the EF operators that run SQL (every `...Async` member of `EntityFrameworkQueryableExtensions`, `Load`, `ExecuteDelete`, `ExecuteUpdate`), `DbSet<T>.Find` and `FindAsync`, `DbContext.Find`, `ExecuteSql*`, and the framework members reviewed by exact type and name as enumerating a sequence they are given (the constructors of `List<T>`, `HashSet<T>`, `SortedSet<T>`, `Queue<T>`, `Stack<T>` and `LinkedList<T>`, `AddRange`, `InsertRange`, the set operations of the sets, `string.Join`, `string.Concat`). A builder returns a query that still runs nothing: the lazy LINQ operators (including `CountBy`, `AggregateBy`, `Index`, `LeftJoin`, `RightJoin`, `Shuffle` and the whole of the asynchronous LINQ), `ConfigureAwait` and `WithCancellation`, the EF shaping operators (`AsNoTracking`, `Include`, `ThenInclude`, `AsAsyncEnumerable`, `IgnoreQueryFilters`, ...), `FromSql*` and `AsSplitQuery`. A builder's result is a query whatever static type it has (`IOrderedEnumerable<T>`, `IIncludableQueryable<T, P>`, `ConfiguredCancelableAsyncEnumerable<T>`), and a lazy operator is no access where it wraps the query: the execution is judged where the result is consumed, at the terminal or the loop, under the frontier live there (`ABuilderOverAnEfQueryIsAQueryWhateverStaticTypeItReturns`, `ALazyOperatorOverAnEfQueryRunsNothingWhereItWrapsSoTheExecutionIsJudgedWhereTheResultIsConsumed`, `ALoopOverAWrappedAsyncQueryHoldsItsReaderAcrossTheBackEdge`, `TheOperatorsOfAnEfQueryAreTheSameAsExtensionMethods`). A query reaches a member's sequence parameter (`IEnumerable<T>`, `IQueryable<T>`, `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` and the like) only to be enumerated or built on; any other framework member handed a query is none of these, because it stores the query, defers it, takes it as an element (`List<T>.Add`, `Task.FromResult`, `Enumerable.Repeat`, `Append`, `Contains`) or hands back its enumerator (`GetEnumerator`, `AsParallel`, `ToBlockingEnumerable`, `TryGetNonEnumeratedCount`, `ToQueryString`), and the query is then refused where it is built (`AFrameworkMemberThatStoresOrDefersAnEfQueryIsRefusedWhereTheQueryIsBuilt`). Identity is exact: an operand is an EF query only when it is a read of a DbSet the framework creates (a property of EF, an authored set property of a sealed context whose body is `Set<T>()` or that nothing authored assigns, or any DbSet under `DbProviderTypesClosedByUse`), a `Set<T>()` call on a closed context, a `SqlQuery*` call, a builder over an EF query, or a local every value of which is one (a local is judged by its initializer and its plain assignments, a local written in any other way holds nothing nameable, and a local assigned from a builder over itself, the conditional-filter idiom, is a query when its other values are, without the analysis ever looping: `AQueryReassignedFromItselfIsStillAQueryAndNeverLoopsTheAnalysis`); a lookalike `DbSet` from another assembly, an in-memory list or array, an in-memory `AsQueryable` and an unfollowable value are not, and keep the judgement they had (`ALookalikeDbSetFromAnotherAssemblyIsNotAnEfQuery`, `AnInMemoryQueryableIsNotADatabaseAccessAndStaysUnreviewed`, `ANonQueryingUseOfADbSetOrAnInMemorySequenceIsNotADatabaseAccess`, `ABuilderOverAnInMemorySequenceIsNoDatabaseAccess`). Each query site raises the connection, command and query callbacks of every context its query is built from: the owner of each DbSet read or `Set<T>()` at the root of every operand of every builder and of every value of every local, so a query over two contexts raises both (`EveryContextAQueryIsBuiltFromRaisesItsCallbacks`, `AnExecutedQueryRaisesTheConnectionAndCommandCallbacksOfTheContext`). A root that is read through a holder that is no context (`ADbSetOfAHolderThatIsNoContextIsRefusedBecauseItsContextCannotBeFollowed`), a set property whose getter is anything but the context's own `Set<T>()` (`ASetPropertyWhoseGetterReadsAnotherContextIsRefused`) or a facade nobody can name is refused, and an implied `Set<T>()` inside a context is judged by that context and the authored contexts derived from it, not by every context of the program (`AnImpliedSetOfASealedContextIsJudgedByThatContextAlone`). A query is executed where it is consumed, so a query value that is consumed anywhere the analysis cannot follow to its execution is refused where it is built: a read of a DbSet, a `Set<T>()` call or a builder result must be the receiver or source of a builder, a terminal or a non-executing `DbSet` member (`Add`, `Remove`, `Update`, `Attach`, ...), the operand of a loop or spread over a provable query, a discard, or a local every use of which is such a consumption and that is never captured, passed by reference or reassigned from a non-query; the one return it allows is the context's own `DbSet X => Set<T>()` property, whose value reaches the read that consumes it. An argument to an authored method, a return, a field or property store, a collection element, a tuple, a conditional, a capture and a local reassigned from an unfollowable value are `HOSTED_SITE_UNCLASSIFIED` naming the query (`AnEfQueryValueThatEscapesWhereItIsBuiltIsRefused`). That refusal is what makes the authored-enumerables premise sound for the one framework runtime type whose enumeration is a database access: a sequence-typed parameter or return cannot be the place a query hides. The shipped code reads a DbSet only as the receiver of `Add`/`Update`, which `ADbSetPropertyThatReturnsSetOfTIsTheFrameworkIdiomNotAnEscape` and the production graph pin.

**Effect on the Shipped Graph.** The serving `CovenantConnectionEnrolmentInterceptor`, the state handler it subscribes, the connection initializer and the drain they reach are entered at the EF operations that raise them (and, for the disposal callbacks, at the disposal of a container scope), so their sites (`DbConnection.Close` and `CloseAsync`, `SqliteConnection.ClearPool`, `DbCommand.ExecuteNonQueryAsync` and `ExecuteScalarAsync`) are rows of every root that has such an operation, each under the Work and Effect frontiers live at that operation: a callback runs under the frontier of its operation and holds what that frontier holds. Those seven site keys are the only keys the lanes add to the graph. The production graph reports no diagnostic of any code, so every one of those rows carries the Work of its root, `LongRunningOperationStartupHostedService.ContinueInBackgroundAsync` and `LongRestSweepHostedService.ExecuteAsync` included, and no root reaches the 8192-state cap (`HOSTED_TRAVERSAL_STATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`). The data-retention sweep, which declares its container scope inside the block of the `await using` statement that holds its lease, disposes it under the lease: the handle it forwards to the sweep service is no escape (Interceptor and Logger Lane, Disposal). Every limit is the frozen one (`LimitsAreFrozen`). The callbacks are real code, so the roots that touch an EF operation visit states for them, the headroom under the cap of the largest roots is the figure to watch, and the Headroom Tripwire (§13.1) pins it.

`IsConfigured`, `AddInterceptors` and `UseModel` on `DbContextOptionsBuilder` and `DbContextOptionsBuilder<T>` are reviewed provider-neutral members, matched by exact assembly identity and not by name: they record state on the builder and run no code of their own, so the unconfigured fallback of a caller-created context (the stopped-host reset creates its own `ArcanumDbContext`) is judged instead of left unclassified. A same-named type from another assembly or from source, and every other builder member (`UseInternalServiceProvider`, `ReplaceService`, `UseApplicationServiceProvider`, ...), stays `HOSTED_SITE_UNCLASSIFIED`.

An authored `extern` method is an unreviewed external boundary. A call to an ordinary, body-less, non-partial, non-abstract `extern` method that is not an interface member (a `[DllImport]` or `[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.InternalCall)]` declaration included) is `HOSTED_SITE_UNCLASSIFIED` with the detail `Type.Method` at the call, unless an exact reviewed contract names it. There is no body to enter, and the call never supplies an exact value, receiver, origin or cleanup. Admitting such a call from a hosted root with no site and no diagnostic would hide a plain extern and a native `unlink` alike. Because the refusal is itself a diagnostic, a fixture that uses an `extern` as its "unknown value" can satisfy a negative assertion that accepts `HOSTED_SITE_UNCLASSIFIED` without the lane under test refusing anything. Fixtures therefore build an opaque value from a settable static property, or an authored method that returns one, and an opaque callee from an authored body that writes one; the lane then has to refuse for its own reason. An `extern` stays in a fixture only where the assertion pins the lane's own code, detail or identity, or where the extern is the subject. The refusal covers ordinary methods, the only members that can bind native code (`[DllImport]` and `[UnsafeAccessor]` attach to methods). A body-less `extern` operator, conversion or indexer is already `HOSTED_CALL_TARGET_UNRESOLVED` through its own lane, while an `extern` property accessor, constructor or event accessor binds nothing and is admitted silently with no site and no diagnostic, so none of them is an opaque-value vehicle that R97 marks. A change to this rule is audited by disabling the refusal and running the whole fixture partition: the deliberate extern tests are the only tests that may fail.

Production carries no returned proof and calls no member on a lease for attestation: the live lease travels as an ordinary by-value argument into the sealed facts reader, which forwards it to an abstract gate member that the DI alias binds to the sealed gate, so the real bound body is both the traversal target and the body whose lifetime effect is judged. The `LeaseArgumentAttestation` fixtures pin this in an ordinary hosted root: the acquired Work and each send's own group Effect hold before the attestation, in the abstract facet and its store, and after it, and a physical effect inside the bound body is found under that Work. A disposing bound body, an incomplete gate registration, a delegate escape and an opaque-object escape each end the Work. A default interface body would be walked in place of the bound override, so a disposing override behind one would not end the Work; that is why the member is abstract, and why every interface slot that takes or returns a lease or a group is: `No_interface_slot_that_takes_an_authority_handle_has_a_default_body` (Limit Pins, (10)) refuses a body on any of them, the Lease-Handoff slots included. Binding the acquired lease into a holder stores it on the heap and ends its lifetime at the `Bind`, so the by-value path is certified only without a holder.

**Lease Receiver Proof (CK-3).** A `TryBeginExternalEffectGroup` call is the Effect of a send only when its receiver is a must-alias of a work lease the traversal knows; a group on any other receiver (a ternary, a coalesce, a loop-carried previous lease or a fake lease) satisfies no site. The receiver must be an identifier (parentheses and `!` aside) of a parameter, or of a local that is never written anywhere in the member, nested lambdas and local functions included, and never mentioned in one. A variable counts as written when anything can overwrite it: an assignment (compound, coalescing and deconstructing included), an increment, and handing it out by reference, spelled or implicit (an `out`, `ref` or `in` argument, a `ref readonly` parameter, a `ref` local or return, an address), because `Unsafe.AsRef` writes through an `in` reference. Its one reaching definition must be the out designation of the guarded `TryAcquireWorkLease` call, a copy `x = admitted!` of that designation, or a formal whose binding is one acquisition location with no inexact marker and which is never written anywhere in its declaring method, nested callables included; the formal may be the member's own or that of the method a lambda or local function of the member is nested in, because a formal that is never written holds the bound value however a closure captures it (a detached body is traversed with its admission detached and so has no binding). A binding is made at `BindArguments`: an argument that is not itself such an identifier keeps its may-alias origins and gains the single marker origin `<inexact-lease-alias>`, which is never an acquisition location, so every membership test over an origin set sees no new acquisition while the formal can never satisfy the proof; the marker is part of the state identity and survives every further hop, so a lease passed through any number of formals stays exact only while every hop is. The binding of a formal is read from the state's own map every time; only facts that are a pure function of the syntax (whether anything in a symbol's scope writes it, which acquisition defines a local) are memoised, per symbol and scope, so no proof is reused by a different binding state. The admission binding identity that keys the may-alias caches labels a parameter or local by its declaration, never by its ordinal or name alone: a lambda sees the formals of the method that declares it as well as its own, and two binding maps that label their formals `parameter:0` and `parameter:1` are not the same map when one binds the formal a body reads and the other binds nothing it reads. A pre-declared local filled by `out`, a join, a conditional, a coalesce, a switch, an opaque return, a holder property read, a lease supplied by a delegate, a loop-carried value, a null-forgiven value, a captured or reassigned local and a reassigned formal have no such definition and are refused. The proof runs at the three places a group is recognised: `FindRetainedAdmission` and its manual-ownership twin (a refused group is retained by nothing), `AddSite` (a group is the Effect of its own site only when the receiver is also the lease whose Work the state holds; a state that holds none, because the lease was disposed, handed away or bound into a holder before the group, judges the group by its receiver alone, as the Lease Spine does for a paid door whose lease departed, since the group stands and every send under it reports its own missing Work through `HOSTED_SITE_WORK_FRONTIER_MISSING`; the one thing such a group may not do is meet a Work the same member starts afterwards, so a later `TryAcquireWorkLease` in the member refuses it, because a send under both would pair the Effect of one lease with the Work of another, and a Work started in another frame is not judged against it here), and `RecoveryEffectFrontierAt` (the shell's group must be begun on a lease the shell itself acquired and on the lease its Work belongs to, so a group on a second acquisition mints no recovery effect). A refusal is `HOSTED_ADMISSION_RECEIVER_MISMATCH` at the group's coordinate and completes nothing. A group whose receiver is not a must-alias is retained by nothing, so the send behind it reports `HOSTED_SITE_EFFECT_FRONTIER_MISSING`; a group on a sound lease that is merely not the one holding the Work (a second acquisition) is still found by the send's own scan, so the send keeps that group's identity without a capsule and the mismatch at the group is the refusal; and each external-effect recovery tuple that would have inherited the shell's group reports `HOSTED_RECOVERY_EFFECT_FRONTIER_UNPROVEN`. A directly called local function is traversed without the enclosing method's admission bindings, so a local function that begins a group must take the lease as an argument rather than capture it: the attachment processor's batch flush does, and the retention prune core's optional lease is the one reviewed null case below. The rule only removes authority: lifetimes, escapes and the other refusals still read the may-alias sets. No member is exempt from the rule: whatever context a member carries, a group whose receiver is not such a must-alias grants no Effect, and a group begun on a holder's lease is refused here like any other. That includes a recovery handler, which is dispatched from a shell that holds the Work and the recovery effect and has no lease of its own: a group it begins on a fake lease, a forgiven `null` or a holder's lease is refused at its coordinate and is no Effect of the handler's send, which keeps the shell's group and nothing else (`LeaseReceiverProofRefusesAGroupBegunInsideARecoveryHandlerOnALeaseThatIsNotTheShells`). The `LeaseReceiverProofGrantsTheGroupsEffectToAMustAliasOfTheAcquiredLease` and `LeaseReceiverProofRefusesAGroupWhoseReceiverIsNotAMustAliasOfTheAcquiredLease` theories pin it: a group on the out designation, on `lease = admitted!`, on `using var lease = admitted`, on a formal reached through two hops, on a formal a lambda captures, on a lease passed through a local delegate and on the worker's lease while a second, unused acquisition exists keep both frontiers; a fake lease built in place, a ternary with a fake lease, `?? fake`, a loop-carried previous lease, a reassigned local, `null!`, an opaque return (with and without the lease as its argument), a holder property read, a delegate-received lease, a delegate-supplied lease, a second acquisition, an inexact first hop, a reassigned formal, a captured outer formal that is written, a reassigned, captured or unguarded designation, a captured copy and a local written in a lambda each give exactly one mismatch at the group's coordinate and no Effect on the group or the send (the downstream send reports its missing frontier, and an opaque return handed the lease itself also loses the Work, as the checker already ends it at that escape); and the production text of `SettleAdmittedAsync` spliced into the recovery matrix, with the external-effect tuples of the BlobEncryption, Backup, DataRetention and A2A kinds, keeps the shell's group as every handler's Effect, while the same shell with its group on a second acquisition leaves every handler without one; a shell that is handed an exactly bound lease, whose Work is that very lease, is refused by the own-acquisition rule alone. `LeaseReceiverProofNeverReusesTheProofOfAnotherBindingState` pins that one lambda reached by two callers (one binds the declaring method's formal to the acquired lease, the other reaches it through a local function whose formals carry the same ordinals and origins) is judged per state, `LeaseReceiverProofCountsAByReferenceUseOfTheReceiverAsAWrite` pins that an `in` or `ref readonly` hand-out of the designation, of a first-hop copy or of a formal refuses the receiver, and `LeaseReceiverProofJudgesAGroupBegunWithoutWorkByItsReceiverAndKeepsItFromALaterWork` pins the no-Work rule above: a group on a departed lease stands and its send reports the missing Work, a fake receiver is refused, and a group that meets a Work the member starts afterwards is refused. An optional lease (the retention prune core, which is reached once with no lease on the recovery path and begins its group only under `workLease is not null`) is handled by the recovery value evaluator: a lease-typed value that the traversal knows to be the null constant matches an `is null` pattern, so the guarded branch is dead in the traversal that passes `null` and its group is neither an Effect nor a refusal, while an unguarded call on the null-bound formal and a guarded call on a lease that is not the null constant keep the full proof (`LeaseReceiverProofPrunesADeadGroupOnlyForAGuardedNullLease`). "Known" is only as sound as the evaluator, which knows a local as its initializer and the plain assignments before the use, and that is the local's value only when nothing else can write it. A local handed out by reference (`out`, `ref`, `in`, a `ref` local, an address, `Interlocked`), written by a compound or coalescing assignment, a deconstruction or an increment, written in a local function (which may run before it is declared), or written after the use by a loop or a jump that carries the write back is unknown to the evaluator for every decision it makes (`is null`, `is not null`, `is { }`, a switch arm, a condition), so the guarded region is traversed and its sends are reported. `LeaseReceiverProofPrunesTheRegionOfAProvablyNullLease` and `LeaseReceiverProofKeepsTheRegionOfALeaseThatIsNotProvablyNull` pin both sides for `is not null` and `is { }`: a literal `null`, a never-written local and `default` prune the region, and an `out` fill, a `ref` local, `??=`, a deconstruction, `Interlocked.Exchange`, a loop-carried write, a `goto`-carried write and a write in a later-declared local function keep it, each reporting the raw send with the group's refusal.

**Single Gate Census.** A Work origin is an acquisition on the reviewed admission gate, and the inventory grants one only while the analysed source declares no implementation of the gate contract beside it. The analysis follows every acquisition as a call through the contract's `TryAcquireWorkLease` slot, which reaches whichever implementation its receiver holds, so a second gate in the analysed source (a class, a record or a struct, nested or not, implementing the contract directly, through a base class or through an interface that extends it) is a gate that can mint a lease the real gate never admitted, and a lease it mints is the proof of admission every later send relies on. The census is a property of the analysed compilations alone, computed once per discovery and shared by every root worker (`InventoryFacts.UnreviewedGateImplementations`). It lists every concrete type that implements the contract and is not `RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Infrastructure.Data.GrimoireConnectionAdmissionGate`, matched on its exact type key so a lookalike in another namespace, or a subclass of the reviewed gate, is a finding, and it lists the reviewed gate again when two analysed assemblies declare it. An abstract implementer is no finding of its own, since every instance is of a concrete subtype, which is. While the census has a finding, every acquisition through the slot is refused with `HOSTED_ADMISSION_GATE_UNREVIEWED`, which names the acquisition and the gates that make it untrustworthy; the acquisition is no site, the retained-admission scan and the must-alias origin scan skip it, and so no Work is granted and a group begun on the lease it returned is no Effect. A call whose receiver has the second gate's own static type is not a call of the reviewed slot at all: the slot maps to the contract only for the reviewed gate, so it is an authored method like any other and returns no Work. Fixtures that need a gate declare their stub as `RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Infrastructure.Data.GrimoireConnectionAdmissionGate` and nothing else; a fixture that declares a second gate beside it is asserting the refusal. `SingleGateCensusTests` (Build) holds the other half in the production source and runs each pin on a synthetic source built to break it: the reviewed gate is the one implementation of the contract, sealed and declared in the one reviewed file; the container registers exactly the reviewed gate (by a factory that creates it, and nothing else constructs it) and the contract (by a factory that resolves the reviewed gate); and `IGrimoireWorkLease` and `IGrimoireExternalEffectGroup` are implemented only by types nested in the reviewed gate, so a lease that exists was minted by it. The pins are semantic: types, registrations and constructions are found by symbol, never by text.

**Departed-Lease Group.** A send holds a Work and an Effect, and the pair is one lease's: the Effect is the group begun on the lease whose Work is live. Inside one member the Lease Receiver Proof refuses a group that meets a Work the member starts afterwards. Across frames the Effect carries the origin of the lease its group was begun on (the acquisition location, or the root lease formal of a handoff root, which is the origin the receiver proof resolves), appended to the group's location after an `@lease:` marker, so a group begun on a lease that has since been disposed, stored or handed to a callee, while no Work was held, cannot stay open into a callee that acquires its own lease and sends under that lease's Work, which would grant the send a Work and an Effect of two different leases. The group's own site, a later send in the same member, the shell's recovery effect and an inherited Effect all spell the same string. A send whose Effect's lease origin is not the origin of the Work live at the send loses the Effect, with `HOSTED_ADMISSION_EFFECT_LEASE_MISMATCH` and the `HOSTED_SITE_EFFECT_FRONTIER_MISSING` that follows. The granted shapes are: a send in the frame that began the group, a callee that takes the lease as a formal bound to the acquisition and sends, a callee that begins its own group on that formal, and a handoff root whose formal is both the Work's origin and the group's receiver.

**Lookups into unread trees fail closed.** The analysis reads the trees under `src/` that are not generated; a declaration in any other tree (generated code under `obj/`, a tree outside `src/`) has no semantic model in the traversal. A symbol the analysis follows can still be declared there, such as a delegate-typed field a generator emits, and every lookup of an analysed tree's model goes through one accessor that refuses instead of throwing: it refuses the traversal's completion and reports `HOSTED_TREE_UNANALYSED` naming the declaration, and its caller takes the value it takes when it cannot prove the declaration (unresolved target, unproven source, no closed callable, a callable that is not proven absent, an unknown value flow). A callable declared in an unread tree is never proven absent, with or without an initializer, because that tree can assign it in code nothing here sees. Nothing indexes the dictionary of models directly, which `Every_lookup_of_an_analysed_trees_model_refuses_instead_of_throwing` pins in the checker's own source with a twin that finds an indexer in synthetic text.

A readonly field initializer carries the analyzed semantic model of its own syntax tree, including when an implicit constructor is created from another analyzed compilation. The value context retains the constructor's bound arguments and construction environment. An unavailable initializer model reports `HOSTED_TREE_UNANALYSED`, refuses traversal completion, and removes the unproven field binding. Cross-compilation cleanup fixtures keep an effectful positive and a quiet negative control.

Compiler-generated record equality has a separate source contract. It accepts only exact source-owned nongeneric record structs or sealed record classes, compiler-selected generated equality slots, and a complete instance-backing-field closure over the reviewed framework bool/int/string leaves or supported nested records. An authored typed `Equals` body remains an execution target. Formal arguments used by generated equality retain their original value sources; current-receiver scalar property evaluation consumes only exact typed literal construction bindings. Construction and initialization lifetime checks still decide whether inherited work and effect authority survives.

Execution discovery does not certify a conversion. When the original operand uses a compiler-selected authored conversion, its single immediate constructor return may identify the actual record receiver under the same bounded source proof. Its failed conversion certificate remains failed: the generated operator keeps its own refusal, and the discovered equality body receives no inherited work, effect, or recovery authority. Missing, generic, opaque, or incomplete source does not become a closed equality certificate. The initializer, repeated-call and converted-receiver controls require actual physical effects to remain visible rather than accepting a refusal in place of traversal.

**Admission origins follow handles, not data.** The origin walk that decides which locals and formals can carry a lease or an external-effect group is a may-alias walk: a value computed from an expression that mentions the lease counts as derived from it, and a disposable built from such a value counts as a possible carrier, so a call on it is a retained handle passed to an opaque callee and an exact disposal or hand-off of it ends the lease's lifetime. That is right for an object that could hold the handle and wrong for one that cannot. A reference to a local or parameter whose static type is a **Handle-Incapable Value** contributes no origin, however the value was produced. A type is closed pure data when no instance of it, whatever its runtime type, can hold or reach a reference to anything but more closed pure data: an exact CoreLib scalar, `string`, enumeration, `Guid` or other reviewed value leaf (the leaves of Closed-Value Equality); a one-dimensional array, `Nullable<>`, `ValueTuple` or `ImmutableArray<>` of closed pure data; or a struct or sealed class declared in analysed source whose base is exactly `object` or `ValueType`, that implements neither `IDisposable` nor `IAsyncDisposable`, declares no instance event (the delegate behind an event, field-like or with explicit accessors, is state that a scan of the type's fields does not list, and a subscriber can be a closure over the group), and whose every instance field, backing fields of properties included, is closed pure data (a constructed generic is judged on its substituted fields). An interface, `object`, `dynamic`, delegate, type parameter, pointer, ref struct, unsealed class, type with an authored base, type declared outside analysed source (its non-public fields are not visible, so they are not reviewed), authored lookalike of a framework type (judged by its own fields, never by its name) or type that reaches itself is not closed, and keeps every origin and refusal it had. The verdict is cached per type, a verdict reached after the work budget ran out is not kept, and the lease, the group and every disposable stay tracked. This is why the Long Rest stores, which build a command from the parameters of an accepted paid result, do not count every call on that command as an escape of the lease their caller passed to the paid door (`ADataValueOfClosedPureDataKeepsTheWorkAndEscapesNothing` and its twins `ADataValueThatCouldHoldAHandleKeepsItsOriginAndTheRefusalItHad`, with the end-to-end twin `AValueThatCarriesTheHeldGroupInAnEventStillEscapesAndStillCostsTheSendAfterItItsEffect` for a value whose event subscriber holds the group). It also makes the telemetry pair shapes uniform: a string derived from the lease is never an escape in any pair shape (alias, unknown `object` formal bound to it, authored lookalike pair, outer user conversion), while the held group as the payload still is in every one of them, and a carrier that stored the group in a static keeps costing the send after it its Effect (`ExactFrameworkPairPayloadRefinementRetainsUnprovedPayloadEscapes`, `ExactNamedAuthoredPairCannotUseFrameworkPayloadRefinement`, `ExactPairOuterUserConversionCannotEraseDisposableHandleCarrier`). What the rule leans on is the carrier model's treatment of a store. A handle written to storage that the origin walk cannot follow leaves the tracked environment at the store and ends the admission there, so every send after it loses its Work and its Effect (`AHandleWrittenToStorageEndsTheAdmissionAtTheStoreSoTheSendAfterItLosesItsEffect`). Static storage is process-wide ambient state and never a supported home for a lease or an external-effect group, so a store of a handle into it is also refused where it happens, as a `HOSTED_ADMISSION_HANDLE_ESCAPE` on the assignment: a static field or property, an element or indexer reached from one, a member of an object reached from one, a coalescing or compound assignment and an element of a deconstruction all count (`AHandleWrittenToStaticStorageIsRefusedAtTheStore`), while a local copy, a closed value derived from the lease and a disposable unrelated to the lease are not stores of a handle (`ADataValueALocalCopyOrAnUnrelatedDisposableIsNotARefusedStore`). Without that refusal, a closed key, index or conversion could read a stashed group back past a rule that rightly gives closed data no origin. Instance storage is where a holder would keep a lease, and the Lease Spine pins a lease stored in a field as ending the Work at the send, so a store into a field of `this` or of another object is not refused by itself. The Ambient Holder Refusal drops the Work of a member that reads a lease back out of an instance property or field of authored source whose declared type is exactly `IGrimoireWorkLease`, through a member access or a conditional access, under an ordinary hosted root and in a recovery handler as in any other member.
