It does not read a lease that comes out of an object some other way (a simple name inside the holder, a property pattern, a method's return, a slot of a class that implements the interface, a lambda body): the Lease Receiver Proof refuses any group begun on the value such a read produces, so the discovery is refused at the group whichever spelling reads it. The Authority Carrier Ban refuses the storage itself in production. That the store alone is not refused is a known limit, pinned so that it cannot drift (`AHandleWrittenToInstanceStorageIsNotItselfRefusedWhenNoSendNeedsTheAdmissionAfterIt`).

The Long Rest worker's wait is one awaited read of the bounded hint channel on a token cancelled by a `TimeProvider`-backed source. The inventory proves with no site and no diagnostic that every awaitable the wait starts is awaited where it starts, so no timer-backed or channel task outlives the call; a read kept pending across wakes, raced against `Task.Delay`, or started without being awaited leaves such a task alive after its caller and stays refused (`ParkedRescanWakeAsOneAwaitedReadOnATimerCancelledTokenIsProvenWithNoSites`, `AWaitThatLeavesATimerOrChannelTaskAliveAfterItsCallerStaysRefused`). The inventory places no disposal obligation on a `CancellationTokenSource`, whose constructor and `CreateLinkedTokenSource` are allow-listed, so it does not prove that the wake disposes its two sources. That the worker disposes both the timer-backed source and the source linked over the stopping token on every wake, so the host-lifetime stopping token keeps no registration per wake, is pinned from the production syntax (`TheLongRestWakeDisposesBothOfItsCancellationSourcesBeforeItReturns`, with `ThePinOnTheWakeSourcesSeesAnUndisposedSource` showing that the pin refuses an undisposed source) and, for the timer, by the armed-timer counts of the Parked Rescan behaviour tests. The production lane pins the whole worker root separately from its remaining residue (the unclassified Long Rest histogram, owned elsewhere): no `HOSTED_ADMISSION_HANDLE_ESCAPE`, missing Work or Effect frontier, unowned callback or unresolved disposal is reported under `LongRestSweepHostedService.ExecuteAsync` or under the admitted maintenance's Lease-Handoff Root below, every database access below the accept callbacks carries the Work of its root, and both paid sends carry the root's lease-formal Work, which one binding row ties to the worker's kind-17 acquisition, and the group begun on the lease parameter (`TheLongRestHostedRootOwnsItsWaitItsLeaseAndItsPaidSendsWithNoEscapeOrMissingFrontier`).

**Lease-Handoff Root.** The Long Rest closure below the admitted maintenance is judged once, as its own root, instead of once more under every caller's state budget. The catalog declares `LongRestMaintenance.ProcessAdmittedAsync` in the worker's service as an ordinary hosted root of work kind `LongRestSweep` with `leaseFormal: "admission"`: the named by-value `IGrimoireWorkLease` parameter is the root's admission origin, the **Root Lease Formal**, so the escape, lifetime and receiver rules apply to it exactly as they apply to an acquisition, and the root starts with no Effect and with the Work that origin mints. That Work has its own capsule. The root's first row is an `EffectFrontier` row whose callee is `IGrimoireWorkLease.RootLeaseFormal`, which names the root's work kind and is the frontier every Work capsule of the root's operation resolves to; the manifest parser accepts it wherever it accepts a `TryAcquireWorkLease` row, and `Validate` accepts it only in an operation whose catalog entry declares a lease formal (`HOSTED_SITE_LEASE_FORMAL_UNDECLARED`). A caller re-roots instead of traversing the callee in line when the call resolves to exactly that method and all of these hold: the caller is an ordinary root of the same service and the same work kind; the caller's Work at the call is the Work of the lease argument, which is a must-alias of one acquisition (the Must-Alias Lease Demand); the call is `await call` or `await call.ConfigureAwait(constant)` directly in the caller's own method body, not in a lambda or local function (a `ConfigureAwait` argument is evaluated after the root has started and before the await, so it would run while the root does and could end the lease there; only a compile-time constant evaluates nothing); no external-effect group and no recovery effect is open at the call; nothing in the argument evaluation has ended the lease (`AdmissionEndedBefore` at the call's end, which with a constant `ConfigureAwait` argument is also the end of the await); no other argument and not the receiver may hold the lease, because the canonical root binds its formal alone and a second alias of the lease (a second lease parameter given it, a holder built from it, a receiver constructed from it) would reach the root unbound, outside every escape and lifetime rule the cut grants Work under (an argument of closed pure data or a cancellation token holds none, however it was computed from the lease); no closure of the caller mentions the lease; and a call that can run again (in a loop, or behind a backward jump) is cut only if the root preserves its formal, since a root that disposes it would be handed the same ended lease on the next pass. The traversal then continues under the root's operation id with the root's canonical member (the declared root's factory context with the formal bound to its own origin), the canonical Work and no Effect. That is the very state the declared root's own traversal starts from, so within one worker the state cache admits the closure once, whichever of the two reaches it first, under the root's own 8,192-state budget. The analysis pool takes whole families, and a service that declares a handoff root is one family (`HostedProducerRootWorkers.FamilyOf`): the roots that cut to the handoff root and the handoff root itself always run on the one worker whose cache they share, so the closure is admitted once for the whole run whatever the pool size (a guard refuses a plan that splits them). Within the family the caller's root precedes the handoff root, so the closure's elapsed time is charged to the caller that reaches it first and the handoff root's own entry shows almost none, while its states are always counted under the handoff root's operation. The closure's rows carry the formal's capsule, and the caller gets one `LeaseHandoff` row for each proven call site, in the caller's operation, whose callee is the root's operation id and whose Work capsule is the caller's acquisition. The manifest ties the formal to each acquisition through those rows, and its parser refuses a formal that no binding row names, a binding row whose root has no formal, and a binding whose Work frontier admits another work kind than the formal (`HOSTED_MANIFEST_HANDOFF_UNBOUND`). A handoff root may hand its own lease on to another handoff root declared in its closure, which is how a further handoff point is added if the budget is ever pressed again: the inner call is cut under the same conditions with the outer root's Work, and its binding row carries the outer root's formal in place of an acquisition. Any other call to the root, from a root that fails one of the conditions, is `HOSTED_LEASE_HANDOFF_UNPROVEN` with the failing condition, and is traversed in line under the caller's budget exactly as before. Two further rules close the edge. **Formal Preservation:** the caller's lease lifetime continues after a call to the root only if the root proves that its formal is never disposed, returned or stored, never handed to a callee the lifetime walk cannot follow, and never captured by a closure anywhere in its closure; the lifetime walk consults that proof at every call to the root, so a root that captures the formal in a closure or a spawned task, which the walk alone does not see, ends the caller's Work at the call and the caller's later reads report `HOSTED_SITE_WORK_FRONTIER_MISSING`, while a root that disposes or stores it ends the Work as the walk always did. The proof only ever removes authority. The caller side of the same rule is the closure check above: a closure of the caller that mentions the lease can end it at a time no position names, so the cut is refused; a capture in an ancestor of the caller is not judged at this edge and rests on the Authority Carrier Ban (§21.16.4), which refuses a closure over a work lease wherever it is. A declared root that no analysed call binds is reported at discovery (`HOSTED_LEASE_HANDOFF_ROOT_UNBOUND`), not only when the manifest is parsed, and `Validate` accepts a binding row only toward a declared handoff operation of the caller's own service (`HOSTED_SITE_LEASE_HANDOFF_UNDECLARED`). The **Handoff Caller Census:** every syntactic reference to the root's method in analysed production source (the method, an interface slot it implements, a method it overrides) must be an invocation that some traversal proved as a cut edge; a method group, a delegate, a refused call, and a call that no root reaches are each `HOSTED_LEASE_HANDOFF_CALLER_UNANALYSED`, whatever reaches them at run time. The Session shell enters the same coordinator core as the hosted worker through request-path code that no root traverses, so the census cannot judge it. It is accepted only because it funnels into the one call site the worker proves, and because the work kind it carries is the root's: the shell mints its own kind-17 lease, and the port and the maintenance each throw on a lease whose kind is not `LongRestSweep` before they use it, which the inventory does not prove and `ActualLongRestSpineCarriesOneLeaseByValueFromMintToExternalEffectGroup` pins from the production syntax. `TheLongRestHandoffChainHasExactlyItsReviewedEntries` pins the exact callers of that chain: the maintenance method is called only from the owned run, the owned run only from the shared core, the shared core only from the hosted port and the shell, the port only from the worker, and the shell only from the Session turn preparer. Each link is matched on the method's identity, never on the type a caller happens to name: the method, the interface slots it implements, the methods that implement a slot, the methods those override or are overridden by, and the method groups that name any of them (`HandoffChainReferences`, which the admitted entry census reuses), so a caller of the registered class instead of its port is a caller of the link (`TheChainPinSeesACallerThatNamesTheConcreteTypeInsteadOfTheInterfaceSlot`, `TheChainMatcherFollowsTheSlotItsImplementationItsOverridesAndTheMethodGroupsAndNothingElse`). The projects the inventory does not analyse are scoped out of the pin, and the scope-out holds only while none of them names a link: `NoProjectOutsideTheAnalysedCompilationsNamesAnyLinkOfTheHandoffChain` scans the development host, the clients and the benchmark and smoke harnesses for the chain's identifiers (the unit-test projects, which exercise the chain, are the only ones excluded). `TheChainPinSeesAnotherCallerAnAddedCallAndAReferenceThatIsNotACall` shows that the pin refuses a second caller, an added call and a method-group reference, so a new entry into the chain must be reviewed together with the root it feeds. The budgets are untouched: the worker's root falls from about 13,200 states to about 3,700, and the maintenance root costs about 5,400, each under 8,192 and under the 6,144 a new root is held to. The fixtures pin both sides. `ALeaseCarriedAwaitedCallCutsToTheRootWhoseSendsCarryTheFormalCapsuleAndWhoseBindingNamesTheAcquisition` pins the cut (the root's send carries the formal capsule and the group begun on it, the binding row carries the acquisition, and the caller's root holds none of the closure's sites), `ACutCallLeavesTheCallersLeaseAliveForItsLaterSendsWhenTheRootPreservesTheFormal` pins that the caller keeps its Work when the formal is preserved, and `ACallThatFailsAnyPreconditionIsRefusedAndTheClosureIsJudgedInLineUnderTheCallersRoot` pins each refusal with its reason: an argument that is not a must-alias, an open group, a lease disposed before the call or during the argument evaluation, a call that is not awaited or whose task is stored, another work kind, a call inside a lambda, a second acquisition, an omitted lease argument, an await configured with a non-constant argument, a second alias of the lease (another parameter, a holder built in the argument or in a local, a receiver built from it), a call in a loop or behind a backward jump when the root disposes its formal, and a caller closure that mentions the lease (a closure made after the call, or one made before it that only reads the lease, reaches that precondition; a closure made before the call that disposes the lease ends it there, so the lifetime scan refuses the cut for want of live Work first; `ASecondAliasOfTheLeaseThatTheRootKeepsStillCostsTheRootsSendItsWorkExactlyAsTheInLineTraversalDid` pins that the refusal reproduces the escape the in-line traversal reported, and `ACallInALoopOrBesideAnUnrelatedClosureIsStillCut` pins the controls; `ACallFromARootOfAnotherServiceIsRefusedWhateverItsWorkKindAndTheRootIsJudgedInLineThere` pins the service condition). Two preconditions have no handoff fixture: a caller that carries a recovery context (only the recovery dispatch produces one, and its own fixtures exercise it) and a caller with an open recovery effect (it needs the exact settle shape of the reconciler). No root of a handoff service reaches either, and both only remove authority. A formal passed by reference is refused as a declaration, so the call-site by-value check is not reachable with one (`AHandoffFormalPassedByReferenceIsAnUnresolvedRootAndItsCallIsUnproven`). `AHandoffRootThatHandsItsOwnLeaseOnIsCutFromItsClosureAndBoundToItsOwnFormal` pins the nested root and its manifest ties, `AFormalTheRootDisposesStoresOrCapturesEndsTheCallersLifetimeAtTheCall` pins Formal Preservation for a disposed, stored, closure-captured and task-spawned formal, `AReferenceToTheRootThatNoRootProvedIsAnUnanalysedCallerWhateverReachesItAtRunTime` and `ACallThroughADelegateIsNotACutEdgeAndItsReferenceIsAnUnanalysedCaller` pin the census, `EveryProvenCallSiteOfTheRootGetsItsOwnBindingRow` pins one binding row for each call site, `TheRootsClosureIsTraversedOnceWhetherTheCallerOrTheDeclaredRootReachesItFirst` pins that the cut reaches exactly the declared root's states, that the caller's states and the root's states together are exactly the states the in-line traversal visits, and that the caller's root falls by the root's own count less the one state both roots visit under different Work (the lease's `MaintenanceRevocation` getter, read by the coordinator under the worker's Work and by the maintenance under the root's formal: two Work frontiers are two states, where the in-line traversal visits the one they share), `TheRootsOfAServiceThatDeclaresAHandoffRootRunOnOneWorkerSoThePoolAdmitsTheClosureOnce` and `ARootsFamilyIsItsOwnUnlessItsServiceDeclaresALeaseHandoffRoot` pin that two callers and the root run on one worker for every pool size and family order, with the same sites, diagnostics and closure states as a single worker, `TheManifestOfACutEdgeIsRefusedWithoutItsBindingOrItsFormalOrWithAnotherWorkKind` pins the manifest ties, and `AHandoffDeclarationWhoseFormalIsMissingOrNotALeaseIsAnUnresolvedRoot` pins that a declaration whose formal does not bind once to a by-value lease parameter is `HOSTED_ROOT_UNRESOLVED`.

The Serve/Long Rest fixture additionally checks a finite **conditional source-association** contract: the canonical public Serve callback forwards to its authored host body; that body composes one builder and builds and awaits the same application; the reset-aware registration and awaited worker scope route retain their canonical source shapes. A separate direct-consumer overlay checks Build → application Services → scope → scoped factory and deliberately makes no Start claim. Opaque, replaced, conditional, escaped or custom-provider relationships remain unproven within this grammar. These test-local checks do not establish DI winner selection or runtime activation, do not confer analyzer authority, and do not relax the inventory, admission or effect gates. Catalogued worker roots establish analysis coverage only. Existing shipping, Native AOT and live qualification gates separately establish the actual host behavior for the exact candidate. Configured HTTP factory hooks are not consumed by the scope-owned Long Rest transport; historical factory probes explicitly invoke their supplied factory and retain separate opaque-dispatch refusals or authored effect-frontier obligations.

Framework collection interface indexers require complete receiver value provenance in the exact bound environment. The inventory follows authored returns, asynchronous completion, conditionals, constructor-bound readonly storage, and exact record/init payload construction through the shared value-flow engine. Reviewed terminals are exact framework arrays, direct collection construction, supported collection expressions, and exact framework materializers; `ReadOnlyCollection<T>` additionally requires proven backing. Production code that receives a broad collection contract snapshots it into, or preserves it as, an exact `List<T>` or array before indexing when the original receiver cannot be proven closed. A declared `List<T>` return type alone is insufficient because an authored subclass can reimplement an interface indexer. Reassigned parameters or locals, unclosed mutable storage, ref/out or deconstruction replacement, unresolved record `with` values, unknown factories, cycles, and exhausted proof budgets remain unclassified. Local reassignment is rejected regardless of source order, including writes inside callbacks and local functions, because loop back-edges can carry a lexically later replacement into the next indexer use. Item projection additionally requires closed collection contents and rejects aliases or mutation escapes. Indexer proof caches are isolated from cleanup proof caches. The virtual `Exception.Data` getter has no blanket exemption.

A delegate seam is proven never invoked in production only when no authored write anywhere can set it. The traversal skips a delegate invocation whose receiver is a private or internal nullable delegate field, property or event with no initializer and no authored write, or a closed callable with no target. Authored writes are found in every production syntax tree, not only in member bodies: a field or property initializer can set a seam through an object initializer or a `with` expression, and a deconstruction writes each element of its tuple target. A property counts as unassigned only when assignments to it are the only writes that can change what it returns: an auto-property, or a getter that is exactly the `Value` of a private readonly framework `AsyncLocal<T>` field of the declaring type that nothing outside the property's own accessors names. Abstract, virtual, override, extern and partial properties, and any other accessor body, keep the call unproven. A reset is a write too: a production `ResetTestSeams` that assigns a seam `null` leaves invoking it unproven, so a test seam that hosted work reaches is a flow-local property over such an `AsyncLocal<T>` that only its tests set and nothing resets, as `WorkspacePathPolicy.LinkTargetReaderForTests` is (`HostedGrimoireProducerInventoryTests.AFlowLocalTestSeamIsProvenAbsentOnlyWhileProductionNeverAssignsIt`). A positional property of a sealed record class is set only by its primary constructor, an initializer or a `with` expression, so it holds exactly the primary-constructor argument of each authored construction: its value is resolved through that constructor parameter like any other constructor-bound callable, and the traversal enters the bound target instead of skipping the call. An initializer or `with` write, a record struct (whose default value runs no constructor), an unsealed record (which a derived record constructs through its own base clause) and an argument the analysis cannot close leave the value unknown, so invoking it is an unproven callback.

Cleanup provenance shares that proof. A delegate invocation whose receiver the traversal proves absent produces no cleanup value, because production never takes it, so a factory that returns a test seam's stream when the seam is set and an exact construction otherwise keeps the construction's exact cleanup provenance; a seam production can write keeps its stream's cleanup unproven. `FileSystemAclExtensions.Create(FileInfo, FileMode, FileSystemRights, FileShare, int, FileOptions, FileSecurity)` is an exact trusted cleanup factory beside `File.OpenRead`, matched on that signature and the framework assembly identity, because it returns a new `FileStream` its caller owns; a same-named method from another assembly is not trusted.

Closed-period ledger cleanup preserves the original cancellation or lease-loss exception even when physical-close reporting or exact-pool clearing refuses. It rethrows that same exception with its original dispatch information without reading or modifying the virtual `Exception.Data` property; a user-defined getter cannot replace the control-flow exception. Secondary cleanup errors are no longer attached to cancellation/lease-loss exception metadata. Cleanup attempts, tracked-handle disposal, and the existing gate-closure behavior remain unchanged.

Automatic retention is the durable producer that may keep one operation across those generations. Its process-local ownership token prevents generic recovery from adopting the expired row while the scheduler is deliberately parked, and its private same-owner lease refresh cannot be reached through `ILongRunningOperationStore`. The retained continuation is captured before scope disposal, so Stop or disposal failure can release that exact claim even when no reopened database scope may safely be created. The pending candidate journal distinguishes a frontier refusal, where no effect began and the same owner may resume without another attempt, from a winning frontier whose cancellation or failure must retain normal reconciliation semantics.

**Acquisition and physical-drain boundary.** The gate, `CovenantConnectionEnrolmentInterceptor`, and `ICovenantConnectionDrain` are singleton-composed for every serving `ArcanumDbContext` options path. The interceptor remains the sole serving EF admission route. Every serving raw live-Grimoire acquisition uses `GrimoireOrdinaryConnectionFactory`; it acquires a generation-bound open ticket before native work, revalidates after open, enrolls the physical handle, and retains that enrolment until the owning connection or lease is physically closed. `CovenantConnectionSource` accepts only the exact `Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.SqliteConnection` runtime type from either EF or an ordinary lease and rejects provider subclasses before retaining or returning them, so virtual command, reader, transaction, and cleanup dispatch cannot escape the closed application inventory. The closed-period ledger performs the same exact-type check before it inspects or changes connection state, and both schema-repair entry paths reassert it before a connection can be captured by the post-disposition journal finalizer. A refused or post-open race-losing ordinary connection is closed and its exact provider pool is cleared before its ticket becomes terminal.

Closing records deferred revocation on every work lease whose effect group has already won. Releasing that group delivers cancellation outside the gate monitor, even when the work scope was released first or a proven stage-one abort has reopened admission. Callback failures cannot prevent terminal drain completion. A surviving old lease remains in the next closure's census and cannot start another effect. An unpromoted request surviving an earlier aborted generation cannot be promoted in the reopened generation: refusal leaves Ordinary admission, authority, and census membership unchanged, so a later requestless close still drains that old request through disposal. Both stage-two closure and proven abort calculate a checked generation before mutating authority or phase; exhaustion leaves the exact closing owner in place and does not signal reopen.

**Which workers observe a maintenance revocation, and what that means for Apprentice.** Revocation is a boundary signal rather than preemption: a group that has not begun refuses, while a group that already won finishes and receives revocation only when it releases; the gate delivers that cancellation outside its monitor. The gate checks it before admitting a later effect group. `GrimoireStreamQuiescence` supplies it to a `QuiesceableStream` producer, which honours it between frames (§10.7). Long Rest's hosted sweep links it into its pending-work read, and the admitted maintenance path links it across a unit; each paid provider dispatch is protected by its own external-effect group, so maintenance lets a paid call and its acceptance finish before cancellation arrives. Attachment indexing opens the same kind of group around a PDF worker process, begun only once the document's bytes have been read, and links the revocation to that worker, so maintenance waits for a running worker, up to its wall clock, instead of killing it, and a document reached once maintenance is pending, including maintenance that arrived while its bytes were being read, starts no worker, because the group it would need is refused (§21.8). Startup recovery links no revocation: the Long Rest recovery handler is a Pure Park Handler that acquires no lease (§10.8.2), and every recovery kind keeps its own token. The Apprentice runtime still does not link revocation into its provider/tool token: an effect group spans a whole provider call and the tool calls that follow it, so an in-flight step cannot be preempted. Maintenance waits through that step for the stage-one bound (`Grimoire.WorkDrainTimeout`, five seconds); a step that outlives it fails closure with `Grimoire.WorkDrainTimeout` (503), admission reopens, and the step continues to finish normally (`ApprenticeServiceReliabilityTests.MaintenanceDrainWithInFlightStep_FailsWithWorkDrainTimeoutAndReopens` pins that sequence through a real `ApprenticeService`). An operator who needs a maintenance window sooner pauses or cancels the Apprentice first. Shortening this wait would require splitting the step into smaller effect groups, which the runtime deliberately does not do.

Nested request and work lifetimes retain the exact live finisher authority across execution-context flow. Releasing a lifetime changes shared liveness, so a flowed copy grants no independent authority. Admission and current-head disposal skip released ambient predecessors, preventing repeated non-LIFO disposal from retaining a history of completed lifetimes while preserving live ancestors. The deterministic gate characterization uses dedicated barrier participants for admission, frontier, disposal, and drain-waiter races; generation exhaustion uses a test-only field accessor, and retained ambient ancestry is inspected only in tests.

Stage two is ordered: close ordinary admission for the exact generation; resolve every in-flight native-open ticket as opened, failed, or refused-after-open; wait for enrolled ordinary handles to physically close; clear the relevant SQLite pools; and only then issue the generation-bound `IGrimoireExclusiveClosedLease`. The caller's cancellation is checked before the first step commits, where refusing is a no-op, and it is still observed by every later wait: a cancellation after the commitment is reported with the gate `Closed` on the burned generation, no lease issued, and the exact closing owner retained for retry, never as "nothing happened". The closed lease is therefore a process-local proof that no admitted ordinary handle or pool can race closed-period work; it neither proves sidecar absence nor replaces the later physical-storage proof.

No database work in a closed period has an ambient opener. `IGrimoireMaintenanceConnectionFactory` offers one narrow method per maintenance purpose, each consuming one owner-, generation-, purpose- and lane-bound capability, returning an unpooled tracked lease, and reporting physical closure back to the lane. Seven methods rather than one taking a purpose, because an acquisition is catalogued by the member that performs it and a single entry point would collapse seven distinguishable routes into a line a reviewer cannot tell apart. A handle whose native open started and whose phase then unwound without reporting an outcome is recorded as abandoned rather than as closed: nothing observed that connection, so nothing may claim it closed, and the handle stays in its closure's live set. The lane's wait for its handles is bounded, and it hands the process-wide adoption interlock back when that wait expires, because waiting forever would turn one leaked handle into a wedged process; the leak is reported rather than forgiven, since closed-lease disposition still refuses while any handle is live. The lane owns the capability lifetime and prevents closed-lease disposition until its handles and release complete. **Neither a path nor a mode is a caller's to choose.** The purpose is the only argument, and the gate derives both from it — the staging file read-only for an export verification, the canonical database for everything else — and hands them back on the capability, which the factory reads instead of restating literals. A caller that could name the file could name a different one, and the comparison the gate makes on the way back in would then be comparing a caller's value with the same caller's value. Where those two files are is an injected authority rather than a static read inside the gate, so a suite that drives a real erasure can say which database it means; a gate answering from the installation's own paths would point every one of those tests at the developer's Grimoire and then prove the bytes gone.

**The separate legacy maintenance adapter is gone.** A Covenant reset and a healthy-catalog factory erasure now take the Grimoire's own closure — closing owner, stage-one drain, stage-two close, one maintenance lane — as the fifth and last item of the authority order, and every open of the closed period goes through it. A second maintenance path is indistinguishable from having no closed period at all, so there is now exactly one.

**A closed period still has to write its own row, and that is what the scoped permit is for.** The terminal compare-exchange the journal binds itself to happens while admission is shut, deliberately: a row terminalized after the reopen would leave a window where the journal has been discarded and nothing says which answer the row was supposed to carry. Ordinary admission refuses every ordinary open, so the erasure takes a permit over the one exact connection object its operation store issues statements on, opens it directly for that one step, closes it, and clears its pool — the ledger's connection string leaves provider pooling on, unlike every maintenance connection, so a closed handle would otherwise return to a pool rather than release the file. The permit is taken when the closure is, not at the write: a closure that cannot keep the ledger usable is one the erasure must not enter at all, because discovering it at the terminal step would leave a family already erased and no row able to say so.

**The inventory reads take the closed period's route too.** Every bounded snapshot an erasure counts from — the pre-canonical preflight, each database and managed-file page, the disclosure exposure — is opened read-only through the same authority, because ordinary admission is shut for the exact generation being erased. The one read that still takes the ordinary route is the launch-time source tuple, which happens before anything is closed and could not be served by a closure that does not yet exist.

**Erasure inventory refusals identify the blocker without exposing its contents.** `CovenantInventoryFailureDetails` is closed in-process metadata on `Error`, excluded by the source-generated JSON contract. A refusal may name independently validated nonempty label and artifact GUIDs and a declared `SensitiveArtifactKind`; malformed identifiers, undeclared enum values, label/digest payloads, paths, provider text and exception text are never diagnostic data. The shared label materializer rejects unknown artifact/provenance kinds, numeric overflow and wrong SQLite storage classes before constructing a label. Adopted producer revisions, active work's expected-source revisions and checkpoint counters, and resumed work's two counters require the raw SQLite INTEGER storage class and a nonnegative signed 64-bit value. Campaign root resolution requires a positive INTEGER path revision. REAL, TEXT or BLOB values are refused before they can be narrowed by a driver getter into ownership or filesystem authority; healthy integer boundaries remain exact. Missing adopted managed ownership is `ManagedOwnershipMissing`; malformed or mismatched ownership is `ManagedOwnershipMismatch`. Both use `Covenant.ManualArtifactErasureRequired`, and neither grants authority to erase a path manually.

Inventory `StorageBusy` (SQLite primary 5 or 6), `StorageUnavailable` (7, 8, 9, 10, 13 or 14, or an I/O/access failure), and `AdmissionUnavailable` use `Covenant.Unavailable`. Classification uses numeric primary result codes, including the primary byte of extended codes, and closed connection-failure metadata, never driver message matching. A query/schema fault, including a missing declared table (SQLite 1), is `StorageFault` with `Covenant.IntegrityFailure`; it is not an instruction to retry busy storage. `InvalidDataset`, `SnapshotMismatch`, `MalformedLabel`, `UnknownArtifactKind`, `UnsupportedRequest` and `CapacityExceeded` also use `Covenant.IntegrityFailure`. A transaction or lease disposal failure is visible as `CleanupFailed` / `Covenant.MaintenanceFailed`. Cleanup attempts transaction disposal and then lease disposal even after a read fails; caller cancellation remains cancellation if either cleanup attempt fails. Reads remain effect-free and bounded to one owned connection and one transaction, including catalog, dataset, disclosure and label reads; preflight neither opens an auxiliary handle nor repairs canonical state.

For a pre-effect refusal, including an authenticated retry, the coordinator emits one warning after finalization reports its outcome, naming the durable operation, phase, safe blocker and actual admission outcome. If finalization fails, the warning retains the original blocker and says that admission reopening is unconfirmed. It never renders arbitrary `Error.Message` or attaches a collaborator exception. The existing completion carries only `BlockingErrorCode`: reset/factory callers retain that code and generate their existing operation/proof/disposition guidance, while detailed label/reason facts remain in the safe warning. A journal-proven rollback may terminalize the durable row with `grimoire.offline_transition_not_applied`, even though the caller keeps the specific refusal code. Writer restoration or finalization failures can replace the caller code with `Covenant.MaintenanceFailed`; the safe warning retains the original inventory cause. Cleanup/writer restoration or unresolved authority can keep admission closed; better diagnostics do not authorize a reopen or a new operation. Operator actions are in Command Reference, **Covenant erasure inventory refusal**.

Stopped-host installation-reset planning and apply carry a separate one-shot authority minted from the already-held `ArcanumMaintenanceLock` after it proves the guarded Grimoire directory. The planning, identity/evidence, apply, and marker-pair paths pass that authority to `StoppedHostGrimoireConnectionFactory`, which opens only the canonical unpooled target for the fixed operation and mode. A running host therefore causes local planning to stop at lock contention before provider open; no ambient lock lookup or host API fallback creates stopped-host authority. The protected erasure's closed period cannot run over a read-only lease, and for a global or all reset the stopped-host process runs that period, so the connection model changes for exactly that step. The plan and the replan stay on the query-only plan-read lease, with the process's Covenant runtime established or verified on it (`StoppedHostCovenantAuthority`). A stopped-host lease is invisible to the connection drain and is not closed by a context composed over it, so the erasure's closed period cannot run over one: the nested step closes the stopped-host lease first and runs the Global data step over the CLI's ordinary admission and Grimoire closure, with the held installation lock lent for the length of that one call. The issuer mints a one-shot lock-loan authority (`IssueStoppedHostFactoryErasureLockLoan`, operation `InstallationResetFactoryErasure`) that authorizes no connection, and `InstallationResetMaintenanceLockAccessor` lets the transition-journal phase authority borrow the exact held lock while the loan lasts. A loan is bound to its database path, spent once, refused over a released lock, and refused beside a lock the accessor already holds with `Data.ControlPathUnavailable`, so a serving host's own attachment is never detached by it. The reset service reaches the loan through `StoppedHostLockLender`, which hands the borrowed lock to one call and takes the loan back when the call returns, so the service itself names no accessor and keeps receiving the exact held lock explicitly. The ambient lock lookup stays absent: nothing but the issuer mints the loan, and nothing but the hosted service and the loan attach the accessor. The facade, `StoppedHostFactoryErasure`, runs only for an authenticated reset record that is prepared, past its point of no return, and holds a `Claimed` receipt naming the requested operation.

**Immutable launch binding, so a transition names its target before it can close anything.** `CovenantOfflineTransitionLaunchV4` and `DataRetentionFactoryTransitionLaunchV2` are the two checkpoint shapes a launch commits at `InventoryPrepared`, and each records the operation identity, the durable ledger kind, the recovery policy, the canonical effect digest, the exact source dataset generation and `AcceleratorEpoch`/`KeyReclamationEpoch`/`EnvelopeKeyEpoch` tuple the plan was made against, the preselected target generation and tuple, and the row revision observed immediately before the commit. The target is preselected rather than generated inside the canonical transaction because that transaction stamps a new generation and advances all three epochs in one statement, so a recovery pass that found the family already replaced could not otherwise tell its own commit from an unrelated one. Each target epoch is required to be the successor of its own source, compared member by member rather than as a set: a launch whose accelerator and envelope targets were transposed satisfies any rule that only asks whether every target is some source plus one, and would then verify a replaced family against a counter it does not belong to. A source epoch of zero, or one already at the ceiling its update trigger refuses to move, is refused here rather than by the database after admission has already closed.

**The launch persists names, not wire codes, and its recorded revision is history rather than a compare-exchange value.** The recovery policy travels as its declared name because the numeric code is also a public operator-API value governed by a different compatibility promise, and a durable payload that borrowed it would let a wire decision rewrite recovery state; the ledger kind travels as its own string for the same reason, and the exclusive operation and phase keep the name encoding §10.20.3 already required. `StartingRevision` is the revision the row carried before the checkpoint was written: committing the checkpoint advances the revision, so no payload can name the value it will itself produce. The revision a terminal compare-exchange actually uses lives in the journal, which is written after the commit and is refused if it does not name a revision past the one the launch recorded.

**One projection, and a legacy row that can never become a launch.** `GrimoireOfflineTransitionLaunchBinding` is what either launch shape projects onto, in the same way one projection already serves both legacy erasure checkpoints, and `GrimoireOfflineTransitionLaunch` is the only seam between the durable row and the journal. It admits exactly what the codec admits — one rule about what a launch is, rather than a second one free to drift from it — computes the domain-separated `DatabaseOperationLaunchBindingDigest` the journal commits to instead of copying those fields, and builds the journal binding itself, so no caller can publish a journal claiming to be bound to a launch it is not. A row at any earlier checkpoint version is refused by the recovery window before a payload is projected at all. That refusal is decided by the version rather than by the content, so it holds for a retired payload that is still perfectly well-formed — which is the case that matters, because those shapes recorded an owner and a phase and no target, and filling the missing target in from the live database, a plan, or a default would authorize a transition against a generation nobody committed to replacing, with the evidence gone by the time the family was already gone.

**Three answers about an observed state, never two.** The preselected pair is what turns "did the canonical transaction commit" from an unanswerable question into a decidable one, and the comparison that reads it back is deliberately narrow: the exact source generation and epoch tuple is exactly-not-applied and may retry against the already-journaled targets, the exact target generation and tuple is exactly-applied, and everything else is ambiguous and stays `KeepClosed`. Both halves have to match together — a target generation carrying a source epoch, or a source generation with one epoch advanced, is the shape a partly committed transaction leaves, and calling either applied would accept a database this transition never produced. A state past the target is ambiguous rather than more-applied-than-expected, and an absent generation is ambiguous rather than a source that happens to be missing: a zero generation is what an uninitialized read yields, and running the effect against a database nobody has established the state of is the one outcome the whole arrangement exists to prevent.

**One exact terminal compare-exchange, a reread of the winner, and no repair.** After the owner-bound reopen and candidate verification, while ordinary admission is still closed, the reconciler reads the row, revalidates its kind, recovery policy, checkpoint version and reference, and the launch digest its payload projects to, then performs one compare-exchange to `Completed` or to a `Failed` the journal proves is pre-effect, and rereads the winner under the same rules. A row already carrying the intended terminal is idempotent success with the identical winner digest, which is what lets a process that crashed between the write and the publication recording it come back and reach the same conclusion.

Where the journal names a parent, one more crossing sits between that terminalization and retirement. After the winner is journaled and before the journal's own `ParentReceiptSatisfied` step, the handler publishes the `Completed` receipt into the outer record, rereads it, and recomputes the binding digest from what came back — so the two records cross exactly once and always in that order. The winner the outer record is told about is the one the journal already holds, not a value recomputed from the database this transition has just closed. An already-exact receipt is reread and never republished: publishing into the outer record advances its authenticated envelope revision, and a replay that rewrote an identical receipt would stale every authority bound to the previous revision for no new fact.

A missing row, a row belonging to another launch, a row standing behind the revision the launch recorded, a row somebody else already terminalized, and a write the store keeps refusing are five separate outcomes, none of them writes anything, and none permits journal retirement: the transition stays in database reconciliation with ordinary admission closed. A parent-bound journal adds three more that permit it no more readily: no valid winner to publish, a receipt that cannot be published, and a receipt that reads back as something other than the exact completion. Each of those parks `KeepClosed` and repeats no effect, because the database is already terminal and two records that disagree about what happened are a state to stay closed in rather than one to resolve by preferring either of them. Overwriting a conflicting row would destroy the only record of the answer already there.

**The launch revision is a floor, not an equality, and a refused write is not an answer.** A row *ahead* of the recorded revision is ordinary rather than suspicious: recovery adopts the operation's lease before it resumes a transition, and that adoption is a revision of its own, so demanding equality would let the first legitimate recovery lock the journal out of the one row it exists to terminalize — permanently, because an authenticated binding cannot be rewritten to catch up. What equality was standing in for is asked directly instead, by the launch digest and the terminal check that precede it. A row behind that revision is refused, because a launch only ever moves a row forward. A compare-exchange the store refuses while the row has not moved is likewise not an answer: every attempt is the same exchange against the revision it just read and so cannot land twice, and it is repeated a bounded number of times before the transition parks rather than holding the closed period open for a store that is not going to accept it.

**A pre-effect failure is proven by the journal, because the row cannot prove it.** An offline phase never rewrites the launch checkpoint, so a row whose family was replaced is byte-identical to one that was never touched, and the existing classifier — which asks only whether a checkpoint exists — parks every crash after the launch commit. The reconciler instead requires the journal to have recorded nothing past the phase that precedes every effect, with no phase in flight, and records its own terminal code when it has: a reader has to be able to tell a transition that touched no storage from a retention mutation that stopped part way, because only the first is safe to simply run again.

This is now the production reset path. A direct Covenant apply commits `CovenantOfflineTransitionLaunchV4` and a healthy-catalog factory apply commits `DataRetentionFactoryTransitionLaunchV2`; the recovery window, both recovery handlers, and the pre-readiness adopter admit exactly those two versions and refuse every other version closed. Nothing here adds a schema, DDL identity, numbered migration, migration kind, endpoint, request or response shape, CLI verb, or configuration key. Parent-receipt publication is part of this path rather than a deferral: a nested transition resolves its parent from the outer record, publishes and rereads the completion receipt inside its reconciliation suffix, and the two records are read as one pair before bootstrap. So is the credential cleanup that publication made safe — the final cleanup of an externally attested full installation reset takes the transition anchor and key after proving the slot terminal (§10.20.12), and every other path still retains both. Launch-gap resumption, the recovery-only unlock, and pre-readiness dispatch are described below; stream quiescence is described above, Entry weaving's work capability and effect frontier are described in §21.6, attachment indexing's in §21.8, and Saga extraction's in §21.9. Adoption by the remaining hosted producers stays with the children after them.

**The original three work-capability consumers establish the pattern used by the complete inventory.** Entry weaving takes one per tick and gives it back only after the tick's scope has gone, which is what puts a background worker into stage one's drain set at all. Until then stage one waited only on request lifetimes, and a worker's physical handle was met later, in stage two's drain, after ordinary admission had already been declared closed for the generation. Its effect group is the frontier §10.20.3 describes in the abstract, spent for the first time: either revocation wins and no provider call begins, or the group wins and the closure waits through the call and every write that follows it. Attachment indexing takes one capability per dequeued request, keeps every processing and failure-classification scope inside it, and spends sequential effect groups so each provider batch and its durable append or failure classification finish together. Saga extraction takes one capability per retained pending session request before creating its scope, holds it across every page and through the scope's asynchronous disposal, and spends one sequential group per page from the extraction-model call through embeddings, inserts or suppression handling, and the exact sequence-cursor commit. The capability is released before any automatic-retry delay, because that delay belongs to a future attempt rather than to the completed work unit. One consequence is deliberate and unchanged — the work-drain checkpoint is five seconds, and an embedding round trip can exceed it, so a transition begun while a group is open can still report `Grimoire.WorkDrainTimeout`. That is the same answer a billable stream gets, for the same reason, and it is fail-safe: no closed lease is issued, no phase runs, and the gate reopens through its proven abort.

Attachment indexing takes the second, and it is the one that shows what the frontier is for. Its unit is one dequeued request rather than a tick, its capability spans the failure-classification scope as well as the processing one, and it spends a sequential group per embedding batch instead of one for the whole unit — so a close between batches keeps every batch already paid for and refuses only the next. It also has what weaving did not: a pending queue identity and an attempt counter, and both survive a deferral untouched, which is the difference between standing a worker down and losing its place. The loop directly awaits the gate's next-open signal with the host token, using the predecessor of the generation observed before the refused lease so both `Closing(G)` and `Closed(G)` resume at the actual reopen even when it precedes waiter registration. It then writes the retained request back to its own queue directly, past an intake that would have deduplicated it against the identity the deferral is holding, and does not dequeue later work while admission remains closed. Its periodic reconciliation takes a capability too — a scope and a four-table transaction on a thirty-second cadence was the unenrolled opener inside the erasure window that the parent could not place.

Saga extraction takes the third, with its durable page cursor as the restart frontier. A close between page N and page N + 1 keeps page N's memories and exact Entry sequence committed, refuses the next page before either provider is called, and resumes from page N + 1 after reopen rather than buying page N again. A maintenance deferral retains the pending session identity and its ordered provenance intervals — each interval's exclusive lower bound, inclusive upper frontier, and attachment policy — under the same deduplication key; it changes neither retry state nor cursor, waits directly for the next open generation with the host token, and writes exactly one signal straight to the channel because its ordinary intake would correctly suppress the still-pending identity. A provider or persistence failure that leaves the page with no durable disposition remains a retry, while the existing partial-success rule may commit a page with at least one inserted or deliberately suppressed conclusion; host cancellation remains shutdown rather than either outcome.

Loremaster uses the same capability for two different bounded units. Its periodic discovery sweep is DB-only: refusal creates no scope and simply returns to the ordinary cadence. The queue consumer keeps the pending session marker after dequeue, takes a fresh `LoremasterSummarization` capability before its scope, and spends one effect group immediately before the headless provider call. A winning group spans that call and the exact campaign-rollup write, then disposes before the session scope and work lease. A refused lease or group unwinds every owned resource before waiting on the predecessor of the observed generation; reopening writes the still-held session to a dedicated priority lane rather than the deduplicating intake. `KeepClosed` leaves the single waiter parked, an immediate reclose repeats admission for the same identity, and a stable reopen runs it exactly once. Only a terminal success, genuine skip, or genuine failure concludes the marker; host shutdown cancels and joins the waiter or winning work without turning cancellation into failure or moving the watermark, except that the rollup write itself runs on a token the host cannot cancel once the provider has returned, so a shutdown at that point keeps the paid-for summary and moves the watermark with it.

**The gate has HTTP consumers now, and the request that closes it does not wait for itself.** Every matched, non-exempt `/api` and `/v1` request takes a request lease before its endpoint runs, held for the whole of its request scope and released only when the container disposes it — after the pooled context has gone back and after every response-completion writer, two of which write to the Grimoire. A request refused there receives the stable maintenance answer of API §8.31 rather than reaching SQLite and being refused by the enrolment interceptor, which is what turned an expected window into a `500` logged at `Error` with the request path. Health and quit are the two exemptions, for the reasons that section records.

Which *kind* of lease comes from the route's own `GrimoireStreamRouteMetadata` rather than from its path, so a route that moves or is renamed carries its classification with it. Exactly the five declared SSE routes — `/api/events/daemon`, `/api/events/mcp`, `/api/events/logs`, `/api/sessions/{id:guid}/stream`, and `/api/apprentices/{id:guid}/chronicle` — carry `GrimoireQuiesceableStream` and take a revocable lease. Every other streaming route carries `FiniteDrain` or `BillableDrain` and every non-streaming route carries nothing, and both take the ordinary finite lease the gate never revokes. Finite is the default for an unmarked route on purpose: forgetting the marker on a new streaming route makes a transition slow rather than cutting a response mid-frame. A bidirectional inventory over `src/**` is what stops it staying forgotten — a streaming construct with no classification fails, a classification naming a construct that has gone fails too, and a catalogued route whose composed endpoint carries a different marker than the catalog records fails as well, which is the join that stops an unmarked route being catalogued as something harmless. Its reach is a syntactic one and is recorded as such: a route that frames itself through a construct none of the five kinds names, and a second route bound to a handler the catalog already lists, are both outside what the scanner can see, and the composed-host half is what covers the second of those for any route that is marked. The reset and factory-erasure routes are not exempt: they run the whole transformation inside the request that asked for it, so the initiating request is *promoted* out of its own stage-one drain, paired with the exact scoped connection the operation store issues its terminal compare-exchange on. Promotion rather than exemption, because a request with no ordinary lifetime at all would be refused by its own erasure the moment it reopened that connection.

**A stage one that cannot drain, or whose caller cancels before stage two commits, reopens rather than staying shut.** Disposing a closing owner clears the active owner and nothing else, so a timed-out or cancelled drain used to leave the gate closed for the life of the process — every later request refused while the Covenant rollback retired the journal that explained why. The proven abort now accepts only the exact owner of an uncommitted `Closing` transition and only after its caller proves no destructive effect occurred; it ignores the already-cancelled ambient token while completing that proof and the final in-lock compensation. A `Grimoire.WorkDrainTimeout` answers **503** rather than 500 for the same reason. What a retry needs is for whatever would not drain to have finished, and the five declared streaming routes now end at a frame boundary rather than being waited out: they take `QuiesceableStream` leases, the gate revokes those on the `Ordinary -> Closing` edge, and each finishes the frame it was writing, starts no next one, and lets its request scope go. A transition attempted while a watcher is connected therefore drains instead of timing out. A billable or finite stream still takes an ordinary finite lease and is still drained through completion, so a transition begun while one of those is open can still reach the timeout — which is the intended answer, because a stream a provider is already charging for must reach the caller who is paying for it. Once stage two has committed, the same abort is refused and the exact owner plus active journal remain the only authority for retry.

**A crashed transition is finished before the database is opened for ordinary use.** The pair matrix's three active-journal answers — `StandaloneTransition`, `NestedBound`, and `NestedReceiptStoredRetirementSuffix` — once stopped startup at a refusal; they now enter `GrimoireOfflineTransitionStartupRecovery` on the lock the host already holds, after the pair is resolved and before `GrimoireDatabaseBootstrapper`. The pass captures one OS-marker sample, performs recovery-only unlock, and then offers authenticated terminal-suffix completion before marker validation. That narrow exception rereads and matches the exact terminal row, canonical catalog identity, authenticated journal, and terminal winner, and can only finish monotonic reconciliation and retirement; it cannot load effect authority, dispatch a handler or coordinator, or publish host-tools policy. If no terminal suffix completes, marker validation remains mandatory before any nonterminal or effect recovery, followed by exact installation-identity verification and provisional host-tools classification, authority load and one-shot consumption, physical close of the probe, both gates Closed, exact held-lock operation adoption, and typed self-settling dispatch. Only a durable verdict — `Completed`, `Failed`, or `Abandoned` — is a resumption. Ordinary bootstrap then installs and verifies schema, publishes the final process-wide host-tools and Covenant facts, restores the same cold disclosure writer, and only afterward publishes Covenant and Grimoire readiness. A parked transition, an adoption that could not take the lease, and every fail-closed arm of the matrix all refuse startup with the one content-free sentence, and which of them it was is deliberately not in the message.

**The recovery-only unlock can open an existing catalog and can do nothing else to it.** `GrimoireRecoveryOnlyUnlock` resolves the passphrase from an existing database beside an existing KDF sidecar, and from nothing else. It opens `SqliteOpenMode.ReadWrite` — not `ReadWriteCreate` — with pooling off, initializes through the read-only connection mode that never attempts a journal-mode change, and proves `SELECT 1`. Five mutations the ordinary bootstrap performs are refusals here, each on evidence rather than a flag: an absent database is refused rather than created, a *pending* KDF sidecar is refused rather than promoted, a database with no sidecar is refused rather than upgraded from the master key, no schema installer is reached, and no restore topology is converged. The absent-database refusal is the point of the component: a journal naming an active transition over a catalog that is not there is evidence disagreeing with itself, and the ordinary bootstrap answers that by creating a fresh empty database.

**The authority is loaded read-only and then checked against the journal that names it.** Before the recovery connection exists, startup captures one OS-marker sample. An authenticated terminal suffix may complete first even when that sample is malformed or unreadable because the suffix proves the terminal row and winner without deriving effect authority or dispatching work; ordinary bootstrap still must establish normal marker and authority policy before readiness. Every path that could classify or resume a nonterminal row rejects a failed marker sample before provisional host-tools classification, authority load, or effect recovery. After recovery-only unlock and successful marker validation, startup verifies the journal's authenticated installation UUID against `covenant_authority_state`, joins that captured sample with the durable authority row and environment, and publishes the result only into a fresh provisional `HostProcessToolsRuntimePolicy`. The real process policy and static host-tools predicate stay unpublished until ordinary bootstrap. `CovenantRecoveryAuthorityBootstrapper` independently rechecks the installation UUID, then reads the canonical envelope state, persisted availability tuple, and one launch row the journal's binding names without writing. Agreement is what it is for: the launch has to decode at one of the two current versions under its exact checkpoint reference, its projected binding digest has to equal the digest the journal committed to, its effect digest has to be the journal's, the operation it names has to be the one the effect-handler table says that journal kind may be, the row's revision has to be at or ahead of the launch's recorded floor, and the persisted dataset generation has to be exactly the launch's source tuple or its preselected target. The provisional policy must permit Covenant, while an already-published real denial remains a veto both at load and immediately before handoff consumption publishes availability or derives keys. A mismatch, tainted or pending marker pair, escape-hatch decision, policy change, or generation that is neither source nor target refuses without dispatch.

**The handoff is one use, bound to the root and revision it was minted under.** `CovenantClosedRecoveryHandoff` publishes the persisted availability and authority facts and adopts the durable recovery owner into `CovenantOperationGate`, in that order, and the claim is interlocked rather than a flag a caller could read and race: a handoff spent twice would adopt a second owner over a scope the first still holds, which the gate answers with a thrown exception rather than a result. It refuses a guarded root that is not the one it was minted under and a journal revision that has moved since it was verified. It publishes no database readiness and mints no reusable token — the facts are present precisely so the one exclusive lease can be resumed, and present facts behind a gate an adopted owner has closed are not availability.

**The lease is adopted rather than waited out, and the lock is the evidence.** The ordinary acquisition admits a row only once its lease has expired, because an unexpired lease ordinarily means somebody may still be working. A caller holding the installation maintenance lock `FileShare.None` has already established that nobody else owns this installation, so the surviving lease is a dead process's and waiting out its remainder would only delay a startup that has to finish before readiness. `AdoptUnderInstallationLockAsync` is the same exact-fingerprint compare-update minus the expiry predicate and asserts the held lock before it writes. It retains the ordinary reclaimable states and adds one narrow lock-only arm: current V4 retention mutation or V2 factory-erasure rows parked as `ReconciliationRequired/Covenant.ErasureIncomplete`. Ordinary acquisition, classified recovery, expiry discovery, unrelated kinds or codes, fingerprint drift, and every terminal row still refuse. The one successful adoption advances the revision exactly once and comes before the handler because the coordinator compares the row's lease owner with the owner it is handed.

An authenticated active transition is stricter than an ordinary adopted row. After the recovery probe is disposed, dispatch resumes the exact Covenant owner, reissues the retained same-owner Grimoire closure without advancing its burned generation, and reads and adopts the operation only through short tracked ledger windows while both gates are Closed. Each window physically closes the exact ledger handle, clears its exact pool, and reports that closure before the owner-bound handler may start; any admission, open, close, pool-clear, or report failure refuses recovery and keeps both authorities closed. The explicit one-shot admission carries the full authenticated journal evidence and is bound by object identity to the creating scoped coordinator and ledger. The coordinator consumes it once, resumes the exact journal without a fresh-journal fallback, and uses those same Covenant and Grimoire authorities rather than reacquiring either. Disposal, identity drift, a live process claim, or failure before a proved terminal disposition keeps the installation closed. In particular, quiesce or exact-journal-resume failure before the phase session is reconstructed spends `KeepClosed` directly on both retained authorities: it does not reopen the writer, settle the adopted row, treat the active journal as absent, or replace or retire that journal.

**Running the handler is the reconciler's own protocol, reached by identity instead of by expiry.** `LongRunningOperationReconciler.SettleExactlyAsync` runs the registered `ILongRunningOperationRecoveryHandler` for one named operation, rereads the row, and compare-exchanges the verdict on `CancellationToken.None`, which is the body the periodic pass runs too. It differs from that pass in exactly two ways, and both are properties of knowing which operation is meant: it takes the operation by identity, and it takes an already-adopted lease. The periodic pass is otherwise unchanged — same discovery predicate, same two startup phases, same paging, same concurrency, and the same skip on an operation this process is already running. The CLI container (`AddArcanumGrimoireForCli`) composes the same reconciler without the generic-discovery and classified-lease ports because stopped-host bootstrap needs only `SettleExactlyAsync`; a generic pass attempted there throws rather than scanning the installation, and `ServiceCollectionExtensionsTests` pins that posture.

**The launch gap closes before readiness rather than after it.** The launch-row commit and the first journal publication cannot be one atomic storage transaction, so a crash between them leaves a committed, nonterminal launch row and no journal. Nothing destructive has happened — the journal is published and verified before admission closes — and the row is both safe to resume and unsafe to leave, because a nonterminal durable operation blocks every later data-retention operation. Until now the pre-readiness adopter handed its owner to the periodic reconciler, which runs *after* readiness on a ten-second budget with the host already serving and the resumption free to spill into the background while requests arrive. `CovenantOfflineTransitionLaunchGapResumption` now spends that owner inside the bootstrap, after the install handle is physically closed and before readiness is marked, and a verdict short of terminal refuses readiness. The scan is unchanged and stays where it is: `CovenantErasureStartupRecoveryOwnerAdopter` already admits only the two launch versions with their exact references and policies, already reports an ordinary retention mutation as no owner at all, and already refuses a second adoptable row and every legacy, malformed, and mis-policied shape — a second scanner over the same rows would be a second answer to one question. The stopped-host CLI composes that same dispatch as a deliberately narrower authority: one recovery-only facade over the host's two production erasure routines, the two current launch handlers, maintenance-lock lease adoption, and an exact-settlement reconciler with no generic discovery or classified recovery port. It registers neither `IDataRetentionService` nor a recovery background service, so owning the installation lets the CLI finish only the launch bootstrap already authenticated and never turns a normal CLI process into another durable-work host. The same container carries the reset-only `StoppedHostFactoryErasure` for the one claim an authenticated installation-reset record names; it is not an `IDataRetentionService`, refuses every operation but a factory reset, and finds every durable thing by exact requested identity.

Startup-owner adoption refusals preserve their cause through the bootstrap boundary. A closed Core reason (`MalformedRow`, `PolicyMismatch`, `UnsupportedVersion`, `UnreadableCheckpoint`, `WrongOperation`, `SecondOwner`, `GateRefused`, or `StorageFault`) and a row identifier only after canonical nonempty GUID validation travel in the `Result` error; in-process metadata is excluded from source-generated error JSON. The existing strict launch validator preserves `WrongOperation` for a mismatched exclusive operation, and checkpoint projection preserves it for an operation ID that disagrees with the row. These failures remain failures throughout; the adopter attaches only the validated row ID, never the rejected payload ID. Storage exceptions are reduced to a closed category and numeric SQLite primary/extended codes. The bootstrap emits one warning with those safe facts and throws their operator message with no original exception attached. No rejected checkpoint/row content, SQL, private exception message or stack is logged. Cancellation still propagates. This adds no adoption authority and changes no checkpoint/gate proof. Existing offline `doctor` checks supply aggregate operation and storage information, not owner reconstruction or repair; the Command Reference's **Covenant startup recovery refusal** section describes that boundary and the safe manual follow-up.

The current V4 mutation and V2 factory handlers settle their own durable terminal row as part of the coordinator's disposition proof. Authenticated-journal dispatch and launch-gap dispatch therefore select an explicit self-settling handler by exact kind and current checkpoint window and map only its proved `Completed`, `Failed`, or attention outcome. They never pass that result through the generic reconciler for a second owner compare-exchange after the coordinator has already terminalized the row and cleared its lease owner. A refusal before the first transition journal exists is the one earlier boundary: a proved pre-effect rollback compare-exchanges the exact adopted launch row to `Failed`, rereads its unchanged launch identity and terminal code, and only then reopens admission; a refused write keeps admission closed. Invalid kind, policy, checkpoint reference, payload, result state, or error shape is attention/refusal; an arbitrary terminal row is never accepted as the handler's proof. Other registered recovery handlers retain the generic exact-settlement path.

Authenticated startup recovery deliberately does not reopen the Covenant disclosure writer inside the coordinator. At that point the fresh process has only durable authority and structurally valid unavailable schema tiers; treating those tiers as healthy would invent proof, while requiring a healthy writer there would strand an already-verified transition. Both committed and proved pre-effect rollback verdicts therefore retire while the writer stays cold. The hosted service carries one explicit restoration flag only for an exact resumed verdict, and ordinary bootstrap reopens the same singleton lifecycle after schema, identity, authority, protected-maintenance recovery, physical install-handle close, and launch-gap completion, but before either readiness signal. A reopen refusal preserves the terminal row and retired journal yet fails startup before readiness; no-journal starts and live-host transitions retain their existing paths.

**Ten literal codes, declared once, and no route DTO owns a second set.** `CovenantResetPhase` runs `InventoryPrepared = 1` through `ReopenedVerified = 10` beside `CovenantFamilyReinitializePhase` and `CovenantSchemaRepairPhase`, which is where its peers already live. The codes are literal because they are persisted, so a reordered member repoints an existing checkpoint at a different step — the same reason §10.20.1 gave for `RetentionDataClass`. An architecture test asserts that no other enum in Core, Infrastructure, API, or CLI declares this exact ten-name set: two vocabularies that agreed on the day they were written would, at the first divergence, let a response describe a step the durable checkpoint never recorded. Zero is deliberately absent, because a default-initialized phase would read as "before the first step" on a checkpoint that only exists because a step already ran.

**`CovenantResetPhaseMachine` is the only reader of that ordering, and it fails closed four ways.** Unknown, zero, skipped, and regressed all resolve to `Covenant.ManualRecoveryRequired`, which is the same single code the checkpoint codec already uses — an operator told "skipped" and one told "regressed" does the same thing in both cases: look at the operation, not at the bytes. `RequireAdvance` accepts *exactly* the successor, and re-saving the phase already held is rejected too, because a pass that rewrote its own phase would be indistinguishable from one that ran the step twice. Comparing phases inline at each call site instead would have made three of those four wrong answers silent.

**The retired shapes are gone rather than kept as legacy reads.** The predecessors of these two launches recorded an owner and the phase they had reached, and no target at all, so nothing could ever turn one into an offline transition — they existed only to be refused. Keeping a shape that nothing writes and nothing can act on would not be a compatibility contract; it would be a second way to describe a launch, which is exactly what the rule above forbids. The rows outlive the types, and it is the version window that refuses them.

**The launch carries no file-entry vector, and that is what keeps the ordinary mutation journal alive.** The one mutation that commits a launch is the Covenant memory reset, which captures no attachment, so the shape stays fixed-width inside the source-generated context's 4 KiB decode bound; a variable-length array there would turn a safety cap into an outage the first time an installation grew past it. Ordinary mutations keep writing the `ARCAMUT2` journal unchanged, which is why a checkpoint written before this build still decodes, still reconciles against the database that is its commit authority, and completes without a second dataset replacement. The version-0 factory arm is untouched for the same reason it was written: a row interrupted between its single-flight insert and its first journal touched no storage, and parking it would wedge every later retention operation.

**Lowercase hexadecimal, not case-insensitive comparison.** One effect has one encoding. Two spellings of the same digest would compare unequal as durable text while denoting the same destructive plan, and the adoption check is the one place that must never be nearly right.

**The factory launch reuses the same ten phases**, because a healthy-catalog factory erasure does the same thing to storage as a reset and differs only in what it preserves. Its kind keeps `MinCheckpointVersion: 0`, so the documented legacy arm — a payload-free row restarted idempotently from durable quarantine state — still recovers exactly as before. A launched factory erasure is resumed from the journal instead, because a factory erasure that already applied its canonical deletion cannot prove that by inspecting the result.

**The data-retention mutation descriptor moved to `BeforeStateWrites`, and the priority belongs to the kind rather than to a version.** That is what makes the legacy arms compatible: version 0 and version 2 move with it and behave identically, while a launched erasure — one caught between canonical deletion and its verified reopen — is reconciled before any ordinary durable writer, optional initializer, worker, or ready-state publication runs. The barrier is asserted in both places it actually lives: the reconciler settles the `BeforeStateWrites` phase before it touches a readiness-phase row, and hosted services start sequentially in registration order with `LongRunningOperationStartupHostedService` after the Grimoire bootstrap and ahead of every workload that could append to the tree an interrupted reset is about to replace. The phase predicate is applied before paging (§10.8.2), including when older ordinary rows fill a page. The closed admission held by the checkpoint remains the authority protecting an interrupted erasure; recovery ordering adds no mutation privilege.

**Gate acquisition is unreachable before the first checkpoint commits, structurally rather than by convention.** `CovenantResetCheckpointInitiator` derives the effect digest, verifies it, commits `InventoryPrepared`, and only then constructs the `GateAdmission` that carries the owner — a nested type whose constructor nothing outside the initiator can reach. An erasure that closed admission first would leave a window in which the family is closed, the operator is waiting, and nothing durable says which destructive plan is in flight, so the next start could neither resume it nor prove it never began. Making that ordering a rule somebody has to remember is how it eventually gets forgotten.

**The requested and server-generated arms read different things, and the difference is asserted.** When the caller supplied the requested-operation triplet, the derived digest must equal the one already written to the normalized identity row, compared in fixed time, and a name with no row behind it is refused before any checkpoint is written. When all three requested fields are null there is no identity row at all, the checkpoint is the sole durable effect-digest source, and `FindRequestIdentityAsync` is never called — a test counts the lookups, because reading a row that was never written would turn every ordinary server-generated reset into a recovery escalation.

**`CovenantErasureEffectDigestCalculator` is the single producer, with two pinned domains.** `Arcanum.Covenant.Reset.Effect.v1` and `Arcanum.Covenant.HealthyCatalogFactoryErasure.Effect.v1` are separated because a reset and a factory erasure over an identical inventory are different destructive plans and must never share an owner.
