## 12. C# language and coding conventions

- **File-scoped namespaces** used consistently.
- **Primary constructor-style DTOs** — positional records for `Error`, `ApiResponse<T>`, `PingRequest`, `IntelligenceEvent`. No `[JsonPropertyName]` on `/api` DTOs; casing comes from `[JsonSourceGenerationOptions]`. **Exceptions:** OpenAI `/v1` types and MCP JSON-RPC contexts use explicit `[JsonPropertyName]` where an external spec mandates snake_case or JSON-RPC member names (API §8.2). `ArcanumConventionTests.ApiWireTypes_DoNotUseJsonPropertyName` walks every first-party type reachable from `ArcanumJsonContext`, Core types included, and allows the attribute only in the OpenAI, Familiar and A2A namespaces and on four named types whose member names another party owns: the OpenAI usage object `ChatCompletionUsage` (the native result frame carries the same snake_case names), the `arcanum.json` root `ArcanumConfigurationFile`, and the two model-output contracts. `IntelligenceEvent` carries no renames: its Ward members are named `ToolName`, `Arguments`, `Allowed`, `Reason` and `Origin`, which the camelCase policy writes as the wire names clients already read.
- **Primary constructors on services** for DI injection.
- **`IDisposable`** on infrastructure services with `SemaphoreSlim` or `ServiceProvider` ownership.
- **One blank line between ordinary statement and member lines** for visual breathing room, but never immediately after an opening or before a closing parenthesis, bracket, or brace (AGENTS.md rule 4); attached control clauses stay tight.
- **Convention scope (project-specific vs inherited).** The conventions in this section plus the README naming metaphor are **specific to Arcanum**. Organization-wide standards scoped to `Corp.Solution.*`-prefixed solutions — Dapper repositories over SQL Server stored procedures, the `Corp.Lib.*` / `Corp.Api.Configuration.Lib` NuGet stack, and Refit "Service Library" API contracts — **do not apply** here: Arcanum is local-first over its own EF Core + SQLCipher Grimoire (no SQL Server, no stored procedures) and ships its CLI/host as one Native AOT application on macOS arm64 and Windows x64/arm64 (Linux is not a shipping RID). The always-on house rules still hold — one blank line after each C# statement except around brackets and parentheses (above), strict CSP with no inline JS/CSS on every web surface, and the documentation contract updated with code (§18).

---

## 13. Testing strategy

`tests/RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Tests` is the xUnit suite for the Core, Infrastructure, Api, and Cli shipping assemblies. It runs on the normal CLR, not as Native AOT, and uses hand-written fakes only (no Moq). A live model provider is unnecessary for ordinary test runs.

Scripted setup tests that replace `Console.In` explicitly select the prompt's redirected-input seam and reject hidden terminal reads with a throwing test double. Replacing the managed reader does not change OS terminal detection; the suite must not wait for keyboard input when launched from a terminal. Separate terminal-under-JSON coverage preserves masked credential input in production.

The coverage runner owns closed, noninteractive OS stdin for its runtime test child. Standalone `dotnet test` runs exercising credential-stdin paths likewise require a noninteractive launch (for example, `</dev/null`): `Console.SetIn` scripts supply test data but do not satisfy the production OS-redirection security check.

Any suite that redirects `ArcanumPaths` or touches configuration, session, MCP, or file roots must set both host environments to `Testing`, point `ARCANUM_TEST_HOME` at a uniquely owned temporary root **before the first path access**, and restore every variable during cleanup. Process-global mutations use the nonparallel `ProcessEnvironment` collection; a suite that already requires another `DisableParallelization` collection (xUnit assigns one collection per class) must provide the same serialization and the same guarded test-home invariant. Tests never read, back up, rewrite, migrate, or delete the developer's real `~/.config/arcanum` files.

That rule is **enforced for direct `Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable` callers**, not only for `ArcanumWebApplicationFactory` dependents. `EnvironmentIsolationContractTests` walks the IL of every method in the Arcanum test assembly, folds compiler-generated types back onto their outermost declaring test class (so lifted async and lambda state machines still attribute to the class that owns them), and closes over first-party helper scopes, so a class that mutates the environment indirectly through a helper — `HostProcessToolsEscapeHatchScope`, for instance — is caught as well. The factory itself is treated as mutating unconditionally because it repoints `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` from native code paths the IL walk cannot see through, and a self-check fails the suite if the walk stops resolving. The Compendium suite establishes the same fixture contract through its own `ArcanumTestHomeScope` (a deliberate twin of the Arcanum copy under `tests/RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Tests/Support`, because the Compendium test project cannot reference the Arcanum test assembly; each copy's remarks name the other and a change to the redirected-variable set belongs in both), which sets `HOME`, `USERPROFILE`, `DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT=Testing`, `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Testing`, and `ARCANUM_TEST_HOME` and restores all of them on dispose — redirecting `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` alone is insufficient because .NET resolves Windows known folders through `SHGetKnownFolderPath` and ignores a post-start `USERPROFILE` assignment.

The Arcanum suite enforces the same two rules mechanically rather than by convention. `ArcanumPaths` deliberately ignores `ARCANUM_TEST_HOME` outside a `Testing` host environment (and stays that way: failing closed there would turn a stray variable into a production start failure), which is the default environment of a plain `dotnet test` run, so setting the variable alone writes the developer's real profile directory. `ArcanumTestHomeScope` (`tests/RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Tests/Support`) is the shared fixture that sets all five variables and restores them, and `EnvironmentIsolationContractTests.Every_test_class_that_sets_ARCANUM_TEST_HOME_also_sets_a_Testing_environment` fails the suite for any test class whose IL (`ldstr` operands resolved alongside the call sites) names the variable without either using that scope, setting a Testing environment, or depending on the web-application factory that sets one. "Setting a Testing environment" means the class (nested closure and state-machine types included) loads both a `DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT`/`ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT` name and the literal `Testing`; naming the variable alone, to read it, clear it, or give it another value, does not count, and neither does `Testing` alone (control theories pin each of those shapes, and the split shape in which a helper takes the value as a parameter). The pairing is a class-wide literal match, not data-flow analysis, so a class that names `Testing` for an unrelated reason and also touches the variable passes. The CLI harness production dependency injection reads and writes the profile too (a name-resolved selection remembers itself in `recent-resources.txt`), so `CliTestHarness.RunAsync` opens a harness-owned scope whenever `TestHomeGuard` finds the ambient `GrimoireDirectory` or `SecretStoreDirectory` at, or beneath, the exact real `<profile>/.config/arcanum` or `<ApplicationData>/arcanum` directory, and leaves a home the test already redirected alone. The guard compares against those exact directories, never the profile as a prefix, because `Path.GetTempPath()` lives under `%USERPROFILE%` on Windows. A second contract, `Every_test_class_that_swaps_the_global_console_runs_in_a_serialized_collection`, requires every class that assigns `Console.SetOut`/`SetError`/`SetIn` or `AnsiConsole.Console`, directly or through the harness, to run in a `DisableParallelization` collection: `GlobalConsole` is the home for CLI command tests, and the `ProcessEnvironment` collection is equally serialized and also accepted, because `DisableParallelization` collections never overlap one another. The rule is serialization, not one collection name.

**A stored identity is held in one spelling, and the schema is what holds it there.** Every governed identity column carries a write-time guard trigger refusing any value that is not uppercase, dashed and thirty-six characters, so a non-canonical identity is rejected whatever produced it — the object-relational writer, a raw `Guid` handed to the provider, an interpolation, or SQL nobody has written yet — and the settlement is proved behaviourally rather than by inspecting source, by driving each converting writer through its outermost production entry point against a real encrypted database and reading the identities it stored back out of the rows; the settlement is what lets a read of this installation's own database compare exactly and seek its index, while a read of a foreign one — a backup archive, a staged restore — still normalises, because another installation's vintage is not this build's to assume.

### 13.1 Commands and coverage authority

From the repository root:

```bash
dotnet test tests/RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Tests/RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Tests.csproj
./scripts/coverage.sh
./scripts/coverage.sh --threshold
./scripts/coverage.sh --feature --threshold  # runtime feedback; not delivery qualification
```

The delivery command is `scripts/coverage.sh --threshold`: it runs runtime tests under XPlat coverage, enforces the line (80%), branch (70%) and security-critical branch thresholds of the table below, then runs mandatory `HostedProducerAnalysis` without coverage instrumentation. Either phase failing fails delivery; an empty analysis selection, a missing result, or a skipped proof also fails. Bare `scripts/coverage.sh` runs both runtime coverage and mandatory source analysis, but does not enforce numeric or security thresholds and is therefore not full delivery qualification. The category contains the whole-program Roslyn producer inventory, its adversarial source fixtures, and the Covenant/CLI source-boundary checks that share those compilations; these analyze production syntax rather than execute the production graph. Its runtime DI-registration check is retained separately in `HostedRuntimeRegistrationTests`, and both halves compare against the same closed vocabulary. Runtime recovery-classification and authenticated-HTTP behavior checks remain in the instrumented suite. No production assembly or coverage threshold is excluded by the runtime/analysis split.

`--feature` deliberately stops after runtime coverage and labels the result as incomplete qualification; use it for development feedback only. Standalone delivery uses `scripts/coverage.sh --threshold`, and the runner's default `full` partition executes the complete universe. CI's `Build, test, coverage` job uses `scripts/coverage.sh --threshold --ci-runtime-only`: that explicit mode requires thresholds, rejects `--feature`, and names the separate mandatory `Hosted producer source analysis` authority. Passing runtime coverage alone is not delivery acceptance. CI schedules five workers on separate `macos-26` runners: `Hosted producer primary analysis`, `Hosted producer additional analysis`, `Hosted producer fixture analysis`, `Hosted producer fixture build analysis` and `Hosted producer serve host analysis`. All five build uninstrumented Release with the same run-resolved stable SDK, discover the same complete production/additional/fixture/serve-host/build-fixture universe, keep a 3,540-second per-worker deadline, and emit a source-SHA-bound selection receipt plus their TRX evidence. The two production workers keep two worker slots. A fixture worker asks for one slot (`--jobs 1`) and the runner plans a fixture partition as exactly one process whatever the slot count: a fixture process keeps the bound production compilations in memory, and a standard `macos-26` runner has about 7 GB, so two fixture processes in one job are never planned. Unmarked production methods route to primary; the five additional-root consumers route to additional; the four Serve host theories, which carry `HostedProducerServeHostAnalysis`, route to serve host; the four Build scan classes (`AdmittedEntryCensusTests`, `AuthorityCarrierBanTests`, `CheckerLimitPinTests` and `SingleGateCensusTests`) and the two Serve worker theories (`ServeWorkerMutationHasExplicitConditionalSourceAssociation` and `CanonicalServeCallbackHasConditionalBuildStartWorkerSourceAssociation`), which carry `HostedProducerBuildAnalysis`, route to fixture build (the `fixtures-build` partition); every other nonproduction fixture routes to fixture. The category, not a name, decides the split, so a renamed method keeps its lane and a new fixture lands in `fixtures` by default; `Serve_host_fixture_lane_is_closed_and_holds_no_production_method` and `Build_fixture_lane_is_closed_and_disjoint_from_every_other_lane` close the two marked sets, and the runner refuses a serve-host or build-fixture subset that is empty, is not a proper subset of the fixtures, or names a method that is not a fixture or whose case count differs, and refuses a method that both subsets name. The `Hosted producer source analysis` job is the fail-closed delivery authority: it runs with `if: always()`, requires all five worker jobs to have succeeded, rejects missing or stale receipts and missing, duplicate or extra partition/TRX evidence, and reuses exact method/theory-count and all-passed TRX validation before emitting its authority summary. `ci.yml` defines fourteen jobs: `Select stable .NET SDK`, `Native SQLCipher asset status`, `Build, test, coverage`, the five source analysis workers (`Hosted producer primary analysis`, `Hosted producer additional analysis`, `Hosted producer fixture analysis`, `Hosted producer fixture build analysis` and `Hosted producer serve host analysis`), the authority job `Hosted producer source analysis`, `macOS workspace-check runtime`, `Windows test suite`, `Windows test suite (arm64)`, `Native AOT IL and executable gates` and `Formatting and shell lint`. `scripts/coverage_workflow_test.py` executes the coverage entry point and all five canonical partition commands against a controlled `dotnet` boundary, then reconciles their artifacts. It verifies disjoint selection, mandatory standalone analysis, runtime threshold enforcement, exit propagation, missing-report refusal, skipped-proof refusal and explicit mode boundaries. `scripts/hosted_producer_analysis_runner_test.py` covers complete discovery, default and explicit partition routing, bounded worker selection, progress reading, process-tree cleanup, receipt reconciliation and fail-closed result accounting.

Arcanum's checked-in `xunit.runner.json` selects conservative scheduling with at most four parallel collections, independent of the host's processor count. All three consumers of the shared production Roslyn compilations (producer inventory, Covenant architecture boundaries, and authenticated HTTP sender architecture checks) share the nonparallel `HostedProducerAnalysis` collection. This prevents the compilation graph from running beside the parallel runtime suite; collection membership is checked from executable test metadata.

Captured CLI command fixtures run through `CliTestHarness` belong to the nonparallel `GlobalConsole` collection. The harness builds its console through `CliConsoleFactory`, as production does, so a captured run is plain on a CI runner without the harness clearing the runner's signal: Spectre's runner enrichment would otherwise enable ANSI even when the capture requests plain output. A harness fixture that asserts the runner case or the no-runner case (`CliOutputFileTests`, `SagaCommandTests`) sets or clears `GITHUB_ACTIONS` through `CliTestConsoleEnvironment`, the harness helper for `GlobalConsole` fixtures, which restores its exact prior value on disposal or setup failure. The console-factory tests (`CliConsoleFactoryTests`) supply `GITHUB_ACTIONS` through `AnsiConsoleSettings.EnvironmentVariables` and never change the process environment. The prompt-console tests (`SensitiveValueInputTests`, in `GlobalConsole`) and the diagnostic-console tests (`CliDiagnosticConsoleTests`, in `ProcessEnvironment`) set and clear `GITHUB_ACTIONS`, `NO_COLOR` and `ARCANUM_NO_COLOR` through their own scopes, each of which restores every exact prior value. The original hostile-control and visible-width assertions remain intact. Ordinary recovery baselines await the actual admitted provider-health effect before asserting its count. Watcher-retry fixtures wait for the published `Watching` status; the internal watcher count also includes construction reservations, so it is not evidence that the factory returned successfully. A held failing factory attempt proves the observation cannot complete early, while the exact attempt count and retry backoff remain asserted. The MCP regex-cancellation fixture holds a real secure file open until the duplicate-id wire rejection and notification-driven cancellation of the registered tool token are observed; the configured regex budget is retained, and the test synchronizes on observed protocol and cancellation effects. Workspace search enters the stream disposal scope before its first post-open cancellation checkpoint, so cancellation closes the validated handle before returning. Workspace-reset lifecycle fixtures await complete workspace-index publication and drain the real producer before resetting; a controlled second-file embedding barrier proves that the seed cannot return while publication is unfinished, and the reset still must leave no victim rows while preserving erasure evidence and keys.

macOS remains the primary full runtime and coverage authority, including Compendium and The Forge. The two Windows jobs, `Windows test suite` and `Windows test suite (arm64)`, each carry native-asset prerequisites, builds, Native AOT diagnostics and shipping/provider smokes. Their Arcanum selection explicitly includes `WindowsCiSurfaceTests`, both NativeSqlCipher classes, real OS credential round trips, Windows process-resource limits and Job Objects, AppContainer policy, restore journals, the real-DACL round trip, host-side broker target resolution, the host-job handshake, broker exit diagnostics and the shared root-lock budget, the broker success-path smoke and the OS-conditional sandbox roots, child-process boundaries and filesystem jails, executable resolution, the Windows durable-delete and weakened-DACL journal cases, owner-only reset-attestation validation, real Windows path-casing/separator containment, default Job Object assignment, PEM export-buffer zeroing, reparse/hard-link refusal and native metadata, the Command Center attachment gate on a real volume (the Windows cases of `CommandCenterTurnAttachmentBuilderTests`, including a file compressed in place with `compact.exe /exe` that the test proves the volume backed through the Windows Overlay Filter's own API; §16.6), read-only maintenance locks, real journal unlink/rename/exchange primitives, denied-delete journal cleanup, the failed-delete report for a temp tree a still-open file blocks (`TestDirectoryCleanupTests`; Windows has no owner-access restore, so the delete is reported rather than repaired), the atomic file replace that keeps the replaced file's attributes, the `config edit` cancellation that ends the editor's whole process tree, and the maintenance read-only reopen of a keyed database under a drive-letter path holding a space, a percent sign and a hash, which is the only test that hands the `file:///C%3A/...` immutable URI spelling to the real SQLite (the separator seam pins the spelling itself on every platform, and the Windows lanes exercise the immutable URI against the real provider, and both Windows lanes select this case by its exact name). Compendium retains its destination-permission hardening case on both Windows architectures. Windows canaries and the real-credential opt-in are enabled, and both lanes assert that the SDK's host RID is the lane's own RID and set `ARCANUM_EXPECTED_WINDOWS_RID`, which `WindowsCiSurfaceTests` compares with the runtime RID and the process and OS architecture. The workflow contract pins that selection; unrelated portable cases continue under the full macOS runtime suite. **Both Windows lanes require the AppContainer success path and real-DACL round trip.** `WindowsAppContainerBrokerTests` re-executes a published apphost (the xunit host cannot broker), so each lane publishes `RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Cli.exe` for its own RID before the suite and exports its path as `ARCANUM_PUBLISHED_EXECUTABLE`; without that variable the class skips, which is why the publish step and the export are pinned by `ContinuousIntegrationWorkflowTests`. `WindowsAppContainerAclTests` is the real-DACL round trip. The broker smoke compares the root's DACL through `WindowsDaclText`: it keeps every ACE and the `P` and `AR` control flags and drops only `SE_DACL_AUTO_INHERITED` (`AI`), which Windows sets on any DACL written through `SetAccessControl` with inheritance propagation and which plays no part in an access check. The ACL round trips that grant and remove first persist the root's current protection choice, so Windows' one-time addition of `AI` has already happened, and then compare the complete descriptor exactly; a fresh root's round trip preserves the exact ACL bytes and every other control flag, allowing only that addition; and the purge-refusal case, where nothing may write the DACL, compares the exact text (`WindowsDaclText.Exact`). The security-capabilities attribute is passed under the `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE` key that `WindowsProcThreadAttribute` builds from the SDK's recipe, which `WindowsProcThreadAttributeTests` pins on every host; a wrong key makes the broker refuse its own setup with exit 73. Success-path qualification requires both Windows lanes to pass the smoke for the exact candidate. **Both Windows lanes also qualify the Long Rest natively.** After the SDK assertion (`Assert the SDK is native to <rid>`, whose `dotnet --info` output is kept as `sdk-info.txt`), a `Test Long Rest` step runs every `RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Tests.LongRest.*` and `Intelligence.LongRest*` test plus `WindowsCiSurfaceTests.Windows_ci_lane_uses_the_expected_native_runtime_identifier`, excluding the `Perf`, `HostedProducerAnalysis` and `LongRestScaleProbe` categories (the scale probe is opt-in and always skips in CI, and the step fails on any skip), with a TRX logger. The step fails unless the results exist and all passed with none skipped, fifteen named contract classes executed, and the canonical-grammar vector (`LongRestPolicyTests.The_durable_canonical_grammar_matches_an_independently_encoded_fixture`) and the native-identity test ran. The TRX and SDK info are uploaded as `windows-long-rest-win-x64` and `windows-long-rest-win-arm64` (always, kept 14 days, and an empty upload fails); `ContinuousIntegrationWorkflowTests` pins the filter, the logger, the artifact and the step order. **Every exact `FullyQualifiedName=` entry in `ci.yml` is resolved against the real test code** (`Every_exact_windows_filter_names_an_existing_test_method` loads the Arcanum test assembly and reads the Compendium test sources, and `Every_contains_filter_in_ci_matches_at_least_one_test_method` does the same for the class-level `FullyQualifiedName~` entries), because a `dotnet test` filter alternative that matches nothing is not an error and a renamed Windows test would otherwise drop out of the only Windows evidence silently.

The shared producer proof evaluates Release compiler inputs without a RID across Core, Secrets, Infrastructure, Api and Cli: source files, constants, reference paths, source generators, additional files and editor configuration. These projects have no OS-conditioned C# source selection; native asset `Content` and publish-only settings do not alter that compiler graph. All relevant jobs consume the same run-resolved stable SDK, subject to the serviced minimum in `global.json`. Native Windows ARM64 separately runs the existing `ProductionCompilationsResolveGeneratedJsonSymbols`, `ProductionCompilerGraphUsesCanonicalProjectReferences` and `ProductionIncludesEveryFirstPartyDependencyAndApiCliRoots` checks. They validate real Windows compilation/generation, references and project closure without invoking producer-root discovery. They are a bounded portability smoke, not a byte-for-byte compiler-input equivalence proof. The complete canonical analysis remains mandatory even when those three checks pass. After the existing explicit vocabulary and reviewed-member checks, a selected ordinary authored extern with an actual source declaration and no executable body receives the existing unclassified-boundary diagnostic and refuses traversal completion. This source-only check excludes interface, abstract, partial and accessor members; exact native classifications and reviewed exemptions retain their existing precedence.

The delivery runner adds bounded parallelism without weakening test assertions. Every method that can initialize the shared production compilation/site graph carries `HostedProducerProductionAnalysis` and runs serially in exactly one process. Within that process, production discovery can use up to three isolated traversal graphs over the same immutable compilations. Each graph prepares the complete catalogue and owns its semantic models, caches and mutable analysis state. A bounded queue assigns whole existing root-budget families, retaining lifecycle/declared occurrences and their original order on the same worker; the 8,192-state and other proof limits hold for every root whatever the scheduling. Exact ordinal scheduling hints prioritize the measured offline-transition startup-recovery, full installation-reset, and Grimoire database-startup families in that order; unmatched families retain original relative order, and proof results still use original occurrence identities rather than execution order. Serial mode keeps its original traversal order. Every planned occurrence must complete exactly once or discovery fails. After joining, the coordinator combines lifecycle reachability and owner associations for whole-catalogue validation, then runs the original ordered external-caller pass against the global stable-site set, routing each external root back to its budget-family owner. Stable sites, diagnostics and counters are aggregated deterministically. Main production discovery and additional-root discovery have no scheduling dependency; the partitioned CI workers may execute them independently, while full standalone mode retains both proof sets in its complete selection.

One planned declared whole-root occurrence may reuse an earlier, fully completed automatic lifecycle occurrence in the same graph and authority family. Both existing context binders and environment projections still run. Reuse requires the original whole syntax with no partial selection on that member, the exact assembly/compilation/tree/member and complete environment, and every retained frontier, publication and completion input. Lifecycle remains part of ordinary state identity; the directed root lookup creates no declared-state alias. Private completion facts propagate incomplete children and cached results independently of site evidence. Cycles, cutoffs, unknown dispatch/callback/cleanup, exceptions and entered bounded-data rollback proofs prevent reuse. Delegated recovery-target resolution also refuses this witness because its cached target array has no completion fact. Both outer occurrences retain progress/finally accounting; a reused repeat admits zero new states, while source sites, admission failures, lifecycle coverage and final validation remain intact. Nested, external, reversed, probe and cross-graph paths cannot use this whole-root witness. A separate, one-way nested lookup may reuse a freshly completed body beneath an incomplete automatic root only during its later exact planned declared occurrence. It preserves the complete root and child identities, original raw child path, earlier occurrence and entire active ancestor state set; current binding, projections, depth and cycle guards still run. Pending nested witnesses seal only on normal automatic-root return and are discarded on exception. Any ordinary cache hit or directed reuse makes that enclosing subtree ineligible to publish a new raw-path witness, without discarding earlier fresh siblings or changing ordinary completion/evidence. Partial or independent lanes invalidate the cohort. Entry into either bounded-data proof helper permanently disables all new nested publication and lookup in that graph, including previously sealed witnesses and cached proof paths. The shared state cap holds throughout.

Closed-enum forwarding retains a finite compiler-selected substitution in the existing concrete-binding slots: one ordinary static authored method type parameter, constrained by `struct` and authenticated `System.Enum`, with nongeneric containing types and a closed nongeneric enum. A forwarded caller-own type parameter permits one already-certified lookup; conflicting, open, converted or unsupported generic shapes retain conservative value-source traversal. Partial expression projection preserves that certified own-type slot even when the expression does not spell the type parameter. It takes no part in value/ref provenance demand, state identity, cache semantics or proof budgets. The managed-source enum-copy contract is conditional source evidence, not native intrinsic execution proof. Exact demand may omit only an authenticated immediate byte-by-value read from the sole owned enum-T parameter through the selected CoreLib 10 or System.Runtime 10 `Unsafe.As<T, byte>` profile. Every other executable parameter use, non-immediate/ref alias, mutation, escape, lookalike or unsupported signature retains demand; compiler `nameof` is the only additional permitted mention. Ordinary dependent enum edges require direct finite own-T forwarding, captured edges remain conservative, and every binder separately requires the explicit selected-call enum certificate and an eligible source form. Excluded wrappers, local aliases and uncertified substitutions retain their original sources. Independent demands and all authored guards/effects still traverse; this is neither a global Unsafe allowance nor a native-lowering claim. A selected property ingress can omit only its receiving enum fallback after a positive finite source proof: an executable authored nonvirtual getter on a sealed nongeneric container or a compiler-implicit positional getter on a source sealed nongeneric record class whose associated property, primary-constructor parameter, ordinal, type and containing record identities match in the admitted compilation, a direct same-member by-value receiver or independently stable uncaptured local. Its original two-method grammar requires one immediately returned own-T forwarding edge and the authenticated immediate byte-copy leaf. A separate fixed ten-role grammar accepts the copied byte-to-uint tail only when all selected source bodies match: the receiving byte local and three zero-range branches, immediate owned-copy leaf with its size/support guard, support predicate, three type-equality predicates, 47-type positive predicate, positive-range helper, ten-branch maximum helper and range expression. All roles must be distinct ordinary static authored definitions in the same nongeneric type, tree and compilation, with exact own-T selected slots and complete statement/use coverage. The proof authenticates framework Type equality, SizeOf and exception constructors, fitting literal-to-byte conversions, byte-to-Int32 comparisons and byte-to-UInt32 result flow; it never evaluates a predicate or skips a branch or throw. Extra statements, byte mutation/escape/capture, ref aliases, concrete substitutions on an own-T edge, cycles, user operators/conversions and unresolved or bodyless roles refuse. Every original enum-formal use is inventoried, including nested callable syntax; extra uses, captures, aliases, conversions, unresolved or bodyless dependent calls refuse. Every true exact demand is a veto, the selected closed type slots are kept, and the caller, getter and effect traversal is the ordinary one. The ten-role certificate covers direct property calls into the extracted GetCode tail, including the independently authenticated generated positional getter; declared and child lanes remain observations. A separate fixed outer-wrapper certificate admits two explicit identity by-value arguments only when the whole ordinary static own-T/string-to-uint body is one try that returns the result of the ten-role child as it is and one exact framework Exception catch: the filter is the original ArgumentException-or-ArgumentOutOfRangeException type pattern, and its only statement throws the authenticated ArgumentOutOfRangeException(string message, Exception innerException) with the original string formal and catch local through the observed implicit exception upcast. The enum formal has exactly one selected child-argument use, the string exactly one constructor use, and the catch local exactly its filter and constructor uses; aliases, mutation, extra statements or filters, finally, alternate catch types and unaccounted operations refuse. The selected child alone becomes its own proof root in the same compilation with both closed own-T and enum-formal slots retained; its same-tree, same-container and distinct-role rules apply to it. Both ingress argument-count checks require this same complete selected-call certificate for two arguments. Ordinary string binding, independent true demands and all argument, caller, factory, getter, constructor and effect traversal proceed as for any call. The receiving certificate applies to the selected copied enum argument independently of unrelated uses of its original receiver; this does not certify general enum/numeric purity, native execution or a cached false demand.

Copied-enum ingress requires the selected argument to pass its own exact getter, receiver, selected formal, fresh finite binding and complete receiving-grammar certificate. A separate receiver comparison, capture, escape or later reassignment does not invalidate that already copied enum value. Those operations retain their original caller and source traversal, as do uncertified getters and receiving targets; an unsupported or mutated own-T formal still retains its own source contexts. This finite per-argument proof does not recurse through binding or demand analysis and does not change the original caller/getter traversal, true-demand veto, retained own-type slots, state identity, caches, frontiers or budgets.

Expression dependency queries exclude operands only when the current semantic model identifies a compiler `INameOfOperation`. Runtime siblings, surrounding call arguments, member accesses and ordinary same-spelling `@nameof` methods retain their existing source-dependency analysis; unknown or invalid operations keep the existing traversal. This naming distinction grants no general constant purity or change to effect/site traversal, binding identities, caches or proof budgets.


Recovery metadata has one conservative execution fallback. When source contains an exact recovery dispatch, a `LongRunningOperation` construction, or an owner-recovery catalogue root, the coordinator precomputes immutable matrix facts without resolving the matrix, emitting diagnostics, or activating owner validation. A valid matrix retains the requested parallel traversal. Invalid applicable metadata uses the original serial traversal before any additional graph is created, preserving diagnostic first-use ordering and bounded-data probe rollback exactly; no root, validation or limit is skipped. Ordinary inputs without those source triggers still use the requested workers even when their reference pack includes production assemblies. Metrics expose the selected root-worker count so parity tests verify both real parallel paths and the serial fallback. Primary discovery and the focused additional-root discovery have independent immutable compiler inputs and graph state; neither initializes or waits for the other. Their CI partitions may therefore execute on separate hosts without changing roots, limits, diagnostics, manifests or proof assertions.

`ARCANUM_HOSTED_ANALYSIS_ROOT_WORKERS` accepts exactly `1`, `2` or `3`; absence selects serial discovery and invalid values fail explicitly. The runner sets this only for production children and removes inherited values from fixture children. Its `--jobs`/`ARCANUM_ANALYSIS_JOBS` value remains total scheduled analysis capacity: production reserves up to three slots, fixtures one each, and excess shards wait for capacity. With one slot the combined lane remains serial; with two or three, fixtures queue behind production; with four, production's three internal workers overlap one fixture process. Independent synthetic fixture methods are balanced by discovered theory-case count, so production discovery is not repeated in fixture shards. A local machine uses up to sixteen slots while reserving two logical processors; `ARCANUM_ANALYSIS_JOBS` can lower that value from one through sixteen. Each production worker uses two slots and runs only its production process (primary the unmarked methods, additional the marked ones), and each fixture worker uses one slot and runs one fixture process, with no root-worker or progress variable set. Windows does not repeat the production traversal or fixture suite. Each partition's complete discovery plus execution has one hard sixty-minute ceiling (the runner accepts a deadline of at most 3,600 seconds); CI reserves the final minute of each window for runner cleanup by passing a 3,540-second deadline, under a 60-minute step timeout inside an 80-minute job timeout that also covers the checkout and the build. Cancellation, startup failure, deadline expiry, SIGTERM, or Ctrl+C terminates and reaps the runner's complete `dotnet`/VSTest/testhost process groups. A denied or already-inaccessible child is reported per process without preventing cleanup of the remaining children or replacing the primary timeout/interruption failure. Windows children launch suspended, enter a kill-on-close Job Object, and only then resume, so cleanup still owns testhost descendants after the top-level `dotnet` process exits.

**Headroom Tripwire.** A root the checker refuses for size (`HOSTED_TRAVERSAL_STATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` at 8,192 states) reports nothing about the sites below the cut, so the size of a root is a property of the gate and not of its speed. `Every_production_root_stays_within_its_ratchet_ceiling` (production lane, over the shared `ProductionSiteDiscovery`, never a second discovery) holds every primary root to a committed ceiling in `HostedGrimoireProducerInventoryTests.Headroom.cs`, and `Every_additional_root_stays_within_its_ratchet_ceiling` holds every root of the additional partition to a table of its own in the same file, over the shared `AdditionalProductionSiteDiscovery` (its roots do not vary with the arrangement of root workers, and the largest is 3,119 states, `CovenantLaunchGapFactoryResetRecoveryHandler.RecoverAsync`). Each ceiling is: the largest count any arrangement of root workers (one, two or three) reports for the root, plus five percent with a floor of eight states, rounded up to a multiple of eight, and never more than ninety percent of the cap (7,372). The ceiling is therefore a maximum over the three arrangements: the default run is serial, the production lanes in CI run two root workers, and a discovery under any of the three is judged against the same table, so a test at the CI worker count passes wherever the serial and three-worker counts do only while every row is taken from the largest of the three. Measured on 2026-10-17 on the tree this document describes, under one, two and three root workers (the three discoveries reported the same 6,729 primary and 1,491 additional sites and no diagnostic), the two Long Rest roots, `LongRestMaintenance.ProcessAdmittedAsync` (root type `LongRestSweepHostedService`) and `LongRestSweepHostedService.ExecuteAsync`, stand at 5,493 and 3,654 states in every arrangement, and their rows are the rule's maximum plus the margin, 5,768 and 3,840, with the reason stated beside them; every other row of both tables equals its maximum over the three plus the margin, and the largest ceiling is 7,200 of the 7,372 the cap allows. A root the discovery reports that has no row, a row that names no root, a repeated row or root, a root above its ceiling and a ceiling above ninety percent each fail, and fixtures pin each refusal. A ceiling follows the measured count of its root: a change that makes a root cheaper lowers its row in the same change, and a change that makes one dearer raises it only after the change has earned the room, only to the rule (the maximum plus the margin), never past the ninety percent bound, and with the reason beside the row. The cap itself is frozen (`LimitsAreFrozen` reads the six budgets, the cap, the environment member and depth bounds, the traversal depth bound, the three work budgets of 256, the callable-mutation budget of 256, and the defaults the production entry passes, from the code). A selection root such as `StartAsync::call:...#0~<digest>` is named without its digest, which the capsule manifest already pins. The count of a root is not always the same from one arrangement to the next, which is why the ceiling is a maximum. A root that a lease-handoff or a self-admitted task handoff re-roots into is entered once from its own declaration and once from the traversal that hands off to it, with different frontiers. Under one worker both entries share one state cache and the closure is admitted for each distinct entry; under two or three workers an entry that lands on another worker admits its own, and which worker a family lands on is decided by timing, so one run reports the sum and the next only one of the two (in the measurement above `ApprenticeService.RunApprenticeAsync` analysed 3,090 states under one worker and 1,545 under two and under three, and `InitializeGlobalAsync` 484 under one and three and 242 under two; two other discoveries of near-identical trees reported `RunApprenticeAsync` at 1,545 under three workers and `InitializeGlobalAsync` at 484 under each in one, and `RunApprenticeAsync` at 3,090 under three workers and `InitializeGlobalAsync` at 242 under two in the other: the count under a given number of workers is itself decided by timing, so another discovery of the same tree can report the pooled count where this one reports the sum). The serial count is the union of the entries and so is never smaller than a pooled count, and a one-, a two- and a three-worker discovery of the same tree must report the same sites and diagnostics (a proof of no change is run at two workers as well as at one and three, because two is what CI runs); the ceiling is taken from the largest of the three. State containment: every rule that removes a binding from a state's identity does so only for a binding nothing in the member's closure reads, and each has a fixture that keeps the binding when something does (the foreign parameter of an ordinary method for a member that cannot be nested, a constant by value, a cancellation token, a payload that is only moved, the receiver of `CreateParameter`). The shipped graph reports 6,729 primary and 1,491 additional sites and no diagnostic, with the largest primary root at 6,856 states (the pre-bootstrap transition recovery) and the second at 6,266 (the attested full reset, whose shared data step reaches the stopped-host fresh and resume arms' steps as well). The stopped-host reset's own roots stand at 5,864 states (the resumed apply), 5,011 (the fresh apply) and 1,369 (the reset-only erasure facade), each the same under one, two and three root workers, and the Grimoire's start stands at 5,620. Remeasured on 2026-10-22 for the Comprehension format extractors under one, two and three root workers (each discovery reported the committed 6,863 primary sites and no diagnostic), `SessionAttachmentIndexingService.ExecuteAsync` stands at 3,066 states in every arrangement, because the extraction host's detached parser callback reaches the seven format extractors and their package, XML and walker members; its row is 3,224 (3,066 plus 154, rounded up to a multiple of eight), and every other primary and additional row equals its unchanged maximum plus the margin. Remeasured on 2026-10-23 for PDF text-layer extraction under one, two and three root workers (each discovery reported the regenerated 6,870 primary sites and no diagnostic), `SessionAttachmentIndexingService.ExecuteAsync` stands at 3,192 states in every arrangement, because the isolated PDF path adds the external effect group, the authenticated snapshot read inside it and the worker seam's provider call; its row is 3,352 (3,192 plus 160, a multiple of eight), and every other primary row measured its unchanged maximum. Remeasured on 2026-10-23 after every document host was given one shared reserve-and-read step, with the parse the only per-host code, under one, two and three root workers (the three-worker regeneration reported the regenerated 6,865 primary sites and no diagnostic), `SessionAttachmentIndexingService.ExecuteAsync` falls from 3,192 to 3,188 states in every arrangement, because the snapshot read is analysed before the extraction's effect group is begun, not inside it, and both hosts reach the one shared read; 3,188 plus the margin is still 3,352 (3,188 plus 160, rounded up to a multiple of eight), so its row stays at 3,352, and every other primary row measured its unchanged maximum. Remeasured on 2026-10-23 after the isolated worker kinds became format-neutral and the in-process parse observed the fault of cancelling a source it had already disposed, under one, two and three root workers (the one-worker discovery matched the committed 6,865-row manifest with no diagnostic), `SessionAttachmentIndexingService.ExecuteAsync` grows from 3,188 to 3,192 states in every arrangement: two states are the isolated host reading its heading and verdict reasons from its format's worker profile, and two are the continuation by which the in-process host's cancellation request observes that fault, which the checker enters as an asynchronous callback (with that request alone restored, the root measured 3,190); 3,192 plus the margin is still 3,352 (3,192 plus 160), so its row stays at 3,352, and every other primary row measured its unchanged maximum under one worker.

The primary partition measured on 2026-10-20 reports 6,833 sites and no diagnostic under one, two and three root workers. A readonly-field initializer uses its own authored semantic model and syntax identity while retaining the constructor's bound arguments, including when an implicit constructor is reached from another compilation. An initializer whose tree is not analyzed fails closed. Cross-compilation fixtures require the effectful initializer to remain visible and its quiet counterpart to remain quiet; primary discovery separately requires exact agreement with the 6,859-row manifest and the committed headroom table.

**Manifest Regeneration Protocol and the Diff Row Classifier.** The reviewed capsule manifest (`hosted-grimoire-producer-capsules-v1.tsv`; one row is one site seen from one root: the root, the site, and the frame, which is the Work capsule, the Effect capsule and the admitted work kind) is both what `ReviewedCapsuleManifestExactlyMatchesProductionDiscovery` compares the whole primary discovery with and the catalog `EveryDiscoveredProducerSiteIsCataloguedExactlyOnce` reads. Only that test writes it, with `ARCANUM_UPDATE_HOSTED_PRODUCER_CAPSULES=1`, only when the discovery has no diagnostic of any code (a discovery with one writes nothing and fails), and once for a change, because a regeneration is reviewed and not trusted. A frame column holds the capsule id of the acquisition or group site it names, and a capsule id is the SHA-256 of that site's own source path, member identity, kind, callee, syntax ordinal and syntax fingerprint, so every reference resolves inside the manifest that carries it. The review is `python3 scripts/classify-manifest-diff.py --committed <old manifest> --regenerated <new manifest> --git-base <revision the old manifest was regenerated for> --parity <parity manifest>`, which labels every row the regeneration adds or removes (a row changed in its frame is a removed row and an added row that share their site) and exits non-zero when one is unexplained. The parity manifest is what the same checker renders over the base source: the test assembly is built at the head, `src/` is replaced by the base revision (the files added since are deleted), and the shared production discovery is run without a rebuild and rendered with `RenderCapsuleManifest` (the checker reads the production source at run time, so the swap is what changes the analysed program). A discovery over the base source reports diagnostics of its own, because the base lacks types the head's roots name and carries shapes the head's rules refuse (94 in the parity run of 2026-10-15, none of them a limit: the two Long Rest roots and the strategy binding whose types the base lacks, two receiver mismatches, the missing and unproven Effects of group shapes the head's rules refuse, and eleven unclassified or unproven callback sites in shapes the head's rules refuse); only its rows are read. With it the cause of a row is known by construction: the old manifest (C) and the parity run (P) share the source and the new manifest (N) and P share the checker, so an added row that P also has was introduced by the checker and one it does not have by the source, and a removed row that P lacks was removed by the checker and one P still has by the source. A row of the source is `a` (its own site is in an edited source), `b` (its Work or Effect capsule names an acquisition, group or Root Lease Formal site in an edited source, in its own manifest or in that of the row it is paired with by site) or `r` (a site and frames in unedited sources that an edited call reaches, and only when a reviewed table of such calls, `REACHED_THROUGH`, names the row's root and site and the edited file whose call reaches it: the text the call is spelled with has to be in that file at the head and not at the base, or, for a removed row, at the base and not at the head; the tool does not infer a call chain, so a row of this kind that no entry explains is `d`, and the reviewed entries are the Covenant coordinator's two calls to `BackupRestorePhysicalTopology.Reconcile`, which reaches `ProveAbsent`, and the three causes by which the attested full reset's closure moved when the stopped-host reset became the protected erasure: it reaches the stopped-host executor's measured-inventory plan and its reset-only erasure facade, and it does not reach the recovery of an unfinished row by summary match that the executor ran before); `n` is a row of a root the old manifest did not have that the classifier's `NEW_ROOTS` names, which is the root reviewed and not its rows one by one, because the old manifest holds no row of it to compare with (the three roots the checker's non-hosted catalog gained for the stopped-host reset, `InstallationResetService.ApplyFreshUnderMaintenanceLockAsync` and `ApplyUnderMaintenanceLockAsync` and `StoppedHostFactoryErasure.ApplyAsync`, each with its reason); `b-format` is a pair that differs only by the `@lease:` marker an Effect id carries (none in the regenerations below, because the manifest holds capsule ids and not Effect ids). A row of the checker must match the predicate of a named rule or it is `d`, unexplained, and the review requires none. The rules are the footprints of five lanes, each with a positive and a negative twin in `scripts/tests/test_classify_manifest_diff.py` and each type it names checked there against the product source: `interceptor-and-state-handler-callbacks` (Interceptor and Logger Lane, Connection State Handlers: an added row whose enclosing type is `CovenantConnectionEnrolmentInterceptor`, `CovenantSqliteConnectionInitializer` or `CovenantConnectionDrain`, the seven site keys Effect on the Shipped Graph names), `base-constructor-initializers` (Implicit Call Census: an added `FileSystemEffect` or `FileSystemRead` row whose callee is `System.IO.FileStream..ctor` or `System.IO.Stream..ctor`, the `: base(...)` initializer of an authored subclass, at one of three reviewed members that build one, `SecureFileReader.TryOpenRegularFile` (`SecureRegularFileStream`), `GrimoireOfflineTransitionJournalOpenedFile.GetStream` (`RelativeFileStream`) and `DaemonProcessRunner.RunAsync` (`CappedOutputStream`), each checked against the source: the member names the subclass and the subclass is declared as deriving from that base, while a direct `new FileStream(...)` is no entry and its row is `d`), `runtime-type-dispatch` (Accessors and virtual methods the runtime type selects, Reviewed Closed Override Sets: an added row whose enclosing type is an `Infrastructure.Security` file primitive that the secret stores and the `CredentialMirror` set write through (`FileHandleIdentityInterop`, `MirroredOsCredential`, `OwnerOnlyAtomicFile`, (`FileStream`, `File.Open*`, `File.Create*`, `OpenHandle`), because the stream is not a file; a file-backed stream anywhere in the member leaves the row `d`). **In-Memory Package Readers and Recursive Parsers.** The in-process Comprehension format extractors (every format but PDF, below) are reached from `SessionAttachmentIndexingService.ExecuteAsync` through the extraction host's detached parser callback, so every member they call is judged like any other. They read only memory, and the checker proves it rather than reviewing the framework readers by name. A `DeflateStream` (`IsReviewedInMemoryInflaterMember`) is no producer when its constructor's stream has in-memory provenance (the rule a `StreamReader` already follows) and when a read or its cleanup is on an inflater so built; over a file stream it stays refused. An `XmlReader` reads and releases whatever stream it was handed, so `XmlReader.Create(Stream, XmlReaderSettings)`, `Read`, `Value` and `Dispose` are no producers only under `IsReviewedInMemoryXmlReaderMember`: `Create` over an in-memory stream (a `MemoryStream` creation, or an authored static method whose every return is one) with settings built in place that clear the resolver, refuse or ignore a DOCTYPE and set nothing outside a reviewed set (no resolver, validation type or schemas), and `Read`, `Value` and `Dispose` on the `Reader` of `BoundedXmlReader` (directly, or through a local or a readonly field holding only it), when that type is closed over such a reader: sealed, one declaration, a get-only auto-property `Reader` each of its private, non-chaining constructors sets once from its own parameter, and every construction (only the type itself can make one) handing that parameter such a `Create`. The `XmlReader` members that only report the node already read (`NodeType`, `LocalName`, `NamespaceURI`, `Depth`, `IsEmptyElement`, `EOF`, `HasValue`, `GetAttribute`, `LookupNamespace`) and the `XmlReaderSettings` option bag are reviewed by name, `ArraySegment<T>` and `StringBuilder.ChunkEnumerator` are intrinsic and closed enumerations, `MemoryMarshal.TryGetArray` and the `ReadOnlySpan<T>` constructors are bounded intrinsic members, `double.TryParse` over a character span is held to the exact invariant provider its string overload already is, and the sink the extractors write to is a reviewed closed dispatch (`ISessionAttachmentDocumentTextSink.TryAppend` and `MarkTruncated` to `BoundedDocumentTextSink`, the one implementation). Fixtures pin each rule and each premise's refusal (a parsed DOCTYPE, a resolver, a validation type, a file stream, settings changed after they are built, a public or unsealed reader type, a settable `Reader`, a `Value` read from a reader `BoundedXmlReader` did not make). Three checker rules keep the recursive parsers analysable. The value of a call that `RecoveryValue` reads from its returns is unknown when the guarding condition of one of those returns calls back into a member whose returns are already being read (`ReadShapes` and `ReadShape` of the Visio reader each return from under a call to the other), so the evaluation of a mutually recursive pair ends. The transitive producer-site scan settles a member it has finished without finding a site and does not scan it again from another path in the same scan, which is plain reachability while every path the scan ends meets the member with the bindings the path holds; a scan that ends a path at a member held with other bindings and finds nothing is scanned again path by path, so the answer is the path-by-path answer either way, and a recursive group of members (the Wordprocessing walker is one) is scanned once per member rather than once per path through it. A detached callback must reach no producer site, and a re-entry of a state the callback's own traversal is already in, by a call that names exactly that member on the same instance or statically, adds no evidence, which is the least fixpoint over the states the callback reaches; a re-entry through a dispatch or on another instance (a decorator whose inner store the model cannot tell from itself, as the OS credential store is, which keeps the bounded OS credential read a reviewed exception) and a re-entry of a state that was in progress before the callback began stay inconclusive, and when the callback reaches evidence after all, every state whose evidence left a re-entry out is recorded as inconclusive, so no later traversal reads the evidence it left out. Two production shapes keep the readers provable: `BoundedXmlReader.Create` leaves the `MemoryStream` it built to the collector when the reader fails to open (an explicit `Stream.Dispose` is a file-system effect by its static type, and the stream holds nothing to release), and `SessionAttachmentComprehensionPolicy.TryGetFormat` walks the registry's own array rather than the read-only collection that wraps it (a collection's enumerator runs whatever list it wraps).

**The Isolated Document Worker Seam.** PDF is the one Comprehension format that is not parsed in this process, and the checker neither reads its parser nor traverses the runner behind it. The isolated host reaches its worker only through `IDocumentExtractionWorker.RunAsync`, one member of the closed external-call vocabulary (the `Vocabulary` table of `HostedGrimoireProducerInventory`) classified `ProviderCall`: the member starts and awaits a child process, owns its limits and teardown, and returns only after the child is gone, which is the shape a paid provider dispatch has. `SessionAttachmentIndexProcessor` names the isolated host by its concrete type and calls it only after `TryBeginExternalEffectGroup`, and names the in-process hosts by theirs, outside any group, so the analysis tells the two paths apart: the worker call is a provider site reached only inside the group, while the in-process parse stays a detached callback that must reach no producer site. `BeginPage` is not a vocabulary member: only the isolated host calls it, on the concrete `BoundedDocumentTextSink`, outside any parser callback, so the sink's reviewed closed dispatch stays `TryAppend` and `MarkTruncated`, both to `BoundedDocumentTextSink`, the one implementation. The vocabulary entry has its row in `EveryClosedVocabularyMemberIsDiscovered` (the member is found where it is called), and the scoped production probe `ProductionAttachmentExtractionRetainsItsExactAdmittedLifetime` asserts that the isolated host's `ProviderCall` site is present, that `CappedChildProcessRunner` is not traversed, and that the root reports no diagnostic. The new Infrastructure sources enter the input catalog and the capsule manifest through the Manifest Regeneration Protocol above.

Progress is both live and durable. The console prints `[analysis completed/total]` for every terminal test result and start/complete records for each production root. With the existing `ARCANUM_HOSTED_ANALYSIS_PROGRESS` opt-in, `HOSTED_PHASE_PROGRESS` also records external-invocation scan counts (every 1,024 inspected calls), each worker's `complete-discovery`, parallel `merge`, and additional-root preparation/traversal. Phase records carry stage, worker, count, total and elapsed time; worker zero denotes coordination. A phase emits `complete` only after its work finishes, and interrupted scopes emit `error`. A final root completion does not imply the external invocation scan or whole discovery completed. Root and state records include the isolated worker and planned occurrence identifiers; writes to the shared progress file are serialized. Each partition's `.tmp/coverage/analysis/` retains a combined log, one log and TRX per shard, `hosted-producer-roots.log`, and `hosted-producer-analysis-receipt.json`; CI uploads that entire directory even on failure. The receipt binds the exact source SHA, complete typed universe, additional, serve-host and build-fixture subsets, selection and shard declarations. The authority downloads all five artifacts and emits `hosted-producer-analysis-summary.json` only after reconciliation: the five receipts must name the same universe, the same additional subset, the same serve-host subset and the same build-fixture subset, each must select exactly what its partition's rule selects, and every method and case must be selected by exactly one partition. Receipts are schema 3 (they carry the serve-host and build-fixture subsets). Its schema-3 `partitionAccounting` records exact case totals and SHA-256 hashes of canonical sorted method and expanded case multisets: method records are `kind`, fully qualified method name and duplicate occurrence; case records append the zero-based case occurrence. TRX remains authoritative for the final gate: every selected result must exist exactly once and have outcome `Passed`. Console parsing is used only for human progress, so test output or a receipt-only success flag cannot forge a green gate.

**Verification Speed.** The Serve fixtures (`ServeBuildMutationHasExplicitConditionalSourceAssociation`, `ServeCompositionMutationHasExplicitConditionalSourceAssociation`, `ServeScopedConsumerHasExplicitConditionalSourceOrigin`, `ServeWorkerMutationHasExplicitConditionalSourceAssociation` and the two canonical ones) each analyse the production compilations with one or two trees replaced, so each case is a whole discovery, and the lanes that hold them (`serve-host` and `fixtures-build`) are the sum of those cases. The callback judgement of the sites-only graph (`FrameworkValuesRunAuthoredCallbacks`) is what a case would spend almost all of its time in without the rules below: in the profiled case it was 119 of 151 thread CPU seconds, because for each of 68 distinct carrier types and families it asks every one of about 2,000 authored formatters, for every type a generated record member reaches, whether the formatter is assignable to the type and implements the slot (343 million asks, each rendering display names), and it asks again for every implementation unless the answers of one implementation are reused by the next type that asks. The same judgement also holds every worker of a production discovery behind the sites-only graph's lock. Nothing else in a case costs more than about ten seconds. Without the indexes below the production traversal itself (thread CPU, three root workers) spends a fifth of its time in questions that are answered by passing over the whole program: the call sites of a method are found by binding every invocation of the program and comparing method identities, the constructors of a type by testing every member, and the implementers of an interface method by testing every member against every interface it has. Five rules cut the work; each is an exact equivalence with the loop it replaces, and none caches anything that depends on a binding, a frontier or evidence.

- **Formatter Index.** The authored formatters are indexed once per graph by every type they are assignable to and by the slots they implement, as ascending positions in the order the list has. The candidates of a receiver type and a slot are the formatters assignable to the receiver (`IsFormatterAssignableTo`: any object, any value, any type parameter, or a formatter whose assignable names hold the receiver's original definition) that have a callback of the slot (`FormatterRunsSlot`: the virtual reads a framework `ToString` makes, or an implementation of the slot, compared by kind, name, containing type, assembly and arity as `SameEnumerationSlot` compares two symbols). Reading the intersection of two ascending lists selects the formatters the loop selected, in its order. `TheFormatterCandidateIndexSelectsExactlyWhatItsDefinitionSelects` compares the two over a wide sample of production receivers and slots, and fails on the first pair that differs.
- **Formatting Steps.** One resolution of the members a value runs (a collector and the nested collectors that share its visited set) takes each step, a slot of a type, once. Taking it again adds no member and no framework method, because every member the first step reached is in the visited set, so the second is skipped before it asks for the implementation. It could add one thing only: a repeated name in `Unresolved`, because `Add` (and `AddSynthesizedByName`, in its default and `<Clone>$` branches) names a slot it cannot resolve before the visited set is asked, so a retaken step that does not resolve would append the same name again. That is harmless because `Unresolved` is consumed only as a set (`Distinct`, as in the detail of a refusal) or as a test for empty (`Count != 0`, `Count == 0`), never as a count, and `UnresolvedIsOnlyReadAsASetOrTestedForEmpty` pins it: it reads the checker's own sources and refuses any read of an `Unresolved` member that is anything else (a count compared with a number other than zero, an element, an indexer, a LINQ count, a sum), with twins that are refused and twins that are accepted. A step is the pair of symbols, never a name.
- **Implementation Answers.** Whether the members one authored implementation of a callback slot runs can reach a producer site is a function of the implementation, the slot and the anchor member alone; the resolution starts from the implementation in a collector of its own. The anchor is the whole `AuthoredMember` and not its syntax, because the answer reads its model, the bindings its classification consults and its syntax: two members made over the same syntax with other bindings are two keys. The answer is remembered for every type and family that asks, under the rule the answer for a type already follows: it is stored only when no cycle cut was counted while it was computed, and an answer computed under a cut is computed again. The answer for a type is the answer of the implementations judged for the anchor, so its key holds the anchor itself (by reference, as the key of an implementation does) beside the type's display and the families, and so does the set that detects a cycle: a second anchor never reads the answer of the first, at either level. `TheAnswersForAnImplementationAreKeyedByTheWholeAnchorMember` and `TheAnswersForAnAuthoredTypeAreKeyedByTheWholeAnchorMember` pin the two keys, and `TheCallbackJudgementResolvesEachProductionImplementationOnce` pins the work (an implementation is resolved at most once, a second receiver that asks about the same implementations resolves none, and the steps are bounded by a small multiple of the implementations) and compares the answers with resolving every implementation from scratch whichever way the production source falls, not with a constant.
- **Shared Semantic Models.** The semantic model of a tree in a compilation is a function of the compilation object and the tree object alone: the references the compilation was made with and the source of the tree decide every answer. The model is therefore made once for the pair and every discovery over the compilation reads that one, so a Serve case finds the Core, Secrets and Infrastructure source bound by the case before it. A compilation made from another (`ReplaceSyntaxTree`, `ReplaceReference`) is another object and reads models of its own, even when it holds the very tree; the models of a compilation the process lets go of are let go with it. Two process-wide tables are shared by discoveries: the models themselves, and the per-model memo of whether a callable written in a member can mutate a symbol between two positions (**Program Indexes**), which is keyed by the model and so is shared by every discovery, xunit collection and root worker that reads that model. Sharing the memo is sound because its computation is static and reads nothing but the member's syntax and the model, the key holds the member's syntax, the symbol and both positions, and a model belongs to one compilation (so does every symbol it returns); concurrent first callers compute the same value. Four more things are shared by the whole process, and each is sound for a reason of its own. The production compilations, the production and additional discoveries over them, the validation of the sources and the reviewed capsule manifest are lazy singletons, built once and then only read. The sites-only graph is one per list of compilations (`sitesOnlyGraphs`, keyed by the list object), so its own memos (the formatter index and the answers for an implementation and for a type, **Formatter Index** and **Implementation Answers**) are shared by every discovery over that list; every use of it is made under its lock, so one thread at a time reads them, and it is only ever asked a question that is a function of the list of compilations and the question alone: whether a member rebuilt over its own syntax with no bindings can reach a site (`SitesOnlyReaches`), whether the implementers of a type and the families a value carries reach one, judged through the graph's own first member as the anchor (`FrameworkValuesRunAuthoredCallbacks`; the type and the families are in the key), and which types' static initialization reaches one. No binding, frontier or evidence of the asking discovery reaches it. The targeted production overlays (`ProductionOverlays`) are keyed by the exact fixture source and the overlay kind and each is built once from the shared production compilations, so a key names its whole input. The names of the Microsoft assemblies the test host has loaded (`hostLoadedAssemblies`) are keyed by the simple name of an assembly, and what the host loaded does not change in a process. Every other table, scan, cache and metric of a graph is its own. `ADiscoveryReadsTheModelOfItsCompilationAndNoOtherCompilationDoes` and `ADiscoveryOverAReplacedTreeNeverReadsTheModelsOfTheCompilationItWasMadeFrom` pin both halves, and a repeated discovery repeats its verdict. The Build scans (the admitted entry census, the checker limit pins, the single gate census and the authority carrier ban) read these same models (`SharedSemanticModels.Of` answers with `HostedGrimoireProducerInventory.ProcessSemanticModel`) instead of a table of their own, because a model keeps everything it has bound and a second table held a second copy of it, and each of those classes lets the models go when it is done (`SemanticModelScope`, an `IClassFixture`): the Serve worker discoveries that follow them in the `fixtures-build` lane analyse compilations of their own and read none of them. A model is made again when the next reader asks, so releasing changes no answer. `SharedSemanticModelsTests` pins that the scans and the checker read one model per tree, that a released model is rebuilt with the same answers, and that every Build class that reads the production compilations carries the scope.
- **Program Indexes.** The sites and the members a graph holds are read when the graph is made and never change, so a question about them is answered from a group, in the order the pass it replaces would have met them. The invocations, object creations and constructor initializers are grouped by the identity of the method they bind to (`ResolveParameter` reads the calls of one method instead of every call); the constructors by the type that declares them (`ExactReadOnlyFieldValues`); and a method's identity is built once per method symbol. Three questions whose answer is a function of their inputs alone are remembered under that key: the members that implement an interface method (key: the method), whether a parameter is ever written (key: the parameter), and, per semantic model, whether a callable written in a member can mutate a symbol between two positions (key: the member's syntax, the symbol and the two positions; the memo lives with the model and is let go with it, and a symbol is a symbol of the compilation its model belongs to). What a constructor does to a field is read once per constructor and field. `TheProgramIndexesAnswerWhatThePassesTheyReplaceAnswer` compares every index and memo with the pass or computation it replaces over a sample of the production source and fails on the first query that differs.

A cache joins this list only with its key spelled out and a fixture that pins the key: the key must contain everything the answer reads (a binding, a frontier, a piece of evidence, an anchor), and an answer computed while a cycle was being cut is never stored. The limits (`LimitsAreFrozen`), the refusals and the scans are untouched, and a change to this section is judged by the outcomes of the three fixture partitions, the sites and diagnostics of both production partitions at one, two and three root workers (two is what CI runs), and the per-root analysed-state counts of the Headroom Tripwire, which must be identical to those before the change, arrangement by arrangement.

**Verification Memory.** A standard `macos-26` runner has three processors and about 7 GB, so a lane is judged by running it as CI runs it (the runner's own command, the same slot count and root-worker count) under `DOTNET_GCHeapHardLimit=0x160000000` (a 5.5 GiB heap) and `DOTNET_PROCESSOR_COUNT=3`. The proxy measures the test host alone, so the workflow keeps every build server off the runner while the analysis runs: each of the five workers builds with `--disable-build-servers` and runs `dotnet build-server shutdown` before the runner starts, because a default build of this test project leaves the Roslyn compiler server and the MSBuild nodes resident (a review saw the compiler server at 5.45 GB, on a machine whose server is shared with other builds, so an upper bound, and ten MSBuild nodes at 0.17 to 0.25 GB each) and none of that is in the figures below. `Source_analysis_workers_leave_no_build_server_resident_while_the_analysis_runs` pins both steps and their order in every worker. The runner's own `dotnet test --no-build` starts no build server (the process list is the same before and after it). The primary production lane's memory is dominated by the caches of cleanup provenance and cleanup value flows (`completeCleanupProvenance`, `completeCleanupValueFlows`). They are keyed by the cleanup binding identity of the member, a string that holds the bindings of every caller in the chain (up to 96,000 characters), built again for every expression asked about and kept in the key of each entry, and about 97 percent of the characters in those keys repeat an earlier key by content; a discovery that keeps every copy grows to a 10 GB heap (6 GB of it large-object-heap strings) and an 11.3 GB resident set unconstrained, and under the proxy ends with `OutOfMemoryException` in the root workers after about 300 s. **Cleanup Binding Pool.** `CleanupIdentity` takes that string from a per-graph pool (`pooledCleanupBindings`), one instance per distinct content, so the keys share it. A key is still compared by content, so the pool changes no answer, site or diagnostic, and `TheKeysOfTheCleanupCachesShareTheStringOfTheBindingsOfAMember` pins the sharing and that a key still equals one made with an unpooled copy. With the pool the discovery peaks at about a 5 GB heap, of which 1.7 GB is fragmentation, and a 6.2 GB resident set unconstrained, and every lane below completes without exceeding the heap limit. The fixture lanes' figures were found with a sampled resident set of the test host beside the runner's progress lines, and the one process that ran both fixture selections before the split was also profiled by live set (a forced collection every few seconds). In that process the production compilations cost about 2.8 GB of live managed memory to the first test that reads them, and the Build scans that follow (the admitted entry census, the checker limit pins, the single gate census and the authority carrier ban) bind every tree of them. What those scans hold when they finish is dead weight for the rest of the lane, because the Serve worker discoveries at its end analyse compilations of their own and read none of it: a platform reference set per class (a reference holds its assembly's metadata in native memory, so that is one image of every platform assembly per class), a table of semantic models beside the checker's (every tree bound and held twice), and the models themselves until the end of the run. The scans read one reference set (**Analyzer fixtures** below) and the checker's models (**Shared Semantic Models**), and each Build scan class lets the models go when it is done, so the `fixtures-build` lane, which runs the Build scans and then the Serve worker discoveries, holds about 4.1 to 4.5 GB through those discoveries and peaks at 4.54 GB (a resident set sample; the split lanes were not live-set profiled). The split cuts the time of the longest fixture lane (619 s as one process, 495 s for `fixtures-build`) and does not cut the peak of the `fixtures` lane, which still reads the production compilations: the fixture partials of `HostedGrimoireProducerInventoryTests` ask them for reference sets and premises, and `MirroredCredentialConstructionTests` (a fifth Build class, which carries `SemanticModelScope` and binds the trees of `ProductionCompilations`, but is not one of the four scan classes of `fixtures-build`) scans every tree of them. The `fixtures` lane, which runs the other 6,088 cases, therefore reaches 5.0 GB after two of its three minutes and peaks at 5.45 GB at its end, about what the two selections together peaked at alone. The peak of a lane under a heap cap moves with when its collections happen: the selection of the two fixture lanes together, run as one process, peaked at 5.35 GB alone on the tree of the table below (**Verification Lanes**). The margin is moderate and is not a measurement of a runner: the largest test host peaks at 5.81 GB (`primary`, one lane at a time; 5.65, 6.12 and 5.81 GB in three runs of the tree), the runner's own `dotnet test`, vstest console and python add about 0.28 GB, and the operating system and the runner agent take a share of about 7 GB. A lane that grew by a GB would need another heap probe like the ones that found the pool, the platform references and the models.

**Verification Lanes.** The five CI lanes, run as CI runs them under the memory proxy above on an Apple M5 Max on 2026-10-17 on the tree this document describes (one lane at a time, on a machine with no other build running), and as a standard `macos-26` runner (three cores, about 7 GB) ran them in CI.
