The deadline of each is 3,540 seconds including the five discoveries of the runner's own tests (about 3 seconds each here, 24 to 58 seconds together on the runner); the share is the runner's wall time over it, and the multiplier beside it is how many times longer the lane could take on the runner and still meet the deadline. The runner is slower than this machine, and not steadily so. In a CI run whose five analysis lanes all passed (GitHub Actions run 39034206699) the lanes took 2.1 to 2.9 times their wall time here, measured from the start of the analysis step to its end: `primary` 1,476 s (24 minutes 36 seconds), `additional` 437 s, `fixtures` 381 s, `fixtures-build` 1,395 s and `serve-host` 1,410 s (the runner column of the table). The one shared production discovery of `primary` took 22 minutes of that, 1,321 s from the first of its 142 root traversals to the last, on two root workers. In a second CI run of the same analysis code (run 39042677321) the `primary` lane exceeded a 1,740-second deadline: the runner reported `exceeded its 1704-second deadline`, which is the 1,740 s less the 36 s its five discoveries had taken, with the production discovery 93 root traversals in, while the other four lanes finished in 368 s (`additional`), 558 s (`fixtures`), 1,341 s (`fixtures-build`) and 1,266 s (`serve-host`). The same lane therefore varies by more than 17 percent between two runs of the same code (`primary`) and by up to 46 percent (`fixtures`, 381 s and 558 s), which is why the deadline is 3,540 s: 2.4 times the longest lane of that run, and twice the 1,740 s that `primary` did not meet. CPU time and the heap are measured here only; the runner's logs record wall time, and the memory margin is the proxy's (**Verification Memory**). A fixture lane that takes more than about 85 percent of 3,540 s (3,010 s) on the runner is split by category into a further fixture lane (a theory moves between the lanes by its category alone), with the same receipt, aggregate and workflow-test changes, and never two fixture processes in one job. The selection of `fixtures` and `fixtures-build` together (6,264 cases), run as one process on the same tree, took 619 s (CPU 719 s) and peaked at 5.35 GB.

| Lane (job) | Slots | Selection | Tests | Wall here (s) | CPU here (s) | Peak RSS here (GB) | Wall on the runner (s) | Share of the 3,540 s deadline on the runner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `primary` | 2 | the unmarked production methods, two root workers | 58 | 556 | 939 | 5.81 | 1,476 | 42% (2.4x) |
| `additional` | 2 | the five marked production methods, two root workers | 5 | 161 | 275 | 4.62 | 437 | 12% (8.1x) |
| `fixtures` | 1 | every fixture but the Serve host theories, the Build scan classes and the Serve worker theories, one process | 6,088 | 182 | 259 | 5.45 | 381 | 11% (9.3x) |
| `fixtures-build` | 1 | the four Build scan classes and the two Serve worker theories, one process | 176 | 495 | 577 | 4.54 | 1,395 | 39% (2.5x) |
| `serve-host` | 1 | the four Serve host theories, one process | 40 | 480 | 637 | 3.92 | 1,410 | 40% (2.5x) |

The authority reconciles the five receipts only when every selected result of each is `Passed` (6,367 of 6,367 here). The three fixture lanes are balanced by what they cost, not by their size. `serve-host` spends 461 s in its four theories (Build 185 s, Composition 167 s, Scoped consumer 97 s, canonical build 11 s), `fixtures-build` spends 474 s, of which the two Serve worker theories (3 and 1 cases, whole discoveries too) take 361 s and the four Build scan classes (172 cases) 113 s, and `fixtures` spends 162 s in its 6,088 cases; a theory moves between the lanes by its category alone, and only together with its cost. The sites and diagnostics of both production partitions are the same under one, two and three root workers (6,729 primary and 1,491 additional sites, no diagnostic), and so are the per-root analysed-state counts but for the handoff roots, whose count depends on the arrangement by the timing rule in the Headroom Tripwire (`InitializeGlobalAsync` is 484 under one and three workers and 242 under two in the measurement there).

Analyzer fixtures share one immutable metadata-reference set for the trusted platform assemblies (`TrustedPlatformReferences.Shared`): the inventory fixtures and the Build scans (the admitted entry census, the checker limit pins, the single gate census and the authority carrier ban) compile against it, and `TrustedPlatformReferencesTests` refuses any test source other than the helper that reads `TRUSTED_PLATFORM_ASSEMBLIES`. Each fixture still creates its own syntax tree and compilation; the reuse/isolation contract verifies both bounded metadata identity and separate source symbols. A reference copies its assembly's metadata into native memory when a compilation first reads it and holds it for the life of the reference, so the set is made once for the test host: recreating every platform PE reference for each adversarial fixture caused a brief testhost RSS spike that sparse live snapshots missed, even without coverage instrumentation, and a set per class holds one more image of every platform assembly for the whole run. Reference reuse removes that repeated metadata allocation without changing the analyzed sources, referenced assembly identities, or proof selection. The two fixtures whose subject is that compilations do not share their platform symbols (the retargeted authority carrier case and the enumerator modelling case) ask for `TrustedPlatformReferences.Separate()`, a set of their own.

Traversal-state identity projects an evaluation environment only after its token is complete and contains no backreference. It may discard an unused parameter owned by the current ordinary method. **Foreign Parameter Projection** extends that to a member that cannot be nested inside a method (an accessor, a constructor, an operator, a conversion or an explicit interface implementation): every binding of a parameter an ordinary method owns is dropped, because such a parameter is no name in that member or in anything it runs. An instance call reaches it only by passing its caller's whole context on to the members of the receiver, which multiplied an accessor's states by every distinct binding of every caller above it. A lambda or a local function keeps every binding, because it may be declared inside the owner. Two questions read every admission binding of a member and not the one an expression names: whether the member holds an admission seed and whether it may contain an admission origin. They apply the same rule, so a lease that an ordinary method passed on is no seed in an accessor that cannot name it whether or not the projection ran, and the verdict on a callback declared in such a member does not depend on whether a lease was passed. **Inert Payload Parameter.** A parameter whose type is a type parameter and whose every use in the member is the argument of a call that moves it on to an authored member (which moves it in turn), or the right side of a plain assignment to a field of `this`, is a payload the member only moves. It is never a receiver, never converted, tested, cast, disposed or compared in the member, so the concrete type a caller bound for it decides nothing there; only that concrete binding is dropped, and the parameter's admission, callable and value bindings are untouched. A payload stored in a field is read later through the field by members the rule does not inspect, and that stays sound only because the traversal resolves such a field from the value source its caller bound to it and never from the parameter's concrete binding, and a field of a type-parameter type resolves to nothing for any payload; fixtures that dispose or dispatch on a stored payload, in the constructor, in a later member and through a holder that is itself disposed, pin that every payload type stays refused. `Result<T>.Success`, its constructor and its implicit conversion are one state each, not one per payload type, while a member that reads, forwards to a reader, or converts its payload keeps one state per type. Inherited or captured bindings, constructor parameters, fields, and recovery bindings remain conservative because sibling helpers can consume them through shared receiver or closure state. This prevents irrelevant caller callbacks from multiplying equivalent tail states while retaining exact provenance across helper chains.

The projection cache stores only syntax-dependent requirements. Each invocation adds its own recovery bindings after lookup, so visiting an unbound root first cannot remove another root's authenticated recovery evidence or change its reachable effects.

Binding-symbol identity strings reuse only completed immutable results within one graph, keyed by the exact consuming compilation reference and exact symbol reference. First use retains the original identity construction and declaration-tree registration order; external symbols do not register a compilation merely for cache lookup. Member identity separately reuses only its completed method-name string for the exact queried method-symbol reference, while its assembly, consuming compilation, tree and syntax-span fields are evaluated on every call in their original order. Both string builders build the strings they build without the reuse. This does not cache whole member identities, evaluation environments, fingerprints or context-dependent proof answers, and graph-local identifiers never cross worker boundaries.

Bound-value normalization reuses completed results within one analysis graph, keyed by the exact immutable caller instance and exact expression instance. Only the original queried normalization pair is cached; intermediate suffixes and cycle-cutoff results are not published. Evaluation-source wrapper normalization preserves value-changing casts, including nullable numeric conversion and boxing, instead of collapsing them into their operands. Identity casts and built-in reference casts over reference operands may retain the same source; contextual authored conversions and dynamic values remain unsupported. An expression-bodied method or local function forwards a source only when its returned by-value parameter is the exact selected method's own parameter in the authenticated ordinal slot. A captured outer parameter with the same type and ordinal is a different source. Refused wrapper normalization retains the current raw source and publishes no completed normalization entry. Existing concrete bindings remain part of environment identity; this is not a separate proof of arbitrary conversion equivalence. Expression-specific environment projection retains that caller instance when every candidate binding survives, including the empty case; completed partial projections reuse their filtered environment for the exact caller/expression reference pair within that graph. All six binding collections are filtered before publication, retaining selected source references and constructor/recovery contexts. A retained projection is not a proof certificate: existing token and fingerprint logic still rejects incomplete or cyclic proof, while already completed exact proof can avoid repeated physical work within the frozen limits (`LimitsAreFrozen`). Different bound environments and source occurrences retain their own mutation and ordering checks.

Exact-value dependency and expression-projection walks reuse immutable compiler symbol lookups, including null results, within one graph and keyed by exact semantic-model and syntax-node references. The same context lazily retains the original ordered assignment-node list per exact syntax-root reference, including empty scopes, without resolving or grouping symbols. When an exact caller/expression projection is not already retained, dependency answers, required-symbol comparisons, assignment filtering and cycle/completion decisions are recomputed, including binding-only context changes; initializer-first short circuits and nested-callable scope boundaries apply.

Cleanup value-flow queries also retain immutable source facts per graph, keyed by exact compilation identity and Roslyn type or field symbol. Closed sealed cast queries reuse cross-compilation escape checks, record `with` checks, and exact construction sites; assigned-field queries reuse declaration initializers, assignment sites, and unsupported-reference checks, preserving declaration order and each original semantic model. Every query still evaluates its own selected constructor, caller bindings, right-hand values, ownership, and cleanup provenance. Reusing source facts never reuses a caller-dependent cleanup conclusion. Work-count fixtures require one source scan per exact key and retain distinct known/unknown results across source symbols, compilation instances, and caller contexts. The cleanup value-flow and provenance walks already end re-entry and exhaustion conservatively (their active sets and 256-unit work budget yield an incomplete result), but they recurse natively to that budget's depth, which an unoptimized build cannot fit in the runtime's default 1.5 MB secondary-thread stack; discovery and every root worker therefore run on a dedicated 64 MB analysis thread, so the budget rather than the caller's stack ends a walk, with no limit, root or result changed.

Recovery-condition evaluation shares one context within an exact projected traversal state. Local-value queries reject assignments to other symbols before checking their reachability, and reuse only completed known local values. Cross-member or bound-source evaluation does not inherit that context. While a reachability plan is being built, nested checks use conservative direct reachability instead of recursively building the same plan. Deterministic query-count regressions cover shared assignment chains alongside plan parity and bound-environment isolation; wall-clock timing is not the performance assertion.

Generic by-value Boolean forwarding retains only compiler-known constants or stable already-bound by-value Boolean parameter chains ending in one. The original source/caller remains in the existing projected environment identity; true and false contexts cannot share a proof merely because they pass through the same wrapper syntax. **Constant Value Identity:** a bound value whose normalized source is a compile-time constant is the one exception, and is identified in the environment's token, cache identity and fingerprint by its value and its type instead of by position, syntax fingerprint and caller. A constant has no side effects, depends on no caller binding and folds to the same value from any call site, and every consumer evaluates it and none reads where it was written. A walk that follows a bound value to its caller must therefore skip a constant, because a constant carries no instance and its caller is not part of the state it names; the walks that name an environment (`EvaluationEnvironmentIdentity` and its cache identity) do, and `EveryEnumerationOfAMembersValueBindingsIsGuardedAgainstAConstant`, a scan of the compiled checker, fails any other enumeration of a member's value-binding sources that does not skip a constant (apart from the reviewed readers, which only name, compare or copy sources whole). So a flag passed as `false` at ten call sites is one state of the callee and `true` is another, while `0` and `0L`, `1.0f` and `1.0`, `'a'` and `97` stay distinct. A source that is not a constant, or a constant this analysis cannot spell exactly, keeps its position and its caller. Locals, calls, properties, ref/in/out forwarding, unsupported conversions, mutation, cycles, and exhausted existing environment depth remain unknown for this additional rule. Both forwarding and direct consumption of a bound Boolean parameter reject later writes, ref escapes, or invoked captured mutations that can revisit that exact use through a loop or backward jump; unrelated later straight-line writes do not invalidate the earlier use. Existing consumer-side stability checks still apply.

**Token Identity.** The exact `System.Threading.CancellationToken` carries no cleanup obligation, no ownership and no authority. Copying one hands on a reference to a source that only the source itself can dispose, so a token is never what a cleanup resolves against, a lambda that captures one needs no more than the lambda already has, and where a token came from decides nothing the traversal reads. A parameter of that type is therefore never bound to its source, and no parameter is demanded only because it flows into one. A `CancellationTokenSource` and a `CancellationTokenRegistration` are disposable, are different types, and keep their provenance. Binding every token split each helper that forwards one by every call chain that supplied it.

Code that restarts work after a landed effect is written as a loop of passes, not as a recursive call. Bound-value normalization stops at the first repeated source occurrence, so each recursion level carries its caller's environment into the next; with more than one re-entry edge those environments never converge and the traversal re-walks the callee graph at every level until the per-root state budget is spent. `GrimoireOfflineTransitionJournalStore.RecoverAsync` is the reference shape.

Exact metadata `System.Single.IsFinite(float)` is a closed external predicate only through its authenticated framework assembly, special type, ordinary static signature and absence of authored source. Its selected scalar contract is the exponent-bit test; this does not establish native intrinsic lowering or general numeric purity. A direct call keeps the existing actual-argument and conversion proof. A method group also keeps its complete callable origin, and an exact framework `Func<float, bool>.Invoke` consuming a closed external predicate must separately prove its actual argument values and conversions. Authored or unknown conversion operators retain a scoped refusal when their work cannot be closed; recognizing the predicate never supplies authority for evaluating its argument. Ordinary helper, receiver, capture and authored counterfeit effects remain reachable with their required work and effect frontiers.

Compiler-selected user conversion operators are executable edges even when the syntax has no cast. Contextual return, local-initializer, assignment and argument conversions follow their exact `IConversionOperation.OperatorMethod`, including separate nested conversions. Each occurrence binds the actual operand to the selected authored parameter. The source body receives work and effect frontiers queried after operand completion, retaining the conversion syntax for region checks; the strict lifetime comparisons include an operand call ending exactly at that boundary. A bounded conservative check with the existing cleanup proof budget retains inherited conversion authority only through explicitly listed structural/data operations, built-in non-dynamic conversions, ordinary by-value argument wrappers, and already checked call/construction lanes. Unknown operation kinds refuse authority, including getters, user operators, generic `new T()`, record copying, constructor bodies, and unsupported branching, patterns, collections or awaits; parameterized construction, opaque unreviewed execution, cycles and exhausted proof also refuse. The check walks transparent children one budgeted operation at a time and does not infer safety from the absence of a known dangerous operation. The same bounded exact-declaration certificate checks source entry for both called authored helpers and the selected authored conversion operator: all indexed partial class declarations must match the exact containing symbol and contain no static constructor or evaluated static field/event/property initializer. Missing or unsupported declaration evidence refuses inherited authority; method-body operations alone cannot establish that entry omits type initialization. This is a local conversion-entry requirement, not a type-initialization interpreter or a general change to ordinary-call analysis. Compiler-generated parameterless construction remains eligible only for fully indexed exact class declarations with an authenticated direct `System.Object` base, no evaluated field/event/property initializers across any partial declaration, and no static constructor. Missing declaration evidence, non-object bases and hidden initializer or type-initializer execution refuse; no constructor purity interpreter is inferred from `IsImplicitlyDeclared`. This check does not execute values or certify purity, and skips uninvoked callable bodies. Ordinary factory, getter, argument and conversion-body traversal remains independent. An unavailable operator body retains its own exact source-location refusal unless its external member has an existing reviewed effect-free contract. Awaitable or lazy conversion results without completion proof retain detached-work refusal. Conversion occurrences are deduplicated only within the current traversal state, so the existing full bound-environment and frontier identity, recovery guards, callable boundaries and traversal budgets remain authoritative. Locally accepted SDK construction cannot discharge an earlier conversion's execution obligation.

Nullable cleanup preserves completion only through the exact returned non-null arm of a conditional access and its existing outer join. Evaluating a conditional receiver, abandoning the returned task or awaiting a different task supplies no completion authority; an unknown cleanup target remains unresolved.

Conditional cleanup needs no concrete target only when its exact receiver is proved null through stable local or constructor argument sources. This bounded proof rejects mutation, ref escape, cycles and exhausted source chains. It checks compiler conversions before peeling parentheses, null suppression or built-in reference/nullable casts; authored and dynamic conversions cannot turn their null input into absence evidence. Unconditional cleanup and unknown receivers retain their target requirement. Earlier generic provenance normalization remains separate; this conditional proof supplies no target, effect or admission authority.

A published framework `Task` has completion ownership when its single-variable declaration is immediately protected by a `try/finally` whose sole finally statement unconditionally awaits that exact local (optionally with a constant framework `ConfigureAwait`). By-value field/property publication and tracking inside the try may throw without abandoning the join. Reassignment, ref/out/ref-local or captured uses, extra initializers, throwing gaps, conditional/wrong-task joins, and evaluated configuration arguments do not receive this proof. The existing tracked-catch and other completion proofs remain separate.

Readonly interface fields can preserve a manually constructed receiver's exact cleanup provenance. Constructor bindings are reused only for a same-instance field read in its declaring type; conflicting constructed environments, unknown or mutable sources, ref-alias escape, and another instance's field remain unproven. Resolving the interface to a concrete type alone is insufficient: the receiver's bound construction context must also agree. An independently authenticated DI receiver can recover its exact construction context from one framework registration for that exact service contract, using either its unique public implementation constructor or its exact factory construction and actual same-type delegation chain. This does not infer DI ownership for arbitrary manually constructed or unknown receivers.

Constructor-parameter cleanup proof checks the actual source and constructor mutation before consulting concrete dispatch types; a sealed type hint cannot substitute for exact dependency provenance. Constructor-initializer forwarding retains the existing exact, stable identifier requirement. Receiver demand includes same-instance helpers inside contained callables, and explicit `this` reuses only the current exact-type receiver context. Indirect primary-constructor captures pass through the same bounded demand and stability checks as direct captures; retaining an input does not execute an uninvoked callback or authorize another receiver's construction.

Demand retention also follows same-instance authored getters, exact selected-constructor assignments to get-only auto-properties, and stable constructor-local initializer dependencies under the existing depth, visited, and mutation guards. A single guaranteed final constructor assignment supersedes an earlier readonly-field initializer; the initializer cannot authenticate a later unknown or derived value. Constructed readonly-field bindings, including delegated bindings, reject unreviewed `ref`/`out` escapes and ref aliases before retaining a source, using the same mutation checks as ordinary field cleanup flow. An actual constructor argument using `GetRequiredService<T>` retains DI provenance only when its exact syntax and parameter position belong to the unique authenticated registration factory and its own stable provider parameter; rejected explicit sources never fall back to a global registration.

For a private field on a sealed owner, including a nested sealed owner, exact selected-constructor cleanup demand may also retain a mutable field when every non-constructor assignment only relinquishes it to null. Constructor sources remain tied to the same receiver; unknown replacement, exposed fields, unreviewed ref/out and ref aliases remain refused. A local snapshot survives the later clear, including an authenticated framework Interlocked.Exchange-to-null result on the implicit or explicit current receiver; the binding cannot be borrowed by an exchange on another instance, and the proof does not generalize to arbitrary mutable carriers or replacement exchanges.

Mutable auto-property cleanup provenance is accepted only for a sealed authored carrier whose complete writable domain is visible: a private nested carrier is closed over its private access root, while an internal carrier requires every syntax tree in its exact authored compilation to be indexed. Every non-null initializer and assignment is evaluated in its own member context and contributes to the value union. Custom accessors, public carriers, tuple or compound writes, unknown/ref escapes, captured callable mutation, unindexed declarations, and unknown construction escape refuse the proof. A later known writer cannot hide an earlier unknown one.

Exact collection provenance includes a locally populated framework `List<T>` and a private readonly `ConcurrentDictionary<TKey,TValue>` whose complete `TryAdd`, indexer-write, and removal flow is visible. `TryRemove` may bind either a declaration expression or an existing stable local. Factory-return and `foreach` flow retain all exact element sources, while an unknown writer in a nested lambda or local function refuses the collection proof even if the callback is not proven invoked.

A nullable factory result narrowed by an empty non-null pattern is followed only after a terminating negative guard or within a direct positive conditional's true arm, and while the pattern local remains stable. Optional `GetService<T>` resolution requires a unique registration and an authenticated provider source. A forwarded scope parameter must trace back, without intervening mutation, to an actual `await using AsyncServiceScope` declaration or a `using IServiceScope` declaration created by the exact framework `IServiceScopeFactory.CreateScope` method, with its scope factory independently proven. A forwarded registration-factory provider instead requires the exact framework registration and factory-parameter identity, stable forwarding, an exact service construction, and a terminating null guard before the optional service is consumed. A custom provider or declared provider/scope type alone is not sufficient evidence.

An exact registration factory may use an expression body or a block that constructs one returned local and performs only authored same-instance void configuration calls before returning it. Reassignment, alternate construction/return, ordinary escape, the wrong receiver, or mutation of a constructor dependency from a configuration method refuses the construction context. Optional `GetService<T>` constructor arguments remain exact only with the same authenticated provider and one exact registration whose implementation is established by the existing service binding; the registration may use one direct constructed instance or one exact expression factory. An absent optional service may use its declared null default only when the exact framework registration and provider shapes plus the complete applicable registration catalog prove that no registration exists. A required or otherwise unauthenticated missing service, and ambiguous, counterfeit, wrong-provider, or unknown-return registrations, remain unresolved.

The pinned default `IOptionsMonitor<T>.OnChange` subscription token is reviewed mechanical cleanup only when the exact framework call flows from an authenticated DI receiver, the same exact service collection has a must-execute `Configure<T>` composition, and the existing whole-composition proof finds no escape or unknown mutation. Any applicable closed/open registration, factory, replacement, descriptor mutation, or stable `Type`-local override refuses the default summary. An authored custom monitor also refuses this summary; its interface-return dispatch remains unresolved by this rule rather than being mistaken for the framework token.

Registered constructor dependencies may pass through a bounded chain of same-type `this(...)` initializers, including a factory-created overload that delegates to a primary constructor. Each hop must preserve the exact dependency parameter without mutation, alias escape, or substituted values. An exact hosted-service alias resolving an existing singleton is not a second constructor activation; the underlying activation must still be independently proven. Lifecycle constructor context comes from the actual unique framework-hosted activation: its direct constructor, its exact factory creation, or its exact alias to one service factory. A separately registered singleton cannot supply construction context to an independently activated hosted instance.

Invocation-based mutation checks respect argument evaluation order: an enclosing call has not executed while its arguments are being evaluated, but completed calls in earlier arguments can already have changed a captured value. Forwarding a callback therefore does not itself invalidate a dependency before the enclosing call runs; an earlier invoked mutator still does.

A declared operation root may import constructor context from its unique exact framework factory registration. Only private readonly fields demanded by the root or its bounded same-instance helper calls are retained, with the source bindings needed to evaluate those fields. This demand includes a bounded traversal of readonly sibling-field assignments; transparent null-forgiving syntax does not change receiver identity. The proof does not infer registrations for arbitrary downstream objects or transfer a root's field values to another instance. Missing, ambiguous, and custom registration paths remain unproven.

An exactly constructed receiver retains the readonly field context demanded by its method and same-instance helpers. This projection also preserves directly used primary-constructor parameters, including reads through exact same-instance helpers and getters, but does not copy unrelated constructor values into every call. Potential captures in contained lambdas and local functions retain their required bindings; retention alone does not execute those bodies or add producer sites. Each demanded field source retains its own proven dependency closure. Its selected constructor and actual same-type delegation chain remain part of the bound environment and cache identity even when no constructor parameter needs retention. When no exact constructor is bound, competing instance-construction paths, including implicit and synthesized constructors, are treated as ambiguous rather than borrowing another overload's field assignments. Conditional receivers may discard only proven empty alternatives. A complete finite family of nonempty alternatives may retain separate complete, non-backreferenced construction environments when every executable source belongs to the proven exact cleanup-candidate family; the same effective cleanup member is then traversed once per distinct environment. An incomplete, backreferenced, unknown, or out-of-family source refuses the family, as do alternatives that resolve to distinct cleanup member identities. Sealed positional-record properties preserve a service source only through an exact constructor-argument mapping, without an overriding initializer or unproven property implementation. Constructor-parameter mutation and alias escape must not resurrect the original factory value through a readonly sibling field.

Explicit calls through authenticated framework `IDisposable.Dispose` and `IAsyncDisposable.DisposeAsync` slots resolve the receiver through the same effective-cleanup proof as implicit disposal. The receiver's static authored contract is preserved separately from the selected framework slot, so existing closed-interface proof remains available without selecting a same-named public pattern body. They retain the compiler-selected interface implementation, bound authored receiver context, exact external read/write classification, and proven mechanical cleanup; unknown or mutated receivers remain unresolved. Opaque admission-handle cleanup requires an exact current-value proof at the receiver use, not a historical may-alias origin: authenticated out values and stable aliases remain eligible, while reassignment and ref escape invalidate proof. A conditional acquisition into an untouched null local may support guarded terminal cleanup but grants no effect authority to the nonacquired branch. Their work/effect frontier is the invocation position, not scope exit, and asynchronous cleanup must have an observed completion before inheriting that frontier. The interface slot alone is not an effect-free callback or method-group proof.

The explicit admission cleanup certificate also checks later writes, ref escapes and invoked captured mutations that an enclosing loop or backward jump can carry to the same use. A dominating acquisition alone does not certify every visit; stable repeated uses remain eligible, while an uninvoked callable does not mutate its capture merely by being declared. This proof-local guard does not change shared may-alias admission origins.

Bootstrap console restoration retains the real framework `Console.SetOut`/`SetError` operations as filesystem effects under the ordinary authority checks, separately from its owned writer disposal. Inherited `Component.Dispose` is reviewed mechanical watcher cleanup only for a complete exact framework `FileSystemWatcher` source with the existing same-owner lifecycle proof; exposed, mutated, unknown, derived and counterfeit receivers do not acquire this exemption. Manual ownership and explicit completion share the exact two-statement finally proof for a captured framework `ValueTask`: successful completion or a synchronous join of that same task exhausts the paths. Wrong tasks, inverted guards, missing joins and potentially throwing intervening work remain unproven.

An observed caller may retain completion through the exact serialized disposal-cache shape: a private initially empty Task field is coalesced once into a single local under the owner's lock, and that same local is immediately returned in the real framework ValueTask wrapper. Other cache sources, writes or escapes, another returned task, intervening work and an unobserved caller do not gain this proof. Merely storing a task in a field is not an ownership transfer.

Cleanup of an authenticated client returned by the pinned MCP SDK's exact factory is a provider effect, not a mechanical release: session disposal may send HTTP DELETE or terminate a stdio process. The abstract session spelling alone grants no receiver proof; unknown, replaced, escaped or counterfeit sources remain unresolved, authored implementations retain their own traversal, and an unjoined cleanup retains no caller authority.

The ordinary-initializer runtime control drives the real SDK through a failed tools-list response and an in-process blocked HTTP DELETE. Maintenance drain and effect/work lease release must wait for that cleanup, in DELETE-then-effect-then-work order; event barriers provide the proof, with timeouts only as outer deadlock guards. This failed-start control does not waive or redefine timed retirement ownership.

Exact object-initializer property extraction permits multiple simple auto-`init` assignments only when every sibling preserves the same safe assignment semantics. Custom setters, nested initializers, and unknown or mutated sources do not become trusted merely because the requested property uses an auto-accessor.

An unassigned nullable auto-`init` property is known to be empty only on an exact construction with no property initializer, a zero-parameter compiler-generated constructor, and a direct `object` base. Authored constructor assignments, copied record state, and base-constructor effects are not silently treated as null.

Exact-value requirement discovery visits each reachable method/parameter pair once per query, including diamonds and cycles, and caches only the completed root answer. Expression-level local dependency walks likewise reuse completed results only within one query for the same member and required symbol; a negative answer affected by an active cycle is not cached. Assignment-before-use ordering is preserved. A recursion cutoff therefore cannot become a reusable false negative. Receiver-state discovery retains a referenced primary-constructor parameter when its actual bound value can carry cleanup provenance; the parameter's declared type is never itself accepted as proof. Exact authenticated framework `FileStream` subtype provenance follows the compiler-selected cleanup override, while unknown values and multiple distinct authored cleanup targets remain unresolved fail-closed.

Deadline tests must not race a short cancellation timer against a later success timer: an overdue thread pool can deliver those callbacks in either order. The bounded HTTP-client fixture remains pending until cancellation. Subagent renewal tests advance the manual clock only after the renewal loop registers its next timer, proving four renewals over twenty simulated minutes and the current revision at completion. Completion wait bounds remain deadlock guards; they do not drive behavior. The daemon lease tests synchronously establish the blocked state before release and retain their existing two-second guard under the bounded runner load. Terminal-recovery refusal fixtures publish structurally valid mutations through the production canonical journal codec and synchronize on the terminal-finisher entry boundary; a host failure before that boundary propagates with its original cause instead of masquerading as the expected refusal.

Windows serial verification uses host PowerShell and the normal user NuGet cache:

```powershell
$env:NUGET_PACKAGES = "$env:USERPROFILE\.nuget\packages"
dotnet test tests/RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Tests/RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Tests.csproj --configuration Release -- xUnit.ParallelizeTestCollections=false
dotnet test tests/RetroDownfall.TheForge.Tests/RetroDownfall.TheForge.Tests.csproj --configuration Release
```

Run `scripts/coverage.sh --threshold` from Git Bash for the normal parallel coverage gate. Threshold evaluation prefers Python and falls back to Windows PowerShell on Windows; the xUnit run itself remains parallel.

| Post-exclusion metric | Default/local target | CI target (`macos-26` `build-test`) |
|-----------------------|----------------------|------------------|
| Line coverage | ≥ 80% | ≥ 80% |
| Branch coverage | ≥ 70% | ≥ 70% |
| `Cli` line coverage (reported assembly, outside the aggregate) | ≥ 75% | ≥ 75% |
| `Secrets` line coverage (reported assembly, outside the aggregate) | ≥ 60% | ≥ 60% |
| Security-critical branch coverage | 100%, except `ApiKeyDigestCache` ≥ 85% | 100%, except `ApiKeyDigestCache` ≥ 85% |

The security-critical set is `ApiKeyEndpointFilter`, `ApiKeyDigestCache`, `DataProtectionSecretStore`, `GrimoireKeyDerivation`, `McpSecurityLimits`, `TrustedMcpWorkspaceStore`, `SandboxedFileIo`, `SecureFileReader`, `IdentityOwnedFileSystemCleanup`, `SanctumGuard`, `OutboundUrlGuard`, `HostProcessToolPolicy`, `IdempotencyClaimStore`, `BudgetReservationService`, `WardGate`, `WorkspacePathPolicy`, and `CovenantEnvelopeCodec`. The Python and PowerShell gates hold the same set under a parity test, and both fail when a listed type is absent from the Cobertura report, so a rename or new exclusion cannot silently satisfy its required threshold.

**How the security type is matched.** Coverlet emits every async and iterator body as a compiler-generated state machine nested under its declaring type (`Namespace.Type/<Method>d__N`). The gate folds each of those onto its declaring type — stripping the nested suffix *before* the namespace, since matching on the substring after the last `.` would yield `Type/<…>d__N` and skip every async body — and then aggregates condition coverage across the declaring class plus all of its nested state machines into one branch total per security type. Tallies are keyed by (source file, line) so a line reported by both the synchronous shell and its async state machine is counted once, at its *worst* observed condition coverage (the same worst-case rule the class-level fallback uses), so a covered shell can never mask an uncovered state machine on the same line (`test_same_line_reported_by_shell_and_state_machine_uses_the_worse_rate`).

Security-critical concurrency branches use deterministic transitions rather than scheduler timing wherever the state machine exposes such a seam. For example, `WardGate` separates its post-delay timeout transition so tests cover both a timeout that removes a live ward and one that observes an operator-resolved ward. `ApiKeyDigestCache` is the deliberate exception: its lock-free reader retries depend on observing narrow concurrent publication windows, and forcing each scheduling outcome would make the suite timing-dependent or require test-only access to private state. Its floor is therefore 85%, while behavioral stress tests prove readers never observe torn or zeroized live digests; every other listed type remains at 100%. A regression below the applicable floor makes `./scripts/coverage.sh --threshold` exit non-zero.

Each lane executes a different set of OS-specific branches while the denominator stays the same, so local and CI aggregate floors are both 80% line coverage and 70% branch coverage; environment overrides remain available for platform-specific validation. These aggregate floors do not relax the per-type security-critical gates. The four environment values the gate reads (`COVERAGE_LINE_TARGET`, `COVERAGE_BRANCH_TARGET`, `COVERAGE_CLI_LINE_TARGET` and `COVERAGE_SECRETS_LINE_TARGET`) are each validated as finite percentages from 0 through 100.

The aggregate coverage denominator is Core, Infrastructure, and Api. `Cli` and `Secrets` are instrumented too and appear in the report as separate assemblies, but they are *reported* assemblies: `scripts/coverage_threshold.py` (and its PowerShell twin) removes them from the aggregate by recombining the remaining assemblies' exact per-package rates, weighted by the unique source lines and branches coverlet counted for each (the rebuilt line weights equal coverlet's own `lines-valid` total, and the branch weights land within a couple of conditions of its `branches-valid`, because the root counts a few conditions the class lines do not list; the rates themselves are coverlet's exact attributes, so that drift only nudges the relative weights, by far less than a hundredth of a percentage point), so neither can move the 80% line and 70% branch floors. Each is held to its own line floor instead: `COVERAGE_CLI_LINE_TARGET` (default 75%) and `COVERAGE_SECRETS_LINE_TARGET` (default 60%). The defaults were set under what the Cli and Security test namespaces alone reached when the floors were introduced, so the full suite clears them with margin (the dated measurement sits beside the constants in `scripts/coverage_threshold.py`, not in this document, where a measured percentage would only go stale); a floor of 0 reports an assembly without gating it, and a report that lacks either assembly fails closed the way a missing security type does. The Cli excludes every file under `Cli/CommandCenter/**` (`ExcludeByFile`): the Terminal.Gui Command Center UX is interactive and is not line-coverable, and every Terminal.Gui reference lives in that directory. `Secrets` excludes by type `WindowsOsCredentialStore`, `MacOsCredentialStore`, `LinuxOsCredentialStore` and the three platform `HostProcessToolsMarkerSlot` types, because those are mutually exclusive by platform and whichever do not match the runner would park structurally unreachable lines in the report on every lane. The historical `WindowsOsCredentialStore` defect is pinned by `OsCredentialStoreRoundTripTests` against the real backend on the Windows lane, never by this gate. `scripts/coverage_threshold_test.py` pins both halves: the runsettings contract (both assemblies in the Include filter, the exclusions naming real files) and the gate behaviour (a report without the Cli fails, a Cli under its floor fails, and a poor Cli leaves the aggregate untouched). The aggregate case is pinned against a report whose root `line-rate`/`branch-rate` carry the blended rates with a 5% Cli in the denominator, so reading the aggregate from the root attributes (the behaviour before the Cli was instrumented) fails it; a second case recombines two gate packages of unequal line and branch weight and asserts the printed aggregate equals the weighted gate-only value, which also separates an unweighted mean and a recombination that reuses the line weights for branches. The same two cases run against the PowerShell twin on a host with `pwsh`. The Forge and Compendium run as separate test projects. Configuration lives in `tests/RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Tests/coverage.runsettings`, `scripts/coverage.sh`, and `scripts/coverage_threshold.py`; HTML is written to `.tmp/coverage/report/index.html`.

CI's runtime coverage gate is (the source analysis is the separate mandatory `Hosted producer source analysis` authority job):

```yaml
env:
  COVERAGE_LINE_TARGET: "80"
  COVERAGE_BRANCH_TARGET: "70"
- run: |
    python3 -m unittest scripts/coverage_threshold_test.py scripts/coverage_workflow_test.py scripts/hosted_producer_analysis_runner_test.py
    ./scripts/coverage.sh --threshold --ci-runtime-only
```

Do not publish a historical test count or coverage percentage as a release claim. GitHub Actions uploads HTML + Cobertura as `arcanum-coverage-report`. Compendium runs as a separate `dotnet test` step. `TheForge.Ux` — and through it `TheForge.Core` — is compiled by the `build-test` job because the release workflows package and ship it, and the Forge test suite runs there as its own `dotnet test` step. No test project in `RetroDownfall.Arcanum.slnx` is excluded from `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: a whole-project exclusion leaves no trace in any test report, so a suite nobody runs is indistinguishable from one that passes. `ContinuousIntegrationWorkflowTests.Ci_runs_every_test_project_the_solution_carries` enforces that; quarantine an individual test with `Skip` and an issue link instead.

### 13.2 Test data, ownership, and parallel collections

- Checked-in immutable inputs live under `TestData/<Feature>/` and are copied with `CopyToOutputDirectory=PreserveNewest`. Copy them into a temp root before mutation.
- Mutable workspace trees, Grimoire copies, and CODEX writes use `Support/TempWorkspace` or fixture helpers. Cleanup owns one exact unique root and never infers an ancestor by walking parents.
- API-host tests set `ARCANUM_TEST_HOME` while the environment is `Testing`. This is required on Windows because changing `HOME`, `USERPROFILE`, or `APPDATA` after process start does not redirect .NET known-folder paths.
- Concurrency tests synchronize on observable state transitions, not narrow scheduler windows. `SseStreamWriterTests` holds one `MoveNextAsync` behind a signal until a heartbeat write is observed, then releases the enumerator; its long `WaitAsync` bounds are deadlock guards and never cancel the stream under ordinary coverage-run suspension.
- No test's time bound includes Windows PowerShell's start-up. PowerShell 5.1 has taken more than ten seconds to cold-start on a loaded `windows-latest` runner, longer than several tests' deadlines, so a test whose child is PowerShell does one of three things. `Support/WindowsPowerShellWarmUp` runs PowerShell once per test process, outside every measured run (a class awaits it from `InitializeAsync`, or a Windows-only test awaits it first; it is a no-op on every other host), and a deadline that only guards a hang sits at sixty seconds, far above a warm start, which a passing run never approaches. A bound on what the code under test did is measured from a signal the child gives once it is up and not from `Process.Start`: `CappedChildProcessRunnerTests` has the child create a ready marker file before its real work and bounds the time from that file's write to the runner's return, and `FamiliarProcessRunnerTests.Runner_KillsProcessWhenAggregateOutputExceedsCeiling` starts its stopwatch at the first frame the stub delivers. A cancellation that has to land on a partial result waits for that result to exist and does not fire from a timer (`RunAsync_cancellation_deletes_partial_spilled_output` cancels once the spill file is on disk), because a timer that wins the race against a slow start proves nothing and still passes. A test that deliberately expects a timeout or a cancellation of a child that never speaks is exempt, since its deadline fires whenever the child starts.
- A synchronisation barrier is an observable effect, never a fixed sleep: `SagaExtractionServiceTests.ExecuteAsync_IdlesWhenDisabled_NeverCallsIntelligence` enqueues an ineligible item, waits for the single FIFO reader to log its decision, enables the policy, enqueues an eligible second item and waits on that item's provider call before asserting the first never reached the provider and stored nothing, so deleting the production guard turns it red regardless of timing. A barrier that polls the pending snapshot until it is empty is only sound if an empty snapshot implies the abandoned segment is already recorded, so `SagaExtractionService.PendingRequestsForTests` takes the policy lock that abandonment holds while it removes the pending work and retains the segment (`PendingRequestsForTests_waits_for_an_abandonment_in_flight_instead_of_reading_between_its_two_writes`); without that, `ExecuteAsync_DuplicateOfAbandonedInterval_MergesWithItsRetainedPolicy` read the gap between the two writes and failed under load.
- A test never swallows an exception without saying why. `EmptyCatchContractTests` parses every test source file once and fails an empty catch-all (`catch` or `catch (Exception)` without a filter) whose `try` awaits (an `await` expression, `await foreach`, or `await using`) or blocks on a task (`Wait`, `WaitAll`, `WaitAny`, `GetResult`, `.Result`), so a timeout, an early cancellation or a fault in the code under test cannot disappear behind it (narrow it to `OperationCanceledException`/`TimeoutException`, or to the specific I/O exceptions the cleanup can raise), and any empty catch-all that carries no comment naming the swallowed path. The contract bans the filter-less catch-all only. A typed catch of `OperationCanceledException` is the ordinary end of a cancelled wait, and a typed empty catch that names a `TimeoutException` must carry a comment (`Every_empty_catch_of_a_timeout_names_why_it_is_the_expected_end_of_the_wait`). A cleanup wait therefore does one of two things with a lapsed timeout: it reports it to the diagnostic sink (`PausedTurn.DisposeAsync` in `CovenantErasureSameProcessTests`), or it drops it under a comment that names the assertion that already reported it (the drains in `FakeElicitingMcpServer.DisposeAsync`, `WatchSseTransportTests` and `WizardIntelligenceProviderTests`). Cleanup of a killed process tree goes through `Support/TestDescendantProcess`, which tolerates a descendant that is already gone (including the `AggregateException` `Process.Kill(entireProcessTree: true)` raises when part of the tree cannot be killed) and nothing else. Temp-directory cleanup goes through `Support/TestDirectoryCleanup.TryDelete`, which reports a failed delete to the xUnit diagnostic sink instead of hiding it.
- A theory never takes a delegate parameter. xunit cannot serialize one, so a `TheoryData<Func<...>>` collapses into one opaque test case (and prints a "Non-serializable data" notice on every run, visible because `diagnosticMessages` is on); `TheoryParameterContractTests` fails any theory with a delegate parameter, and the data passes a case index or name that the test resolves instead.

xUnit runs collections in parallel and tests inside a collection serially:

| Collection | Purpose |
|------------|---------|
| default | Pure logic; no shared process state. |
| `Grimoire` | SQLCipher template database with per-test file copies. |
| `ApiHost` | Shared `ArcanumWebApplicationFactory`, isolated persistent root, PID file and background batch poller disabled; collection parallelization disabled. |
| `ProcessEnvironment` | Process environment/global `ArcanumPaths` mutation (including built-in Spell fixtures) and Grimoire tests that mutate it; parallelization disabled. |
| `OutboundUrlGuardDns` | Process-global DNS resolver seam; parallelization disabled. |
| `WorkspacePathPolicy` | Static path-comparison seam, the containment-check observer, and the file-I/O test hooks; symlink behaviour is exercised only through real links in temp directories (no resolver seam); parallelization disabled. |

### 13.3 SQLCipher and API-host fixtures

Grimoire tests use `[SkippableFact]` and skip when `e_sqlcipher` is unavailable (`GrimoireFixture.SqlCipherAvailable`). The probe disables SQLite pooling, reports available once an encrypted connection opens, and deletes its temporary DB best-effort in a `finally`, so a failed probe cannot leave its file behind either (`A_failed_probe_leaves_no_database_file_behind`). It runs from a static constructor, so it catches **every** exception and reports it as `SqlCipherUnavailableReason`: a squatted temp path, a read-only volume, a locked probe file, or a native library without encryption support must degrade to skipped tests, never to a failed type initializer that turns every later `Skip.IfNot` into `TypeInitializationException`. The two other things the static constructor does hold to the same rule, and both catch a failure of any type: the probe's delete (`TryDeleteProbe`) lets only the I/O and access failures a held handle produces pass quietly (`A_probe_whose_delete_is_refused_by_a_held_handle_passes_quietly`) and reports anything else to the diagnostic sink instead of letting it escape, while the start-up sweep (`TrySweepAbandonedTestArtifacts`) lets nothing pass quietly and reports every failure, an I/O error included, because a path it cannot remove is something the next run should hear about (`A_sweep_that_fails_with_an_io_error_is_reported_instead_of_passing_quietly`). Cached-template validation/remediation and main DB/sidecar copying share one in-process lifecycle lock, so nothing can observe or delete a partial template; there is deliberately no named cross-process mutex, because the template is private to the process and a machine-wide name could only make unrelated runs queue behind each other. The template directory is private to the test process — `arcanum-tests/grimoire-template-<pid>-<guid>`, removed at process exit. At start-up a 12-hour sweep (`GrimoireFixture.SweepAbandonedTestArtifacts`) collects everything a killed run leaves directly under `arcanum-tests/`: `grimoire-template-*` directories, `grimoire-<32hex>.db` copies with their `-wal`/`-shm`/`-journal`/`.kdf` companions, `probe-<32hex>.db`, `api-host-<32hex>` profile directories and bare 32-hex workspace directories (`TempWorkspace`); nothing younger than the grace period or outside those names is touched, and a path the sweep cannot delete is reported rather than silently skipped (a tree a killed run left with a read-only directory has its owner access restored on POSIX hosts before one retry, so one such orphan cannot be reported on every later run; the restore walks real directories only and never follows a symlink out of the doomed tree, because `chmod` acts on the link's target, `DeleteTree_does_not_change_the_permissions_of_a_directory_a_symlink_points_at`). Test infrastructure that has no `ITestOutputHelper` (a fixture deleting its `TempHome` during disposal, the sweep) reports through the xUnit diagnostic sink, which `DiagnosticSinkTestFramework` captures and `xunit.runner.json` (`diagnosticMessages`) surfaces. It used to be one machine-global path, and the locks were not enough: the fingerprint check and `Concurrent_template_rebuild_and_copies_produce_complete_databases` both delete template files, so any second test process sharing a temp directory — two developers, one CI agent running two jobs, a filtered run beside a full one — destroyed the other's template and produced "file being used by another process" and missing-`.db.kdf` failures across roughly 158 suites unrelated to either change. The caching that matters is within a run, where every collection fixture still shares one built template.

Shutdown-checkpoint tests create their WAL precondition explicitly: a pooling-disabled SQLCipher connection disables automatic checkpoints, writes a probe row, and stays open but transaction-free while `CheckpointOnShutdownAsync` runs. Tests must not assume schema initialization will leave a nonempty WAL after its final connection closes; SQLite may checkpoint or remove that WAL.

`ArcanumWebApplicationFactory` references `Api.DevHost`, seeds an encrypted copy under a unique testing root, disables the production PID file, replaces `ISecretStore` and `IArcanumIntelligenceProvider`, and exposes `CreateAuthenticatedClient()`. It sets `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT`, `DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT`, `ARCANUM_TEST_HOME`, and `ARCANUM_SKIP_KEY_BOOTSTRAP=1` **before** top-level `Program` reaches `CreateSlimBuilder`. `ArcanumPaths` honors the test-home override only in `Testing`; global MCP, Grimoire, secret, and log paths all remain inside that root.

Factory construction and first host start can be separated by other serialized fixtures. `CreateHost` therefore rebinds its own isolated profile before the entry point composes path-based services or inventories encrypted artifacts; a later-created factory must not redirect that startup into its own blob directory. The delayed-start regression plants an encrypted-envelope marker only in the other temporary profile and verifies startup uses the empty owned inventory without changing that foreign file. This is a serialized test-host guarantee, not support for concurrently changing process-global profile paths.

Each factory registers `ArcanumDbContext` with an explicit SQLCipher connection rooted at its own `TempHome`; later process-environment changes cannot redirect scoped repositories into another factory's DB. Every factory-creating class belongs to `ApiHost` (a reflection guard covers the performance baseline). The factory retains the exact `IHost` returned by `CreateHost` and idempotently awaits its stop before delegating framework disposal, so delayed hosted-service shutdown still observes the factory's test-home paths. Only after host stop and Grimoire checkpoint does disposal clear pooled SQLite connections, restore the process environment, and only then delete an owned isolated root, so a slow or failing root deletion can never leave the process resolving paths into a half-deleted tree. A constructor that throws part-way (the environment is already redirected by then) restores the captured environment and then releases an owned profile before rethrowing, because a constructor that throws is never disposed (`Constructor_failure_restores_the_environment`, with the order pinned by `Constructor_failure_restores_the_environment_before_it_releases_an_owned_profile` and, for disposal, `Disposal_restores_the_environment_before_it_deletes_an_owned_profile`); a cleanup that fails during that unwinding is reported to the diagnostic sink instead of thrown, so it can never replace the failure that explains the bad constructor (`Constructor_failure_is_not_replaced_by_a_failure_to_release_the_owned_profile`). Sync disposal routes through the same async lifecycle.

`AddArcanumSerilog` must not resolve options or the ring-buffer sink through `GetRequiredService` inside the `AddSerilog` configure callback during host `Build()`; that re-enters logging DI and deadlocks while `HostFactoryResolver` waits for `HostBuilt`. The sink is registered on first emit. Testing resolves the log directory inside the isolated root before any directory/ACL work and skips the rolling-file sink.

### 13.4 First-class reasoning coverage matrix

Reasoning tests are organized by the production boundary they protect, not duplicated merely to increase counts:

- **Contracts/configuration:** `ReasoningContractsJsonTests`, `ModelEntryJsonConverterTests`, `PricingSettingsTests`, `ConfigurationValidatorTests`, `PingRequestBoundsValidatorTests`, model endpoint/source-context tests, and Compendium descriptor/parity/preservation tests cover the retained configuration graph, unknown/removed-path rejection, credential references, editable-key parity, strict enum wire names, pricing fallback, control-support × wire-dialect combinations, legacy bare model strings, capability metadata, and AOT JSON registration.
- **Provider/engine:** `ReasoningChatOptionsAdapterTests`, `ModelCallExecutorTests`, `ProviderAttemptCommitTrackerTests`, and reasoning cases in `WizardIntelligenceProvider*Tests` cover typed/default/no-op JSON, all closed dialects, ignored controls, buffered/streaming/ interleaved/protected reasoning, fallback commitment, no-tools restart, same-provider continuation, guardrail buffering, context/reservation boundaries, and strict replacement order.
- **Projection/usage:** `ReasoningProjectionEndpointTests`, `TurnEngineProjectionCharacterizationTests`, `OpenAiChatUsageJsonTests`, and OpenAI endpoint tests cover native buffered/NDJSON and OpenAI buffered/SSE fields, shared reasoning/error rules, real HTTP semantic validation, answer isolation, legacy result data, total-token authority, `cached_tokens`, missing/inconsistent usage, and reasoning-token details. `OpenAiV1ParityTests` directly owns choice-only terminal chunks, `include_usage` false/true, the separate choices-empty usage chunk, and 40-character tool-argument fragmentation/reassembly; exact parity with the helper projection is not assumed. A real Master → TurnEngine → native projection → Apprentice test guards answer-only handoff.
- **Accounting/persistence:** `CostCalculatorTests`, `BudgetReservationEstimateTests`, `TurnAccountingHandleTests`, `InferenceAccountingStoreTests`, `GrimoireSchemaCatalogTests`, `GrimoireSchemaInstallerTests`, `GrimoireSchemaIdentityTests`, `CovenantSchemaInstallerTests`, `CovenantSchemaManifestTests`, `CovenantCanonicalSchemaTests`, `CovenantAcceleratorSchemaTests`, `CovenantAvailabilityTests`, `CovenantStoreTests`, `CovenantQueryPlanTests`, `CovenantMutationKernelTests`, `CovenantQuotaTests`, `CovenantOwnerCleanupTests`, `CovenantSearchIndexTests`, `CovenantIndexRebuildTests`, metrics tests, and audit tests cover cached/reasoning subset pricing, nullable-vs-zero rates, reservation headroom, nested ambient restoration, reconciliation, raw-SQL token columns, the schema tree's one-object-per-file and idempotency conventions, fresh install/transactional rollback/idempotent re-open, schema identity and drift detection, the compiled-model/installed-schema agreement and no-EF-entity guards, three-tier install with per-tier failure isolation and fail-closed version/fingerprint/metadata refusals, closed installed manifests with exact index-shape validation and pinned FTS5 shadow tables, external-content FTS5 ghost-token freedom under rank-1 integrity, the bounded one-command turn load with its indexed plan, transactional mutation with receipt replay and lane compare-and-swap, canonical and turn-capacity ceilings, trigger-owned owner-deletion catch-up, whole-sequence accelerator synchronization with a resumable rebuild, and count-only telemetry.
- **Clients:** CLI API/rendering/command tests, Command Center tests, The Forge NDJSON/Tome/trace tests, Compendium notifications, and `ApprenticeStreamFramePolicyTests` cover known/unknown/ malformed frames, discriminator preflight, one-byte and multibyte fragmentation, bounded ephemeral rendering, no-op notification suppression, spinner/viewport/cancellation cleanup, trace redaction, and no reasoning handoff. First-frame UI transitions observe emitted updates instead of racing wall-clock delays.
- **Concurrency:** daemon overlap tests start one signal-gated execution, await its actual start, then invoke the competitor directly; scheduler delay is never mistaken for production locking.

Focused examples:

```bash
dotnet test tests/RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Tests/RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Tests.csproj --configuration Release --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ReasoningContractsJsonTests|FullyQualifiedName~ReasoningChatOptionsAdapterTests|FullyQualifiedName~ReasoningProjectionEndpointTests"
dotnet test tests/RetroDownfall.TheForge.Tests/RetroDownfall.TheForge.Tests.csproj --configuration Release --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ArcanumApiClientNdjsonTests|FullyQualifiedName~TomeViewModelTests|FullyQualifiedName~InferenceTraceViewModelTests"
dotnet test tests/RetroDownfall.Compendium.Tests/RetroDownfall.Compendium.Tests.csproj --configuration Release --filter "FullyQualifiedName~SettingDescriptorParityTests|FullyQualifiedName~GenericSettingsPreservationTests"
```

### 13.5 Database, CLI, process, and workspace safety

SQLCipher/schema/accounting tests use `GrimoireFixture` scratch/template databases only. Never point tests at `~/.config/arcanum/arcanum.db`. Scratch contexts disable pooling and keep one encrypted connection open until disposal releases the Windows file handle. Tests must not migrate, reset, or inspect a real Grimoire. A developer DB created before the current reasoning-accounting install script must be handled outside tests: stop Arcanum, back up if necessary, delete the DB plus `-wal`/`-shm`, then restart to reinstall (§5.4.5).

`Cli/Infrastructure/CliApplicationFactory` builds the System.CommandLine root from a test `ServiceCollection`; use `Spectre.Console.Testing.TestConsole` for output assertions. Test C# follows the repository's blank-line convention.

Windows process-boundary behavior lives in `ProcessResourceLimiterWindowsBehaviorTests`, `WindowsJobObjectSessionTests`, and `ChildProcessBoundaryBehaviorTests`: Job Object failures use hand-written API fakes; stream failures use custom `Encoding`/`Decoder` implementations; cleanup uses unique owned roots; process-tree tests use immediate-exit or bounded 30-second children with prompt termination assertions and unconditional cleanup. `WindowsAppContainerRestoreJournalTests` covers the broker's kill-proof undo log on every host — replay order, a broker that cleaned up after itself, torn and corrupt records, reported residue, SID-only records restricted to per-run AppContainer SIDs (a user, group, built-in package or capability SID is never recorded or replayed), and two overlapping runs on one root each removing only their own ACE from a synthetic DACL — because the ACL mutation it protects is Windows-only but the log itself is not. The rest of the broker's Windows-only logic is pinned on every host through seams: `ChildProcessSandboxRootsTests` (an explicit OS argument shows Windows gets no POSIX runtime roots, and every root returned exists), `ChildProcessFilesystemJailTests.Root_normalization_drops_every_root_that_is_neither_a_directory_nor_a_file` (the jail's own normalization, which feeds both the Seatbelt profile and the broker payload, drops a missing root), `WindowsBrokerTargetResolverTests` (pure PATH/PATHEXT/file-exists resolution, case-insensitive PATHEXT matching and extensions outside PATHEXT, batch-script refusal and the `cmd.exe /c` caveat for user-profile shims, relative PATH entries never searched, root-relative/UNC/device/drive-relative names refused rather than rebased, the user-profile read/execute grant), `WindowsAppContainerJobAssignmentTests` (an inherited job without the host's confirmation never lets the target start), `WindowsAppContainerBrokerExitTests` (every broker-owned exit 70–75 writes one `sandbox-exec:` line, an incomplete payload names its missing member, an access-denied launch names the directories an AppContainer can reach), `WindowsProcThreadAttributeTests` (the security-capabilities and handle-list keys are rebuilt from the SDK's `ProcThreadAttributeValue` recipe), `WindowsDaclTextTests` (the comparison removes only `AI`, leaves an entry's text untouched, still fails a restore that lost an entry or protection, and refuses non-DACL SDDL), `WindowsJobObjectSessionTests` (a brokered job allows exactly one more active process than the configured count, the runner reserves that slot before it assigns a started broker, and a tool assigned directly keeps exactly the count), and `WindowsAppContainerRootLockBudgetTests` (contended root-lock waits share one deadline instead of stacking). The real kernel path — `WindowsAppContainerBrokerTests` (a bare `cmd` through `CappedChildProcessRunner` with a published apphost as broker, asserting exit 0, stdout, a workspace DACL equal to the one before the run apart from the `AI` control flag (compared through `WindowsDaclText`) and no leftover profile; the same command under a `MaxProcessCount` of 1, which the broker's own job slot keeps runnable; a confinement probe in which the target is refused a read and a write in a directory only the current user may touch, outside every granted root, while a write inside the workspace succeeds, recognised by what the refusal leaves behind rather than by its localised text; plus an in-process broker given an incomplete payload, asserting exit 70 and a `sandbox-exec:` line naming the missing member) and `WindowsAppContainerAclTests` (two real grants on one directory, removing one leaves the other, and removing both restores the complete DACL after Windows modern inheritance initialization; protected and unprotected roots preserve their protection and propagate each run's grants to existing child directories and files; a fresh root preserves exact ACL bytes, DACL protection and every other control flag, allowing only Windows' documented addition of `SE_DACL_AUTO_INHERITED` (`AI` in SDDL) on the first DACL write; replay of an absent per-run SID twice must leave the complete DACL unchanged without a DACL write under the existing root lock; a purge naming the user, Administrators or ALL APPLICATION PACKAGES is refused and leaves the DACL unchanged, compared exactly (`WindowsDaclText.Exact`) because nothing may write it; two grants and a removal on roots another run holds locked finish within one shared budget) — skips off Windows; both Windows lanes execute this selection with a published apphost supplied through `ARCANUM_PUBLISHED_EXECUTABLE` (§13.1). Both lanes require the stated exit, output, ACL and cleanup assertions to pass. `MacOsDescendantSupervisorTests` parks the kqueue monitor loop inside a tick through an injected hold, which is the only way to prove that disposal waits for the loop before releasing the event buffer without depending on scheduler timing. `SpellVersionPathPolicyTests` covers labels/sidecars without filesystem I/O. `WorkspacePathPolicyTests` and symlink variants separately cover lexical, symlink-component, and handle-revalidation boundaries independently of Sanctum. `WorkspacePathPolicyFailClosedTests` holds every refusal arm to the 100% security gate on macOS: unnormalisable roots and candidates, a root that is a link loop, missing or a file, a candidate spelling the kernel refuses, empty and unreadable link targets, the directory-creation diagnosis, and a root handle the kernel cannot name. What the filesystem cannot be made to answer on demand goes through seams: `WorkspacePathPolicy.LinkTargetReaderForTests` (a `readlink` that fails or finds no target between the `lstat` and the read, and target text no POSIX link can hold; flow-local, so a reader one test installs never answers another flow's walk and needs no reset, `WorkspacePathPolicyFailClosedTests.LinkTargetReader_DoesNotReachAnotherFlow`), `SetUseWindowsReparsePointClassificationForTests` (a reparse point that names no location is an ordinary entry on Windows, in the style of the ordinal-ignore-case comparison seam) and `FileHandleIdentityInterop.TryGetHandleKernelPathForTests`. A Windows drive- or root-relative link target is refused by the classifier as a target no walk can follow, the same fail-closed arm as an empty target.

Focused normal-CLR run:

```bash
dotnet test tests/RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Tests/RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~WorkspaceSearchToolTests|FullyQualifiedName~ApplyPatchToolTests|FullyQualifiedName~MultiFileCommitCoordinatorTests|FullyQualifiedName~MandatoryGrimoireRepositoryTests|FullyQualifiedName~WorkspaceCheckToolTests|FullyQualifiedName~WorkspacePathPolicy|FullyQualifiedName~ToolRiskClassifierTests|FullyQualifiedName~ToolAttunementTests|FullyQualifiedName~ArcanumInternalToolServerTests|FullyQualifiedName~McpToolMergerTests|FullyQualifiedName~DiagnosticMcpInvocationServiceTests|FullyQualifiedName~SessionEventHubTests|FullyQualifiedName~InferenceAuditLoggerTests|FullyQualifiedName~WizardIntelligenceProviderTests|FullyQualifiedName~ArcanumMetricsTests|FullyQualifiedName~PrometheusMetricsExporterTests|FullyQualifiedName~MetricsEndpointTests|FullyQualifiedName~AuditEndpointTests"
```

- `WorkspaceSearchToolTests`: strict line scope/mixed newlines/no cross-line regex, ordinal literal case, AOT-safe non-backtracking → interpreted fallback without `Compiled`, deterministic order, strict UTF-8/binary/symlink policy, every cap/status, and cancellation checkpoints. No Weave.
- `ApplyPatchToolTests`: parser vs planner, all-files-before-mutation, strict text/newline/mode, bounded unique relocation, alias/cycle/topology/metadata rejection, dry-run, result ordering/caps, bound receipts, all four persistence outcomes, independent calls, cancellation classification, rollback, relative recovery, and the non-isolated/crash boundary.
- `MultiFileCommitCoordinatorTests`: all-stage-before-mutation, sequential visibility, destination/artifact revalidation, concurrent edits, cancellation, reverse rollback, incomplete cleanup, identity-safe retention, and deepest-first directory cleanup. Passing proves reversible rollback, not multi-file isolation or crash atomicity.
- `MandatoryGrimoireRepositoryTests`: deterministic receipt/Entry IDs, exact payload readback, assistant-call before system-result, recovered idempotence, failed/partial/mismatched/ambiguous classification, bounded cancellation, and no generic duplicate append.
- `WorkspaceCheckToolTests`: closed/custom profiles, `--no-restore`, reserved tokens, sanitized env, trusted executable/SDK/global.json/package identities, read-only roots, owner-only outputs, count-unbounded streamed restore seeding, owner-only input manifest, Sanctum byte policy, deadline admission/cleanup, diagnostic caps, timeout/cancel cleanup, macOS advertisement, Linux/Windows unavailability, open-network disclosure, and the unproved malicious detached-descendant boundary. Real process cases are macOS-capability-gated.
- Tool-risk/attunement/internal-server/merger/diagnostic tests cover catalog presence, option refresh, the empty intrinsic-Ward inventory, eligibility-based `workspace_check` advertisement, explicit `ForbiddenArts` filtering, and diagnostic blocking of `apply_patch` / `workspace_check` even on colliding external names.
- `SessionEventHubTests` proves bounded process-local fan-out and slow-reader drops; persisted Entries remain replay authority.
- Audit/metrics tests prove successful-turn-only rows, default argument redaction/no result bodies, closed tool outcome values, and `arcanum_apply_patch_artifact_cleanup_total` outcomes. They do not claim globally bounded `tool_name` cardinality; unknown direct invocation names remain distinct within per-value/request limits.

All filesystem/process tests use unique owned temporary roots; receipt tests use scratch Grimoire fixtures. The reliable editing loop changes no schema and requires no real-database migration or reinstall.
