| `SetupStateMachineTests` / `SetupProviderProbeTests` / `SetupCommandTests` / `SetupInteractiveTests` / `SetupCommitterTests` | Documented step order, back/re-enter, and rejection of an unknown step; probe classification for reachable, model-absent, empty-model-list, authentication-failed, other-status, malformed, TLS, DNS/connection, timeout, and guard-rejected endpoints, non-billable `/models`-only request, bearer-token handling, five-second budget, endpoint-class derivation, and an oversized body refused without being buffered first; plan-writes-nothing with a precise masked diff and full completion summary; ordered commit of credential → configuration → preset → context; blocked commit on failed validation and explicit override; configuration restore plus new-credential deletion on preset failure; actionable partial-commit report when an existing credential was replaced or cleared; a cancellation raised inside the commit rolling back on an uncancelled token and reporting the partial state, while a cancellation before anything is applied still propagates untouched; idempotent re-run and preservation of unowned settings; no secret in argv, stdout, stderr, or JSON, including `SetupDraft.ToString()`; abort at every step index and on declining the final plan leaves configuration, credentials, and context untouched. |
| `SystemPromptBuilderTests` / untrusted-fence tests | Lexicon DATA inclusion/omission, control/newline hardening, byte truncation, adaptive fences for Codex/Spell/instructions/Chronosync/summary/attachments, and sanitized Data Stream ids. |
| `UnseenServantDaemonJobTests` | Deterministic bounded daemon-state name, enabled Lexicon state/instruction, disabled omission, and missing-state fail-open kickoff. |
| `LongRestPolicyTests` / `LongRestSweepRecoveryTests` / `LongRestSweepStoreTests` / `LongRestMutationMatrixTests` | Literal canonical digests and permutation-independent decisions; recovery that only parks, in each checkpoint shape; Atomic Readmission, the Sweep Failure Budget and cooldown, Parked-Is-Active request admission and Fresh-Authority Retire; and, for every mutation class, the mechanism that refuses it at the next step (§21.16.3). |
| `LongRestMaintenanceTests` (currency drift and currency edges) / `LongRestFenceCurrencyTests` / `LongRestCapabilityStateTests` / `LongRestLiveFenceTests` / `LongRestReplayDocumentationTests` | A completed sweep replays while it still describes the installation and is replaced by a new generation, never refused, when a setting, the dataset or (inside one boot) the fence has moved, clean and protected; a Covenant availability publication that changes no capability fact (a new canonical sequence, a pass that removed nothing) ends no sweep, park or completed sweep, and a clean sweep that spans one completes, while a change to the feature switch or the canonical tier still ends it; a protected park whose generation can still resume is returned unchanged, and one that can no longer resume (its fence moved in its own boot, its recipe is not the one in force, or a source it froze can no longer be proved) is retired and replaced by the next turn that carries live authority, a request without that authority writing nothing; a generation stored before an upgrade that the code in force can no longer read (a moved pairing version or fixed bound) is retired from the columns of its row, never parsed whole, by every route that ends its sweep (the worker abandoning a clean one, a protected park retired as a stale configuration, one an operator cancelled), and is replaced by the next request; a setting changed and changed back ends no completed sweep (it still ends a parked one, whose work in flight the epoch protects), and the deletion of the newest tracked memory of another scope ends no completed, in-flight or parked sweep; a request that raced the completion of its own replacement, or that arrived after a generation completed and before its operation settled, joins that sweep instead of creating another generation (one left parked in that interval, protected or clean, for the authority class that would readmit it is joined, or settled as stale configuration when it no longer describes the installation; a park only an operator can clear is neither joined nor settled, and the request is answered by a generation of its own), and a candidate superseded or invalidated after the lookup is never replayed; the capability term's encoding is pinned against an independent implementation; and the documents state each rule (§21.16.3). |
| `SanctumEnforcementTests` / `SanctumGuardDenialKindTests` / `ToolExecutionPipelineSanctumAuditOnlyTests` / `ToolExecutionPipelineSanctumRedirectModeTests` / `WebResearchSanctumWardTests` | `AllowsContinuation` overrides only policy refusals; an unrecorded breach and an unreadable Campaign are refused in both modes; an audit-only Sanctum records every breach of a call; the initial target of `read_url` and `browse_web` is recorded and allowed in AuditOnly, while a redirect hop and a research citation outside the allowed domains are recorded and refused in both modes. |
| `SanctumCampaignResolutionTests` / `SanctumCampaignResolutionRegisteredSpellingTests` / `SanctumGuardWorkspaceCampaignTests` / `SanctumGuardRegisteredSpellingTests` / `CampaignRepositoryContainedPathTests` | Which Campaign governs a turn: every claim a request names, the stricter Sanctum winning, the tie order, and every spelling of a registered root at any depth, the composed and decomposed spellings of an accented name written as scalar values (`CampaignRootContainmentTests`, `PathKeyGlobalizationTests`, which refuses the globalization library's normalization in the sources that fix a path's identity). |
| `AttachmentSourceSanctumTests` / `SessionAttachmentSanctumEndpointTests` / `AttachmentSourceResolverTests` | The Sanctum decision of the two live attachment source routes: the governing Campaign chosen from the Session's claims and the three readings of the spelled path (the root containing its text, the root containing its directory with the links resolved, and the nearest root over every form; a link out of a root, a root reached through a link to it, a link into another root and a directory link into another root each still the first Campaign's read), Strict refusing and recording, AuditOnly recording and letting a policy refusal through, no mode overriding an unreadable Sanctum, an unevaluable policy or an unrecorded breach, a path no Campaign claims left unrestricted, the resolver handing the guard both the spelled and the resolved path, each surface recording under its own name, and the listing of a Session's attachments revalidating a source without a Sanctum decision. `SessionAttachmentToolInjectionTests` pins the in-turn `refresh_session_file` decision (the turn's Sanctum, its mode, no Campaign asking nothing) and `CampaignRepositoryContainedPathTests` the text-only lookup. |
| `ContinuousIntegrationWorkflowTests` | The five-worker hosted-producer partition, the build-server and per-lane pins, and the Windows lanes' native Long Rest qualification (filter, TRX logger, retained artifact, SDK assertion and step order). |

The hosted-producer inventory treats detached callbacks as separate lifetimes: it checks captured caller admission before removing inherited authority, so a callback that retains a parent lease cannot claim the parent’s later work, while a callback that independently reacquires admission remains eligible under its own proof. Its strict capture query shares the existing 256-work limit across syntax nodes and child edges, nameof semantic checks, and nested operation, origin, alias, assignment, and carrier-type visits; exhaustion and a known origin in an unsupported carrier fail closed. Compiler-authenticated cases cover direct and aliased captures, callback-owned reacquisition, nameof-only references, bounded no-handle callbacks, exhaustion, and a lease hidden in a non-disposable holder, while callback effects continue to be traversed. Recovery startup acquires its lease inline, passes its own cancellation token and binds nothing: the Long Rest recovery handler is a Pure Park Handler that acquires no lease (§10.8.2), so no holder records a lease and no bind can fail or leak. The inventory tests establish these authored-source contracts only; complete production-graph qualification remains a separate gate.

### 13.8 Exclusions, runtime budget, and CI

Types excluded through `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` carry an inline reason — a trailing or immediately preceding comment, or a `Justification` — and `CoverageDenominatorTests` fails on any type-level exclusion under `src` that has none; the hosted-service lifetime shells (`CovenantMaintenanceHostedService`, `GrimoireSchemaTransitionHostedService`, `DataRetentionSweepHostedService`, `LongRunningOperationStartupHostedService`, `McpServerBootstrapHostedService`, `BatchProcessingService`) name the tests that cover the pass each one drives. A type-level exclusion removes the whole type, and for a partial type every part, from the denominator, so it is reserved for code with no portable test surface, and the largest security-deciding body in the tree is kept out of it: the internal MCP tool server (`ArcanumInternalToolServer` and its partials under `Mcp/InternalTools/`, about eight thousand lines of workspace, file and process tool handlers) is inside the 80/70 floors, pinned by `CoverageDenominatorTests`, and code in it that genuinely cannot run on a lane is excluded member by member with a reason rather than by type. Six smaller types near a boundary still carry the type-level attribute, each with its inline reason: `ArcanumSecurityStartupChecks` (it only runs and logs the file-permission self-check and the listen-any banner), `McpConnectionManager` (it spawns external MCP server subprocesses), `WindowsAppContainerLauncher` (Windows kernel/ACL integration whose broker and real-DACL checks execute on both Windows lanes, with the pure parts it relies on, including the `WindowsProcThreadAttribute` key pin, and the portable policy seams covered on every host), `LinuxLandlock` (the Linux-only Landlock syscall ABI, on a platform that is not a shipping RID), `SandboxExecHelper` (the sandbox re-exec entry that hands off to Landlock and `execv` on Linux or to the AppContainer launcher on Windows and never returns, while the broker-capability decision before it is covered) and `WindowsJobObjectInterop` (Windows-only job-object kernel interop, exercised through `IWindowsJobObjectApi` fakes on every host and through the Windows-conditional kernel tests selected by both Windows CI lanes); converting each to member-level exclusions is outstanding work rather than a policy exception, and `CoverageDenominatorTests` fails if any of these attributes remains while this paragraph stops naming the type. Source-generated JSON contexts are excluded by `coverage.runsettings`; generated files, migrations, and framework artifacts are likewise excluded there. Full-suite duration is host-dependent; the expensive fixed costs are Grimoire template creation and ApiHost startup. The whole-program hosted-producer inventory retains complete Roslyn compilations and its recursive analysis graph, so its test class runs in a dedicated `DisableParallelization` collection; this prevents coverage-instrumented tests from forcing a bounded production scan into sustained memory-pressure thrashing. Use the serial Windows command when validating shared process state.

`ArcanumPerfBaselineTests` is a manual wall-clock baseline harness, not a gate: its budgets are machine-load sensitive and would fail the CI run for reasons unrelated to any code change. It is excluded by `--filter "Category!=Perf"` in `scripts/coverage.sh` and on every `ci.yml` lane that runs the Arcanum suite, and `PerfCategoryExclusionTests` guards all three halves of that contract — the filter must exist in the script, no `dotnet test` of `RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Tests` in `ci.yml` may be able to select the category, and every test class in `Tests.Performance` must carry `[Trait("Category", "Perf")]`. A plain unfiltered `dotnet test` still runs the baselines; the production path they touch (`GET /api/health`) is separately covered by non-`Perf` tests, so the exclusion costs the gate no coverage.

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on pull requests and manual dispatch; push-triggering is intentionally disabled. **One SDK policy builds everything:** the root `global.json` requires at least SDK `10.0.401` and enables `rollForward: latestMajor` with `allowPrerelease: false`, so local commands select the highest installed stable SDK at or above that serviced floor. `.github/workflows/resolve-dotnet-sdk.yml` runs `scripts/resolve_dotnet_sdk.py` once per CI or release run against Microsoft's fixed HTTPS `releases-index.json` endpoint. The resolver selects the highest stable `latest-sdk` from active or maintenance channels, including newer stable major versions; it excludes preview and end-of-life channels, refuses unknown channel feeds and malformed metadata, and fails clearly when no supported stable SDK meets the floor. Downloads have a 20-second timeout and 1 MiB response cap, with at most 128 channels; failure never falls back to the minimum. All twelve compiler lanes use `.github/actions/setup-dotnet` with that exact resolved version. The action validates it, installs into a private runner-temporary SDK directory, verifies actual `dotnet --version` equality and records it in job logs and the step summary, so a runner image cannot substitute another installed SDK. The unified release passes its selection to both reusable platform workflows; standalone platform dispatches use the same resolver. `Every_workflow_uses_the_same_resolved_stable_dotnet_sdk` guards the workflow wiring, while `scripts/tests/test_sdk_selection.py` exercises selection and refusal behavior using controlled metadata. **Every job is bounded:** each job in every workflow that does not call a reusable workflow declares a job-level `timeout-minutes` of at most 270 (`Every_job_declares_a_job_level_timeout`) — 270 for the macOS build-test lane (the whole runtime suite under coverage) and for the two Windows test lanes (each runs its Windows selection and the Long Rest suite, publishes the apphost twice and audits it once), which took about 120, 124 (x64) and 131 (arm64) minutes on the hosted runners and are limited to about twice that, so a runner slower than the one measured still finishes, 150 for the macOS release (a Native AOT diagnostic audit, a Native AOT publish and three notarizations), 120 for the macOS workspace-check lane and the macOS Native AOT lane, 90 for the Windows packaging lane, 80 for the five hosted-producer analysis lanes (a 60-minute analysis step after checkout and build), 60 or less elsewhere — so a hang is cut at a stated ceiling instead of holding a signing keychain or a scarce runner for the platform default of six hours; the ceilings bound a hang rather than describe a normal run, and a lane measured on the hosted runners is given a safe multiple of its slowest measured time rather than a figure tightened to it (about twice for the three long lanes and the macOS Native AOT lane, three times for the workspace-check lane). Inside the jobs, `notarytool submit --wait` carries `--timeout 30m`, every `dotnet test` in `ci.yml` and under `scripts/` (the Arcanum, Compendium and Forge suites in the CI lanes, `scripts/coverage.sh`, and the `verify-published-apphost.sh`, `verify-local-ollama-aot.sh` and `verify-local-ollama-long-rest.sh` verifiers that run the Arcanum suite) carries `--blame-hang-timeout 15m --blame-hang-dump-type none` so a hung test host is named and killed without writing a process dump (the local Ollama vision qualification carries 30m in baseline mode or a closed 45m in explicit PDF mode, because its one selected test legitimately spends longer than 15 minutes in cold model turns, and the local Long Rest qualification carries 90m, because its one selected test seeds a corpus through real extraction and then runs a complete sweep, an interrupted and recovered sweep and a turn on a large model), and `ReleasePipelineTests.Every_dotnet_test_invocation_detects_a_hung_test` scans every one of them. `xunit.runner.json` sets `longRunningTestSeconds: 60` together with `diagnosticMessages: true`, the setting that makes the runner print the notice, and a test pins the pair. The macOS portable Native AOT compatibility bridge retains its SHA-512 allowlist in `Directory.Build.targets`: a source-built SDK whose bundled runtime pack is not in that table fails the bridge restore/publish until the pack is audited and its hash added. Latest-SDK selection does not weaken this provenance gate.

1. `native-sqlcipher-assets` (Ubuntu) reads `native-source-manifest.json` and publishes, per RID, whether a verified hermetic SQLCipher asset is checked in. It builds nothing; it exists so a lane whose RID has no asset can be skipped rather than failing at `dotnet build` with ARCSQLC002, and can return on its own once the asset lands.
2. `build-test` (macOS 26) restores/builds Arcanum + Compendium + `TheForge.Ux`, tests Compendium and The Forge, installs ripgrep (the runtime suite's warning-scan fixtures run the real ripgrep, which the runner image does not ship, and `The_macos_build_test_lane_installs_ripgrep_before_it_runs_the_runtime_suite` pins the install ahead of the suite), then runs the runtime coverage gate (`scripts/coverage.sh --threshold --ci-runtime-only`; the hosted-producer source analysis is item 8) and uploads the report. `TheForge.Ux` is compiled because both release workflows ship it, and without that a compile break would merge green.
3. `macos-workspace-check` (macOS 26) pins a root-owned dotnet host and exercises the production `sandbox-exec` jail, then runs the macOS AOT gate plus the admission and Covenant benchmark gates.
4. `windows-suite` (native Windows x64) runs an explicit Windows selection of the Arcanum suite (the Windows-specific classes, the shared `SpellDirectoryTests`/`SpellRepositoryTests`/`SpellScannerTests` that exercise native spell mutation and read containment, plus, by exact name, every test that skips unless the host is Windows; `Every_windows_gated_test_is_selected_by_both_windows_lanes` fails when a Windows-gated test is selected by neither this lane nor the arm64 one) and one Compendium test, never the `Perf` or `HostedProducerAnalysis` categories; the portable suite runs once, on macOS, except that the Long Rest classes also run natively on both Windows architectures (§13.1). It first asserts that the SDK's host RID is `win-x64`, then runs the Windows selection and the `Test Long Rest` step (uploading `windows-long-rest-win-x64`), then runs `./scripts/verify-aot-il-warnings.sh win-x64`, and only then runs the warning-free shipping publish and provider-contract smoke. It is gated on `native-sqlcipher-assets` reporting a verified `win-x64` asset. The gate stays while the asset is present, because the hermetic SQLCipher targets refuse to build a RID without one and no test in the job would execute if it were ever removed.
5. `windows-arm64-suite` (native Windows arm64) runs the same Windows selection and the same native Long Rest qualification (`windows-long-rest-win-arm64`) against the arm64 asset and SDK, runs `./scripts/verify-aot-il-warnings.sh win-arm64`, and only then runs that RID's warning-free shipping publish and provider-contract smoke. It is gated on its own verified asset and rejects an emulated x64 SDK.
6. `aot-il` (macOS 26) installs the run-resolved latest stable .NET SDK above the `global.json` floor, runs `./scripts/verify-aot-il-warnings.sh` for the host RID, and then runs `./scripts/verify-shipping-publish.sh --rid osx-arm64`. It installs ripgrep for both fail-closed warning scans and uses that serviced SDK's compatible Apple linker. Each build or publish leg uses a fresh temporary artifact root, every warning scan ignores caller ripgrep configuration, and the shipping gate launches the exact published apphost as both host and `run --new` CLI through first-session creation and a deterministic in-process OpenAI-compatible streaming provider stub. Cached output, a workstation-specific search policy, or a managed in-process test host therefore cannot substitute for the release behavior the lane reports. CI never contacts Ollama or another real model; real inference, multi-turn context, attachment-version, and vision qualification are local release checks on a machine that owns those provider resources.

7. `static-analysis` (named `Formatting and shell lint`, Ubuntu) tests and checks the C# blank-line formatter, validates every shell script with `shellcheck` and every workflow with `actionlint`.

8. `hosted-producer-primary-analysis`, `hosted-producer-additional-analysis`, `hosted-producer-fixture-analysis`, `hosted-producer-fixture-build-analysis` and `hosted-producer-serve-host-analysis`, with the `hosted-producer-analysis` authority job (named `Hosted producer source analysis`), described in §13.1.

The real-model counterpart is deliberately opt-in and local-only. With Ollama already running and an existing Native AOT apphost already published, run:

```bash
./scripts/verify-local-ollama-aot.sh \
  --executable /absolute/path/to/RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Cli \
  --image /absolute/path/to/checkout/tests/assets/stop-sign.png \
  --model gemma4:e4b
```

`--model` remains the fallback for both roles. Optional `--text-model flint:40b --vision-model qwen3.8:27b` overrides the text and image roles independently, regardless of argument order; specifying only one role leaves the other on the final `--model` value (or its existing default). Missing or whitespace-only supplied names fail before the managed harness starts. The wrapper supplies `ARCANUM_OLLAMA_QUALIFICATION_MODEL` for the effective text role and `ARCANUM_OLLAMA_QUALIFICATION_VISION_MODEL` for the effective image role explicitly, overriding inherited role variables. Direct managed opt-in retains the single-model fallback when the vision variable is absent. Both distinct installed tags are checked only after the existing live opt-in. The initial conversation, Perplexity continuation, independent text recall and attended memory recall use the text model; the attached-image turn uses the vision model. The isolated configuration advertises a distinct text model with vision disabled and tools enabled, a vision model with both enabled, or one shared entry with both enabled. Its default model is the text role; the operator's defaults are untouched. A final read-only SQLCipher check grades `Entries.ModelUsed` for the exact finalized reply sequence, excluding tool wrappers, without adding model data to the product's Entry API contract. Baseline mode does not qualify PDF extraction or embeddings; the explicit PDF phase below adds functional PDF evidence while dedicated embedding qualification remains separate.

For the stronger live search qualification, add `--perplexity --perplexity-key-variable ARCANUM_PERPLEXITY_API_KEY`. The selected environment variable must already contain a nonblank credential; the argument is its name, never its value. This mode authorizes the registered Perplexity provider's paid external request and requires an installed text model that actually invokes native tools and an installed vision model for the image turn (one model may fill both roles). Missing credentials fail before the wrapper launches the managed harness. Without `--perplexity`, the local vision and memory-recall probes remain available and WebBrowsing stays disabled.

The wrapper never publishes Arcanum and never starts or stops Ollama. It builds only the managed qualification harness with warning rejection, then invokes the one qualification method through its exact fully qualified test name. The test writes an independent versioned receipt only after every assertion and cleanup succeeds, and the wrapper rejects a missing, extra-line, or wrong receipt so zero discovered tests cannot report qualification success. The test itself rejects a non-loopback provider endpoint, a missing/non-native Mach-O or PE apphost, a symlink/script, an image whose SHA-256 is not `713ec8279747a2a33ee6e7407155f5c75be51037545aaec18677f0d7f91bf3da`, or an absent model. The pinned user-supplied PNG is tracked unchanged at `tests/assets/stop-sign.png`; local qualification requires those exact bytes, and replacing them requires an intentional fixture rebaseline. After validating the operator path, the test copies the image into its private workspace, validates the snapshot again, and uses only the snapshot's bytes so a concurrent source replacement cannot alter the qualification. The test redirects `HOME`, `USERPROFILE`, `APPDATA`, the Arcanum testing home, configuration, Grimoire, credentials, and workspace into one freshly created child of the platform temp directory, uses the guarded testing credential backend, redacts the synthetic Ollama credential, explicit Perplexity credential, and every known/disclosed master credential together from child-process diagnostics, and retries then reports temporary-tree cleanup failures after stopping only the two Arcanum host processes it owns. The operator's Arcanum home and Keychain/Credential Manager are never consulted. Enhanced configuration stores only the qualification-owned environment reference; after clearing inherited environment, only the owned initial/restarted Arcanum hosts receive that reference's value. CLI processes receive no Perplexity credential, and the wrapper removes the selected source variable from the managed build environment.

The qualification permits three minutes for each cold host/model boundary. The original published CLI `run --new` creates the first Session, introduces a fresh opaque conversation marker and retains exactly its marker-only user/reply pair. The independent CLI recall proves that pinned attachment v1 supplies the initial file fact and recalls that marker. The source is then changed and refreshed to v2; the test proves both versions remain in history, explicitly unpins v1, pins v2, uploads the fixed stop-sign PNG under neutral filename metadata, and restarts the same published host against the same isolated Grimoire. The old master key must still authenticate after restart and no replacement key may be disclosed. After restart, the test exports and byte-compares/dehashes both text versions and the image, then checks every managed attachment payload for an `ARCABLOB` envelope and absence of plaintext token/image bytes. The final CLI vision turn independently recalls the marker, recovers the opaque corrected token from v2, and identifies the explicitly attached image as `OBJECT=STOP SIGN`, `COLOR=RED`, `SHAPE=OCTAGON`, `SIDES=8`, and `TEXT=STOP`; none of those expected values is present in its prompt. Field names, separators, and opaque marker/token values remain exact, while natural-language vision values are compared case-insensitively so harmless `Stop Sign`/`Red` capitalization cannot invalidate correct inference. Local vision mode retains exactly three adjacent user/assistant pairs, six entries.

The same run also creates a separate, provider-free timestamp Session through the public Session and append-entry endpoints. It captures the host-assigned Entry identities and fractional instants, deletes a middle cursor Entry, and checks that the exact older page is returned for equivalent seven-fraction `Z`, `+05:30`, and `-07:00` cursor spellings both before and after the existing host restart. The cursor remains usable after its Entry is gone. A read-only SQLCipher connection, opened with only the isolated installation’s own Data Protection key ring and KDF sidecar, independently checks the actual stored instant text on Entries, Sessions, attachments, pins, inference runs and billable operations; API date serialization alone cannot satisfy the oracle. Every surviving Entry must retain the same timestamp bytes across restart, and another storage check follows the final recall turn. The probe deletes its private Session before the existing transcript checks resume and enables MemoryManagement only in the isolated test configuration. It adds no model turn, and every timestamp assertion precedes the qualification success receipt.

Enhanced mode inserts one authenticated `POST /api/intelligence/ping-stream` continuation in the known Session between the original marker turn and the independent CLI recall. It requires exactly one native `web_search` for the bounded NASA Voyager factual query and no other calls. The dedicated source-generated `PingRequest`/`IntelligenceEvent` client uses `ResponseHeadersRead` and the full caller-controlled three-minute turn budget. It requires successful `application/x-ndjson`, allows blank heartbeats and informational status/context/Ward frames, and drains the stream through EOF. Malformed or duplicate JSON properties, read failure, an incomplete suffix, fatal error/toolError, missing/extra/swapped calls or results, and missing/duplicate/early terminal results fail. Native call/result frames must carry the same nonempty opaque ordinal CallId, exact `web_search` name and argument JSON. Raw accumulated token data must equal terminal `result.message`; `result.data` is a token count. The successful Perplexity payload supplies a nonempty framed answer and valid retained HTTP(S) citations. The first retained citation's actual index and URL form the oracle, including index gaps; no expected URL/index appears in either prompt, and optional absent/zero usage remains valid. The immediate search answer must consume that exact oracle and a fresh opaque search marker. The later independent published CLI recall must reproduce the original marker, attachment-v1 token and exact citation without another search.

Enhanced persistence contains four turns and ten entries: the original marker pair, the search user/finalized-assistant pair followed by adjacent assistant `[ToolCall: web_search({...})]` and system `[ToolResult: {...}]` wrappers, the independent recall pair, and the post-restart vision pair. Sequence order comes from reversing the repository's descending retrieval; finalization changes the reserved assistant's content without moving it after the tool rows. Ordinary persisted wrappers have no native CallId join. Exact captured argument/result strings and unique session-scoped Entry IDs tie native evidence to the durable rows. The qualifier requires all eight pre-restart entries to retain their exact identities, Session and content after restart and through the final ten-entry transcript. Missing, duplicate, fabricated or misordered rows, unsuccessful provider data, changed payloads/identities, and incorrect immediate or later citation consumption fail. Only enhanced success after cleanup emits `local-ollama-aot-perplexity-qualification:v1`; its wrapper rejects the older `local-ollama-aot-qualification:v1` vision-only receipt. Final delivery requiring search runs this enhanced gate on the exact final published candidate with one executed pass and zero failures/skips. The test reserves an ephemeral loopback port and releases it immediately before launch; because another process can claim that port during this unavoidable hand-off, a bind/start collision is reported as a failure rather than retried with mutated persisted configuration. This remains an attachment-backed durable-context correction test, without rewriting prior transcript entries or extracted Saga/Covenant memory. Model text remains probabilistic even at temperature zero, so this is a local release qualification with precise failure diagnostics, never a CI gate. Source-contract tests prevent any workflow or deterministic shipping gate from setting its opt-in or explicitly invoking it; ordinary CI only compiles and reports the default-skipped test.

**Explicit PDF phase.** Add `--pdf` to the same wrapper only when dependency model traffic is authorized. The required PDF invocation uses `--text-model flint:40b --vision-model qwen3.8:27b --pdf --pdf-embedding-model qwen3-embedding:8b`; `--pdf-embedding-window` and `--pdf-embedding-dimensions` default to the existing Long Rest recipe's 40960 and 4096. The opt-in live harness verifies the selected tag is installed, its `/api/show` advertises embedding capability and the same unambiguous context window, and the existing Long Rest dimension probe measures the configured vector width before host startup. It does not install a model, start Ollama or change operator configuration. In PDF mode only, the isolated configuration enables the existing coupled `AttachmentRetrieval` and `Comprehension` gates, which resolve the embedding substrate as enabled even with the standalone `Embeddings` feature false. A separate embedding provider entry has its own verified window/model/dimensions and synthetic credential. Both isolated provider entries use the existing recording forwarder with distinct closed chat/embedding credential identities; baseline mode retains its direct endpoint and existing feature configuration.

The PDF mode has a closed 45-minute hang ceiling; baseline remains 30 minutes and neither mode permits process dumps. With search, the named serial allowances are five original model turns at 3 minutes (15), two host starts at 3 minutes (6), three installed-tag checks at 30 seconds (1.5), the shared PDF metadata/dimension preflight at 5 minutes, and the PDF phase at 10 minutes: 37.5 minutes before control and cleanup work. The PDF phase links each 3-minute turn and the 3-minute index wait to its 10-minute caller/phase token; its separate loopback-only model client avoids the control client's 45-second timeout. The 45-minute ceiling supplies headroom for control/cleanup; it is a hang detector, not a guarantee that every independent control operation can consume its individual maximum cumulatively. The release guard admits only this wrapper's exact baseline/PDF branches and values, refusing unknown variables, extra assignments, zero/unbounded values and changes to another branch. Other wrappers retain their existing literal bounds.

The PDF Session is created in the same fresh isolated Grimoire only after all original main-Session transcript/model and timestamp assertions. A deterministic five-object one-page C# PDF contains fresh per-run opaque seals and manifest quantities/rejects. Neither prompts, neutral `evidence.pdf`/`evidence` metadata, configuration nor unrelated text attachments contain the expected answers. Canonical multipart upload must persist Binary `application/pdf`, exact bound Session identity, length, content hash, name and version. Export through the canonical content route must return exactly the uploaded bytes/hash; the retained payload must have an encrypted `ARCABLOB` envelope without the PDF or either seal in plaintext. The first text-role turn explicitly references that attachment and must calculate the winning manifest's net quantity and seal. The attachment is then pinned with its exact content hash. The second text-role turn omits explicit attachment references and must extract a different inspection seal absent from the first answer. Provider evidence must contain the current Attachment pin frame with the exact source ID, PDF page heading and complete facts, while both actual requests and persisted `Entries.ModelUsed` identify the text model. Completed `stop` outcomes, zero unsolicited tool calls, exact user/reply pairs, unchanged first-turn entries and an unchanged original main Session are required.

A bounded read-only SQLCipher check waits for the exact PDF source hash/version's published index generation, extraction/index timestamps, page text, complete manifest facts and matching chunk/vector dimensions and byte widths. This tests the embedding-enabled index publication path; explicit attachment/pin materialization itself is not called a durable extracted-text cache. The existing forwarder records the actual successful embedding model/request kind/credential and counts variable chunk/query traffic; these functional dependencies do not substitute for the dedicated Long Rest/embedding qualification, which runs LAST. A successful PDF run after every original assertion and all owned cleanup emits `local-ollama-aot-pdf-qualification:v1`, or `local-ollama-aot-pdf-perplexity-qualification:v1` when search is also required. PDF mode rejects baseline/search-only, missing or trailing-byte receipts. Offline fixture/parser, serialized transport, SQLCipher query, evidence-grader and fake-wrapper contracts qualify the harness; they do not claim a real PDF/model run occurred.

**The Long Rest counterpart.** `./scripts/verify-local-ollama-long-rest.sh --executable <apphost> [--chat-model gemma4:e4b] [--default-model qwen3.8:27b] [--embedding-model qwen3-embedding:8b] [--embedding-window 40960] [--embedding-dimensions 4096] [--endpoint http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/] [--report-dir <existing directory>] [--all-embedding-models] [--no-mutiny]` qualifies Long Rest (§21.16) against real models in the same way and under the same refusals: opt-in (`ARCANUM_RUN_LOCAL_OLLAMA_LONG_REST_QUALIFICATION=1`, set by the wrapper, never by a workflow), local-only (the wrapper and the test refuse GitHub Actions), against an already published Native AOT apphost the wrapper never publishes, in a temporary Arcanum home the test creates and removes beneath the same `arcanum-tests` boundary with the same guarded in-memory credential backend, so no key is read from or written to the operator's configuration, home or keychain and no keychain prompt can appear, with a literal-loopback `/v1` endpoint and synthetic provider credentials the test owns, and without starting or stopping Ollama. It selects one test by its exact name under a 90 minute hang bound and accepts only its own receipt, `local-ollama-long-rest-qualification:v1`. `--report-dir` keeps the progress log, the summary and the calibration report (text and JSON) after the wrapper's temporary directory is removed; the calibration is printed either way.

The isolated installation has two provider entries at the one endpoint, as the embedding-window rule of the Compendium requires: `Ollama` (the chat models, each declared text-only with tools; the default pair remains `gemma4:e4b` and `qwen3.8:27b`; `contextWindowLimit` 131072) and `Ollama Embeddings` (the embedding model, `qwen3-embedding:8b` by default; `contextWindowLimit` from `--embedding-window`, 40960 by default, the context length that model reports; a credential variable of its own). `fastModel` is the chat model, so it must serve every Long Rest chat call; `defaultModel` serves the ordinary turn. The two roles may name the same exact tag (for example, `--chat-model flint:40b --default-model flint:40b`), in which case the isolated configuration declares that text model once and retains the fast role's standard reasoning metadata for adjudication with reasoning off. The sweep grader requires actual Long Rest chat purposes (both summary and adjudication in the first sweep, at least one Long Rest chat call in recovery) on the exact fast tag with the chat entry's credential, and embeddings on the exact embedding tag with the embedding entry's credential. Ordinary chat and unclassified requests during a sweep are findings; metadata cannot substitute for required positive chat evidence. When the chat/default tags differ, any sweep traffic naming the default tag remains a finding; when they coincide, the report identifies the shared tag and relies on request purpose and credential rather than claiming the default tag served nothing. Offline contracts exercise this configuration and the actual grader against requests recorded by a fake loopback forwarder; they do not establish live model quality or coverage beyond the existing qualification. As before, `integrations.embeddings` names the second entry with `--embedding-dimensions` dimensions (4096 by default, `qwen3-embedding:8b`'s own size; `embeddinggemma` returns 768 and reports a 2,048-token window), which must equal the embedding model's own vector size because the host's Saga writes ask for the provider's default size and refuse a vector of any other length, so the test asks the model for one vector before it creates anything and fails at once, naming the flag, when the sizes differ; Saga, Embeddings, Annals, Metrics and `longRest` are on and the Covenant is off, so only the clean partition is exercised. Both entries point at a loopback forwarder the test owns, in front of Ollama, which forwards every request unchanged and records the model id, the credential class (never its value), the decoded text the provider was shown, the usage it reported and whether the response reached the host, so that "which model served this call", "was this memory ever sent" and "what did the provider bill" are read from the wire and not from the host's own account of itself. It can reach nothing but that endpoint: a request path that would resolve to another scheme, host or port, to a URI carrying credentials, or out of the endpoint's `/v1/` path is answered `502` and never forwarded. It can also receive the provider's whole answer to a chosen request without passing on a byte, run a hook, and then withhold the answer for good, which is how scenario B kills the host after the provider has answered and billed a call and before the host has seen any of it. Before any child process is started the test proves, from the environment that child is about to be given, that the product's own testing gate (`TestCredentialStorePolicy`) selects the in-memory credential store, and refuses to start it otherwise, so a gate that silently failed could not turn into a keychain prompt; the failure names the variables and never their values. A test that needs durable evidence the API does not carry (the provider-effects journal, the sweep rows, the generation's hierarchy and its search index) reads the isolated Grimoire read-only, the way `arcanum doctor` opens it: SQLCipher with the passphrase derived from that home's own Data Protection key ring, KDF sidecar and sealed secret, never the operator's installation and never an operating-system credential store.

The corpus is seeded through the host's own Saga extraction, because that is the only way the host writes a Saga memory: five Sessions tell it thirty-seven facts (clusters of near-paraphrases, two confusable pairs of neighbours, two exact-duplicate pairs and unrelated singles; no Session holds two facts of one cluster, so the extraction model keeps them apart), the memories it writes are matched back to the facts they came from by word overlap, and the operator then retires one memory of a cluster and pins one of another through the API. The memories are not corrected afterwards, because the host offers no way to write a Saga memory except extraction and what extraction writes is what the sweep reads; a corrected Session-owned memory stays a source all the same (its operator-stated version names no Session, which the ownership check accepts, §21.16.1). A small local model sometimes answers a seeding prompt with a tool call the isolated host refuses (a delegated subagent needs a budget the qualification does not give it), which ends the turn with exit code 1 before anything is remembered; the run then tells that Session again, up to three attempts, reports each retry as an observation, and never retries a turn that left memories behind, because they could not be attributed. Extraction runs only while the corpus is seeded; the host is then restarted gracefully with Long Rest on and extraction off.

The host's Prometheus exporter starts with the host (it is resolved at startup and not by the first scrape), so after every restart the run answers a few authenticated requests and then makes the first scrape, and a first scrape that carries none of them is a finding: it would mean the exporter only started at that scrape and lost what was measured before it, the Long Rest counters included. The test then proves three scenarios in order. **A, a clean Global sweep:** it completes with no invalid adjudication answer and no park only an operator clears (a park of that kind is still answered with `arcanum operation retry`, up to twenty-four times, so the run can go on, but each one is a finding), accepts at least one summary and one adjudication and writes receipts that name consolidated memories, folds nothing into a survivor about something else, folds both exact-duplicate groups (a duplicate pack is folded locally, without a model call) and at least half of the paraphrase folds the labelled clusters allow, sends no adjudication request that holds memories of more than one labelled cluster or an unrelated single beside others, leaves the retired and the pinned memory unconsolidated and their text in no request the provider received, leaves the completed generation's search-index rows at zero while its nodes remain, is served by the fast model alone with the chat entry's credential for chat and the embedding entry's for embeddings, settles every paid unit (none left `Prepared`, `Disclosed` or `Sent`) and reconciles three figures that must agree exactly: the journal's paid calls and tokens, the responses the provider delivered, and the budget's spend at synthetic prices; it counts no park for a transient reason or a stale generation and no refused clean request, every needs-operator park it counts is one the run answered, and an unchanged request replays the completed operation without one more provider call. Every accepted summary of the completed generation fits the Embedding-Bounded Summary limit the recipe derives from the embedding window (8192 UTF-8 bytes, the most a recipe may carry, at the default 40,960-token window; 1766 at 2,048 tokens), the receipts the consolidated memories name are fetched through `GET /api/memory/saga/long-rest/receipts/{id}` and each must be the receipt that memory names, name that memory among its targets and the survivor it was folded into, and carry no memory text, and `GET /api/health` after the scenario is not `Unhealthy` and carries a healthy `LongRest` component and, once every sweep has settled, a healthy `DurableOperations` component. **B, a forced restart:** the pinned memory is unpinned, so the next sweep is a new one; the forwarder holds back the provider's answer to the first Long Rest chat request of that sweep, and the host is killed with SIGKILL at that moment, after the provider has answered and billed the call and before the host has seen a byte of it, with the attempt `Sent` in the journal. The wait for that moment fails at once, naming the operation and the traffic so far, if the sweep ends, or ten minutes pass, without such a request, instead of waiting out the sweep budget. The same published host is started on the same home and its worker must recover the sweep **without an operator**: the sweep's first park must be a resumable code (a killed owner's stale lease is `long_rest.interrupted`, never a code only an operator clears), it must be seen running two attempts beyond the dead owner's (the takeover that parks it and the worker's readmission) before the run first answers a park as an operator, and the run answers a park with `arcanum operation retry` only once that readmission is observed, when the park belongs to the sweep running again (a paid answer the model got wrong parks under `LongRest.InvalidOutput`, which only an operator clears; the dead owner's lease must lapse first, about five minutes after its last renewal). An operator retry before the readmission is still given, so that the scenarios after it report, but it is a finding, because an operator's readmission also stamps a park and counts an attempt and would hide a failed automatic recovery; and a park seen before the readmission under a code the worker does not resume is a finding of its own. The sweep must complete, the interrupted attempt must be settled (failed as unknown usage, or released) with no paid call counted twice, the answer the provider billed and the host never received is reported as unknown usage and never counted as paid, the readmission and the crash park are both counted, and the restarted host must report at least one of each (the worker counts the `long_rest.interrupted` park where it readmits the sweep, in class `resume_later`, because the Pure Park Handler that wrote it has nothing to count with), the first sweep's operation stays `Completed` with its generation's data deleted, and the summary-bound and health checks of scenario A apply to the new generation and the restarted host. The interrupted send's budget reservation stays held until it expires, because unknown usage is never estimated or written as zero; the run reads that hold from the Grimoire, reports it, requires no more holds than interrupted units, and adds it to the priced provider usage before comparing the budget's spend. **C, one ordinary turn:** with clean debt outstanding (a pin and an unpin of an unconsolidated memory), one Session turn on the default model must succeed on that model through the chat credential, the sweep its clean request starts belongs to the background worker, and cancelling that sweep must reach a terminal state, after which `GET /api/health` is read again.

Every consolidation either sweep applied is also graded against the corpus's labels: a memory folded into a survivor that says the same thing is right, a memory folded into a survivor about something else has been suppressed from recall for good, and each such fold is a product-level finding. A finding does not stop the run (the scenarios after it still report their results), and the test fails after the last scenario with every finding and writes no receipt. **The Mutiny Scenario** then repeats scenario A's sweep on a second, freshly seeded installation in which the forwarder rewrites every adjudication answer into the all-pairs verdict ("every one of these memories states the same fact"), whatever the model said, keeping the usage the provider reported. It proves the half of the guarantee that does not depend on the model: no request ever held memories of two topics, so a model that agrees to everything folds every cluster (at least nine tenths of the folds the labelled clusters allow) and folds nothing across topics, except the pairs the calibration counts at or above a floor, which is none on an embedding model that separates topics. `--no-mutiny` skips it. The calibration report is always written, before scenario B can fail: for the labelled corpus it lists the lexical coverage of within-cluster and cross-cluster ordered pairs against the nomination bar (200 thousandths), the leaf-to-leaf cosines of the real vectors, the Background Floor of each labelled memory (read by the product's own sampler from every leaf of the generation) with the margin of each true pair above its anchor's floor, the margin of each other pair below it and the share of true pairs the gate keeps, and the cosines of each summary to its children, to the leaves it covers, to the leaves it does not and to foreign summaries against the summary gate, with each distribution and a threshold table. `--all-embedding-models` runs the whole qualification once for each embedding model installed in Ollama (its window and vector size read from Ollama itself, one report directory per model; there is no fixed list, so a model that is not installed is simply not run, and an installed model that Ollama will not describe is named and fails the wrapper after the others have run, never skipped silently), because whether the gate alone carries the guarantee is a property of the embedding model. The calibration measures and reports; nothing in the product reads it, and asserting it is deliberately loose (the report has pairs to compare, true pairs rank above the others, at least nine tenths of the true pairs are at or above their anchor's floor, and every other pair is under its anchor's floor, which is a finding on a model that does not separate topics). The test writes its receipt only after every scenario, the graceful stop of the last host, the plaintext-credential scan and the cleanup have succeeded. Model text and model latency remain probabilistic, so this is a local release qualification with precise failure diagnostics, never a CI gate; source-contract tests (`LocalOllamaLongRestQualificationContractTests`) prevent any workflow or deterministic gate from setting its opt-in or invoking it.

**Why a Windows lane exists.** Every Windows-only test guards itself with `Skip.IfNot(OperatingSystem.IsWindows(), …)`, which is right on a developer machine and worthless as a signal: on the Linux and macOS lanes those tests report green while asserting nothing. For a long time no job ran the suite on Windows at all, so the entire Windows surface — Credential Manager, Job Objects, AppContainer, `PATHEXT` resolution, NTFS permissions — was effectively untested. That is how `WindowsOsCredentialStore` shipped persisting uninitialized heap in place of the operator's API key.

`Skip` is the required idiom for a platform gate, and not merely a convention: a bare `if (…) { return; }` reports **Passed**, which is indistinguishable in a test report from a test that ran, whereas `Skip` says out loud that nothing was asserted. Two exceptions stay on the bare form. The require-variable lane guards (`WindowsCiSurfaceTests`, `WorkspaceCheckToolTests.Macos_ci_requires_real_workspace_check_production_surface`, `GrimoireFixtureConcurrencyTests.Ci_has_packaged_sqlcipher_native_asset`) are meant to no-op outside their lane rather than advertise a skip on every developer machine. And `CA1416` reads a bare `return` as a platform guard while a `Skip.If` call tells it nothing, so a test that then calls a platform-restricted API (`File.SetUnixFileMode`, `File.GetUnixFileMode`, and friends) keeps the bare form — converting those would trade honest reporting for dozens of platform-compatibility warnings.

A lane that skips everything looks identical to a lane that passes, so the job sets `ARCANUM_REQUIRE_WINDOWS_SUITE=true` and `WindowsCiSurfaceTests` turns that case red: it asserts the runner really is Windows, that a credential backend is reachable, that `ARCANUM_TEST_OS_CREDENTIAL_STORE=true` is set, and that the Windows-gated test classes still exist. This mirrors the macOS lane's `ARCANUM_REQUIRE_MACOS_WORKSPACE_CHECK` guard. The credential-store assertion closes the one hole the other three left open: `OsCredentialStoreRoundTripTests` gates on that variable *before* it gates on the platform, the variable is set in exactly one place, and nothing asserted it — so deleting or mistyping that one line silently removed every real-backend round trip while the whole lane stayed green. The class-count guard excludes `WindowsCiSurfaceTests` from its own count and additionally requires at least one counted class to carry a `[Skippable*]` attribute, because most classes whose name contains "Windows" drive fakes and pure logic and run identically on every OS: without that second assertion the count could stay above its floor while the only genuinely platform-gated class was deleted.

The lane is gated on the asset: it runs when `win-x64` has a verified hermetic SQLCipher asset and needs no workflow edit when one is built, verified, and checked in, which is what the gate is for. `native-sqlcipher-assets` emits a workflow warning naming any pending RID, and `ContinuousIntegrationWorkflowTests.No_workflow_builds_on_a_runner_whose_native_sqlcipher_asset_is_missing` keeps an ungated lane out of this workflow and any other. A gap is not closed by adding a probe or a fallback to the NativeSqlCipher targets; ARCSQLC002 exists to prevent precisely that.

`ProcessRunnerResourceLimitTests.Process_exceeding_cpu_limit_is_terminated_and_breached` and `…_memory_limit_…` prove a runaway child is actually killed on a CPU or memory breach rather than that a `ulimit` string was assembled. They spawn a process the kernel must reap, so they are opt-in behind `ARCANUM_TEST_RESOURCE_LIMIT_ENFORCEMENT=true` on macOS and Linux. macOS memory is additionally pinned unconditionally: `MacOs_MemoryLimit_Is_Enforced_By_Footprint_Monitor` runs a child that allocates 256 MB under a 32 MB ceiling and passes only when the footprint monitor kills it and the breach is attributed to memory (a child that escaped the ceiling sleeps 30 s and completes). `ProcessResourceLimiterTests.Prelude_FailsClosed_WhenUlimitRejected` and `ProcessRunnerResourceLimitTests.Pre_exec_limit_failure_is_reported_as_a_resource_limit_apply_failure` run the real prelude under a lowered hard descriptor limit and prove the target never runs. They are real tests and not `[Fact(Skip = "…")]` declarations: an unconditional skip cannot be switched on without editing source, so it would leave no way to run them manually.

`CampaignRootCaseSensitiveVolumeTests` need two directories whose names differ only by case, which the default macOS volume cannot hold (there `proj` and `Proj` are one directory, so a case-sensitivity bug cannot be shown). They attach a 32 MB case-sensitive APFS disk image with `hdiutil` through `CaseSensitiveVolume` (no privilege and no browser entry, mounted inside a private temporary directory and detached when the class is done) and skip wherever one cannot be attached: every non-macOS host, or a sandbox without `hdiutil`. They cover the contained lookup, the spelled lookup and the attachment source authorizer (the reference and refresh routes), each with a strict registration beside a case-sibling one. `CampaignRepositoryContainedPathCostTests` registers three thousand roots on disk and compares the fastest of five unrelated lookups, contained and spelled, with a 250 ms ceiling, an order of magnitude above the measured cost and below the cost of canonicalising each root, so it fails on a regression to a per-root path walk and not on a busy machine; the spelled case also asserts that a path spelled through a link inside a root is still that root's and that a root registered through a link is found from the physical spelling.

`OsCredentialStoreRoundTripTests` is the one test that writes to a real OS secret store rather than `InMemoryOsCredentialStore`, so it is opt-in behind `ARCANUM_TEST_OS_CREDENTIAL_STORE=true` and stays off on developer machines; CI runners are disposable and set it. It is platform-agnostic on purpose — each OS reaches a different implementation through the same contract, and a round trip that compares the exact secret back is precisely the assertion the Windows defect would have failed.

Packaging workflows are separate manual workflows: the Windows set (Native AOT Arcanum, Compendium and The Forge, one RID per run) and signed/notarized macOS arm64, both of which `release.yml` calls. `build-windows.yml` validates that its SDK is native to the selected RID, runs that RID's AOT diagnostic profile, and only then performs the normal warning-free publish and packaging; release evidence therefore belongs to the exact commit and architecture being archived rather than to an earlier CI run. The Windows packaging lane carries the same `native-sqlcipher-assets` gate as `ci.yml`, for the same reason and with more of it: a `workflow_dispatch:`-only pipeline fails no pull request, so an ungated one stays broken invisibly until an operator reaches for it to cut a release, and then presents as a packaging failure at the worst possible moment rather than as the missing prerequisite it is. `linux-x64` is absent from the manifest by design rather than by omission — Linux is not a shipping RID (§5.4.4a), which is why `package-linux.sh` exits 2 with that same guidance — so no workflow carries a Linux job: a job gated on a RID the manifest does not ship can never run and only reads as a dormant feature (`No_workflow_job_is_gated_on_a_rid_absent_from_the_manifest`). Restoring Linux means adding the RID, building and verifying its asset on a native runner, checking it in, and adding its job to the release workflows together. The old `private-beta-release.yml` (a one-RID Windows path beside that dead Linux job, without the per-RID audit) was deleted so that `release.yml` is the only release entry point. Every action reference in every workflow is pinned to a full commit SHA with the version in a trailing comment, `ReleasePipelineTests.Workflows_pin_every_third_party_action_to_a_commit` enforces that repository-wide rather than only where secrets are in reach, and `.github/dependabot.yml` bumps the pins. SQLCipher tests retain their normal skip behavior when the native asset is absent.
