## 17. Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **RDG** | ASP.NET Core Request Delegate Generator for Minimal API handlers. |
| **NDJSON** | Newline-delimited JSON: one complete JSON value per line for native inference and machine-readable watch output. |
| **Grimoire** | Encrypted local SQLite (EF Core + SQLCipher) session store. |
| **Comm Link** | Operator alerting (`ICommLinkDispatcher`, webhook, MCP `send_commlink_alert`, `POST /api/commlink/send`). |
| **Eye of the World** | Situational directory perception (§15). |
| **Chronosync** | Temporal workspace delta vs last `WorkspaceContext` baseline. |
| **MCP** | Model Context Protocol — tool servers over stdio / HTTP / in-process (§4.2). |
| **Heraldry** | A2A Agent Card (§5.7.1). |
| **Sending** | A2A task (inbound or outward via `dispatch_sending` / `POST /api/conclave/sendings`). |
| **Archmage Client** | Outward A2A delegate (`dispatch_sending`, `arcanum conclave dispatch`). |
| **Delegation chain** | Opaque per-process node ids carried in A2A message metadata for cycle detection (§5.7.1). |
| **The Proving Grounds / Trial / Inquisitor** | Ephemeral LLM validation runner (§20). |
| **Resilience** | Provider health + fallback retry (§10.1); default off. |
| **The Weave / Divination / Imprint** | Embedding substrate / cosine search / stored vector (§21). |
| **Lore** | Legacy operator key-value (`/api/lore`); not model-directed. |
| **The Lexicon** | Model-writable entity memory (§10.6). |
| **Saga** | Auto-extracted associative memory (§21.9); no model writes to it, and an operator curates one memory at a time through §21.13. |
| **Arcane Resonance** | Spell `dependencies` injection (§10.2.2). |
| **Spell Routing** | Pre-flight spell selection (`FullGrimoire` / `DirectResonance` / `FilteredDivination`). |
| **`vec0`** | Historical: an optional sqlite-vec KNN index. Removed — the hermetic runtime omits extension loading, so managed cosine is the only search path (§5.4.4a, §21.2). |
| **Schema family** | Which capability owns a schema object: `Core` or `Covenant`. Independent of transaction tier (§5.4.5). |
| **Transaction tier** | Which install transaction an object lives or dies with, and therefore its failure domain: `Core` (startup-blocking), `CovenantCanonical` (Covenant unavailable on failure), `CovenantAccelerator` (inspection search degraded on failure) (§5.4.5a). |
| **`grimoire_feature_schemas`** | The per-tier metadata table recording family, tier, version, source-definition and installed-catalog fingerprints, install time, and health. Its version means the tier is completely at that version and was validated there. Replaces a migration history table (§5.4.5a). |
| **Version chain** | A tier's ordered, closed statement of every version it has had and how to reach the one this binary declares: the head manifest plus one step per version above 1 (§10.25). |
| **Version step** | One move from a version to the next: an ordered list of statements from `Transitions/V<n>/`, a pinned fingerprint for the version it leaves, and at most one resumable sweep (§10.25). |
| **`grimoire_schema_transitions`** | The core journal holding one row per tier while a version run is in flight. The row's existence is the phase; there is no phase column (§10.25). |
| **Schema backfill** | A bounded, checkpointed, idempotent data sweep a version step depends on before that version may be recorded. Its cursor is written inside the batch's own transaction (§10.25). |
| **`CovenantRuntimeGenerationProvider`** | Sole mutator of one immutable live generation containing envelope keys, authority, and availability (§5.4.5b). |
| **`ICovenantAvailability`** | Read-only lock-free projection of the current runtime generation's complete availability snapshot (§5.4.5b). |
| **Covenant operation lease** | The generation-bound capability every Covenant database access holds for the whole operation. Scoped to Global or one Campaign, or installation-wide through the sole `CovenantInstallationReadLease` (§10.11). |
| **Exclusive recovery owner** | The operation ID, operation code, and effect digest that closed a Covenant scope. Resume compares all three; a different one can never adopt that closed scope (§10.11). |
| **Canonical search sequence** | The counter one canonical batch advances when a head changed. The accelerator's applied tuple is compared against it to decide FTS eligibility (§10.11). |
| **Search outbox** | The content-free canonical delta queue the accelerator consumes in whole sequences. It carries identities and one nullable desired-version pointer, never Covenant text (§10.11). |
| **Output Formatting Directive** | Terminal-safe Markdown subset for CLI (§10.5). |

## 18. Document maintenance

The repository maintains seven canonical documents plus the focused chat-loop companion. Resolve a contradiction in the document that owns that contract. Update the owning document in every change set.

- `Arcanum.DESIGN.md` for architecture, design decisions, persistence, runtime behavior, testing, and packaging;
- `Arcanum.API.md` for native and OpenAI-compatible routes, wire contracts, status mapping, and public error codes;
- `Arcanum.Command.Reference.md` for CLI commands, arguments, options, aliases, interactive commands, output modes, and exit behavior;
- `Compendium.README.md` for the complete public configuration surface and editor behavior;
- [`docs/Arcanum.Engineering.md`](Arcanum.Engineering.md) for concise agent/operator orientation and runnable commands;
- `Arcanum.Design.Human.md` for human navigation without duplicating technical or configuration contracts;
- `Arcanum.DEBUGGING.Human.md` for verified breakpoint and debugging recipes.

`Arcanum.CHAT-LOOP.md` is a deliberately narrow companion to §10.7. Keep it synchronized when the shared model/tool loop, attachment continuation ordering, materialization ledger, attachment memory gate, or Command Center context projection changes.

Architecture, contract, configuration, persistence, MCP, CLI, desktop, or distribution changes are incomplete until the owning canonical documents are updated in the same change set.

## 19. The Tower and The Forge — the authored-resource domain and the desktop Inference IDE

Two distinct surfaces, described together because they are the two halves of the same workflow, and named apart because one name for both is what makes a reader conclude that Campaigns, Spells, and Prompts need a desktop application to exist:

1. **The Tower** — the server-side Campaign/Spell/Prompt/Session/Codex registry (`Core/Tower`, `Api/Tower`, `Infrastructure/Tower`, `Cli/Commands/Tower`). It is reachable over HTTP and from the CLI, and runs headless.
2. **The Forge** — the cross-platform Avalonia **Inference IDE** (`RetroDownfall.TheForge.Core` / `.Ux`) that consumes Arcanum exclusively over HTTP.

The desktop app does not run inference, open the Grimoire, or duplicate server business logic. Nothing the Tower offers requires it: an operator who never installs The Forge can create, name, and manage every authored resource through the API and the CLI.

### 19.1 Data models

| Entity | Storage | Notes |
|--------|---------|-------|
| **Campaign** | `Campaigns` | Path, settings JSON, `SanctumConfigJson` (§11.15) |
| **Prompt** | `Prompts` | Versioned; nullable `CampaignId` (null = global); partial unique indexes |
| **Spell sidecar** | Disk `SPELL.json` | Sibling of `SPELL.md`; legacy `SKILL.json` read fallback |

### 19.2 Architecture

Campaign/Spell/Prompt endpoints → repositories → Grimoire; `CampaignBackedWorkspaceRegistry` bridges campaigns into `/api/workspaces`. Spell bodies remain on disk.

Campaign mutations use parameterized, field-scoped SQLite updates on the scoped context's admitted connection and current transaction. Header edits own name (and normalized `NameLower`), type, description and settings; Sanctum edits own only `SanctumConfigJson`; bundle import owns only settings; workspace edits own only name and type. Each also writes the caller-supplied `UpdatedAt`, preserving the last writer's timestamp rather than treating it as a monotonic revision. The statement returns the stored row, so a stale detached read cannot overwrite another owner's fields. Any tracked copy of that Campaign is detached after the write attempt to prevent a subsequent EF save from replaying it. A missing row returns `Campaign.NotFound`; the authoritative `NameLower` unique-index collision returns `Campaign.DuplicateName`. The workspace bridge maps those outcomes to its existing workspace errors. Prompt updates likewise return `Prompt.NotFound` when deletion wins after their read, while retaining their unique-version and Campaign foreign-key mappings.

### 19.3 Key decisions

- Operator term **Campaign** / `/api/campaigns` (no `/api/skills`).
- The read-only provider connectivity probe uses one five-second deadline for its outbound HTTP request and capped response-body read, including a body that stalls after headers. Caller cancellation propagates independently; deadline expiry returns an unreachable probe result. The response cap remains 4 MiB and does not buffer a declared oversized body.
- `SPELL.json` preferred; writes never create `SKILL.json`.
- Export wire `spellJson` (legacy `skillJson` on import).
- Prompt `/test` = assemble only (`SkipSpellRouting`) and return the model-aware `ContextTokenBreakdown` for the assembled system/user messages, current MCP tool schemas, provider framing, safety margin, and reserved answer; `/execute(-stream)` = live inference.
- Schema is installed by the embedded SQL-script/bootstrap path on host start; there is no supported user-data migration program (§5.4.5).

### 19.4 Disk layout

`{campaign}/.arcanum/` on register; prompts export under `.arcanum/prompts/`; workspace spells at `{workspace}/spells/{name}/SPELL.md` + optional `SPELL.json`.

### 19.5 Error codes

Forge codes on `ErrorCodes` + `ArcanumErrorMapper` (API §8.23). A few endpoint-local literals remain at call sites.

### 19.6 Apprentice orchestration

Persistent agents + Chronicle SSE — behaviour in §5.7. Table `Apprentices`; Chronicle in-memory only. Conclave / Simulacrum / Second Wind / Shifting Fate / Divine Intervention: §5.7.

**Placement.** The Apprentice lifecycle contracts live in `Core/Conclave/` under `RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Core.Conclave`: the entity and its checkpoint, `PlanStep`, the status and Chronicle event enumerations, the request and response DTOs, the execution policy and plan parser, the repository and runtime ports, and `IConclaveArchmage` with its cast request. They are contracts of the multi-agent coordination domain rather than of any one client that consumes them, and the desktop workbench is one such client. The eight `ApprenticeStatus` names are the literal text persisted to the `Apprentices.Status` column, so renaming a member is a schema change wearing a source-compatible edit's clothes.

**`GET /api/apprentices` ordering and the identity tie-breaker:** results order by `(UpdatedAt DESC, Id DESC)` and page on the same bare-timestamp `beforeUpdatedAt` cursor the session list uses, so they carry the identical tie contract described in §11.16. Ties are ordinary here rather than exceptional — a Conclave fan-out creates a batch of child Apprentices inside one clock tick — so without the `Id` component the order among them would be undefined and the keyset cursor could not reason about a tie straddling a page boundary. Pages are therefore cut at tie boundaries: every row sharing the first excluded row's timestamp is deferred to the next page, which the strict `UpdatedAt <` predicate then admits in full. A page whose rows are all one timestamp widens to the complete tie group instead and may exceed the requested `limit`, so the cursor always advances. The filter, the order, the `UpdatedAt <` cursor, and a `LIMIT` of one row past the page all run in the direct SQLite query, so rows beyond the page and their `Plan` and `CheckpointData` blobs are never read (the prompt list pages the same way with `ORDER BY Name, UpdatedAt DESC` and `LIMIT`/`OFFSET`). Only the widened tie group costs two further bounded queries, the group itself (at most 1,000 rows, a ceiling that does not move with `limit`, so a `limit` above 1,000 whose whole page is one timestamp always fails; a larger group fails loudly rather than clipping, as the Session list does, and the route answers it as the logged **500** `Hub.Unhandled` an unexpected `InvalidOperationException` always is; `ApprenticeEndpointTests` pins the route's status, code and log line against a seeded 1,001-row group) and an existence probe for older rows. The prompt list's `ORDER BY "Name"` is SQLite's binary collation, which compares UTF-8 bytes and so orders by code point; the client-side ordinal sort it replaced compared UTF-16 code units. The two differ only between a supplementary-plane character and one in U+E000–U+FFFF, and no prompt name is expected to straddle that.

### 19.7 Desktop project model and architecture

The desktop Inference IDE is part of `RetroDownfall.Arcanum.slnx`:

| Project | Responsibility | Dependency |
|---------|----------------|------------|
| `RetroDownfall.TheForge.Core` | Forge-local models, mirrored API DTOs, settings, source-generated JSON contexts, API-key resolution; no Avalonia | `RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Core`, `RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Secrets` (the OS keychain read of API-key resolution) |
| `RetroDownfall.TheForge.Ux` | Avalonia desktop application | `RetroDownfall.TheForge.Core`, `RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Infrastructure` (installation mutation coordination and the shared outbound address policy only) |
| `RetroDownfall.TheForge.Tests` | xUnit tests | `RetroDownfall.TheForge.Ux`, `RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Infrastructure` (the mutation coordination the local-write tests drive) |

All inherit `0.1.0-beta` from `Directory.Build.props`. Core references the portable Arcanum Core leaf and the isolated Secrets project, through which `ApiKeyResolver` reads the OS keychain. DTOs that live in the ASP.NET-heavy Api assembly are re-declared locally rather than adding an Api project reference. The Ux is an HTTP client of the host and names Infrastructure for two things only: the installation mutation coordination around local file writes (`AddArcanumClientMutationCoordination`, driven by `TheForgeLocalMutationRunner`), and the shared outbound address policy `OutboundUrlGuard.IsBlockedForUntrustedEgress`, by which `MarkdownImageSsrfPolicy` judges the addresses its pinned image sockets connect to (§11.11). `CliInfrastructureBoundaryTests` pins the Forge sources that name Infrastructure, and pins this table's dependency column to each project's references.

The Ux follows MVVM with `CommunityToolkit.Mvvm`; every ViewModel derives from `ViewModelBase`. `ServiceCollectionConfigurator` composes `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection` without a service locator. Only the named-HTTP `ArcanumApiClient` calls `HttpClient` directly; per-route services wrap it. `ArcanumSseClient` handles server-sent events. `ArcanumConnectionService` polls `GET /api/health` every five seconds while `AutoConnect` is true and exposes connection state to The Anvil.

The client supports both stream families:

- NDJSON: `POST /api/intelligence/ping-stream`, `POST /api/spells/{name}/execute-stream`, and `POST /api/prompts/{id}/execute-stream`.
- SSE: Session live streams, Apprentice Chronicles, and `/api/events/logs|mcp|daemon`. The parser recognizes `data: ...\n\n`, terminal `[DONE]`, and ignores `: keep-alive`.

The desktop bundles as self-contained Avalonia on .NET 10 and is not NativeAOT. This does not relax the Arcanum host's source-generated wire contracts or AOT-analyzer discipline (§9).

At startup The Forge parses the shared Core deep-link envelope before opening a resource. A valid link waits for `ConnectionState.Connected` without inventing a timeout, then routes through existing ViewModel/navigation services. Waiting survives a transient `ConnectionState.Error`: the health poller settles there after three consecutive missed polls but keeps polling, so a link that arrives while Arcanum is restarting or still booting routes once the connection recovers. The one terminal answer is an auth-class failure (`Security.MissingApiKey`, `Auth.Unauthorized`), whose rejected key is cached for the process lifetime — waiting for a recovery that can never come would hang the link silently, so it is rejected and the caller's failure whisper fires. Wrong-target, malformed, and unsupported future-schema links are rejected without exposing their raw payload. Normal startup remains unchanged when no link is present.

### 19.8 Desktop wire contracts

- Native `/api` JSON uses `ApiResponse<T>`: `{data?, isSuccess, error?, traceId?}` in camelCase. Failure/default data is omitted. `Error` is `{code,message,details?}`.
- Forge-local mirrors for Api-owned types include `HealthReportDto`, `HealthComponentDto`, integer-valued `HealthStatus`, `InstanceMetadataDto`, `GrimoireStatsDto`, `BudgetSummaryDto`, `OptionalWorkspaceRequest`, and diagnostic `ToolInvokeRequest`/`ToolInvokeResponse` whose arguments/result are `JsonElement`. There is no blanket `JsonStringEnumConverter`; per-type converters preserve the server wire, including integer `HealthStatus`.
- `POST /api/providers/test` accepts `AiProviderKind.OpenAICompatible` only — it is an endpoint connectivity probe, and a Familiar has no endpoint. Familiar readiness is `GET /api/providers/{name}/familiar-probe` instead. `POST /api/intelligence/arsenal` accepts an optional `OptionalWorkspaceRequest` and returns `WorkspaceArsenalDto`. Its URL-validation path shares the guard's parsing, DNS resolution, and address policy while retaining typed syntax/DNS/policy outcomes; existing guard callers keep their original codes and messages. Connect-time pinning retains typed DNS/policy refusal on the existing `OutboundConnectException`, without changing its type or inner transport causes. Probe failures log at Warning with only the configured host and a fixed reason class; they never log the endpoint, query, userinfo, API key, resolved address, provider body, or exception. Model-list parsing rejects malformed/missing `data` and invalid entries, while an empty `data` array remains reachable. The Forge's actual provider data source preserves failed-envelope `Error.Message` in the visible test result. The five-second deadline still spans request headers and capped body reads, and caller cancellation propagates.
- `WardDto.WardId` is a string and expiry is `ExpiresAt`. Allow/deny uses one `POST /api/wards/{id}` with `ResolveWardRequest(bool Allow, string? Reason)`.
- `IntelligenceEvent` token text is `data`, not `message`. Terminal `result.message` is the complete answer; legacy `result.data` is the decimal total-token string. Native usage may also include cached/reasoning counts. The string discriminator is camelCase: `token`, `reasoning`, `toolCall`, `toolResult`, `toolError`, `warded`, `wardResolved`, `status`, `sessionBound`, deprecated `conversationBound`, `context`, `result`, or `error`. Reasoning is typed `{text,output}` and never carries provider-protected data.
- The NDJSON reader preflights the discriminator before strict source-generated deserialization. Unknown nonblank future values are skipped; malformed JSON and missing/non-string/blank/padded types are logged and skipped. A bounded line reader over The Forge's own `StreamingTextReader` (which hands characters over after every single stream read and never goes back to the stream for more to fill a buffer) reassembles multibyte UTF-8 split across transport reads, caps each protocol line at 1 MiB, discards an over-cap frame, and resumes at the next line. The SSE parser applies the same line cap plus an 8 MiB aggregate event cap.
- The Tome renders reasoning in a separate live role and never appends it to the answer. Mutable live buffers publish coalesced snapshots with a final flush and explicit truncation: 64 KiB for reasoning and 200,000 characters for other live messages.
- `ChatCompletionUsage` retains OpenAI snake_case members inside the otherwise camelCase native envelope.
- `ApprenticeDetailDto.Status` is a PascalCase string (`"Running"`, etc.); Plan/step statuses are free-form lowercase strings compared case-insensitively. Lineage is a client-side walk of `ParentApprenticeId`.
- Chronicle frames are flattened: pass-through Master fields are top-level, not nested under the legacy `wizardEvent`. Forge deserializes a local `ChronicleFrame` with raw `Type`. `CastSent`, `SimulacrumStarted`, and `SimulacrumCompleted` are PascalCase on the wire; other event types are camelCase.
- OpenAI `/v1/files` and `/v1/batches` use `OpenAiCompatApiClient` and bare OpenAI DTO/error envelopes, never `ApiResponse<T>`.

Transport failures do not escape ViewModels as exceptions: route services synthesize failed `ApiResponse<T>` values with `Connection.Failed` or `Connection.Timeout`. HttpClient's own request timeout is one of those failures on every verb, including status-only deletes, which report it as a failed delete rather than as caller cancellation. A `the-forge.json` value that cannot be turned into a request is rejected before the send with its own envelope rather than a raw framework exception: a `BaseUrl` that is not an absolute `http`/`https` URL becomes `Config.InvalidBaseUrl`, and a master API key carrying a line break or NUL becomes `Config.InvalidApiKey`. Both guards belong to the client layer rather than to one client, so the OpenAI-shaped `/v1/files` and `/v1/batches` path returns the same two codes as an `OpenAiResult` failure instead of raising `UriFormatException` or `FormatException` out of a fire-and-forget command. Status-only deletes return a `DeleteOutcome` carrying `Http.{status}` or the transport code rather than a bare boolean, because a route whose body is deliberately never buffered has no other channel for the reason, and a single flag forced each data source to invent one — which is how a refused connection, a 403, and a 500 all reached the operator as "not found". Buffered `/api` and OpenAI-shaped JSON/error bodies are read with `ResponseHeadersRead` and a 64 MiB hard ceiling; over-cap bodies become `Api.ResponseTooLarge`; status-only deletes complete after headers and do not buffer an ignored body. JSONL previews stop at their byte ceiling even when the input contains no newline. File downloads stream to a same-directory staging file, flush, and atomically replace the destination only after a complete transfer; cancellation or I/O failure removes the staging file and preserves any existing destination. The Hearth's local terminal reader caps each stdout/stderr line at 64 Ki characters, retains a bounded prefix with an explicit truncation marker, and continues with later lines; after the shell exits it drains stdout/stderr for a bounded window and then closes its read ends, so a command that leaves a background descendant holding the inherited pipe cannot wedge the panel. The Ledger's `git` runner bounds captured output the same way but keeps that capture machine-readable: truncation is reported only through the result's `StdoutTruncated`/`StderrTruncated` flags, the cut is taken back to the last complete line so no partial path can parse as a change row, and no human-readable notice is ever spliced into the captured text. Those flags are read by the panel that shows the result: a truncated `git status` banners the change list as incomplete and marks the status line `INCOMPLETE`, and a truncated `git diff` appends its own notice below the rendered hunks, because a silently short change list is indistinguishable from a clean tree and is how work gets left uncommitted.

### 19.9 Connection, authentication, and desktop settings

`TheForgeSettings.BaseUrl` defaults to `http://localhost:5001`. When Arcanum uses ListenAny / `ARCANUM_HOST_ANY`, the host is HTTPS-only; use `https://localhost:{HttpsPort}` or the remote HTTPS authority. The Forge never disables certificate validation. It sends `X-Arcanum-Key` on every `/api` request (the server also supports Bearer for other clients).

The Forge's named API client and Compendium's authenticated Familiar probe disable automatic HTTP redirects, so a redirect response cannot send the Master key or open a connection to its target.

Settings live at `~/.config/arcanum/the-forge.json` with `reloadOnChange:true`; an old `forge.json` is renamed on first launch when the canonical file is absent. The persisted desktop state includes base URL, theme, last Campaign, dock layout, auto-connect, and active Session. Fresh installs use the light theme; existing dark selections remain dark. Dock layout resets through **View → Reset Window Layout**. Dock layout covers tool placement, visibility, ordering, active tab, and region size: the Grid definitions bind one-way to a collapse-aware computed size, so each GridSplitter commits its resolved width/height back to the owning group on drag completion (clamped to the region's min/max, and skipped for a collapsed region so an empty region never stores a zero).

| Desktop setting | Meaning |
|-----------------|---------|
| `baseUrl` | Arcanum authority; default `http://localhost:5001`. |
| `apiKey` | Obsolete migrate-and-strip field; keep null in new files. |
| `theme` | `light` by default; existing `dark` remains honored and changes live through **View → Theme**. |
| `lastCampaignId` | Active Campaign for menus and The Anvil. |
| `layoutState` | Persisted dock layout; null selects the default shell. |
| `autoConnect` | Enables the health polling/automatic connection flow. |
| `activeSessionId` | Last active Tome Session. |

The Master API key is never retained as active plaintext in that file. Resolution order is:

1. shared OS credential store (`service=arcanum`, `account=master-api-key`);
2. migrate-and-strip a legacy `apiKey` from `the-forge.json`;
3. trimmed `THEFORGE_ARCANUM_KEY` for process-only private-beta/automation use (never logged or persisted);
4. `arcanum key show` from stderr, persisted to the OS store when possible; then
5. an operator paste dialog, persisted to the OS store when available or held process-only with a warning.

Step 4 resolves the CLI itself instead of handing a bare `arcanum` file name to the process launcher: The Forge walks `PATH` and launches only a fully qualified candidate, skipping relative `PATH` entries, and skips the step entirely when no absolute candidate exists. A bare file name would let Windows' `CreateProcess` search order run a planted `arcanum.exe` out of whatever working directory The Forge inherited (`arcanum open …` hands down the operator's shell directory). The recovered value is also shape-checked before it reaches the shared `arcanum`/`master-api-key` slot — single-line printable ASCII, 8–512 characters — so CLI diagnostics or prose can never be persisted as a key.

Declining paste suppresses repeated prompts until **The Anvil → Enter API key…**, which also clears a cached bad environment key. Rotate with `arcanum key set` (or the shared OS credential) and restart The Forge. Linux requires libsecret and a running Secret Service for shared keychain access; The Forge cannot decrypt Arcanum's `security.dat` fallback.

Operators connect or disconnect through **View → Connect to Arcanum** or The Anvil connection chip. `arcanum doctor` reports whether the shared Master-key identity is present without exposing it.

Deep links do not carry connection endpoints or credentials. The optional connection-profile field is a safe identifier reserved for a profile registry; when absent, The Forge uses its ordinary settings and authentication flow. Resource routing begins only after that flow reports Connected, and a link is rejected — surfacing the ordinary "could not be opened" Whisper — as soon as the flow reports Error, because an authentication failure caches the rejected key for the process lifetime and would otherwise defer the link forever.

### 19.10 Desktop vocabulary and implemented surfaces

| Surface | UI name | Responsibility |
|---------|---------|----------------|
| Center editor tabs | The Workbench | Spell editor, Tome, Scriptorium, Codex, Proving Grounds, comparisons, markdown |
| Campaign/workspace tree | The Atelier | Campaigns, workspaces, Spells, Prompts, Sessions, import/export |
| Session viewer | The Tome | Answer-only transcript plus separate ephemeral live reasoning |
| Apprentice orchestration | The War Table | Apprentice state, lineage, flattened Chronicle |
| Retained active Ward records | The Gatehouse | Inspect/resolve compatibility Wards |
| MCP/tools/models | The Arsenal | MCP lifecycle, Scrying Pool diagnostics, read-only providers/models |
| Budget | The Treasury | Read-only budget/spend snapshot |
| Status bar | The Anvil | Connection, Campaign, spend, Wards, Apprentices, MCP |
| Output/logs | The Foundry Floor | Detailed output behind short Whispers toasts |
| Local shell | The Hearth | Local shell panel; not a PTY and not Arcanum HTTP |
| Git | The Ledger | Desktop-local Git status/diff/commit; no push/pull/reset/rebase |
| Command palette | Incantation | Search and execute IDE commands |
| Trials | The Proving Grounds | Build/run Trials and local suites |
| Search/context | Divination / The Eye of the World | Semantic and global search |
| Memory | Lore Browser / The Archive | Operator Lore and Saga |
| Markdown | The Illumination | Source, split, preview with Markdig |
| Spell dependencies | The Resonance Map | Arcane Resonance graph |
| Session tabs | The Council Chamber | Multi-Session tab management |
| Entry inspection | The Loupe | Inspect one Session Entry and its metadata |
| Context help | The Codex | In-product help/documentation |
| Notifications | Whispers | Short success/error toasts; non-error toasts auto-dismiss after five seconds and errors stay until dismissed; details stay on the Foundry Floor |
| Settings handoff | Compendium | Launch the standalone `arcanum.json` editor |

Other implemented operator surfaces include Campaign CRUD, Spell metadata/version diff (**The Mirror**), Prompt designer (**The Scriptorium**), Session memory, Workspace explorer/index inspector, Audit/guardrail browsers, OpenAI Files/Batches, MCP diagnostic fixtures, comparison/inference traces, Mana visualization, Servants' Quarters, Comm Link alerts, and Sanctum breach monitoring.

Workbench documents never discard operator work silently. The Codex editor enables editing and Save only after a successful load with a Codex payload, including an absent or valid empty file. Starting another load revokes that permission, so a failed reload cannot save a stale buffer; a subsequent successful reload enables editing and Save again. The Spell editor refuses a reload or a version activation while the body buffer holds unsaved changes and tells the operator to save or discard first, matching Compendium's save-or-cancel gate; the Scriptorium's Load button carries the identical guard, so the two editors cannot disagree about whether a buffer is worth protecting. Version activation also holds the editor busy for the round trip and reports a transport failure through `LastError` like every sibling version command, rather than leaving the buffer editable across a reload that will overwrite it. The Mirror surfaces belong to the newest version selection: a superseded fetch that returns late is discarded rather than appended, so rapid selection never leaves another version's diff on screen. Closing a Workbench document cancels the run it owns, so a Spell execution stream ends with its tab instead of continuing against a spell the operator has deleted. A Proving Grounds suite run re-reads the suite immediately before persisting and contributes only the new run record, so Trials added — or run history cleared — during a multi-minute run survive it; a suite deleted mid-run reports that its results were not saved instead of claiming success. Export and active-campaign failures report through `LastError`, the Foundry Floor, and an error Whisper rather than escaping the command. Every destructive single-item delete confirms first (Cancel default) because the server has no undo for any of them: an operator Lore entry, whose Delete shares a button row with Save; a Saga memory, which cannot be retyped from the surface that deletes it; a whole `CODEX.md`; and a session transcript entry. A delete cancelled by the operator's own token — closing the window mid-request — ends the command quietly instead of escaping onto the dispatcher, and a delete the server refuses reports the status it actually returned. The Ledger reports commit blockers before it prompts: an empty index and an empty message are unconditional refusals reported inline — a prompt whose Yes answer cannot commit is not asked, and the empty index is reported first because it is the blocker the commit box does not show — leaving the confirmation for the large-commit case, whose Yes answer does proceed.

Live client-side buffers are bounded, because the panels holding them stay open for the life of a session. The Hearth caps scrollback at 5,000 lines, the Foundry Floor caps its shared output/log buffer at the same 5,000 and offers an operator Clear, and the War Table's Chronicle retains the newest 2,000 frames, dropping the tail. The Chronicle also clears on every (re)activation: the server replays the plan/escalation/step preamble on each reconnect, so retaining the previous entries would show that preamble twice. Selecting an apprentice activates its Chronicle exactly once — the selection change owns activation, so the timeline is never opened, cancelled, and reopened against the same apprentice. The Chronicle timeline and the Logs pane render through virtualizing list controls rather than realizing one visual subtree per retained entry.

Campaigns remain server-side solution containers. All create/open/edit/unregister/import/export operations use HTTP; no client project-file discovery or direct Grimoire access occurs. A loopback client may choose a local folder, while a remote connection must submit a path meaningful on the Arcanum host.

The Forge does not edit `arcanum.json`. **Open Compendium** launches `RetroDownfall.Compendium.Ux`; `SettingDescriptors.cs` remains Compendium's editable-key authority. Disabled-state banners show retained setting paths and offer copy/open actions without reproducing a complete configuration inventory. Comparison reads pricing from the server configuration surface. War Table and Chronicle text retain canonical **Master/Apprentice** terminology.

Deep-link routes use the same surfaces: Session and Prompt open Workbench documents; Campaign selects the Atelier; Apprentice selects the War Table; and Spell opens a Workbench document. For a Workspace Spell, the CLI sends the opaque `WorkspaceInfo.Id` as `ResourceScopeId`. After authentication The Forge resolves that ID through the Workspace API and uses only the returned server-host path internally. Campaign and Apprentice navigation falls back to their direct detail endpoints when an item is outside the currently visible list, and reports a routing miss when the canonical ID does not exist. Remote resources therefore never depend on a client filesystem path.

The Proving Grounds is a singleton Workbench tab opened from **Trial → Proving Grounds**, Spell **Create Trial**, or Scriptorium **Open in Proving Grounds**. It targets a Spell, Prompt, or Apprentice Goal; supports Regex, JsonSchema, and Semantic Inquisitors; and runs through `POST /api/proving-grounds/trials/run`. Local suites are versioned JSON under `~/.config/arcanum/the-forge-trial-suites.json`.

Other desktop-local histories (suites, comparisons, traces, fixtures) are versioned JSON under `~/.config/arcanum/`, not Grimoire tables. Inference traces may retain reasoning event type, output mode, and token count, but replace the message with a fixed redaction and null `data` before local persistence or export. A trace keeps the latest 2,000 events of a capture (a turn streams one frame per token) and at most 16,384 characters of one event's data (a cut never splits a surrogate pair, so the kept text always serializes), and every trace panel (The Tome, the Spell editor, The Scriptorium and the Comparison Workbench) saves to the same local trace store and exports through the file dialog. Reload/export remains answer-only.

### 19.11 Current desktop limitations

- No true PTY Hearth or OS-level floating tool windows.
- No provider, pricing, budget, or model-metadata editor; no per-model Session token/cost breakdown.
- Guardrail policy editing remains in Compendium.
- No advanced import-conflict wizard, full Campaign settings editor, or advanced file merge.
- Illumination does not support relative workspace binary images, Mermaid, or native math.
- Local Trial suites cannot yet be created from completed batches.
- Ledger has no push, pull, reset, or rebase.
- Diagnostic MCP remains external-tool-only; reserved internal handlers require the Master pipeline (§11.28).
- Cross-platform process launch starts a new desktop instance unless a future platform activator can prove that it reused/focused an existing instance; the current launcher never makes a false focus claim.

### 19.12 Build, packaging, and maintenance

```bash
dotnet build RetroDownfall.Arcanum.slnx
dotnet run --project src/RetroDownfall.TheForge.Ux/RetroDownfall.TheForge.Ux.csproj
dotnet test tests/RetroDownfall.TheForge.Tests/RetroDownfall.TheForge.Tests.csproj
```

`App.axaml` uses `Name="The Forge"` so the macOS menu bar is correct during development; packaged apps set matching `CFBundleName` / `CFBundleDisplayName`.

**Cutting a release:**

- **Release creation is explicit.** `ci.yml` intentionally has no push trigger and calls no release workflow. An operator dispatches `release.yml` (or an authorized orchestrator calls its reusable-workflow surface) for the exact commit to release. The prepare job reports that commit's latest CI state as passed, failed, running, or never run so the operator cannot decide blind, but it does not turn CI into an implicit release gate or manufacture evidence that was never collected.
- **The version comes from an explicit workflow input or from `Directory.Build.props`, which is also what the build stamps into every assembly**, so a release cannot disagree with its own binaries. A blank input reads the project version. A bare channel there — `0.1.0-beta` — means *cut the next beta*: the release finds the highest `v0.1.0-beta.N` already cut and uses N+1. A fully written version — `0.1.0-beta.12`, or `0.1.0` — is used exactly as written. Changing `0.1.0` restarts that count, because the count is per base version. The next number is read from the releases API rather than from git tags, because a draft release holds its tag name without creating the ref, so counting tags would hand the same number to every unpublished draft; `github.run_number` would avoid that too, but it jumps whenever any workflow runs, and `beta.7` after `beta.4` reads as three lost builds. The `prepare` job also refuses to proceed when `v{version}` already exists as a published release (an explicit or declared non-channel version is otherwise used as written, and `--clobber` would replace public assets in place); it fails closed when GitHub cannot answer, and only an absent release or a draft passes. `release.yml` declares a top-level `concurrency` group, `release-<version or auto>`, with `cancel-in-progress: false`, so a run in progress is never cancelled and two dispatches that both leave the version blank are serialized instead of computing the same beta number and interleaving their per-file uploads. GitHub keeps one pending run per group, so this is not a queue: a second dispatch waits behind the running release and a third supersedes the one that was waiting. That group is keyed on the requested input, so a blank dispatch that resolves to `vX` and an explicit `vX` dispatch fall in different groups; the publish job therefore carries a second group, `release-publish-<resolved tag>`, also never cancelling, and its upload step asks again whether the release is still a draft immediately before uploading, refusing a release published since `prepare` checked and failing closed when GitHub cannot say. Both release workflows also move a reused draft's target to the commit the run built (`gh release edit --target "$GITHUB_SHA"`) before uploading into it, so publishing the draft tags the commit its binaries came from rather than the commit of the run that first created it (`ReleasePipelineTests.Every_gh_release_upload_rechecks_the_draft_and_retargets_it_first`).
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` is the one entry point that produces a release. It takes a SemVer version, calls `release-macos-arm64.yml` and `build-windows.yml` (once per Windows RID) rather than repeating them, and assembles a single draft GitHub Release from the nine archives they upload plus one `SHA256SUMS.txt` covering all of them. The per-platform workflows remain individually dispatchable and behave exactly as they did alone; a reusable workflow cannot detect that it was called, because `github.event_name` inside one reports its caller's trigger, so `release-macos-arm64.yml` takes a `create_release` input that defaults to `true` on dispatch and `false` when called.
- It refuses to start unless every shipping RID already has a verified hermetic SQLCipher asset checked in, and refuses to assemble unless every expected archive arrived — named one by one rather than globbed. Each build workflow's own copy of the asset check *skips* instead, which is the honest report for a build of one RID and the wrong one for a release: a release that shipped whichever platforms happened to succeed would be named for every platform and carry a subset, with nothing downstream saying so.
- The release defaults to a draft. Setting the dispatch/reusable `publish` input explicitly to `true` publishes it; no automatic path makes it public.

**Windows and Linux distribution:**

- `scripts/packaging/windows/package-windows.ps1` produces `arcanum-<rid>.zip`, `compendium-<rid>.zip`, optional `the-forge-<rid>.zip`, and `SHA256SUMS`, where `-Rid` selects `win-x64` (the default) or `win-arm64` and everything else about the script is architecture-agnostic — the RID is a folder name, an archive name, and a value passed through to `dotnet publish`. `-SkipForge` produces the Arcanum + Compendium set. `-Sign` enables Authenticode and requires `WINDOWS_CERT_PATH` plus `WINDOWS_CERT_PASSWORD`; otherwise outputs are unsigned. The script captures and removes `WINDOWS_CERT_PASSWORD` from its process environment before it launches any build or signing child, imports the PFX into a unique `Cert:\CurrentUser\ArcanumPackaging-<guid>` store, and tells `signtool` to use that exact CurrentUser store with `/s` plus the selected leaf thumbprint. Its `finally` path deletes every private key and certificate in that owned store, deletes the store itself, verifies absence, and reports cleanup failure alongside any primary packaging failure. It never opens or modifies the user's `My` store and never puts the password in a child environment or command line, keeping the packaging script inside the project's own "secrets never appear in argv" rule (§11.2.1, §11.7).
- `scripts/packaging/linux/package-linux.sh` is a deliberate fail-closed placeholder: it accepts the historical Linux RID arguments, explains that no verified SQLCipher asset exists, exits 2, and produces no archive. No workflow carries a Linux job; restoring Linux follows the explicit add-RID, build-and-verify, check-in, add-job path in §5.4.4a.
- `.github/workflows/build-windows.yml` builds the complete Arcanum + Compendium + The Forge set for one Windows RID, chosen by its `rid` input, and each architecture builds on its own architecture: `windows-latest` for `win-x64`, `windows-11-arm` for `win-arm64`. After proving the SDK host RID matches that selection, the workflow runs `verify-aot-il-warnings.sh` for the same RID before packaging; the ordinary publish remains warning-free, while the preceding diagnostic profile rejects first-party warnings that exist only on one Windows architecture. `windows-11-arm` is free for this repository because it is public.
- The Windows CLI is a Native AOT apphost **plus the genuine native sidecar files that SQLitePCLRaw and onigwrap ship for these RIDs** — every publish emits `e_sqlcipher.dll` and `libonigwrap.dll` beside the apphost. The packaging script stages the whole publish directory, renames only the apphost to `arcanum.exe`, rejects a managed CLI assembly, `hostfxr.dll`, or `hostpolicy.dll`, and requires both native sidecars. The Forge and Compendium remain self-contained multi-file Avalonia folders. These channels are unsigned by default.

**macOS Apple Silicon distribution:**

- `.github/workflows/release-macos-arm64.yml` is a manual **Release macOS arm64** workflow on the Apple Silicon `macos-26` runner, and is also what `release.yml` calls for the macOS third of a full release. Before packaging it runs `./scripts/verify-aot-il-warnings.sh osx-arm64` on the signing runner, the same audit `build-windows.yml` runs for its RID, because the packager's own publish suppresses dependency summary diagnostics after that audit has classified them and a prior CI run may belong to another commit; the audit is a second full Native AOT compile on the release path, accepted so a release cannot ship a first-party IL warning the host-RID CI lane never saw for it. Distribution is through workflow artifacts and a draft GitHub Release, not the Mac App Store.
- Every macOS CI, release, and native SQLCipher verification lane runs on the Apple Silicon `macos-26` runner. The `osx-arm64` SQLCipher build in `verify-native-sqlcipher.yml` retains its strict byte-identical rebuild and checked-in hash checks; a toolchain change requires adopting the rebuilt dylib and its attested provenance when its hash changes. Serviced .NET 10.0.12+ uses Apple's linker with its relocation-anchor repair; LLVM `lld` is required only by the isolated pre-10.0.12 compatibility path. Both shipping paths fail closed when their required native toolchain is unavailable.
- Release signing requires an Apple Developer Program **Developer ID Application** certificate and six repository secrets: `APPLE_CERTIFICATE`, `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD`, `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY`, `APPLE_ID`, `APPLE_TEAM_ID`, and `APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD`. CI imports the P12 into an ephemeral signing keychain and requires the signing identity to start with `Developer ID Application:`. Each packager immediately captures and unsets the exported app-specific password before launching build or signing children, stores the notarytool profile through stdin in a separate per-run owned keychain, and fails unless that keychain, its registration, and its temporary directory are gone at exit; neither a caller's persistent keychain nor CI's signing keychain ever owns the notarization credential.
- Version input accepts `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` with an optional prerelease suffix and rejects build metadata. The full value is the .NET version and `v{version}` Git tag; `CFBundleShortVersionString` is the numeric `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, and `CFBundleVersion` is the GitHub run number.
- `arcanum-osx-arm64.zip` contains the signed Native AOT CLI folder plus the repository-root `README.md`. The packaging script rejects a managed CLI assembly, `libhostfxr.dylib`, or `libhostpolicy.dylib`, rejects every publish warning, and signs every Mach-O in the folder. The CLI entitlement plist is intentionally empty: Native AOT needs no JIT, unsigned-executable-memory, or library-validation exception, so the signed binary receives none of those privileges.
- The zip is submitted with `notarytool --wait`, and packaging stops unless Apple accepts it, but the archive cannot be stapled. The extracted standalone executable is checked with strict `codesign --verify` integrity validation and `codesign -R="notarized" --check-notarization`, Apple's notarization-ticket check for non-app code; `spctl --type execute` is not used because it assesses app bundles and rejects a valid standalone Mach-O as "not an app." Static signature and ticket checks can still pass on an entitlement-less binary that cannot start at all, so `build-arcanum.sh` additionally **launches** the extracted signed binary with `--version`. The release workflow then extracts the same completed zip again and runs the full first-session provider-contract gate against that archive member before upload.
- `compendium-osx-arm64.dmg` and `the-forge-osx-arm64.dmg` contain signed, notarized, stapled `.app` bundles. Desktop publish is multi-file by default so native libraries can be signed individually.
- **Local signing with an operator's own certificate.** `--local-sign` on either macOS packaging script resolves the signing identity from Keychain Access instead of from repository secrets, signs with the same hardened runtime and entitlements as a release, and then stops: no `notarytool` submission, no `stapler`, no `spctl --assess`. That is not a convenience — Apple notarizes Developer ID submissions only, so an **Apple Development** certificate (the kind issued for local development) can sign and can never be notarized, and stapling has no ticket to attach. The path exists because the one macOS failure that no static check catches is a hardened-runtime binary that aborts before `Main` on a wrong JIT entitlement even though static `codesign --verify` succeeds; `--local-sign` therefore ends by launching the signed artifact. Identity selection is deliberate rather than best-effort: `require_local_signing_identity` reads `security find-identity -v -p codesigning`, accepts only common names prefixed `Developer ID Application:`, `Apple Distribution:`, `Apple Development:`, or `Mac Developer:`, and refuses to guess when more than one matches — `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY` then selects one by common name or by SHA-1. A local signature is made with `--timestamp=none`, because it is never distributed and is routinely produced offline where Apple's timestamp authority is unreachable and a release-style `--timestamp` is a hard failure. Artifacts from this path run only on machines that already trust the certificate and are never release candidates.
- Both signing paths — `sign_publish_dir` for the CLI zip and `sign_app_bundle` for the `.app`, which walks the verbatim copy of the same publish directory under `Contents/MacOS/` — order their Mach-O files through one shared helper, `order_macho_paths_deepest_first`. `find` alone is not enough: its walk is pre-order, not depth-first, so it hands back a directory's own files before descending into that directory's subdirectories, and a dependent would be sealed before the library it loads. The helper also refuses to continue if the reordering dropped an entry, because a partially signed tree is one `codesign --verify` still calls valid — it inspects only the main binary. `MacOsSigningScriptTests` executes both functions under `/bin/bash` (3.2 is the runner shell) against real Mach-O files with `codesign` stubbed out.
- Signing and notarization are mandatory for CI release outputs. `--skip-sign` and `--local-sign` exist only for local package-structure smoke tests and local signature verification; `ReleasePipelineTests` fails the build if either flag appears in a workflow, and if any `notarize_submit`, `staple_item`, or `spctl --assess` call in the macOS scripts is reachable without excluding `--local-sign`. `scripts/packaging/macos/common_test.sh` drives the identity-resolution helpers through stubbed `security`/`codesign` and runs in the `build-test` job. A successful workflow uploads all three artifacts and creates or updates draft release `v{version}`; rerunning the same version replaces assets of a **draft** with `gh release upload --clobber`, and a standalone dispatch that creates the release first refuses (before the Native AOT compile) when `v{version}` already exists as a published release, because `--clobber` would otherwise make a notarized public download mutable. An operator spot-checks a clean Mac before publishing the draft.

Changes to desktop architecture, wire contracts, project structure, settings/auth behavior, UI scope, packaging, or release workflows update this section in the same change set.

## 20. The Proving Grounds — Trials and Inquisitors

Ordinary Trials are ephemeral (no Grimoire persistence); the explicit exact-memory comparison extension below persists only protected content-free evidence. Terminology: **The Proving Grounds** / **Trial** / **Inquisitor** only.

### 20.1 Data models (ephemeral)

In-memory `Trial` / `TrialResult` / polymorphic `Inquisitor` (`regex`, `jsonSchema`, `semantic`).

### 20.2 Architecture

`POST /api/proving-grounds/trials/run` → resolve target (spell / prompt / apprenticeGoal) → run inference or plan prompt → adjudicate Inquisitors → `TrialResult`.

### 20.3 Key decisions

Semantic judge uses FastModel→DefaultModel; jsonSchema delegates to `JsonSchemaHelper` and supports only `type` (a string, or a non-empty array of strings in which any listed type satisfies it; an unrecognized member fails, and any other `type` value is an unreadable schema), `properties`, `required`, `items`, `enum`, and boolean `additionalProperties` (not full draft 2020-12; other keywords are ignored and an unreadable schema is a failed verdict). Industry LLM-test jargon prohibited in identifiers.

### 20.4 Error codes

API §8.23 (`ProvingGrounds.*`).

### 20.5 Exact memory evaluation preparation

The separate `Core/ProvingGrounds/MemoryEvaluation` contracts support bounded counterfactual preparation without invoking the ordinary Trial/Wizard retrieval loop. `IMemoryEvaluationSourceReader` borrows the caller's genuine gate-validated `CovenantTurnLease` and the request-issued stateless operator invocation with `NoTools`. Explicit Campaign resolution carries its real availability facts and no physical-root digest or revision. This preparation layer has no provider dispatch or source-mutation port. Each read captures one `AsOfUtc` for the complete source cut; that immutable instant is bound into the source-state fence and therefore execution identity. Revalidation uses a fresh single current instant for eligibility while retaining the original cut in the metadata proof. Durable registration must retain this source cut separately from its later creation timestamp.

Saga and Lexicon interventions must identify their exact current Annals version, format and content digest and satisfy current scope, lifetime, time, sensitivity and recall eligibility. Saga uses the existing exact-source suppression predicate, including its normal pin override. Canonical Saga owner Session and nullable Annals version-author Session are independent coordinates: owner Session identifiers use the canonical uppercase D-form used by `Sessions.Id` and deletion journals; version-author identifiers preserve their retained spelling. Lexicon has no invented Session owner. Owning Session binding/existence and pending owner-deletion evidence are checked. Historical dependency versions remain historical, with their independent owners/authors, validity and sensitivity. The deterministic outgoing closure requires retained sequence-consistent edges and mandatory predecessor/Supersedes evidence, refuses more than 128 unique source coordinates, and never injects dependency plaintext.

Covenant preparation first runs the existing bounded full lawful snapshot and linker, so unselected Campaign shadows and masks still determine eligibility. Metadata-only fences around that read bind the scoped heads, dataset/sequence, key-reclamation state and curation facts; only explicitly selected eligible fragments leave the reader. `CovenantPlanCandidateDecision.RenderSelectedSection` uses the ordinary renderer for each eligible occurrence. Current protected labels are alias-checked and their persisted sensitivity/label digests are verified against canonical reconstruction before source content is admitted. The source manifest and source-state proof bind these exact facts. Saga/Lexicon plaintext byte lengths are checked against the remaining aggregate memory budget before hydration. The reader also refuses source/edge metadata exceeding a conservative 64 KiB canonical-encoding bound and orders explicit target sets canonically before rendering. `ValidateAsync` rechecks only metadata and the borrowed lease, without rehydrating content or invoking the content-bearing Covenant port. All queries are parameterized read-only SQLite on admitted connections; preparation never backfills Annals, writes embeddings, changes pins or advances review state.

`MemoryEvaluationPromptComposer` builds one attributed treatment from the frozen workload and selected store-rendered fragments. `MemoryEvaluationPromptPolicy` independently checks unique exact source attribution, strict UTF-8 ranges, non-overlap, all requested targets, and the 32 KiB memory / 96 KiB complete-prompt ceilings, then removes precisely each selected occurrence and its code-owned separators to derive control. The resulting control must reproduce both original workload strings exactly. System/User message placement is independent of Covenant source lane/CONTEXT-or-DATA placement. Confirmed Covenant retains its CONTEXT framing; Proposed Covenant, Saga and Lexicon use their normal untrusted DATA rendering. No omitted source, dependency content, history, implicit retrieval or larger answer budget is introduced by removing memory. Snapshot and prompt collections are defensively copied.

The focused preparation tests use isolated encrypted SQLite, actual owning-store source writes, real borrowed Turn leases, corrupt/ineligible-source refusals, pending deletion, historical corrected-owner dependencies, bounded closure, unselected shadowing, zero-write observations and SQLite statement tracing for metadata-only revalidation. Neighboring ordinary retrieval and prompt goldens remain the regression boundary. Provider execution, durable evaluation storage and API publication are separate layers.

### 20.6 Immutable memory evaluation evidence

Core v19 adds exactly three table groups: `memory_evaluations` (prepared ownership, explicit `SourceAsOfUtc`, frozen digests and dependency edges), `memory_evaluation_sources` (the complete ordered exact coordinate manifest), and `memory_evaluation_reports` (one terminal aggregate). The published v18 source fingerprint is frozen by `CoreSchemaVersionEighteenFixture`; the V19 transition adds these empty objects, replaces the current UTC-column view, and rebuilds the disclosure-receipt constraint to admit clean controls while preserving all prior receipt bytes (§20.7). Covenant Canonical stays at v6. These are direct-SQL metadata stores with no EF entities and no FK to optional Covenant tables.

`IMemoryEvaluationEvidenceStore` accepts metadata DTOs only. It validates IDs, source-specific canonical Guid spelling, strict UTF-8 opaque Annals identifiers, closed enums, scope, UTC, hash formats, counts, exact manifest binding, dependency endpoints/ordinals and terminal aggregate consistency. Dependency edges bind the dependent store explicitly; target endpoints resolve by the shared globally unique Annals version identity across Saga and Lexicon, refusing missing/ambiguous bindings and Covenant lookalikes. Canonical owner Session remains uppercase D-form independently of the nullable author Session's retained spelling. Source content, workload, patterns/schemas, answers, provider text and executable authority have no accepted fields. Source-generated `GrimoireJsonContext` metadata shapes include the checkpoint while excluding transient request/snapshot/prompt/plan/send/answer shapes. The evidence sink is governed bidirectionally as `ContentFreeMetadataOnly`, with bounded opaque source/scope coordinates explicitly permitted for lifecycle and replay.

An immediate SQLite transaction performs exact replay lookup, reserves installation-wide capacity below 1,024 retained roots, and commits all prepared metadata. Child source rows use a deferred FK so they can be inserted before the root; inserting the root seals the complete bounded manifest, and triggers refuse updates, later source appends, and INSERT OR REPLACE conflicts on retained evaluation/operation identities or terminal rows. A failure rolls the entire set back. Registration preflight bounds both the retained normalized metadata values and the largest legal API evidence projection to 64 KiB, reserving 8 KiB for bounded terminal aggregate/usage overhead before execution can spend anything. The projection bound includes repeated registration/manifest fields; SQLite page/index allocation is not a payload-byte budget. An admitted registration therefore always has room for truthful InsufficientEvidence terminalization. No silent truncation or eviction occurs. The execution layer must commit this registration before every possible first provider send.

Terminal completion appends once, permits exact canonical-digest replay, rejects replacement, and cannot recreate absent/erased roots or missing manifest members. The report digest binds the original source cut independently of registration creation. Report-only cleanup requires confirmation, the exact expected terminal digest and a retained terminal report, then explicitly removes all three groups in one transaction even with FK enforcement disabled. Prepared/running evidence cannot be deleted through this port. Retained operation/request identity remains the execution layer's guard against a second execution after evidence cleanup.

The immutable root `ErasureKeysJson` is generated from the validated manifest and checked against it on reads. Store-qualified subject/claim/version keys preserve exact opaque spelling, including Unicode, case, punctuation and dashes. These coordinates are not GUID identities: lowercasing or removing dashes would merge distinct imported Annals subjects and SQLite ASCII-only folding would miss others. Independent canonical owner and nullable author Session keys use parsed lowercase N-form GUIDs; full source spelling remains digest-bound in the coordinate manifest. Root Campaign ownership has its own index, so a Campaign-owned evaluation over Global sources still follows Campaign deletion.

`MemoryEvaluationErasurePlan` selects the whole root and explicitly deletes reports, source manifests and roots last. The immutable root lookup survives child deletion; exact-subject cleanup does not require the Annals claim still to exist. Shared Annals erasure reaches Saga/Lexicon source and dependency evidence, including protected artifact and staged destination-erasure paths. Covenant entry erasure includes all three targets in preview/apply counts and captures evaluation IDs for its post-delete absence proof. Bulk canonical reset, owner cleanup and staged whole-family purge close Core evidence before removing canonical sources. Core evaluation tables remain outside `CovenantCanonicalContentTables`. Family reinitialize has no production storage transition implementation; its actual coordinator seam requires idempotent Core evaluation cleanup before `DropFamilyAsync`, including recovery at the closed-handles phase.

Native Session deletion closes evidence through canonical source ownership independently of a nullable corrected-version author, while native Campaign deletion also closes explicitly Campaign-owned reports. These paths preserve source memory where the existing owner lifecycle preserves it. Annals status and factory preview/apply include all three groups with child-before-root deletion. Prune preview unions all selected Saga, Lexicon and Session evaluation keys once; apply measures each complete set before the first participating deletion. No independent Annals age rule or configuration key is introduced. Reset selections retain their minimum Core schema version and fail if a table mandatory at the committed version is missing.

Full backup naturally includes terminal history in the encrypted database. After staged destination erasure and generation reconciliation, `BackupRestoreMemoryEvaluationSanitation` removes incomplete preparations and evidence with incompatible dataset, Campaign, canonical owner or exact source-version bindings. It captures affected IDs before deleting manifests, never rewrites source coordinates or report digests, preserves compatible terminal history, and explicitly removes orphan children with foreign keys disabled. Staged publication and committed recovery verify the same condition using read-only proofs. A fresh restored dataset cannot inherit a prepared execution or rebind immutable history to look-alike sources. Retained operation/disclosure/accounting evidence remains governed by its owning lifecycle.


### 20.7 Exact memory evaluation provider boundary

`IMemoryEvaluationProvider` prepares a dedicated two-message, zero-tool provider lane. The request-owned adapter binds each issued plan by object identity to private source-generated configuration bytes, exact configured provider/model, immutable token estimates, final mapped envelope digests and a monotonic configuration epoch. A copied plan is not an issued capability. Every observed configuration transition invalidates old plans, including A-to-B-to-A. Core plans and durable metadata contain no SDK clients, credentials, live configuration objects or accounting handles. Preparation re-proves exact prompt derivation and manifest identity, admits both complete prompts without truncation or retrieval, and commits the alternating pair order and fixed output limit.

`ModelCallExecutor.ExecuteMemoryEvaluationAsync` recomputes the actual arm's closed context estimate and fingerprint, checks identity/reserves/context fit, builds final SDK messages and mapped options, and freezes the exact envelope before invoking the runner's per-arm acknowledgement callback. The envelope records actual mapped temperature/top-p, seed and reasoning effort, zero tools/cache, the exact message text, and system occurrence attribution converted explicitly from UTF-8 byte offsets to UTF-16. Treatment sensitivity carries the admitted sources' real generation provenance; a source-free control carries None and exact empty provenance. The runner owns current authority/source/operation fences and durable disclosure acknowledgement for every arm; the adapter rechecks configuration and cancellation after that callback. An adapter-local order/concurrency guard allows one physical call for each committed arm and stops the plan after any invalid result or accounting failure.

The dedicated factory uses the guarded pinned-address provider transport with redirects disabled, fresh connections and zero SDK retries. A bounded response handler rejects a declared oversized body or reads at most 1 MiB plus one byte before any SDK parsing, for both success and error responses. Within that bound it validates successful raw JSON before lossy SDK normalization: both primary usage counts must be explicitly present nonnegative integers, and the response must have exactly one assistant choice with only text content and no refusal, tool/function call or media. An empty or incomplete usage object cannot acquire SDK-default zero measurements; explicitly reported zero remains measured. A rejected raw shape carries only transient model/completion/usage facts to the executor so independently known paid usage still settles. The executor retains at most 64 KiB of aggregate strict UTF-8 answer/reasoning text, rejects unsupported contents, refusal, missing/mismatched reported model and incomplete finish reasons, and never silently truncates. Measured usage is accounted even when raw or normalized content is rejected, and settlement does not use the cancelled request token. Missing input/output measurements remain null and produce UsageFailure rather than a numeric zero bill. These checks produce transient text only; durable reports retain opaque evidence and closed outcomes.

Financial services are required independently of `ITurnBudget`. Each attempted arm owns one Session-free inference run with Surface `memory-evaluation`, Purpose `counterfactual-arm`, and RequestId `<evaluation-id in lowercase N form>:<zero-based send index>`. Both arms reserve the same conservative complete-prompt upper bound and fixed output budget; the output estimate also covers the higher reasoning-token price without enlarging the provider's output limit. Daily financial admission is rechecked before acknowledgement. The adapter durably marks the reservation UncertainPaid during accounting preflight, then rechecks configuration before invoking the final acknowledgement callback and rechecks configuration/cancellation again after it. No awaited accounting write follows that final callback. An epoch change while the marker write is pending therefore refuses the callback and physical send. Known usage writes one normal measured bill and reconciles the hold even when the answer is invalid. Unknown usage, transport/cancellation ambiguity or failed accounting keeps the estimate outstanding and stops later sends. A marker followed by failed acknowledgement or final validation deliberately remains held even when no SDK send began: this conservative proven-unsent disposition creates no bill and adds no generic release path. Failures before marking can release the ordinary reservation. A disabled financial limit creates no active reservation, but required run/bill accounting and unknown-usage semantics remain intact.

Core v19 also repairs the existing disclosure receipt constraint to admit an empty exact provenance vector only with None sensitivity. The evolution copies existing receipt bytes unchanged inside its version transaction and restores the same indexes and append-only guards; counters, chain heads, ordinals and prior receipts remain untouched. Published v17/v18 receipt SQL remains frozen in compatibility fixtures, and Covenant canonical stays v6. The application sensitivity constructor continues to reject None with nonempty provenance and derived sensitivity with empty provenance.


### 20.8 Request-owned memory evaluation execution and recovery

`MemoryEvaluationRequestScopeFactory` retains the original pre-binding ProtectedRead authority feature and its epoch while canonically resolving Global or explicit Campaign scope. It refuses missing, changed or stale authority and acquires a genuine Covenant Turn lease for `StatelessOperatorTurn` with `NoTools`. The invocation can read protected memory but cannot stage or apply mutations. The scope revalidates both that original authority and the borrowed lease, and registers asynchronous disposal with the HTTP response so the lease survives the later serialization boundary. Neither persisted checkpoint metadata nor a replay creates a request capability.

`MemoryEvaluationRunner` freezes the validated request, looks up its canonical request identity before hydrating sources, and returns retained metadata for exact replay. Changed canonical requests under the same evaluation ID conflict; absent evidence is NotFound when no memory-evaluation request identity exists (including another operation kind), and Gone when that exact evaluation identity remains after erasure. Repeated confirmed report cleanup for an exact retained memory-evaluation identity returns Deleted=false through the store's exact absent-target path; unknown or other-kind identities remain NotFound. When erasure has removed prior ownership, this metadata-only result requires a genuine current Global read scope; it never reconstructs an old Campaign/root or hydrates sources. A singleton installation execution slot and durable active-operation check prevent a second execution. Only after source/prompt/provider preparation fixes the exact plan digest does the coordinator map the evaluation ID to its distinct operation ID. The runner requires the returned operation to be Running, owned by its exact owner and unexpired, then holds the shared process ownership claim through provider and accounting drain. A Created result alone cannot authorize execution.

The execution slot publishes an evaluation-keyed initial-publication signal before the durable request identity can become observable. Exact replay checks kind and canonical request digest immediately, then waits for registration and the first Prepared checkpoint before re-reading metadata. Get and delete wait before ownership lookup, so newly published Campaign evidence opens its genuine Campaign scope. Initialization failure, cancellation and release settle the signal; waiter cancellation does not cancel the owner or release the slot. Metadata absence after that boundary remains Gone for a retained exact identity, including erasure between registration and the first checkpoint. The signal carries no durable authority and never authorizes hydration, dispatch or resurrection. The shared metadata observation resolves an absent ownership read against the exact request identity: a retained identity requires a publication wait and one fresh ownership read before Gone. A genuinely absent/other-kind identity proves NotFound at that observation. Endpoints retain this pre-creation 404 through genuine Global scope acquisition and final original-authority validation, rather than reopening scope or combining old absence with a newly created Campaign. Direct callers still receive ScopeMismatch for actual wrong-scope reads.

The runner commits registration and its complete source manifest before writing checkpoint version 1 or acknowledging any provider send. Every version 1 checkpoint retains the evaluation/operation/request/plan identity, bounded PairCount (3–16), closed phase and bounded progress. PhysicalSends may lag a paid call and is never used as a recovery accounting limit. The fixed alternating control/treatment schedule executes every requested pair without feedback, automatic retry, early success or additional tools. Each arm validates current authority, source, configuration, operation ownership and retained evidence, then durably acknowledges the exact Operation disclosure effect containing the operation ID, one-based dispatch ordinal, plan digest and final envelope/destination digests. Controls are independently required to carry the exact None/empty-provenance sensitivity digest; treatments must match the frozen selected-source sensitivity digest. The actual arm envelope supplies the acknowledged sensitivity/provenance, so the clean control never claims to contain selected Covenant. A final live fence follows acknowledgement. The adapter's accounting marker precedes this callback; no awaited accounting write separates the callback from physical dispatch.

`MemoryEvaluationOperationLifetime` has two independent timers: a one-second admitted state observer cancels active I/O on Cancelling, missing/terminal state, lost/expired ownership or read failure, while the separate heartbeat renews the lease every ten seconds. Heartbeat success in Cancelling cannot mask cancellation. Caller disconnect, host shutdown and Turn revocation are linked too. Each observer read uses a separately scoped admitted connection. Disposal cancels and joins both timers and awaits actual provider/accounting completion before releasing the installation slot; process ownership is released after that drain.

A scored terminal report requires all requested valid pairs and a final authority/source/configuration/operation/evidence fence. Successful immutable report commit is the terminal publication boundary: subsequent ledger-settlement failure or the independent observer noticing the runner's own completed operation cannot publish a replacement insufficient report. Metadata-only recovery can settle the ledger later. Terminal response handling re-reads retained evidence under the original request authority and genuine request/revocation/shutdown cancellation, independently of dispatch-observer cancellation; erasure or lost response authority still prevents returning the report. The durable decision, reason and pair counts determine evidence validity: `Completed` means the request-run has terminalized, and controlled provider/output/usage/accounting/evaluator or stale-fence failures may be `Completed` with `InsufficientEvidence` and their exact closed reason. Explicit cancellation uses `Cancelled`; abrupt interruption and crash recovery use `Interrupted`. Incomplete or interrupted spend remains null even when checkpoint metadata contains a known paid prefix. Terminal run/get/replay responses expose the exact retained `ReportDigest` needed for confirmed report-only cleanup; it is null while nonterminal. Erasure cannot be reversed by late publication, replay or recovery.

The one `memory-evaluation` recovery descriptor uses `AbandonSafely`, reads checkpoint versions 0–1, and writes only version 1. Version 0 is solely the existing creation gap and requires both payload and reference to be null. The strict version 1 codec rejects unknown/duplicate JSON members, invalid identities, out-of-bound counts and inconsistent progress. Both versions use ordinary database recovery admission. Only this kind's Pending attempt-zero operations become discoverable after the named two-minute initial-start grace; fresh Pending operations and every other kind retain their prior behavior. Existing expected-revision recovery acquisition and the live lease CAS ensure stale discovery cannot steal a newly acquired live lease, and a process-owned operation is skipped.

`MemoryEvaluationRecoveryHandler` has only metadata/accounting ports. It never hydrates sources, restores authority or dispatches. A retained terminal report is preserved exactly; a retained registration receives at most one interrupted insufficient report using only proven checkpoint progress; an absent or erased root is never recreated. Exact request identity is checked against the operation and retained registration. With a proven PairCount, recovery selects only Session-null inference runs with Surface `memory-evaluation`, Purpose `counterfactual-arm`, and each exact `<evaluation-id:N>:<index>` for indices 0 through twice PairCount minus one. It refuses ambiguous duplicates, uses the existing run-abandon CAS, then invokes restricted known-measured-bill reconciliation. Prefix matches, unrelated indices/purposes/Sessions, generic reservation release and fabricated bills are excluded. Thus erased-root version 1 recovery can settle known bills independently of evidence retention while unknown spend stays conservatively held. Empty version 0 with no retained root supplies no accounting bound and appends nothing. Retry is metadata settlement only and never repeats a provider send.

Focused behavioral tests use real SQLCipher evidence/source/operation/accounting stores, real request authority and Turn leases, the real dedicated provider adapter with bounded loopback transport, and fake-time/event-driven observer and drain controls. They cover preparation and final-publication fences, exact replay and erasure, committed disclosure/checkpoint ordering, paid-prefix cancellation, detailed durable failure reasons, empty-version recovery and the initial grace/CAS races. HTTP endpoint tests exercise real host authentication/pre-binding authority, strict bounded request parsing, generated wire envelopes, original-authority rotation before response bytes, dynamic 202, and the admitted source/provider/report/cleanup flow.
