The exact selected `Published_executable_creates_initial_session_and_completes_provider_contract_exchange` gate preserves the original streaming first-session exchange and durable entries, then seeds confirmed Covenant through prepare/set/explain APIs and performs three paired native-route comparisons. Its bounded fake captures seven total calls (one original stream plus six alternating nonstreaming arms), exact model/options/no tools and known nonzero-priced usage, then checks content-free Benefit, exact digest replay/get/cleanup and unchanged source head. Managed fixture tests validate this harness; only executing the selected gate against the exact shipping Native AOT apphost proves native execution. The existing `published-session-smoke:v1` receipt remains contingent on every assertion and cleanup succeeding.


## 21. The Weave, Divination, Saga, and The Tapestry (RAG)

**Purpose:** Seven independently feature-flagged, gracefully-degrading RAG capabilities. **The Weave** imprints text as vectors; **Divination** is cosine semantic search; **Saga** is auto-extracted long-term associative memory (distinct from operator Lore / Lexicon); **The Tapestry** is a hierarchical summary tree woven over the corpora the other features already index.

All seven capabilities are implemented (§21.1–§21.2 foundation; §21.6–§21.11 features). The durable table inventory and raw-SQL initialization boundary are in §5.4.4; behavioral and reset invariants stay here.

### 21.1 Embedding infrastructure (shared foundation)

**Layering:** `IWeaveService` / `WeaveService` (**Api** — depends on `IEmbeddingGeneratorFactory` / OpenAI SDK packages, mirroring `ChatClientFactory`). `IDivinationService` / `DivinationService` + the `Data/Schema/` object files + `SqliteVecExtensionLoader` + `WeaveIndexAvailability` (**Infrastructure**). `EmbeddingBlobCodec` (**Core**).

**`IWeaveService`:** `IsAvailable` from live `IOptionsMonitor` (`Enabled` + Provider + Model). Disabled → `Embeddings.FeatureDisabled` (no HTTP). Provider failure → sanitized `Embeddings.ProviderUnavailable`. A successful `EmbedBatchAsync` answers exactly one vector per input, in input order. A provider that answers a different number (fewer or more; Microsoft.Extensions.AI does not enforce it) fails the whole call as `Embeddings.ProviderUnavailable` once, at this boundary, after the billed batch is ledgered, so every consumer indexes the answer positionally and none re-checks the count (`EntryWeavingService`, `WorkspaceIndexingService`, `SessionAttachmentIndexProcessor`, `SpellWeaveCache`, `TapestryWeaver` and `POST /v1/embeddings`; `WeaveBatchContractConsumerTests` fails when a consumer compares the answer's vector count again). Vector *widths* stay each consumer's own check, because `WeaveService` makes no promise about dimensions and a provider pool can answer two widths across sub-batches. Provider diagnostic classification uses only a real `ClientResultException.Status` or `HttpRequestException.StatusCode` in the HTTP 100–599 range. 401 names rejected credentials, 403 refused permission, 404 a missing model or embeddings endpoint, and 413 a request-too-large rejection; 400 and other statuses retain ordinary unavailable handling. Public failures remain `Embeddings.ProviderUnavailable` / HTTP 503 with bounded fixed configuration/action guidance and `arcanum doctor`, without identifier, exception/body, endpoint or credential values. Warning records distinguish resolution, generation, identity refusal and local accounting; a ledger-write failure cannot pretend to be a provider HTTP rejection. Actual provider/model come only from the current first-party lease; the initial configured snapshot is logged separately, and missing actual provenance stays `unknown`. Per-batch diagnostic state resets before resolution. Identifier labels permit at most 128 ASCII letters/digits plus `.`, `_`, `-`, `:`, starting with a letter/digit and excluding `..`; other values are redacted as a whole rather than exposing a truncated prefix. Only safe exception type, closed reason/stage, bounded status, counts and accounting IDs accompany those labels; no exception object or arbitrary message is retained. Embedding batches have no Arcanum whole-operation deadline: the caller cancellation token propagates directly through generator resolution and `GenerateAsync`. `EmbedBatchAsync` remains sequential by `BatchSize`, with provider request/chunk bounds and explicit reservation/usage reconciliation. General embedding inputs retain `ChunkAsync` sliding windows; workspace files use the deterministic line-preserving `WorkspaceCodeChunker` described in §21.7. `ChunkOverlapChars` and `ChunkSizeChars` clamp independently (0–1,024 and 128–8,192), so `ChunkAsync` bounds the *effective* overlap at half the resolved chunk size before deriving its step: the window always advances by at least `ChunkSizeChars / 2`, and a document can never emit more than twice the minimum chunk count. The bound is proportional rather than `ChunkSizeChars - 1` because an overlap one character below the window (1,000/999 — both individually legal) would otherwise collapse the step to a single character and emit one near-duplicate chunk per source character. Operators who set `ChunkOverlapChars` above half of `ChunkSizeChars` therefore get the capped overlap rather than the configured one: the shipped 1,000/100 defaults are unaffected, but re-indexing after raising the overlap past the halfway mark produces different chunk boundaries and different stored offsets.

The OpenAI embedding endpoint treats an explicit `dimensions` as an exact-width contract. It refuses a nonpositive or unsupported width before provider work and checks the assembled vectors against an accepted width before serialization. The configured width uses the same runtime clamp as other Weave consumers. It never slices vectors to satisfy a request; omitted dimensions preserve existing full-width behavior. The shared live/batch chat validator similarly refuses requested token log probabilities (`logprobs: true` or any `top_logprobs`) before inference.

**Operation identity and paid work.** One initial options snapshot supplies availability, expected canonical provider/model identity, pricing and the original reservation. After existing Tapestry validation and caller-cancellation observation, each known resolved lease must match that identity before paid `GenerateAsync`; a mismatch returns fixed `Embeddings.ProviderUnavailable` guidance without sending another batch, replaying or repricing. Earlier batches retain their recorded spend and reconcile through the existing completion handle; an unspent refused operation releases its reservation. Null-provenance legacy ordinary leases remain compatible but explicitly unknown and convey no identity assurance, and provider-returned metadata cannot supply that proof. This guard pins declared canonical provider/model names, not physical embedding space, endpoint or credential identity: same-name endpoint/key rotation retains its existing factory policy, even when it creates another generator. There is no new retry, cache, schema or capsule policy. The previously integrated RV113 independent completion and safe RunId/ReservationId/type cleanup Warning remain unchanged.

**Factory:** resolves `Arcanum:Integrations:Embeddings:Provider`/`Model` as `OpenAICompatible` (including Ollama `/v1`); leases are cached for the process lifetime. A Familiar cannot serve embeddings — it exposes chat completions only — so naming one here is a validation error.

**`IDivinationService.SearchAsync`:** callers pass vec0 table name + PK/embedding columns. If `WeaveIndexAvailability.IsVecAvailable`, vec0 KNN; else strip `_vec` and stream managed cosine over every matching BLOB-companion row (`EmbeddingBlobCodec`, bounded top-K heap, caller cancellation, no total row budget). Never throws — sanitized `Result` failure.

### 21.2 Vector storage — managed cosine over durable BLOB tables

Per feature: one durable **BLOB** table, declared as an object file in the one schema tree (§5.4.5) and installed with the durable schema. Search is **always** the managed SIMD cosine scan over those tables.

**There is no dynamic accelerator, by construction.** The hermetic SQLCipher runtime is compiled with `SQLITE_OMIT_LOAD_EXTENSION` (§5.4.4a), so a loadable extension cannot be loaded into a Grimoire connection at all — `sqlite3_load_extension` is not even exported from the library. The former sqlite-vec probe and its five `vec0` object files were therefore removed rather than retained as code that could only ever fail: `SqliteVecExtensionLoader`, `Accelerators/*_vec.sql`, and the accelerator branch of `GrimoireSchemaInstaller` are all gone. The `Accelerators` schema *category* went with them (§5.4.5); a future **statically linked** accelerator would ship inside the native library, pass its own security review, and install as its own transaction tier rather than as a category. `WeaveIndexAvailability` reports `managed` permanently and is now set unconditionally, independent of Covenant accelerator health — the Covenant FTS5 tier indexes Covenant text and has nothing to do with Weave vector search.

This costs performance, never correctness: the BLOB tables were always the source of truth and the managed scan was always the guaranteed baseline.

**Managed scan shape.** The managed brute-force path scores directly off the stored BLOB and is therefore allocation-free per row: decoding into a fresh `float[]` would double the per-row allocation of a scan that reads every in-scope row on every retrieval, for a copy nothing outlives the iteration. The query vector is invariant across the scan, so its norm is computed once per scan rather than re-derived inside the SIMD loop for every candidate, and results are kept in a min-heap whose peek is the weakest of the current top-K. §16.7's SIMD claim for cosine applies to this loop.

**Dimension mismatch:** bootstrap warns when `Arcanum:Integrations:Embeddings:Dimensions` differs from stored `Dim`; it **does not** auto-truncate — the operator must `POST /api/embeddings/reset?confirm=true` (+ optional `scope`) and then re-index.

**Rows the scan cannot compare are skipped, not scored as zero.** `DivinationService` compares a row only when its blob is a whole number of floats, it has the query's width, and it has a direction (`EmbeddingBlobCodec.TryCosineSimilarity`: non-zero norm, finite result). A row of another width, an unreadable blob, or a zero or non-finite vector is skipped and counted, and the scan logs one warning that carries the three counts and points at the reset above, rather than one line per row. Skipping rather than scoring `0` matters at a similarity threshold of `0`, which a zero score used to clear, and a corrupt blob no longer fails the whole search. If rows of another width were met and no row at all could be scored, the corpus was embedded at a different width than the query and the search answers `Embeddings.DimensionMismatch` (409; API reference §8.23) instead of an empty result that reads as "nothing relevant". A corpus with at least one comparable row answers normally. Equal similarity is ranked by id, lowest first, so which rows a full top-K keeps does not depend on the order SQLite returns them in.

### 21.3 Configuration

Public opt-ins are `Arcanum:Features:Embeddings`, `Arcanum:Features:SessionSearch`, `Arcanum:Features:CodebaseRetrieval`, `Arcanum:Features:AttachmentRetrieval`, `Arcanum:Features:Saga`, `Arcanum:Features:SagaExtraction`, `Arcanum:Features:Tapestry`, and `Arcanum:Features:SemanticSpellRouting`; `Arcanum:Features:LongRest` (default `false`) independently permits billed Saga discovery and consolidation maintenance (§21.16). It counts as embedding-backed only when `Arcanum:Integrations:Embeddings` names both a provider and a model; its chat model is `FastModel` when set, otherwise `DefaultModel`, otherwise the first advertised model (§10.8.2), and an enabled gate whose recipe cannot resolve is a validation warning, a `configuration.long_rest_recipe` doctor row and a Degraded `LongRest` health component, which refuse nothing themselves. Provider/model/dimensions are under `Arcanum:Integrations:Embeddings` (§3.4). The Tapestry adds exactly two operator-policy facts there — `Arcanum:Integrations:Embeddings:Tapestry:RetrievalMode` (`CollapsedTree` default, or `TreeTraversal`) and `Arcanum:Integrations:Embeddings:Tapestry:SummaryModel` (blank → `FastModel` → `DefaultModel`). Watcher debounce/count/reconciliation, attachment extraction/chunking/queue/retry timing, indexing page/checkpoint sizes, retrieval slice sizes, and every Tapestry tree-shaping bound (depth, children per summary, clusters per layer, summary tokens, rebuild cadence) are implementation mechanics, not public user restrictions. Internal bounds protect one allocation, queue, provider request, or checkpoint and continue through reconciliation or a later slice. Public validation requires provider/model facts whenever an embedding-backed feature is enabled, Long Rest included once it names a provider and a model.

### 21.4 Graceful degradation matrix

| Condition | Behavior |
|-----------|----------|
| `Arcanum:Features:Embeddings` and all embedding-backed feature flags are `false` | Pre-RAG behavior; embed APIs return `Embeddings.FeatureDisabled` immediately |
| Provider unreachable or failed | Sanitized `Embeddings.ProviderUnavailable`; callers skip retrieval and continue. There is no Arcanum whole-operation deadline; caller cancellation remains authoritative |
| sqlite-vec unavailable (default) | `Mode=managed`; Divination streams complete BLOB cosine with bounded top-K memory and caller cancellation. Health/`/api/meta`/`doctor` report compatibility row budget `0` (no total row budget) |
| vec0 claimed but unusable | `SearchAsync` returns sanitized failure (no throw) |
| `Dimensions` changed after data | Warning only; no auto-truncate |
| `Arcanum:Features:SessionSearch` = `false` | `EntryWeavingService` idles; `POST /api/sessions/divine` → **503** `Embeddings.FeatureDisabled` |
| `Arcanum:Features:CodebaseRetrieval` = `false` | `WorkspaceIndexingService` idles; no prompt injection; divine/index → **503** |
| `Arcanum:Features:AttachmentRetrieval` = `false` | Attachment creation/listing/tools remain unchanged; no extraction, embedding, or semantic prompt injection; DTO status is `NotEligible` |
| Attachment queue full / transient embedding failure | Creation and inference still succeed; reconciliation recovers dropped work and progress-driven retries continue until success, deterministic non-transient failure, or cancellation |
| `Arcanum:Features:Comprehension` = `false`, or attachment retrieval disabled | Document extraction and materialization are disabled, and existing document chunks are suppressed at retrieval; prior text/image behavior is preserved. A PDF is no exception: it stays an exportable `Binary` snapshot marked `NotEligible`, and no worker process is started for it. `memory search`, an operator inspection surface rather than model context, still searches the stored chunks |
| Reviewed Comprehension document format (the registry of §21.8), both gates enabled | Remains `Binary`; bounded extraction by that format's parser family feeds the existing text paths (§21.8). A PDF with a text layer is extracted by its isolated host's worker process, indexed, retrievable by page, and available to `attach_session_file`, per-turn references, and pins. PDF text is not a visible-text projection: every text-showing run is extracted in content-stream order with no rendered-visibility filter, so white-on-white, zero-size, invisible-render-mode, off-page and overlay-hidden text is extracted and reaches the model as untrusted data, under a label that says it may include text a reader would not see (§21.5, §21.8) |
| Legacy binary Office (`.doc`/`.xls`/`.ppt`), RTF, EPUB, MIME message, Office or OpenDocument template (`.dotx`/`.dotm`/`.xltx`/`.xltm`/`.potx`/`.potm`/`.vstx`/`.vstm`/`.ott`/`.ots`/`.otp`), flat (single-XML) ODF, image outside Scrying, or unknown binary attachment | Attachment remains valid and is marked `NotEligible`; the registry of §21.8 holds the only document formats Comprehension reads; OCR and image captions are not attempted. A reviewed package is recognized by its filename extension (there is no ZIP or package sniffing), so one renamed to an unrecognized extension is an unknown binary |
| Comprehension output empty, or the package is encrypted or uses an unsupported ZIP feature | Valid empty output is `NotEligible` with an extraction timestamp. Password-protected OOXML (an OLE2 wrapper), an encrypted ZIP entry, ODF manifest encryption data, and ZIP64, multi-disk, or a compression method other than stored or deflate are `NotEligible` with a fixed code-owned reason and no automatic retry |
| PDF with no extractable text, both gates enabled (a scan, a blank document, pages that show only whitespace, a page tree with no reachable page, or a document whose text the parser cannot decode) | `NotEligible` with an extraction timestamp, no reason, and no automatic retry. This is the defined input for later image recognition, which is not attempted. A PDF whose text streams fail to decode cannot be told from a scan, so decode damage reads as an image-only PDF (§21.5) |
| Password-protected PDF (one that needs a password other than the empty one, or one protected by a public-key (certificate) security handler, which has no password to give), both gates enabled | Terminal `Failed` with the fixed reason `Password-protected PDFs are not supported.` and no automatic retry. No password is supplied, guessed, stripped, or asked for; a PDF restricted only by permissions opens with the empty password and is extracted (§21.5 for the owner-password limit) |
| Malformed PDF, both gates enabled: not a PDF, truncated, no readable trailer or `/Root`, a cross-reference stream whose entries are garbled, or structure the strict parser refuses (nesting past its ceiling of 256, which a form that invokes itself or a loop of references reaches on its first descent) | Terminal `Failed` with the fixed reason `The PDF document is malformed.` and no automatic retry. When a cross-reference table is damaged, missing or short, the parser finds the objects it does not list by scanning for those written at the top level of the file, so that damage is read, not refused; it cannot find objects that sit inside an object stream, which is the garbled cross-reference stream above. A page whose `/Contents` refers to an object the file does not define is not malformed: it is read as blank (§21.8) |
| PDF over its extraction bounds, both gates enabled: more than 2,000 pages, a cross-reference table that lists more than 100,000 objects (those stored in object streams included), a page of more than 250,000 glyphs, more than 2,000,000 glyphs in all, or the 262,144-character output ceiling reached before any page showed visible text | Terminal `Failed` with the fixed reason `The PDF document exceeds its extraction bounds.` and no automatic retry. Text past the output ceiling on a later page is a truncated extraction, not a failure |
| PDF worker resource limit or wall clock: the worker crosses its 768 MB memory or 15 s CPU ceiling, is ended for a write past its 1 MiB size ceiling (macOS; a backstop, since its jail gives it nowhere to write), outlives its 10-second wall clock, or gives up at its own 8-second deadline | The runner or the worker ends the process tree; terminal `Failed` with `PDF extraction exceeded its resource limits.` or `PDF extraction exceeded its deadline.` and no automatic retry. A healthy PDF queued behind it still reaches `Indexed` (§21.8) |
| PDF worker fault: it crashes, exits with a code of its own, writes truncated or malformed output, or the PDF is over the worker's 1 MiB input ceiling | Terminal `Failed` with the fixed reason `PDF extraction failed.`; no exit code, stderr, exception type, or path reaches a reason |
| PDF worker unavailable on this host: the filesystem jail cannot be applied (the operator escape hatch is never honored), the process limits cannot be applied, the host is not a Native AOT binary (a `dotnet run` or DevHost process, or a managed publish) or cannot re-launch its own binary (an embedding test host, a file that cannot be identified, or a process started as `dotnet host.dll`), or the binary was replaced since the host started | Terminal `Failed` with the fixed reason `PDF extraction is unavailable on this host.`; no worker is started and nothing is retried automatically, because a retry would only repeat the refusal. A non-AOT development host cannot run the worker (§21.5) |
| Maintenance closes Grimoire admission while a PDF is being indexed | No worker starts once maintenance is pending, including maintenance that arrived while the document's bytes were being read: the document stands down as a maintenance deferral, with no attempt spent and no index generation written, and is re-queued after admission reopens. A worker already running is waited for, up to its wall clock, so maintenance that arrives during a slow PDF may fail with the retryable `Grimoire.WorkDrainTimeout`; if the worker returns while maintenance is still pending, its verdict is discarded and the document is read again after admission reopens (§21.8) |
| Comprehension text container or package is invalid, a bomb, over its bounds, or past its deadline | Text container: a missing or incomplete header or invalid UTF-8. Package: an invalid ZIP, entry-count, expansion, or ratio bound, an unsafe or duplicate entry name, a missing required part, content that does not match its declared format, malformed XML or a DTD, or an XML or structure bound. Each, and a timeout of the document's own five-second budget, is terminal `Failed` with a bounded code-owned reason and no automatic retry |
| Comprehension parser family busy: its extraction slot is not acquired within the code-owned 30-second slot wait (attach, refresh, per-turn references, pins) or is not free (indexing, which never waits under its work lease), or an outstanding parser quarantines it | The attempt is `Deferred` with the fixed reason `Document extraction is temporarily busy.`, having read and parsed nothing. Indexing keeps the row `Pending` with that reason and no extraction timestamp, retries it automatically without spending an attempt, and reconciliation re-queues it if that retry is lost; attach, refresh, per-turn references, and pins report the document unavailable for that call (`attach_session_file`: `Not attached: '<name>' vN.` with the busy reason and `Try attaching it again shortly.`) and record nothing durable. PDF follows the same slot rules with one slot for its worker (one PDF at a time per process), and it is never quarantined, because its worker returns only after its process is gone |
| Watcher unavailable or internal watcher capacity reached | Workspace status is `Watching=false`, `Degraded=true`; periodic reconciliation remains active |
| Watcher overflow/error or pending-event capacity reached | Mark potentially stale, expose `Overflowed` for real/cap overflow, discard the lossy event set, and schedule a complete cancellable reconciliation; polling never stops |
| No indexed chunks / empty WorkingDirectory | Empty results / skip retrieval — inference continues with `[None]` |
| `Arcanum:Features:Saga` = `false` | Saga retrieval/divine/read_saga are gated; **browse/delete/stats are not gated** |
| `Arcanum:Features:CampaignScopedMemory` = `false` (default) | Saga retrieval calls the unscoped `SearchAsync` and the Lexicon reads its global tier: identical candidate sets and ordering to a build without the feature. No binding is read and no scope column is consulted |
| Campaign scoping on, turn resolved no Campaign | Saga admits installation-scoped memories only; the Lexicon reads its global tier only. Nothing fails and no turn is refused |
| `Arcanum:Features:Annals` = `false` (explicit opt-out) | Future extraction and claimless Lexicon writes append no automatic claim; semantic Lexicon writes with existing history still publish a consistent successor, while existing history remains readable and retrieval and every prompt byte stay unchanged. Corrections, retirements, and reinstatements that change Saga or Lexicon state still append required evidence; their idempotent outcomes and every pin/unpin append nothing to the Annals. Erasure still removes any existing claim because those records are independent of the automatic-history policy (§21.13) |
| Annals write fails | It shares the memory's own transaction and fails with it, so no memory is ever committed without the claim explaining it. The caller sees the failure its store already reports — a background extraction requeues on its existing ladder with the exact sequence cursor unadvanced, and a Lexicon write returns `Lexicon.WriteFailed`, which the tool surface converts to a tool-result string. No turn sees an exception |
| Campaign scoping on, memory scope still unclassified | That memory is a candidate in no scope until the version-2 sweep reaches it; the turn proceeds with whatever else is in scope |
| Campaign scoping on, Session binding unresolved | The turn draws on installation-scoped memory only, and memories written under that Session are retrievable nowhere until an operator resolves the binding |
| `Arcanum:Features:SagaExtraction` = `false` | Extraction drops; retrieval/API reads are unaffected |
| Extraction LLM/embedding failure or malformed JSON | Exact sequence cursor **not** advanced; the deduplicated queue retries the same checkpoint after a short code-owned delay |
| Valid empty extraction JSON | Exact sequence cursor advances through the reviewed timestamp-group checkpoint inside the active interval (“nothing durable in this page”) |
| `Arcanum:Features:Tapestry` = `false` | `TapestryWeavingService` idles; no tree is built and no hierarchical context is injected |
| Tapestry summary model unresolvable | No generation above a single leaf is published; the scope contributes no context and flat retrieval is unchanged |
| Tapestry build fails, is cancelled, or is interrupted | The staging generation is dropped and the last complete generation stays current. A failure that had paid for summaries backs off before it is tried again (one sweep interval after the first failure, doubling with each consecutive failure of the same build, up to a day) so it does not re-bill them every sweep; a cancellation is the host stopping and is never remembered as a failure |
| Tapestry scope has no complete generation | That scope contributes no hierarchical context; other scopes and other retrieval sources are unaffected |
| Tapestry corpus changes between reading its leaves and beginning the generation | `CorpusChanged`: the weaver re-reads the corpus identity once the staging generation exists and, when it moved, abandons the build before anything is embedded, summarized or published; the next sweep reads the corpus as it now is |
| Tapestry scope holds more leaves than the ceiling (`TapestryLimits.MaxLeavesPerScope`, 50,000) | `TooLarge`: nothing is read, embedded or summarized for that scope, no tree is built or refreshed for it, and a generation it already has stays current; the next sweep counts again, so narrowing the corpus lifts it |
| Tapestry leaf's source row changed after publication | That leaf is dropped at hydration rather than injected under a stale hash; the corpus fingerprint change rebuilds the tree |
| `Arcanum:Features:SemanticSpellRouting` = `false` | `FullGrimoire` → existing LLM `SemanticRouter` unchanged |
| Spell Weave cache / prompt embed failure | Fall back to `FullGrimoire` (Debug log; no regression) |
| `Arcanum:Features:LongRest` = `false` (default) | No billed Long Rest work exists: a Session turn schedules nothing, the background worker idles and creates no scope, `POST /api/memory/saga/long-rest/sweeps` answers **503** `LongRest.Unavailable`, and the root enricher reads no registry. Ranking uses raw cosine with no age, origin or usefulness modifier, no dormancy and no new temporal filter. The operator declaration route (`POST /api/memory/saga/long-rest`) is not gated by the flag |
| Long Rest on, recipe unresolved | One content-free sentence as a validation warning, the `configuration.long_rest_recipe` doctor row and a Degraded `LongRest` health component; startup and ordinary turns are unaffected. A clean schedule refused with `LongRest.Unavailable` is logged, counted as `arcanum.long_rest.clean_schedule_refused` and the turn proceeds. Only a turn that reads Covenant-protected memory in a scope with protected Long Rest sources ends, with `LongRest.Unavailable` carrying that sentence (§10.8.2) |
| Clean Long Rest debt (a queued, running, parked, busy or stale sweep) | A Session turn never fails on it: any `LongRest.*` refusal of the clean request is skipped and the background worker owns execution. A Covenant refusal, a configuration change during the turn, a cancellation and every protected-partition failure (`LongRest.OperationBusy` included) still end the turn (§21.16.3) |
| Provider failure during a sweep | The attempt is settled in-frame and the sweep parks. A transient failure (`LongRest.ProviderUnavailable`, `LongRest.ProviderUnreachable`) is readmitted by the worker after a 30-second cooldown that doubles, at most four times without committed progress, except that each `ProviderUnavailable` failure (and each `ProviderRejected` one) is also one of a work unit's two unknown-usage attempts, so the second such failure of the same unit parks it as `LongRest.TransportUnknown` whatever readmissions remain, while `ProviderUnreachable` sent nothing and is not counted; `LongRest.ProviderRejected`, `LongRest.TransportUnknown` (two unknown-usage attempts of one work unit) and a spent budget wait for an operator, and a protected sweep always waits for its next eligible Session request (§10.8.2) |
| Maintenance closes admission mid-sweep | A clean sweep parks as `long_rest.maintenance_deferred` and is readmitted at once, with no cooldown and no budget spent; a protected sweep parks as `long_rest.authorized_request_required` (§21.16.5) |

### 21.5 Known limitations

No auto re-index on model/dimension change (use `/api/embeddings/reset`); managed vector search is complete but brute-force time grows linearly with matching corpus size when sqlite-vec is absent; watcher and attachment-queue delivery are advisory and periodic reconciliation remains required; workspace indexing shares two active handles across all intake sources, while attachment indexing remains sequential per service instance; HTML extraction is a bounded visible-text projection rather than a browser DOM; Comprehension is IN DEVELOPMENT on `general-enhancements` and reads only the reviewed formats of §21.8, with a cooperative in-process extractor boundary rather than process isolation for every format except PDF, whose parser runs only in a jailed worker process; legacy binary Office, RTF, EPUB, MIME messages, and OCR remain unsupported; PDF extraction is not a visible-text projection and applies no rendered-visibility filter, because deciding visibility correctly requires a renderer and a half-modelled filter would silently drop real content while still missing overlay-hidden text: every text-showing run of every page is extracted in content-stream order, so text a reader would never have seen (white-on-white, zero-size or invisible-render-mode runs, runs positioned off the page, runs hidden behind an overlay) is extracted and reaches the model as untrusted DATA, which is why every framing of PDF text says it may include text a reader would not see, and the replacement text a PDF attaches to marked content (`/ActualText`) is never used because it too is text no reader sees that the file's author controls; PDF text keeps no layout and follows the content stream, not the reading order, and restores right-to-left text to logical order only run by run (a file carries no paragraph direction, so the order of whole runs in a line that mixes directions is the stream's, Arabic presentation forms are not folded to base letters, and a bracket glyph a file draws mirrored may come out as the other bracket); a PDF whose text streams the parser cannot decode reads as having no text, so decode damage can look like an image-only PDF and is `NotEligible` rather than `Failed`; the parser tries the empty string as the owner password as well as the user password and an owner session decrypts the whole file, so a PDF that needs a real user password but has an empty owner password opens and is extracted; PDF glyph bounds are checked after the parser has built a page, so they bound what the extractor keeps and the worker's process limits, not those bounds, are what stop a hostile page; the PDF object bound (100,000 entries that the cross-reference data lists as in use) is checked right after the open, so it bounds what is traversed afterwards and not the parser while it opens, and it does not count an object a file writes but its table omits, of which a file within the 1 MiB intake ceiling holds fewer than the bound; PDF cycles are not caught by a first-party object walk: a cyclic page tree ends with no page (on the visited set of the undefined-contents repair, or through the parser's own page-tree handling), and a form that invokes itself, a loop of references or content nested too deep ends at the parser's nesting ceiling of 256 as malformed, which a loop reaches on its first descent, with the worker's wall-clock, memory and CPU limits behind it; the PDF parser is a pinned pre-release build of PdfPig, because the stable release 0.1.16 ends the process with an uncatchable stack overflow on small cyclic files that the pinned build turns into exceptions, and it moves to the first stable release that carries those fixes; the PDF worker is sized and jailed for the shipping Native AOT binary and is supported only there: a host the runtime does not report as a Native AOT binary (a `dotnet run` or DevHost process, a managed publish, or an embedding test host) has no worker launch, starts no process, and ends every PDF as terminal `Failed` with `PDF extraction is unavailable on this host.`, because a managed apphost keeps its runtime outside the binary, which a cleared environment and a jail cannot reach (a Homebrew .NET install is not found), so a worker started from it would fail without saying why; in every case the host stays up; the worker's Windows route (the AppContainer broker launching the re-executed binary with the document on its standard handles) rests on Windows-only tests that had not been run on a Windows host when it was written; Office, OpenDocument, and Visio extraction is a bounded visible-text projection rather than a renderer: it keeps no layout (a table is one tab-separated line per row), applies no number formats (an Excel date appears as its serial number, an OpenDocument date as its ISO value), does not project headers, footers, master pages, slide layouts and masters, charts, SmartArt, Excel drawings and text boxes, PowerPoint equations, Word `w:altChunk` content or `w:sym` glyphs, automatic list and heading numbers, or the mark and number of a footnote or endnote reference, does not detect text hidden only by colour or size (white-on-white, one-point type), projects the cached text of a data-bound Word content control rather than the bound value, hides a whole Word table whose table style has a conditional format that hides text, and applies a conservative Visio layer rule (a shape on any invisible layer is treated as hidden); Saga extraction deduplicates a live model conclusion only against the exact same content its owning Session already holds in the same derived scope (`AlreadyPresent`) and against retired-equivalent suppression — the same conclusion reached in another Session stays its own row — and its pending requests, per-turn provenance intervals, retry ladders, and the paid response kept for a page whose embeddings all failed are process-local, so the durable sequence cursor prevents already-committed pages from being repeated after a restart but a later successful turn is what re-enqueues any unpaid suffix; a missing original interval is then reviewed under deny-all provenance rather than reconstructing authority the process no longer has; a durable memory written during explicit Annals opt-out carries no automatic claim, and re-enabling Annals neither backfills that period nor synthesizes a prior claim — the schema-v3 sweep was a one-time historical upgrade and this default-policy change adds no migration or rerun — while a later ordinary write follows the then-current enabled policy, so an unclaimed durable row remains a first-class state rather than an error; a Campaign-scoped search always ranks through the managed cosine path, so enabling scoping forgoes vector acceleration for Saga on any future build that ships one; pure spell-routing ties break by stable sort only. Long Rest: discovery reads and verifies every captured leaf for each anchor, and its lexical lane reads the content of every row a query matches, so a scan grows with its generation; the pairing constants (§21.16.1), the lexical coverage bar (200 thousandths), the scorer's constants and the 0.92 summary gate are code-owned constants fitted on one labelled corpus of thirty-five memories and one local embedding model, each bound into the recipe digest so that changing one starts a new generation; the guarantee that no fold joins memories of different topics whatever the chat model answers is geometric, so it holds only as far as the configured embedding model places different topics apart: on `qwen3-embedding:8b` every cross-topic pair of the calibration corpus is far under every anchor's floor, and on `embeddinggemma` the closest cross-topic pair is closer than the most distant paraphrase, so no single scalar separates them and only the chat model's own answer and Number Agreement stand in front of such a pair, which is why the qualification measures the separation for each embedding model; the floor is relative to the generation's own composition, so many memories unrelated to an anchor lower its floor toward the closeness clause (about 0.55 of the way from the median to a perfect match) and narrow the margin that a cross-topic pair has under it; Number Agreement compares the set of digit-bearing tokens and not where they stand, so a value rearranged between two memories (`1.5 GB` and `5.1 GB`) agrees and only the chat model refuses it; minimal pairs built on one template (two cities in sentences of one shape) are a risk the chat model carries; the model path decides `EquivalentObservations` or `NoChange` and never `Supersession`, so a stale value and its replacement both stay current until a correction or an operator declaration; at the default 8,192-token chat window a request holds about 5,328 bytes and the fixed instructions of an adjudication take about 2,300 of them, so two memories whose text together is more than about 3,000 bytes cannot be paired and are not consolidated until the window is raised; a model that ignores the summary bound is accepted up to 8,192 bytes, refused at its embedding with `LongRest.ModelContextTooSmall` when that exceeds the embedding window, and paid for again after a window change starts a new generation; a work unit stops after two unknown-usage attempts (a transient `LongRest.ProviderUnavailable` failure counts as one, a `LongRest.ProviderRejected` one likewise, `LongRest.ProviderUnreachable` does not) and parks as `LongRest.TransportUnknown`, which only cancelling the parked sweep resumes; only an accepted adjudication unit or an advanced discovery cursor resets a sweep's failure budget, not capture, hierarchy or publication progress; a protected sweep waiting for its next eligible Session request has no timer and keeps `DurableOperations` Degraded, and one parked in a boot where its fence then changed (a drained maintenance window, a recovered Covenant authority, a change to the Covenant capability state) is retired by the next Session turn that carries live authority and replaced by a new generation, which pays for its summaries and decisions again; a completed sweep replays only while it is current, so an edit to any setting in the configuration value that is not reverted, or a drained maintenance window or recovered Covenant authority inside the boot that completed it, starts a new generation that pays for its summaries and decisions again; derived plaintext (nodes and accepted summaries) lives until the successor generation completes, the generation is invalidated or the operation is pruned. Usefulness, decay and ranking use the bounded exact-version evidence policy in §21.16.6; retained exposure alone never establishes usefulness.

**Reset scopes:** `POST /api/embeddings/reset?confirm=true` with optional `scope=all|entry|workspaceFile|saga|sessionAttachment|tapestry` (snake-case aliases accepted; default `all`); unknown scope → **400** `Validation.InvalidBody`. The `tapestry` scope removes graph rows from `tapestry_generations`, `tapestry_nodes`, `tapestry_edges`, `tapestry_node_embeddings` and any reachable plain `tapestry_node_embeddings_vec` mirror. The reset captures graph counts inside the truncation transaction before any cascade, clears the reachable mirror, then deletes generation owners before their immutable children; returned per-table counts describe the rows actually removed by that closure. The leaf corpora stay indexed, source-owned `tapestry_leaf_hashes` remain valid, and monotonic `tapestry_scope_revisions` survive so an edit/revert cannot reuse an earlier invalidation epoch. The next sweep rebuilds the trees from those sources. A reset of one corpus (`entry`, `workspaceFile`, `sessionAttachment`) leaves the trees woven from it in place, so a tree does not depend on the reset to be recognized as stale after a model change: its settings fingerprint and every summary's reuse identity carry the embedding provider and model (§21.11), so changing either — even to a model of the same width — rebuilds the tree on the next sweep and reuses none of the old summary vectors. Every scope also empties its plain `*_vec` vector mirror whatever the accelerator flag says, because the mirror holds the embedding itself and an earlier build may have filled it; a legacy `vec0` virtual table this runtime cannot open is skipped, reports zero rows, and does not fail the reset (§10.17).

### 21.6 Session Divination

**Service:** `EntryWeavingService` (`BackgroundService`) — idle unless `Arcanum:Features:SessionSearch` is enabled; uses a code-owned cadence and embeds not-yet-imprinted non-empty `Entries` (SQL `LEFT JOIN`, empty filtered in SQL, then a **per-row** upsert of BLOB ± vec0). The upsert stays per row deliberately, for idempotency and partial progress under WAL with `synchronous=NORMAL`. The tick indexes the provider response positionally against the request without re-checking its length: `IWeaveService.EmbedBatchAsync` answers exactly one vector per input or fails (§21.1), so a short provider reply is already a failed batch before it reaches the tick, instead of an index overrun that would throw into the catch-all retry and re-issue the billable embedding call every second. It is idempotent; failures retry on a capped ladder rather than every tick: a batch the provider refuses (or a provider call that throws) charges each of its entries one failure, and an entry then waits one tick, two, four and so on, up to 360 ticks, before it is selected again. The ladder is process-local bookkeeping (at most 256 tracked entries; a restart starts it over), the read is widened by the number of entries still waiting so they cannot hold the head of the queue and starve the entries behind them, and a success removes an entry from it. Once the provider has returned, the upserts that keep its answer run on a token the host cannot cancel, so a shutdown at that point keeps what was billed instead of leaving the next tick to select and pay for the same entries again.

A tick is also one unit of Grimoire admission (§10.20.3). It takes one work capability before its DI scope exists and releases it only after that scope has asynchronously disposed, so a transition's stage one waits for the whole tick rather than discovering the worker's already-open handle later; and it holds one atomic effect group over `EmbedBatchAsync` plus every resulting upsert. The group is wider than the writes on purpose, because `EmbedBatchAsync` opens an accounting scope of its own and writes an inference-run row before any provider I/O and completes it after — a group starting at the first upsert would leave the billable call and its own durable row outside the frontier. Per-row upsert granularity and the per-tick effect group are orthogonal: the first is a SQL choice about partial progress, the second is an admission boundary about what maintenance must wait through. Three outcomes are therefore distinct rather than two. Maintenance deferral is neither completion nor failure: refused its work capability the tick creates no scope, refused its effect group it has read the pending selection and nothing more, and in both cases it performs no provider call and no write, reports `DeferredForMaintenance`, and comes back on the ordinary cadence with no retry counter to increment and no waiter registered. A genuine product failure still throws to the loop's catch-all, which logs at `Error` and backs off for one second. Host cancellation still ends the loop. Before this, a closed gate reached that catch-all: an expected, temporary refusal was reported once a second, with a stack trace, for the length of the window.

**API/CLI:** `POST /api/sessions/divine` + `arcanum session divine` — gates/errors in §4.3 / API §8.23. Filters `CampaignId` / `Status` (default `"active"`; invalid status → **400**). `NextCursor` is always null; `HasMore` is true only when the answer was cut (more matching hits than `limit`, or the 500-candidate second search filled before the ranking was exhausted), and the filters are applied over a first window of 4× `limit` candidates and at most one second window of 500.

### 21.7 Semantic Codebase Retrieval

**Service:** `WorkspaceIndexingService` — idle unless `Arcanum:Features:CodebaseRetrieval` is enabled. Workspace API registration and inference `WorkingDirectory` registration each request one workspace watcher, two recursive `FileSystemWatcher` instances (one for file names and content changes, one for directory names); a code-owned `MaxWatchers` capacity bounds simultaneous workspace watchers (two native watchers each) and never creates one watcher per directory. Workspace update/unregister and host shutdown dispose obsolete watchers. Create/change/delete/rename callbacks enter a per-workspace, 4,096-path bounded coalescer. After the code-owned debounce window, final filesystem state wins: editor temporary-file rename replacement and out-of-order delete notifications become one target upsert, storms on one path become one action, deleted/renamed-away paths remove chunks and embeddings (a path that is gone takes everything stored under it as a directory too, so a directory renamed into an ignored location, or deleted or moved out of the workspace, leaves nothing behind), and the creation of a directory or its rename into the workspace requests reconciliation. A Changed event for a directory says nothing was added or removed (Windows raises one for the parent of every written file), so it requests nothing.

Watchers are latency hints, never a security or correctness boundary. Every callback is wrapped so a consumer or error-sink exception cannot escape onto a native dispatch thread. Callbacks carry the exact registration incarnation: an obsolete callback cannot mutate, dispose, or resurrect its replacement. Registration reserves watcher capacity before factory dispatch and revalidates the reservation before publishing the returned watcher; shutdown joins in-flight registrations and disposes unpublished instances. Incremental upserts repeat lexical containment, symlink-component resolution, stable path identity capture, opened-handle identity comparison, the shared eligibility rule below, and stable-handle reading. A symlink replacement removes previously indexed content without embedding the outside target.

Scheduled sweeps, watcher drains, and manual `QueueIndexNow` requests share one process-wide scheduler with **two active workspace handles** and at most one handle per logical workspace. The first two identities dispatch directly; only excess distinct identities allocate a temporary intrusive FIFO, which is released when empty. Queued entries contain demand data only, not tasks, cancellation sources, scopes, or gate waiters. Same-workspace requests coalesce into bounded pending demand; work arriving after a snapshot is claimed becomes a follow-up. The pump remains responsive while either active handle indexes or waits through maintenance.

Each active handle acquires Grimoire work admission **before creating its async DI scope or claiming its watcher snapshot**. It revalidates the original root identity after queue delay. Each `IndexFileAsync` call owns one effect group covering stable file reading, every provider/accounting call, chunk writes, metadata, and compensation. Delete-only and orphan-cleanup suffixes are DB-only under the work lease and need no effect group. Admission or frontier refusal is maintenance deferral, not completion or failure: dispose the scope and lease, retain the exact handle and capacity slot, and wait once for the next open generation. Reopen followed by immediate reclose repeats admission without creating a scope; newer demand merges behind the retained identity. Deferral does not advance success status, mark degradation, or spend the scheduled cadence.

A scheduled sweep keeps one shared completion token until all its claimed workspace work settles, including a full follow-up attached to an already-running incremental snapshot. Only an empty, unclaimed sweep can remain due without owning a waiter. Success advances the normal cadence. A genuine failure does not shorten it for every workspace: the failed entry carries its own retry time on an exponential backoff (one second, doubling per consecutive failure, capped at the reconciliation interval), a full unit that belongs to no sweep (a manual request, or the follow-up of one that stopped on its file budget) takes its place on the same ladder when it fails, so the files it did not reach do not wait out the reconciliation interval, a retry-only sweep covers just the failed entries whose time has elapsed and leaves the full cadence untouched, and each sweep's outstanding count covers only the entries it claimed, so one vanished working directory never re-walks the healthy ones. An entry whose root stays unavailable (deleted, moved outside the allowlist, or replaced by another directory) through eight consecutive sweeps is evicted with its watcher; its stored chunks are untouched and the next registration of that path starts a fresh entry. A complete reconciliation clears an entry's failure state. Watcher error, native overflow, the creation of a directory or its rename into the workspace, or pending-path overflow request full reconciliation; when exact hints were lost, reconciliation forces the affected inventory. A watcher that could not be created delivered no events, so it forces nothing: the entry is only marked degraded and re-creation backs off per entry (one immediate retry, then one second doubling up to the reconciliation interval, with the scheduler loop waking at every deadline that fell after its watcher pass began, a creation refused by maintenance staying owed on the ladder instead of being dropped, and an event resetting the ladder only when it comes from a watcher that has run for at least thirty seconds, so a watcher that errors right after it was created keeps climbing instead of being re-created at once forever), and the periodic reconciliation covers the unwatched workspace meanwhile. A watcher that is finally created after such a gap asks for one plain, unforced reconciliation, because it may have missed what changed meanwhile and the next scheduled one can be an hour away. A persistently failing factory therefore costs a bounded number of creation attempts, not a forced re-read per debounce cycle. Ordinary manual/full reconciliation still skips unchanged signatures and reuses content-addressed embeddings. Coalescing a full scan never erases pending watcher force hints: exact pending paths are reread even when timestamp and length collide, newer same-path actions win, and completed forced files are not repeated after a maintenance frontier loss.

`QueueIndexNow` synchronously returns typed `Accepted` or `Coalesced` acceptance. Capacity overflow is accepted, not unavailable; closed intake or dispatch failure returns `Workspace.IndexingUnavailable`. The endpoint preserves its bool **202** response for both accepted outcomes and maps unavailable to **503**. Accepted work belongs to the host, not the requesting client's cancellation token. Stop closes scheduled, watcher, and manual intake together, snapshots the published active terminal tasks, cancels outside the scheduler lock, and joins scope/effect/lease cleanup plus watcher creation and disposal. Caller cancellation or a throwing cancellation callback cannot abandon that cleanup.

Candidate discovery remains lazy: a full walk visits every reachable eligible entry unless canceled, with no aggregate candidate list or total-entry ceiling. A canonical visited-directory set terminates symlink cycles. Each opened file streams through a pooled character page sized to eight embedding chunks and returns the buffer after its page work; there is no aggregate eligible-file-size ceiling or `ReadToEnd` allocation. `MaxFilesToIndex` bounds one embedding checkpoint (one full unit); unchanged files do not consume it, and orphan cleanup runs only from a complete inventory. A file with no text to embed (an empty one) carries no chunk row and so no signature, so every walk meets it again; it is neither a failure nor work the budget bounds, so it never spends the budget or counts as the progress that earns a follow-up. A full unit that stops on the budget with changed files still waiting, having indexed at least one file itself, is progress rather than a finished reconciliation: it does not mark the workspace reconciled, and the scheduler queues a follow-up full demand that takes a fresh work lease and slot once the unit settles (a forced reconciliation stays forced and remembers the files it already re-embedded). Initial indexing of a large repository therefore proceeds checkpoint by checkpoint without waiting for the next reconciliation interval, and a unit that made no progress never asks for a follow-up, so an unspendable budget cannot become a hot loop. Extension, ignored-directory, cancellation, and symlink/handle-identity defenses remain mandatory.

**One eligibility rule.** `WorkspaceIndexEligibility` is the single predicate behind the full walk, the watcher intake, and the incremental drain, so content the full walk would never send to the embedding provider cannot reach it through a watcher event. A path is indexable only when no segment of its workspace-relative path is dot-prefixed, marked Hidden or System, or an ignored directory name (`bin`, `obj`, `.git`, `node_modules`, `.vs`, `.nuget`, `packages`, `dist`, `build`; compared case-insensitively), and its extension is configured. The dot rule is lexical and applies on every platform because Unix `File.GetAttributes` reports only the leaf's own hidden bit, so a file inside `.secrets/` carries no attribute at all; the attribute rule stays for Windows, which hides by attribute rather than by name, and the dot rule applies there too: `.github/workflows` is not indexed on Windows either, deliberately, because a dot-named file such as `.env.json` is as sensitive there as anywhere. The walk judges each entry's own name and prunes a rejected directory before descending. The watcher intake applies the lexical half, and drops a path whose extension is not configured unless it may be a directory that appeared or went away (a Created, Renamed or Deleted event raised by the workspace's directory-name watcher, a second platform watcher beside the file watcher, so every event already says whether it names a directory and the intake never probes the disk on a watcher thread; the path a rename moved away from is always kept, and a Deleted directory event is kept because a directory moved to the Trash or out of the workspace raises no event for its files, so that one path is what removes its stored subtree), before it touches the coalescer, so a build writing thousands of files under `obj/`, or thousands of objects, logs or bytecode files anywhere else, cannot spend the 4,096-path budget or force a full re-walk (the workspace root itself is still queued, so the creation of a directory keeps requesting reconciliation). The incremental drain repeats the lexical half and then reads the attributes of the leaf and of every ancestor directory; a rejected or unreadable path has anything already stored for it, or under it when it was a directory, removed. Once a file is open, the lexical half is applied once more to where the kernel places the opened handle, relative to the kernel's own spelling of the workspace root, so a visibly named link to a dot-prefixed, hidden or ignored target (or a link to such a directory) is excluded as that target: its content is not embedded and anything stored under the link's name is removed. A hidden or dot-prefixed file is therefore never chunked, embedded, stored, or returned by retrieval, and a watcher event cannot revive one the full walk skips.

**Stable chunks:** `WorkspaceCodeChunker` preserves exact source slices, character offsets, and one-based line ranges; it prefers Markdown headings and common code declaration shapes without a reflection-heavy parser, falls back to bounded line-aware splits, and never separates a UTF-16 surrogate pair. That holds at **read-page boundaries** too: page reads fill to a character count and know nothing about UTF-16 pairs, so a page ending in a lone high surrogate holds it back and joins it to its partner on the next page, and a short read (end of stream) emits a genuinely unpaired high surrogate rather than dropping it. Without that carry, both halves would be embedded and persisted with the character replaced by U+FFFD, and the stored chunk would no longer be the exact source slice. `WeaveService.ChunkAsync` guards the window **start** as well as the tail, so no chunk begins with an orphaned low surrogate; the previous window already carried the whole character, so stepping past the low half loses no coverage.

**Atomic per-chunk write:** the chunk row, its embedding BLOB, and the optional `vec0` mirror commit in **one transaction**, so a torn write can never leave a chunk row without its embedding, and a `SQLITE_BUSY` retry restarts from a clean transaction rather than replaying a partial one.

`ChunkId` is deterministic from the immutable first accepted workspace-path spelling, relative path, chunk content, and repeated-content occurrence. The scheduler uses a separate trailing-separator-trimmed key (case-insensitive only on Windows) without changing persisted `WorkspacePath` or chunk IDs. `ResolveIndexedWorkspacePath` maps live aliases to that accepted spelling; Wizard registers then resolves once, and divine/inspector readers resolve once and reuse the exact result for ranking, metadata, counts, and dimensions. Without a live entry, resolution retains the existing full-path normalization: a durable registered `WorkspaceInfo.Path` remains readable after restart, but an arbitrary transient alias from a previous process is not reconstructed. There is no startup/index-table enumeration or alias migration; historic duplicate alias namespaces remain preexisting data reconciled by ordinary reindex. A small edit embeds only newly identified chunks; unchanged IDs retain their BLOB/vec0 embeddings while positional/file-time metadata is refreshed. Rename to a different path rebuilds under the new identity and deletes the old path. Tables: canonical `workspace_file_chunks` includes `StartLine`/`EndLine`, with embedding BLOB/vec0 companions (§5.4.4).

**Inference:** `RetrieveSemanticContextAsync` injects `### Semantic Context (Retrieved Codebase)` (DATA); failures → `null` (never fail turn).

**API:** `.../files/divine`, `.../files/index`, read-only inspector `.../index/status` + `.../chunks` (no mutate; preview capped). Status merges durable counts with process-local `Watching`, `Degraded`, `Overflowed`, `Reconciling`, `LastEventAt`, and `LastSuccessfulIndexAt`; chunk previews include line ranges. These workspace-scoped diagnostics intentionally stay on the index-status route rather than changing global health/`doctor`. Errors §4.3.

### 21.8 Session attachment retrieval

**Extraction:** `SessionAttachmentTextExtractor` accepts strict UTF-8 plain text, Markdown, source code, JSON, YAML, XML, CSV, and logs. Accepted source/document/data extensions are `.txt`, `.md`, `.markdown`, `.fs`, `.vb`, `.ps1`, `.ts`, `.css`, `.rst`, `.adoc`, `.asciidoc`, `.tex`, `.patch`, `.diff`, `.ini`, `.srt`, `.vtt`, `.ics`, `.c`, `.h`, `.cpp`, `.cc`, `.cxx`, `.cs`, `.go`, `.java`, `.kt`, `.log`, `.py`, `.rb`, `.rs`, `.bash`, `.sh`, `.js`, `.cjs`, `.php`, `.sql`, `.json`, `.jsonld`, `.jsonl`, `.toml`, `.xml`, `.xsl`, `.yml`, `.yaml`, `.cff`, `.csv`, and `.tsv`; `.html`/`.htm` use bounded visible-text extraction that removes script/style content and decodes entities. `.env`, `.properties`, `.cfg`, and `.conf` are deliberately excluded because silent indexing can expose credentials. `.ics` is raw UTF-8 retrieval text with RFC 5545 folding/escaping rather than structured calendar parsing. Newlines are normalized deterministically. Invalid UTF-8 fails, NUL-bearing content and unsupported binary formats are ineligible, and character/chunk boundaries never split UTF-16 surrogate pairs. Legacy binary Office, RTF, EPUB, MIME messages, images, and unknown formats remain unindexed; the reviewed document formats, PDF among them, are extracted only by Comprehension, below, and with Comprehension off a PDF stays `NotEligible` like any other binary.

**Comprehension boundary (IN DEVELOPMENT on `general-enhancements`):** `SessionAttachmentTextExtractor` remains the single extraction entry point. With both `Features.Comprehension` and `Features.AttachmentRetrieval` true, it also dispatches the MIME types of one closed registry in `SessionAttachmentComprehensionPolicy`, each paired with the human-readable source-format label that model-facing framing shows (`UNTRUSTED DATA; <label>; layout not preserved`, which for PDF continues `; may include text a reader would not see`) and with the unit its stored chunk ranges count in (lines, or pages for PDF). The registry holds the Arcanum text container (the ASCII header `ARCCOMP1\n` followed by strict UTF-8 text), the package formats, and PDF, tabulated below. A MIME is normalized by one rule, spelled identically in C# and in every SQL statement that classifies a stored MIME (reconciliation, the gate-off retrieval pre-filter, and the Tapestry exclusion): it is cut at the first `;`, only space, tab, CR, and LF are trimmed from its ends, and ASCII letters fold to lower case. A no-break space, a form feed, other Unicode white space, or a non-ASCII letter stays part of the value, so that spelling is not a registry type, and C# and SQL either both read a spelling as the same registry type or both read it as none. A MIME outside the registry has no extractor and stays `NotEligible`. A reviewed package format is chosen by the filename extension (`AttachmentMimeDetector`), whether or not Comprehension is on: there is no ZIP or package sniffing, so a reviewed package renamed to an unrecognized extension, or given none, is an unknown binary and stays `NotEligible`. The detector's established signature checks run first, so bytes that begin with a PDF, PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, or BMP signature are classified by that signature whatever the name says, a name with a `.pdf` extension is `application/pdf` even when its bytes are not a PDF (it then fails as malformed), and a name with no recognized extension whose bytes begin with `ARCCOMP1\n` is the text container. One extraction host exists per parser family (the text container, Wordprocessing, Spreadsheet, Presentation, OpenDocument text, OpenDocument spreadsheet, OpenDocument presentation, Visio, and PDF), so the set of code that can run is closed and visible to review and to the hosted-producer analysis; a macro-enabled variant shares the host of its base format. Every family but PDF is an in-process host constructed over one concrete extractor. PDF's host is the isolated host: it constructs no extractor in this process and reaches the PDF parser only through the worker interface described under **PDF extraction** below. All hosts derive from one abstract host, which callers reach a registry format through and which runs every document in the same two steps (**One pipeline for every source**, below): a reserve-and-read step written once for every host, then the host's own parse. The indexer names each parse by its host's concrete type, so its call reaches the worker only from inside an effect group of its work lease (below); attach, refresh, per-turn references, and pins take both steps through the abstract host under their own request's admission. Quarantine after a timeout is therefore per family: a family whose in-process parser overran defers its own further documents (below) and does not block another family. The package parsers are first-party and bounded, with no third-party document dependency: a library earns its place only where it carries the hard part of a format, and none does for these ZIP-plus-XML formats. PDF is where one does, PdfPig, and it is why PDF is never parsed in this process. Documents retain `Binary` kind and use the same eligibility policy across indexing/retrieval, attach/refresh, per-turn references, and durable pins. Document bytes come exclusively from authenticated `ISessionAttachmentStore.ReadBytesAsync` under the existing text input cap, never a source-path or direct file read. That cap is 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes) and is enforced at intake: a non-image attachment above it is refused with `Attachment.TooLarge` and never becomes a row, so no document larger than 1 MiB is stored or extracted. A `Failed` document is therefore one whose package is damaged or expands past Arcanum's bounds, not one that was too large to attach.

The text-container and package extractors are pure, cooperative, reviewed in-process implementations; PDF is not one of them (**PDF extraction**, below). A bounded output sink enforces a code-owned ceiling of 262,144 normalized UTF-16 characters with surrogate-safe truncation. Each parser family has one extraction slot that serializes its invocations. Attach, refresh, per-turn references, and pins wait at most a code-owned 30 seconds for it. Background indexing never waits: it holds a Grimoire work lease, and queueing for the slot under that lease would hold a maintenance transition's stage-one drain behind other documents' parses, so indexing takes the slot only when it is free. The wait is never charged to the document: a slot not acquired in time, a slot not free for indexing, or a family quarantined by an outstanding parser (refused at once instead of queued behind it, and callers already queued for the slot are released at the same moment) is the transient status `Deferred` with the fixed reason `Document extraction is temporarily busy.`, having read and parsed nothing. Once the slot is held, a code-owned five-second budget begins and covers the authenticated store read and the pure extraction. The caller directly awaits and drains the store read under its admission, cancelling it at the budget's deadline and joining resource cleanup before releasing authority. A read that exhausts the budget is terminal `Failed` without starting the parser. The trusted store must honor cancellation; arbitrary uncooperative I/O cannot be safely abandoned, so the caller retains admission until that read releases its resources. Only already-read bytes, the pure extractor, and its bounded sink may run detached. The caller wait for that pure parser is bounded by the remaining budget; expiry of the document's own budget is terminal `Failed` without automatic retry. An outstanding implementation quarantines its family, and further documents of that family are `Deferred` at once until it ends, so healthy work in other families progresses. This cooperative in-process boundary provides no hard wall-clock preemption of arbitrary I/O and is not a sandbox for arbitrary parser code, which is why a third-party parser such as PDF's does not run behind it. Unsupported MIME remains `NotEligible`; valid empty output is `NotEligible` with an extraction timestamp and is not repeatedly queued. A text container with a missing or incomplete header or invalid UTF-8 fails with a bounded diagnostic reason. A package extractor refuses its input with one of a closed set of rejections, and the host maps each to a fixed, code-owned status and reason that never echoes an entry name, part name, XML text, or framework message: encrypted input and unsupported ZIP features are `NotEligible` (`Encrypted document packages are not supported.`, `Document package uses an unsupported ZIP feature.`); an invalid ZIP, entry-count, expansion, entry-name, missing-part, format-mismatch, malformed-XML (including a prohibited DTD), or structure-bound violation is terminal `Failed` with its own fixed reason; any other extractor exception is `Failed` with a generic reason. Neither status is retried automatically, and both carry an extraction timestamp so reconciliation does not re-queue them. A `Deferred` attempt is neither, and is never durably terminal: indexing keeps the row `Pending` with the reason `Document extraction is temporarily busy.` and no extraction timestamp, and retries it with the existing five-second automatic retry, without spending an attempt because nothing was read or parsed, until it is extracted or fails on its own merits (a parser that never ends keeps its family quarantined, so its deferred documents are retried at that interval for as long as it does). That retry lives in memory, so reconciliation, which re-queues pending rows, recovers the document when the retry is lost to a restart, a full queue, or a gate toggle; the retry backoff and the queue's pending-identity de-duplication keep the two from looping. Attach, refresh, per-turn references, and pins report a deferred extraction as unavailable, like a failed one, consume no inject-once acceptance, and record nothing durable; `attach_session_file` answers `Not attached: '<name>' vN. Document extraction is temporarily busy. Try attaching it again shortly.` The Arcanum text container has no payload-length declaration: a shortened payload ending at a valid UTF-8 boundary is valid text and cannot be recognized as truncated. Reconciliation re-evaluates prior `Binary`/`NotEligible` rows only when their extraction timestamp is null and the effective gate allows them, so a snapshot stored before its format was registered is re-queued once the gate is on; its durable kind is unchanged. That covers earlier `.docx`, `.xlsx`, `.pptx`, and PDF attachments, the only types that were already detected as their registry types (a PDF has always been recognized by its `%PDF-` signature or its `.pdf` extension). An earlier `.docm`, `.xlsm`, `.pptm`, `.odt`, `.ods`, `.odp`, `.vsdx`, or `.vsdm` attachment was stored as `application/octet-stream`, which the registry does not match, and is read only after the file is uploaded again. Retrieval, reconciliation, and Tapestry exclusion select documents by set membership over the registry, so adding or removing a format is a registry change. Gate-off prevents new extraction and suppresses retained document chunks during retrieval. `arcanum memory search` is an operator inspection surface rather than model context, applies no gate, and still searches the stored chunks of any attachment, document chunks included. Documents are unconditionally excluded from the Tapestry attachment leaf corpus until a later change adds support. Retrieval and hydration refuse existing or in-flight attachment generations containing document leaves, including mixed summaries, so derived context cannot bypass that exclusion. Extracted context identifies its source format, states that layout is not preserved, and remains literal untrusted DATA under the existing adaptive fences. For PDF it also states that the text may include text a reader would not see: the registry carries that clause as a property of the format, and the attach, refresh, per-turn reference, and pin notices and retrieval's `source-format:` line all take their wording from the same code-owned description, so none can omit it. The notices read `UNTRUSTED DATA; PDF document; layout not preserved; may include text a reader would not see`; a retrieved excerpt's line reads `source-format: PDF document; layout not preserved; may include text a reader would not see`, with its `UNTRUSTED DATA` warning on the separate `warning:` line above it. When the extraction was truncated (at the 262,144-character output ceiling, or by a retention overflow such as the shared-string limit) or the per-item byte ceiling cut the text, the attach, refresh, per-turn reference, and pin notices read `UNTRUSTED DATA; <label>; layout not preserved; truncated at the extraction limit` (for PDF, `UNTRUSTED DATA; PDF document; layout not preserved; may include text a reader would not see; truncated at the extraction limit`), and a pin whose extraction was truncated reports status `Truncated`; retrieval chunks are not marked as truncated.

**One pipeline for every source.** Every host runs a document in the same two steps, and only the second is the host's own. The first, `SessionAttachmentDocumentHost.ReadSnapshotAsync`, is written once in the abstract host and calls nothing virtual. It reserves the family's one slot: a caller that must not queue (the indexer) is deferred at once when the slot is held, an interactive caller waits at most the 30-second slot wait, and a quarantined family refuses at once, and its quarantine releases a caller already queued. It then reads the caller's authenticated snapshot under the caller's admission within the read's budget, and checks the bytes against the record's length and the caller's ceiling. It returns a `SessionAttachmentDocumentSnapshot` that holds the slot and the bytes until it is disposed, or one that holds nothing and carries the refusal that ended the step: `Deferred` with `Document extraction is temporarily busy.`, or `Failed` with `Document extraction exceeded its deadline while reading its snapshot.` or `Document input does not match its bounded snapshot.`. What differs between hosts in this step is two values each host passes in, never code: the read's budget, and whether the parse spends what the read leaves of it. The in-process host passes its five-second document budget and its parse spends the rest, so a read that ends with none of it left is refused at the read; the isolated host passes its own five-second read budget and its worker has a 10-second wall clock of its own, so there only a read its deadline cancels is refused, as before. The second step is the parse: `SessionAttachmentDocumentExtractionHost.ParseInProcessAsync` for the in-process formats and `SessionAttachmentIsolatedDocumentHost.RunWorkerAsync` for PDF, each declared on its host's own type, each running once on a snapshot its own host read and still holds. The caller keeps the snapshot in a `using` from the read through the parse, so the slot is given back once on every way out, a refusal, an exception, cancellation and a refused effect group included. The one exception is the in-process parse, the only parse that can outlive its caller: it takes the slot over from the snapshot as it starts and gives it back when it really ends, so a parse that overran its budget, or whose caller was cancelled, keeps the slot and quarantines its family until it ends, and the snapshot's disposal then gives back nothing. A worker returns only after its child is gone, so it leaves the slot with the snapshot. Attach, refresh, per-turn references, and pins take both steps in one call (`ExtractAsync`). The indexer owns admission, and only the indexer: it reserves and reads every document through the shared step inside its work lease and outside any effect group; for a PDF it then asks for an effect group of the lease and runs the worker inside it, and a lease whose revocation is already signalled, or a group the gate refuses, stands the document down as a maintenance deferral with no worker started (**PDF and maintenance**, below); for an in-process format it runs the parse with no group. The lease never leaves the indexer: no closure captures it, no host receives it, only its revocation token reaches the worker, and each parse is reached through its host's concrete type and never through a virtual member, so the hosted-producer analysis proves that a worker runs only inside a group.

The in-process document budget uses one `TimeProvider` (system time by default) for the slot-acquisition timestamp, elapsed-time checks, the snapshot-read cancellation timer, and the parse wait. Construction snapshots that provider's positive timestamp frequency, which is stable for its lifetime under the `TimeProvider` contract; elapsed checks read the same provider's timestamp and convert with that captured frequency, keeping clock queries explicit to source analysis. The independent slot wait keeps its own semaphore timeout, and an isolated worker keeps its separate wall clock. Deadline tests advance the document clock only after observing parser entry or a queued caller; they therefore prove quarantine and release without assuming the thread pool scheduled a parser inside a short real-time budget. A budget that expires between snapshot read and parse is still terminal, invokes no parser, and leaves the slot with the snapshot instead of quarantining the family. Snapshot-read cancellation still awaits storage completion and disposal before releasing the slot or the caller's admission.

**Adding a source.** A new document source (RTF, legacy binary Office, EPUB, an email message, text recognized in an image) is the checklist below, in one change set. The slot, the read, the budgets, the release on every path and the indexer's admission come with the host and are not written again.

1. **The registry row.** One `SessionAttachmentComprehensionFormat` per MIME type in `SessionAttachmentComprehensionPolicy.Formats`: the MIME type (lower case, normalized as above), the label `FormatName` that every model-facing framing shows, the chunk range unit `RangeUnit` (`Lines`, or `Pages` when the host marks pages through the sink, as the isolated host does), and `MayIncludeUnseenText` when the extracted text can include text a reader would not see, which adds that clause to every framing (PDF sets it). Retrieval, reconciliation and the Tapestry exclusion select documents by set membership over the registry, so nothing else lists the type.
