It deletes that generation's rows from both FTS indexes and merges them, and it then moves every other Completed generation of the same scope kind, Campaign and protected partition (compared as values, null equal to null) to Invalidated, which the existing invalidation purge answers by deleting everything that generation derived and setting its sweep's phase to match. A Retired generation, one whose request failed or was abandoned, is deliberately untouched: it keeps the paid evidence of that failure and is bounded by how often requests fail. Receipts, suppressions, protected receipt evidence, billing and the operation row, which stays Completed, are not discovery rows and are unchanged. A scope and partition therefore hold at most one Completed generation and the one working to replace it, plus a Retired generation for each failed or abandoned request, which keeps all its derived rows, its index rows included, until its operation is pruned; a successor that is incomplete, failed, retired or invalidated purges nothing; and completed replay reads only generations still Completed, so once a successor completes it is the only one replayed. Node and accepted-summary text is derived plaintext that remains until the successor completes, the generation is invalidated, or the operation is pruned. Nothing is reused across generations, because a successor may see different memories and every set is asked again (§21.16.4), and nodes carry no content-addressed reuse index.

The discovery store additionally implements fold planning, immutable paid-summary staging, atomic fold publication, complete-generation publication and candidate discovery. The store implements the complete internal discovery port, including content-free generation and protected-partition metadata reads. The attempt and sweep stores supply durable physical-attempt transitions, accepted-adjudication staging and atomic canonical application; live executor and request orchestration consume these stores.

**Bounded discovery.** The exact-hash and scalar vector lanes revalidate every exact captured leaf as they rank it. The lexical lane scores the matched index rows first and revalidates a hit in full before it can take a place. Every lane's evidence selects candidates only: it never authorizes a mutation.

*Scoped lexical ranking.* A lexical query is one FTS5 `MATCH` built by `LongRestLexicalScorer.MatchExpression`: `GenerationId : "<generation>" AND Content : ("a" OR "b" ...)`. Its terms are the anchor's distinct, lower-cased letter/digit tokens in first-occurrence order, at most 16 of at most 128 UTF-8 bytes each (a longer token is skipped and does not spend a place). Every term is a quoted phrase, so `and`, `near` or `*` in a memory is never an FTS5 operator, the builder refuses any term that is not exactly letters and digits rather than escaping it, and a test pins the exact text. The index is shared by every generation, scope and protected partition. What keeps another generation's rows out of a score is the join of every matched row to this generation's own leaf node (on the generation and the node) and the fact that the document count and each term's document frequency are taken in managed code over those joined rows alone; the column filter bounds the matched set to the generation, but FTS5 still walks the term postings across the table before intersecting them, so the filter is a bound on what matches and not a restriction on what the engine reads. No other scope, protected partition, retained generation or summary row can change a score, and FTS5's own `bm25()`, whose statistics span the whole table, is never used. `LongRestLexicalScorer` (Core, pure, integer arithmetic only) ranks the matched rows. It scores the plaintext of the generation's own index row, which the lane reads for every matched row before any verification. That is the same captured plaintext the verified path reads from the Saga row in the same transaction, so nothing new is disclosed, and it is guarded by the generation-level read authority (the protected index is read only under a live capability for the exact partition) and by the join; a hit is then verified in full before it enters the lane, so the verified leaf, never the index copy, is what a candidate is. A term weighs a fixed-point approximation of `16 * log2((2N + 2) / (2df + 1))`, with N the generation's captured leaves and df the leaves containing the term, and the weight is defined by its integer computation: the ratio is taken to 16 fractional bits, split into a power of two and a 16-bit mantissa, and the weight is sixteen times the exponent plus the highest step whose rounded-up threshold `ceil(65536 * 2^(i/16))` the mantissa reaches. It equals the exact floor except where the ratio lies within one unit of the sixteenth bit above a step boundary, where it is one step lower (150 leaves with the term in 111 of them weigh 6, the exact floor being 7); it never exceeds the exact value, is identical on every platform and never negative, and a table of golden rows from an independent big-integer implementation pins it. A term's frequency component is BM25's saturating `tf * (k1 + 1) / (tf + k1 * (1 - b + b * length / pivot))` with k1 = 6/5, b = 3/4 and a fixed pivot of 32 tokens (no corpus average), and a document's score is the sum of weight times component. Lower is better for a candidate score, so the recorded score is the negation. The tokenisation, the weights and the frequency component are version 1 of the scoring function; the recipe binds that version (`LexicalScorerVersion`), and a test pins a digest of the function's outputs to it, so changing the arithmetic without moving the version fails a test and a generation is never continued under a different scorer. The lane nominates only hits that score at least the recipe's `LexicalMinimumCoveragePermille` (200) thousandths of what the anchor scores against itself under the same weights, taken in the same pass (a hit passes when `score * 1000 >= selfScore * 200`), so a token nearly every memory shares weighs about nothing and is not evidence (forty memories sharing only "the" form no group, and no paid adjudication). The bar is a share of the anchor and so does not drift with the size of the corpus, as an absolute score would, since every weight grows with the logarithm of the number of memories. Lexical evidence is not separable from unrelated text (in the labelled corpus the weakest paraphrase pair covers about a tenth of the anchor and a pair of different pets covers almost half), so it only nominates: the Pairing Gate below, not this bar, decides which nominees are ever put to the model. Hits are ordered by score and then memory id, and verified lazily in that order until eight eligible neighbours are found; an ineligible hit that outranks them costs one verification and no place, so verification does not grow with the number of hits (`arcanum.long_rest.discovery.lexical_verifications` counts them, without identity or content). The unverified read is not bounded the same way: every row the query matches has its content read and tokenized to count document frequencies, so a token nearly every memory shares makes that read proportional to the generation for each anchor. The index also folds diacritics when it matches, but the scorer compares the lower-cased tokens exactly, so a row the index returns only through a diacritic fold scores nothing for that term. The coverage bar (200 thousandths) is bound into the recipe digest, as is the scorer version. The bar, the scorer's constants, the pairing constants and the 0.92 summary gate below are code-owned constants fitted on one labelled corpus and one local embedding model (§21.5), and the qualification (§13.8) measures them against each embedding model. Changing one moves the recipe digest, re-pins the recipe golden digests and the oracle's coverage, and starts a new generation.

*Vector and exact lanes, and the Pairing Gate.* Managed normalized direction/cosine runs against equal-width observed raw Saga vectors in either accelerator state, and never attributes those vectors to the current configured model. `SphericalKMeans.CosineToDirection` computes the cosine without materializing the normalized vector, performing exactly the arithmetic of normalizing and taking the double-accumulated dot product, so its value is bit-identical. Each lane is a `LongRestLaneBuffer`, a streaming bounded ranking (32 exact, 8 lexical, 8 vector), and one merge through `LongRestDiscoveryPolicy.MergeCandidates` selects the neighbours; the merge applies no similarity cut of its own. **The lanes only nominate; the Pairing Gate (`LongRestPairing`, Core, pure) admits.** A nominee is paired with the anchor only when it is byte-identical (the same content hash in the same format) or both leaves have usable vectors of one width and their cosine is at least the anchor's **Background Floor**; a nominee that cannot be assessed is not paired and is never sent. A lexical or hierarchy nominee faces exactly the same test, so lexical evidence never admits on its own and a leaf expanded from a summary is judged as a leaf. The floor of an anchor is `max(median + Z(N) * sigma, median + 0.55 * (1 - median), 0.5)`, rounded up to the next thousandth and capped at 1. `median` is the median of the anchor's cosine to every other leaf of the generation that has a vector of the anchor's width (eligible or not, so consolidation during a sweep never moves it), read from a fixed 1,024-bin histogram over [-1, 1] as the upper edge of the bin that holds the ceil(n/2)-th value. `sigma` is the interquartile range over 1.349 of the pairwise cosines among the first 64 such leaves in memory id order (at most 2,016 dot products and 64 held directions, whatever the anchor), never below 0.02. The sample does not depend on the anchor: a leaf joins it when its vector is usable and has the anchor's width, which is a fact about the leaf, so every anchor of a generation reads the same sigma for a width. The pairs are taken between the held unit directions with `SphericalKMeans.DirectionCosine`, which gives the bits `CosineToDirection` would, and the sweep, which reads one anchor to a transaction, computes sigma once for each vector width a store sees in a generation and hands it to the anchors that follow (`LongRestSpreadCache`, keyed by the exact generation and the width, a few entries long). Only the arithmetic over the sample is shared: each anchor still reads and digest-verifies every leaf of the generation, refuses a generation that is not current before it asks for sigma, and reads its own median. `Z(N) = 3.5 + 0.2 * max(0, bitlength(N) - 6)`. The first clause keeps a nominee as far above the background as chance allows for a corpus of this size; the second keeps it close to the anchor in the scale of the space. Both clauses are invariant under a positive affine change of the similarity scale, which is what a more anisotropic or differently trained embedding model does to first order, so one set of constants transfers between models. A generation of fewer than sixteen other leaves has no distribution of its own and uses 920, unless it has already collapsed (below). **A floor of 1000, the highest, means byte-identical content only**: at it the gate compares nothing but content hashes, because the cosine of a vector with itself comes out a little over one, exactly one or a little under it depending on the width of the vector and on rounding, and that must not decide whether two different memories are put to the model together. One predicate (`LongRestPairing.Clears`: the floor is under 1000 and the cosine is at least it) is shared by the pairing test, the packer, the Fold Check and the vector lane, so no site can read 1000 as an ordinary threshold. An anchor without a usable vector has floor 1000. A **collapsed** generation is one in which the embedding model has answered one direction for every input (a broken or constant endpoint): the median is the top edge of the histogram, so more than half of the other leaves sit on the anchor's own direction to within one bin, and the sampled pairwise cosines have no spread at all (their quartiles are one edge). Its floor is 1000 whatever its size. With sixteen or more other leaves the formula gets there by itself, because a median of one puts both clauses at or above one; below that the rule gives the same floor in place of the 920 guess, which is sound only for a model that separates anything at all. A degenerate space therefore loses recall and never precision: a hostile adjudicator over a collapsed corpus folds nothing but memories that are byte-identical. The floor is also relative to the generation's own composition: it is read from the anchor's cosines to the other memories the installation holds, so a flood of memories unrelated to an anchor lowers its median and with it the floor, never below the closeness clause (a median of 0.1 keeps it at about 0.6) and the 500 minimum, and narrows the margin that a cross-topic pair has under it; the margins reported for `qwen3-embedding:8b` are those of the calibrated corpus, and the qualification prints every anchor's floor so that an installation can see where its own sit. The floor is a function of the generation's frozen vectors alone, is stored as an integer in thousandths on the anchor's work (§21.16.4) and is published, once the read that queued it has committed, in the counter `arcanum.long_rest.discovery.pairing_floor{floor_le_permille}`, one count per anchor in the fixed bucket of its floor (the smallest upper edge of 600, 700, 800, 900, 920, 950, 980 and 1000 thousandths that is not under it), so a distribution that sits at the top says the embedding model does not separate topics in this installation's memories. The vector lane keeps its top eight by cosine during the pass over the leaves and drops the entries under the floor once the floor is known, which is the set that filtering first would give. The version of the arithmetic (`PairingRecipeVersion`, 2: version 2 added the collapsed-generation rule and the meaning of a floor of 1000) and every constant (`PairingClosenessPermille` 550, `PairingSpreadTenths` 35, `PairingSpreadStepTenths` 2, `PairingSpreadMinimumThousandths` 20, `PairingSampleLeaves` 64, `PairingMinimumLeaves` 16, `PairingFallbackPermille` 920, `PairingAbsoluteMinimumPermille` 500, `PairingHistogramBins` 1,024, `PairFallbackLimit` 15) is bound into the recipe, and a test pins a digest of the arithmetic's outputs to the version. A differential oracle test holds the scan to a brute-force reference over seeded corpora (exact duplicates of every designated anchor and, for one anchor, more than the exact lane keeps, all tied at its cut; near duplicates either side of the floor; ties at each cut; pinned and retired memories, which are never captured and so are in no group; wrong-width leaves; clean and protected partitions): the reference reads every leaf, computes the floor from the plain definition, merges every candidate one at a time and scores the lexical lane over every leaf without any index. Hits that the sweep itself consolidates after capture cannot be built in a corpus that large, so a separate test consolidates twelve identical memories through the sweep's own exact-duplicate decision and holds that those ineligible hits, which outscore the one eligible memory sharing a single token, take no place in the lexical lane.

*Ancestor-Excluded Cross-Cluster Recall.* Hierarchy queries follow the anchor's exact leaf edges to its nearest generated ancestor, the most specific summary of what the anchor is about, whose subtree is at most sixteen leaves. Every node on the anchor's ancestor chain is excluded: never ranked, selected or expanded. A chain node always matches the anchor, so ranking it would hand back the anchor's own tree, and the anchor's fold-mates are found by the exact, lexical and vector lanes instead. Excluding a node from ranking does not exclude it from verification: the nearest ancestor is read and verified in full, and so is the topmost one, whose verification covers its whole subtree and with it every node of the chain between them, so a record altered anywhere on the anchor's chain (a summary, a paid embedding binding, the root) refuses its discovery, as an altered record anywhere else in the tree does when the scan reaches it. Every other summary is compared by known provider/model/destination and paid embedding bindings; at most eight with cosine at least `SummaryMinimumCosinePermille` (920 thousandths, the summary gate) are selected, and each expands to at most 32 eligible leaves, which are only nominees: the Pairing Gate judges each as a leaf, so one summary that covers several topics adds none of them. Branch-fair traversal keeps one content-free path per immediate child with an aggregate frontier of at most 128. The lane then takes leaves from the selected summaries in turn, best summary first (`LongRestDiscoveryPolicy.InterleaveExpansions`), so neither one summary nor the lowest memory ids can fill it; a candidate's `Rank` is its place in that order and orders the lane. An anchor with no ancestor, or whose tree resembles no other summary, has no hierarchy evidence, and a sweep over unrelated memories makes no adjudication call. The summary gate is a code-owned constant (§21.5) that judges two summaries and nothing else: summaries of different clusters are expected to be less alike than leaves, and in the live calibration they stayed far under it, so it is dormant. All lanes merge to 32 neighbors and exact target groups of at most 16. Fixed numeric histograms `arcanum.long_rest.discovery.selected_summaries` (zero to eight), `.frontier` and `.expanded_leaves` expose these actual bounds without identities, content or tags.

**Recursive folds and forests.** Core planning uses stable pages of at most 128 inputs, scalar spherical clustering and deterministic split/merge under the 16-child bound and the recipe's input budget (§21.16.4). Membership seeds hash the domain `Arcanum.LongRest.HierarchyMembership.v1` plus NUL, big-endian version 1, a length-framed recipe digest, child count, and length-framed sorted membership digests. The layer-start frontier ignores parents produced in that same layer, so committing a page cannot shift later page inputs. Singleton carry keeps the existing node, actual layer, vector and paid evidence without a provider call. A child that no summary request can hold, one whose observation block with the fixed prompt is over the recipe's input budget even alone, is never folded: it is carried as a one-child group like a child that found no companion, takes no part in the folds around it, and keeps the forest covering each leaf exactly once; `arcanum.long_rest.hierarchy.oversize_children` counts it, once, when it first reaches a plan, after that plan's cursor is durable. Its text is in no summary request, and no sweep stops over it. Every edge descends strictly (`0 <= child.Layer < parent.Layer`) within one generation. Cross-page generated summaries can recursively fold through six levels; the terminal phase/layer/group and persisted roots describe a complete forest when further reduction is unavailable or the limit is reached. `PublishAsync` validates exact frozen sources, complete leaf coverage, bounded descending edges and finished units before its revision CAS.

**Exact paid publication.** Summary acceptance validates the current fold and current durable accepted attempt, then stores immutable original Work/evidence without advancing the cursor. Fold publication recomputes `LongRestEmbeddingPayloadHash` from the authoritative recipe and exact stored accepted summary, requires exact current accepted completion input/output counts and nullable cost, and commits node/vector/edges/canonical label/unit/cursor together. The single bounded nullable `CompletionJson` field on `long_rest_provider_effects` holds source-generated `LongRestDispatchCompletion` JSON of at most 4096 UTF8 bytes, distinct from cumulative counters. Missing, malformed or mismatching completion cannot authorize acceptance. A new physical attempt must clear that field; the attempt-store producer owns its completion CAS, aggregate increments and idempotent replay. Historical accepted summary evidence is validated as its original paid stage after exact semantic reassociation, never against a later replaced current effect.

The shared embedding payload grammar hashes literal UTF8 `Arcanum.LongRest.EmbeddingPayload.v1` plus NUL, Int32BE version 1, UInt32BE-length-prefixed strict UTF8 provider and model, positive Int32BE dimensions, UInt32BE input count 1, and UInt32BE-length-prefixed exact input. Provider/model identities are nonblank and at most 1024 bytes; input is nonblank and at most 32768 bytes, without normalization. Work, destination, ordinal, output vector and authority remain separate bindings. Task-specific executor/admission composition consumes this same helper. Published-node reads check canonical labels and stored sensitivity/partition/revision metadata before summary text, then verify exact child graphs, original accepted stages and raw generated vector/value/paid-input proof.

Focused tests cover source high-watermark debt, raw vector bindings, current owner and protected authority refusals, canonical labels, backfill and fold rollback, token purge, FK-off cleanup, immutable paid-stage preservation across genuine boot changes, cross-page hierarchy-only recall through a similar foreign summary, a chain that never supplies its own evidence and is verified end to end, interleaving without memory-id bias, measured traversal bounds, singleton carry, deterministic membership, kind16 integrity, populated predecessor preservation and full catalog parity. Further tests pin that pinned, retired and suppressed sources are never captured and a retired memory's text reaches no request; that a completed sweep still replays beside them and stops replaying the day one becomes eligible; that k mutual neighbours cost one adjudication, a set that differs by one member does not reuse it, and a successor generation asks again; that the same set renders to the same request digest whichever member anchors it and whatever node identities were drawn; that a completing successor purges its predecessor and its own index while receipts, suppressions and the operation row stay byte for byte, only within its scope, Campaign and partition and never over a Retired generation. Tests also pin that a refusal only the provider layer sees (the daily budget, a credential) leaves no attempt behind, so a drained reopen still readmits the sweep, and that the withdrawn second attempt of a unit that already sent keeps the first attempt's counters and charges nothing to the Unknown-Usage Cap; that a memory too large for any summary request is carried and the sweep completes without sending its text; that duplicate-only packs sit outside the three-pack envelope; that the skipped-candidate and reuse counters are published only after commit; that a completed sweep still replays beside a pinned memory that has no Annals claim while a claim-less unpinned one stays debt; and that discovery refuses an anchor whose ancestor chain was altered at any level.

#### 21.16.2 Protected canonical application and durable sweep work

`LongRestSweepStore` implements the in-process sweep port. `BeginOrResumeAsync` persists exact scope/partition/configuration for a `long-rest-sweep` operation; discovery links a previously unassigned sweep only to that operation's exact generation. The sweep freezes every pack for one anchor before dispatch (§21.16.4). Each pack has a stable unit and retained ordered source manifest. An accepted adjudication stores the complete original inputs, decision, Work and exact paid attempt independently of canonical effects. Acceptance compares the complete materialized input content and vector as well as source metadata. The accepted row and original paid Work remain immutable across a fresh store or a genuine boot change. Current Work is recomputed separately only after exact semantic association. Applying the accepted decision performs no second adjudication send or billing.

**Closed adjudication contract (member verdicts).** The model is shown the unit's memories numbered `Memory 01`, `Memory 02`, ... in ordinal `MemoryId` order, each block its text alone: no memory id, version id or content hash goes to the provider. For each memory in order it restates the fact in a few neutral words and lists in `sameAs` the earlier memories that state the same fact. The answer schema is closed: `{memories:[{memory:int, fact:string, sameAs:int[]}]}`, every property required and no other allowed. `LongRestMemberVerdict.Decide` (Core, pure) reads it. Non-JSON, or any departure from the closed shape, is Invalid (a paid answer). In a well-formed answer an edge is any reference to another memory in range, counted in either direction; a memory listed twice, an out-of-range reference and a self reference contribute nothing; and the restated facts are read and discarded, never stored or logged. The decision is `EquivalentObservations` (survivor null) only when **every pair** of the unit is asserted (the whole-unit rule) and **Number Agreement** holds, and `NoChange` otherwise. The model path never produces `Supersession` and never names a survivor, so there is no identifier for it to echo wrongly and no label that lets one real duplicate drag a whole pack in; a supersession is a declaration an operator makes (`POST /api/memory/saga/long-rest`), because a request that carries no recorded instants cannot decide one. Equivalence leaves survivor selection to the canonical policy. Number Agreement is the rule that the letter/digit tokens that contain a digit, lower-cased by the lexical scorer's tokenisation (`9:30` gives 9 and 30, `.NET 10` gives 10, `S25`, `4K` and `2027` stay whole), are the same set in every memory of an equivalence. It compares the set of such tokens and not where they stand, so it can only refuse: a token that one memory has and another lacks (`port 9090` against `port 3000`, `9:30` against `10:00`) is never folded as the same fact, but values rearranged between memories carry the same tokens and agree (`1.5 GB` and `5.1 GB`, `3 cats and 4 dogs` and `4 cats and 3 dogs`, version `1.2.3` and `3.2.1`, `555-1234` and `1234-555`), and the model alone stands in front of those. Invalid output retains its normal paid accounting, cannot publish an adjudication, and parks the sweep as `LongRest.InvalidOutput`, which only an operator clears.

**One canonical and cursor transaction.** `CommitDecisionAsync` owns the admitted immediate transaction from current generation/work validation through canonical receipt, companions, suppressions and exact item/cursor completion. Before it applies anything it runs the **Fold Check** (`LongRestPairing.FoldCheck`) on the leaves it has just read: every pair of the applied set must be byte-identical or at least as close as the floor the unit was queued under (read from the work identity, which binds it, and not from the model or the packer), and an `EquivalentObservations` decision must pass Number Agreement. A failure is an `InvalidDataException`, fail-closed with no receipt and no suppression, because it can only mean a defect in discovery or packing, or tampering. This makes the guarantee of §21.16.4 true at the one seam that suppresses memories, whatever the code before it did. Protected paths verify the durable claim, current capability and source metadata before materializing stored adjudication inputs, and revalidate claim/capability at publication. Failure at cursor advancement rolls back canonical writes with the item. Provider-declared `NoChange` completes the exact item without inventing a canonical transformation declaration. `CommitExactDuplicatesAsync` reloads the persisted group, proves at least two exact current equal content hashes and applies the deterministic kernel without an adjudication attempt or fabricated paid evidence; a mixed group must use adjudication. Hierarchy construction can still have its own provider work. Both paths preserve conservative pin, retirement, scope, validity, dependency, embedding and no-chain policy, and unchanged completed-item replay writes nothing.

**Protected policy v2.** The public v1 declaration API and canonical v1 hashes retain their protected `NoChange` behavior. The internal protected path uses a separate versioned canonical grammar that binds the original decision snapshots, exact partition/provenance and per-target canonical LabelId/LabelDigest. It retains historical Annals sensitivity; a currently protected Saga label does not rewrite an originally clean version. Full labels bind the exact owner, observed Saga artifact revision and content digest, while actual content proves the Saga derived-artifact digest separately from the Annals digest. Ambiguous normalized label identities, mixed partitions/provenance, changed manifests and stale heads refuse. Canonical v2 identity excludes executable Work. An internal nonserialized application context carries the full current Work and retained leaves; the kernel recomputes and proves its persisted unit/source/recipe/scope association. This context is data, not request authority. Its companion evidence digest hashes literal UTF8 `Arcanum.LongRest.ProtectedEvidence.v2` plus NUL, Int32BE version 2, the raw 32-byte Work digest and raw 32-byte canonical input digest. Receipt evidence and per-target protected companions are inserted after the receipt and before any suppression in the same transaction. The protected SQL guard refuses suppression without those companions. Replay dispatches by the recorded policy version and verifies retained manifests; v1 historical lookup filters policy before its bounded ambiguity check.

**Own projection and pending groups.** Suppressions intentionally do not advance source mutation epochs. Comparing a frozen leaf therefore permits only false-to-true consolidation/output flag changes independently explained by every actual causer's exact same-operation, same-generation completed unit-to-Applied-receipt association and verified recorded-policy companions. Other facts, external or damaged associations, and true-to-false changes refuse. This proof returns the live flags for eligibility and current policy, alongside the verified original digest for immutable hierarchy membership; it never rewrites captured nodes, source pages or accepted paid evidence. A step, which makes no per-leaf pass, asks the set-based form of the same question instead, as part of the metadata statement every verification asks (`FrozenSourceMetadataSql`): that every receipt or suppression setting a flag that a leaf was not frozen with belongs to one of the generation's own work items, so a foreign consolidation of any leaf is refused at the next step without a read of the leaf, and that every flag a leaf was frozen with still has the row that sets it, so the true-to-false change an ordinary erasure causes (below) is refused at the next step as well (§21.16.3, Seams and Steps). An unaccepted pending group can refresh its current manifest/Work atomically after this proof. A suppressed anchor or a group excluded by conservative current-output/no-chain rules receives an explicit deterministic disposition without a new provider call or invented receipt. An accepted adjudication stays strict when its current decision state changes. The anchor cursor advances only after all originally frozen groups have dispositions; other eligible anchors remain debt.

**Attempt accounting and interrupted transport.** `LongRestAttemptStore` performs exact Work/AttemptId/ordinal/revision/state CAS transitions. A new physical attempt clears current `CompletionJson` while retaining cumulative counters and immutable accepted stages. Completion stores the validated exact bounded completion once; identical replay writes nothing and a changed completion refuses. `SentCount` counts durable sent transitions. `PaidCount` counts Accepted/Invalid provider returns even when usage or cost is zero or unknown, and Failed returns only when a positive usage counter or positive cost supplies paid evidence. A zero-evidence Failed return increments `FailureCount` without erasing a prior known aggregate cost. On genuine boot-only re-admission, an unfinished Sent effect is first joined to its exact pending unit and reconstructed from the original generation fence. Exact original Work, payload kind/destination, ordinal/revision, protected disclosure and null completion must match. The store settles it as Failed with `LongRest.InterruptedTransport`, increments failure/revision once, preserves all reported usage/cost/Sent/Paid/attempt identity, and leaves completion null. Fence update and settlement commit together. A fresh dispatch requires a new attempt/ordinal and, for protected work, a fresh current claim/capability/disclosure. Same-boot Sent, malformed association and late completion refuse. Previous remote billing after interrupted transport is unknown; counters represent reported evidence.

**Closed physical provider lane.** Long Rest, Campaign rollup and memory evaluation chat clients capture and validate the configured output-token wire dialect before credential resolution and apply `OutputTokenLimitWirePolicy` once per SDK call, so their bounded output uses exactly the provider-declared `max_tokens` or `max_completion_tokens` field. An undefined dialect is refused before credential resolution or provider I/O. Long Rest embedding remains independent of this chat-only policy. `LongRestProvider` uses dedicated pinned OpenAI-compatible SDK clients with `ClientRetryPolicy(0)` and no `OpenAiRequestAugmentingHandler`. Campaign rollup maintenance resolves its client the same way: the scoped `CampaignRollupProviderClientFactory` has no `IHttpClientFactory` dependency and, like `LongRestProviderClientFactory`, builds one `HttpClient` over `OutboundUrlGuard.CreateProviderEgressHandler()` in its constructor. Every lease of the scope sends through it, a lease never disposes it, and scope disposal closes its connections (`CampaignRollupOwnedTransportLoopbackTests` count requests against a loopback socket). Its scoped `LongRestProviderClientFactory` directly owns one `HttpClient` over an `OutboundUrlGuard.CreateProviderEgressHandler()` handler, without configured `IHttpClientFactory` actions, filters or additional handlers. The factory owns that one `HttpClient` for the sweep scope and every adapter lease sends through it without disposing it, but its handler sets `PooledConnectionLifetime` and `PooledConnectionIdleTimeout` to zero (One Connection Per Send, §10.8.2), so no connection outlives its response: each SDK call opens its own connection, which resolves and revalidates DNS through the pinned outbound guard, and closes it. The awaited sweep completes before scope disposal disposes the `HttpClient`. No request deadline is imposed: the overall `HttpClient` timeout remains infinite and caller cancellation remains authoritative. Credential resolution receives a private source-generated copy of the selected provider settings, preserving the accepted provider, endpoint, model metadata and adapter lease across its await. Credentials resolve successfully and cancellation is checked before per-attempt SDK options and clients are allocated. Summary and adjudication use code-owned two-message rendering, fixed JSON schemas, a 2048-token output reservation and an empty tool set. The complete rendered input, including schema/framing text, is bounded to 32768 strict UTF-8 bytes. The chat payload digest is domain-separated from the shared one-item embedding digest; both bind the exact selected provider/model and actual owned request. Embedding uses its own input-token admission, exact sole input, positive dimensions and frozen pricing; it bypasses generic Weave truncation and chat routing/injection. The executor recomputes admission and awaits the supplied physical-send fence before creating request objects or sending. Maintenance composition owns exact child/claim/source/disclosure association and publication; the SDK boundary does not confer that authority. Core grants internals access to the API assembly so authenticated composition can issue and renew `LongRestMaintenanceCapability`; the closed friend-assembly inventory records this grant. The grant does not make request data or database metadata a capability.

The process singleton `LongRestConfigurationEpoch` borrows the existing claim-owner boot identity and observes configuration changes. Its private frozen snapshots bind the Long Rest/Covenant gates, provider/model/embedding choices and pricing. Every observed changed value increments the epoch, so off-on and A-B-A transitions cannot revive an older stamp even when the digest returns to its earlier value. Pre-send and post-return checks reject stale stamps. The physical provider requires its registered `IBudgetReservationService` even when budget enforcement is disabled; a missing port refuses before creating an inference run, resolving a client or sending. The concrete reservation service supplies its existing disabled-budget no-op when enforcement is off. Successful SDK usage is recorded through normal `TurnAccountingHandle` accounting before response parsing, vector count/dimension/finiteness checks, cancellation checks or publication fences. Paid usage, audit and accounting completion use `CancellationToken.None`; malformed or stale outputs cannot erase incurred spend. Accounting failure refuses a publishable result. Billing purposes are `long-rest-summary`, `long-rest-adjudication` and `long-rest-embedding`; logs report safe exception types and audit records contain no protected payload or provider exception body. Effect-store completion is a separate metadata CAS and can refuse after source/owner invalidation while the paid operation remains durably billed.

The content-free internal provider and attempt refusal reasons are owned by `ErrorCodes.LongRest`: `CurrentnessLost` records a paid result that cannot pass currentness/application checks; `InvalidAdmission` and `StaleFence` label invalid or stale dispatch admission; `AccountingCompletionRefused` and `AccountingRefused` retain paid-accounting refusal; `ConfigurationChanged` records a changed post-return configuration epoch; `InvalidOutput` records invalid paid provider output; `CancelledAfterPayment` records cancellation after accounted payment; and `InterruptedTransport` labels an attempt a reboot found still `Sent` and settled as failed with unknown billing (it counts toward the Unknown-Usage Cap like `TransportUnknown`, and the fault table classifies it as needing an operator though no sweep parks under it). Their exact `LongRest.<name>` string values remain stable. These internal reasons do not introduce new HTTP error statuses.

**Authority limits.** Work-only attempt methods perform closed metadata projections and in-SQL manifest comparisons; they do not select protected content/vector or deserialize a full stored leaf. Metadata consistency cannot authorize content, payload materialization or a send. Capability-bearing discovery/sweep and executor paths retain that obligation. Long Rest renewal and the protected sweep verifier check the actual durable PendingMaintenance claim, executor, boot, unexpired lease, request/dependency/origin-installation/restore/history/sensitivity facts, existing Session and immutable exact GlobalOnly or Campaign binding; Campaign also proves registry/root/path facts. Renewal preserves immutable claim identity, changes only the permitted deadline/current sensitivity, and cannot revive an expired lease. Claims have no DatasetGeneration field. Request/executor composition must independently fence authoritative live configuration, feature, dataset/restore and owner context before content access, dispatch and publication. `FindCompletedReplayAsync` supplies only a read-only whole-scope candidate after exact recipe/frozen-source/own-projection proof and absence of eligible uncaptured, newly eligible or other-partition debt. Its signature carries no live lineage authority; the request owner must validate live state and the exact returned generation metadata before adopting that candidate.

Focused store tests exercise real claims and canonical transactions, accepted restart identity, interrupted-send settlement/rollback, complete retained input equality, metadata-before-protected-evidence reads, own-projection continuation, direct duplicate application, changed-owner/label/source refusals, protected policy parity, SQL guard rejection, immutable source/history fingerprints, and zero-write unchanged replay. Controlled provider/disclosure fixture producers prove these store boundaries; live admission, journal and request composition are separate obligations.

**Full restore adoption.** Before a `ReplaceInstallation` or `NewProfileRoot` candidate is swapped into place, the common staged path retires every imported Long Rest generation, sweep, work item, provider effect and derived projection in one immediate transaction, using `LongRestLifecycle.GenerationSteps` as its closed inventory. Empty and terminal-owned roots are included. After the content and reuse projections are gone, only kind-16 orphan labels are retired under the existing guard. The same transaction proves every inventory table and kind-16 label absent before commit. Canonical Saga/Annals content, immutable Saga consolidation receipts, billing/disclosure and original claim-origin coordinates are preserved; retained historical terminal operations and checkpoints grant no replay because their executable graph is absent. Selective Session import does not run this whole-database sanitation against its legitimate destination.

The normal Covenant completion reopens the exact committed database read-only with the already-known staged secret and checks the same absence postcondition before marker reconciliation or `CommitAndReopen`. Authenticated startup recovery borrows the bootstrap's actual open installation connection after topology, key and schema verification; its select-only snapshot supplies the same proof before any marker/finalizer or disposition, with no credential read under the resumed closure. The exact committed database path comparison reuses the same trusted macOS system-alias normalization as maintenance-lock topology; arbitrary ancestor links remain refused by that topology. Missing or non-open connections and failed path validation return the typed kept-closed outcome without reopening the borrowed connection; caller cancellation propagates. Missing or unreadable inventory targets, failed reads or nonempty v18 evidence leave the journal active and admission closed. This is inventory-row absence, not a general validator for columns, constraints or triggers; staged and authenticated callers retain their prior schema convergence. A pre-v18 database may prove the whole new family absent; matching main-schema inventory object names are compared with SQLite's case-insensitive identifier spelling, and only exact kind-16 labels participate in the label postcondition. Partially present targets are not silently treated as zero.

Legacy replacement recovery selects committed topology from filesystem metadata without reading a database secret or opening SQLCipher. An identity-proven committed database reports `CommittedDatabaseVerificationRequired` and retains its journal, staging and displaced installation. After host-tools classification and Core convergence, bootstrap lends its exact open installation connection under the same held maintenance lock; recovery rechecks the selected journal and node identities before and after a select-only snapshot proves the same sanitation postcondition, then removes staging. A truly absent database carries no imported graph and can complete from metadata alone. Existing but unproved bytes or cancellation before cleanup retain recovery evidence and refuse readiness. A committed new-profile journal does not record the materialized destination path and needs no proof of it: the side profile's generation was sanitized before the commit published it, so recovery removes the journal and staging as completed without inspecting or modifying the new root or the unrelated current installation, and the current installation's start is never stopped over it. These checks do not reopen or dispose the borrowed connection, issue execution authority or repair a live graph; they rely on the held installation lock and exact recovered topology rather than defending against an independent privileged actor rewriting files after proof.

#### 21.16.3 Durable orchestration and physical authority

**Live request preparation and independent opt-ins.** The authenticated sweep endpoint accepts only exact Scope/CampaignId and schedules clean work through the existing coordinator. It resolves scope/conflicts first, then (while Long Rest is on) enriches the successful Campaign with its registered root through the Long Rest-scoped `ICanonicalCampaignRootEnricher` (§10.12); the turn snapshot revalidates through the same enricher, so policy, revision and digest are retained during later revalidation. Global is initialized GlobalOnly and carries no Campaign/root facts. Management and durable recovery cannot manufacture protected authority.

A live default-context Session turn is eligible when Long Rest is enabled for exact initialized Global/Campaign, or Rollups is enabled for exact Campaign. Nonempty stateless transcripts, preview, inspection, background and no-context paths never prepare Long Rest maintenance. The invocation writer marks newly claimed responses private before any await. Wizard retains one request-local memoized preparation through provider fallback and correction. Common accepted-request identity, input history and pending claim admission precede feature dependency checks and all maintenance; an already owned accepted key cannot become an unclaimed paid request after disablement or context ineligibility. Terminal claims replay before maintenance or assistant begin.

Long Rest schedules clean work through RequestAsync; the existing background worker owns its execution and the live preparer never resumes it. A queued or running clean operation does not delay or discard the accepted Session claim merely because that worker already owns it. Only exact protected work must finish before pending maintenance ends. With genuine read authority the preparer borrows the actual gate-returned turn lease and selects one metadata-only opaque protected partition at a time. Each exact stored operation uses a separate operation-bound root and coordinator Resume; completed exact-partition replay skips capability creation and Resume. The coordinator alone owns worker identity and root consumption. The final capability Claim is copied back in a finally even on refused/cancelled Resume, then carried to the next root, returned snapshot and failure cleanup. No partition/attempt array grows with productive lifetime. Each completed operation describes only its partition. Store dataset composite and exact per-subject source/owner/label evidence, durable pending claim proof, genuine gate lifetime, configuration and worker ownership remain independent checks; scalar source/restore epochs or equal copied lease snapshots cannot replace them.

Rollup ProcessSession/ProcessCampaign/ReadCurrent and prompt artifacts stay inside the separate Rollups-plus-Campaign arm. Long Rest alone performs no Rollup reads or prompt injection and returns the existing snapshot with Artifact=null. Every snapshot still validates the accepted full configuration, applicable opt-ins, monotonic Long Rest boot/epoch/value stamp, genuine authority lifetime and retained canonical facts. Configuration ABA refuses the next assistant dispatch even when settings bytes return to their prior value; the full settings/accepted opt-ins and monotonic stamp are checked again after awaited authority, canonical and artifact validation, including when Artifact is null. Preview remains read-only Rollup inspection. Unbegun failure/disposal attempts to discard the current claim and releases borrowed authority in a finally even when settlement throws; ordinary claimed assistant finalization owns begun settlement.


`LongRestSweepCoordinator` owns the `long-rest-sweep` operation under `ResumeFromCheckpoint`, with one registered Readiness recovery handler supporting checkpoint versions 0–1. The handler is the Pure Park Handler (§10.8.2): it has no dependencies and never runs a sweep. Version 0 abandons without effects (`long_rest.not_started`), and `Cancelling` abandons as `long_rest.cancelled`. A source-generated, strict UTF-8 version 1 checkpoint records only the exact operation, scope/partition, generation, phase, committed revision, cursor and work digest. Initial checkpoint persistence precedes generation/content/effect work. Every later checkpoint follows the durable store commit, so a canonical commit can survive interruption before checkpointing without repeated billing or mutation. A group digest may advance while the anchor cursor waits for the remaining frozen groups. Existing coordinates must match their persisted owning generation; malformed, future or invented coordinates refuse readmission. New Long Rest SQL operation references and continuation cursors use the operation ledger's lowercase Guid N spelling; Work hashing and other stored identities keep their own existing grammars.

The API maintenance implementation processes one bounded capture, hierarchy, publication or anchor unit per call. The coordinator passes the exact acquired worker owner on every call. The admitted Infrastructure reader checks that immutable expected owner against Running state, live deadline and committed checkpoint coordinates before source access, physical sends and canonical publication. Worker heartbeat and protected claim heartbeat use independent scopes and database contexts. Renewal refreshes the live request capability only after current source, worker, gate, configuration and dataset checks; it grants no lineage authority. Heartbeats stop and join before latest-revision terminal CAS. Long Rest cancellation remains Cancelling across expired-lease acquisition and settles Abandoned even if it arrives after the recovery handler returns.

`ILongRestConfigurationProvider` aliases the singleton configuration epoch and exposes one immutable snapshot containing only the stamp, feature gates and exact resolved recipe. Currentness combines that independent configuration with the actual runtime dataset generation, authority generation and Covenant capability state (see Capability currency below), admission generation, canonical Campaign/path facts and exact per-source mutation/label/owner proof. The unpublished Work v1 and stored fence carry no synthetic scalar source-mutation or restore epoch. Frozen insertion coordinates survive genuine boot changes; later insertions remain next-generation debt. Historical paid summary/adjudication identities remain byte-identical, while executable Work is rebound to the new current boot only after exact source and recipe reassociation.

**Capability currency.** The fence's capability term (`LongRestSweepFence.CapabilityGeneration`) is `LongRestCapabilityState.Of(availability)`: a truncated SHA-256 of a fixed, versioned encoding of whether the Covenant feature is on, the canonical tier's health, its schema version and installed catalog fingerprint, and the dataset generation. It is not `CovenantAvailabilitySnapshot.Generation`, the counter every availability publication moves. Publications are routine: each Covenant maintenance pass (about every five minutes while the feature is on and the tier is healthy) republishes even when it removed or applied nothing, and every operator write to the Covenant, every proposal a Session turn commits and every entry erasure republishes with a new canonical sequence. A fence that carried the counter would have been invalidated by all of them: a clean sweep longer than a pass would restart from nothing, and a protected park would never be readmitted in the boot that parked it. A publication that changes none of the four facts therefore leaves the term, and every in-flight sweep, park and completed sweep, exactly as it was, and a capture that such a publication interrupts is not refused for it. One that changes any of them (the feature switched off or on, the canonical tier degraded, evolved to another schema or catalog, the dataset replaced) moves the term, and a sweep or park that a check then observes ends as stale: a clean sweep is settled `Abandoned` and replaced by the next request, and a protected park is retired by the next Session turn that carries live authority (Fresh-Authority Retire) and replaced by a new generation. A change ends a sweep only if a check observes it: a canonical tier degraded and then repaired to the same schema version and installed catalog returns the term to the value it had, so work that made no check in between carries on. Nothing relies on the term for authority, so that is safe: the gate judges the canonical tier's health at every use, and a schema repair holds an exclusive lease that drains and revokes every turn lease. The runtime authority generation and the dataset generation remain their own fence terms, and a borrowed turn lease is judged by its gate (live registration, authority, dataset, canonical health), not by a counter copied into it, so the maintenance capability, Fresh-Authority Retire and the dispatch fence compare a lease's dataset and authority generations with the fence's and compare no publication counter.

Protected capability issuance verifies the exact borrowed turn wrapper in its owning Covenant gate and the actual durable PendingMaintenance claim. A public registration carrying copied snapshot values cannot substitute for that wrapper. Each physical provider callback is single use: it revalidates current facts, prepares its exact attempt and child, durably acknowledges and associates disclosure, revalidates after that await, consumes the exact child, marks Sent and checks again before SDK execution. Each billable unit holds Long Rest work admission and its external-effect group through actual SDK usage, normal accounting, effect completion and disposal. Known paid usage survives cancellation, configuration ABA and accounting refusal as a typed Invalid result with no publishable summary/decision/vector. Exact retained Sent/unit/source guards control Invalid completion; deleted associations are never recreated merely to record usage, and independent normal billing remains truthful.

Recovery parks every started sweep and never runs one, and each authority class readmits only its own parks. A protected sweep parks as `long_rest.authorized_request_required` without materializing sources or reconstructing request authority; only a fresh eligible Session request may revalidate that same operation, after which Atomic Readmission moves it from `ReconciliationRequired` straight to `Running`. A clean sweep parks symmetrically: an expired `Running`/`Waiting` row as `long_rest.interrupted`, an operator-retried row as `long_rest.readmit_requested`, and a worker that lost its lease or was interrupted as `long_rest.worker_unavailable` or, when maintenance closed admission, `long_rest.maintenance_deferred`. Only the hosted Long Rest worker readmits those, under its own kind-17 lease, subject to the Sweep Failure Budget and cooldown (§10.8.2); a clean park whose fault is not resumable, or whose budget is spent (`long_rest.readmit_exhausted`), waits for an operator retry or cancellation. The live preparer still never resumes clean work, and clean scheduling never fails a Session turn: a failed clean `RequestAsync` with a `LongRest.*` error (a parked or busy scope, an unavailable recipe, stale input) is logged by code, counted as `arcanum.long_rest.clean_schedule_refused`, and the turn proceeds, after the turn's own configuration is re-checked so that an A to B to A flip still fails it. Any non-Long Rest failure (a Covenant refusal), a cancellation, and every protected-partition failure, `LongRest.OperationBusy` included, still end the turn (Clean-Only Busy Skip): only exact protected work must finish under the pending claim, and a streamed turn is told once, after a protected partition is known to have maintenance left to finish (a partition whose sweep is already completed has none) and before the first paid work of it, that protected maintenance is about to run; a buffered turn is not told and its preparer is never held. Metadata partition enumeration returns at most one opaque eligible digest, refuses malformed or ambiguous label/owner metadata, and supplies no content or authority. Exact-partition requests can return an unchanged completed operation without writes or repeated spend while another partition still has debt; the whole-scope overload remains conservative (see Completed replay below). The reset-aware hosted shell receives only clean operation identities, checks the feature gate and acquires kind-17 work admission before creating a scope, retains the exact identity across reopen/reclose, and holds admission through scope disposal. A reset-recovery host does not start this ordinary worker.

**Completed replay.** A completed sweep answers a request only while it still describes the installation (`LongRestSweepCoordinator.IsHistoricallyCurrentAsync`, behind the finder's exact scope, partition, recipe digest and completed-corpus proof): the same configuration value digest, the same dataset generation and, inside the boot that completed it, the same fence (admission generation, authority generation and capability state), as `LongRestFenceCurrency.Describes` judges it. The configuration epoch is not compared: it rises on every change including a reverted one and exists to end work in flight, and a completed sweep has none, so a setting changed and changed back is the same setting and a restart would replay the sweep as well. The insertion boundary is not compared for equality either, only required not to have fallen, which it never does (see the source tracking above). A different boot ignores the process-local terms, so a restart ends no completed sweep. A request that finds the newest completed candidate no longer current is not refused with `LongRest.Unavailable`: it falls through to admission and creates a new generation exactly as it does when no candidate matches, and the older sweep stays `Completed` in operation history until its successor completes and supersedes its discovery data (Supersede-on-Completion). The candidate is judged once, after its operation is read, since a completed operation never regresses; one that was superseded, invalidated or purged since the lookup found it is history in the same way and is never replayed. Admission then looks once more for a completed sweep that describes the installation, inside its own immediate transaction and before it would create a generation, so a request that raced the completion of its replacement joins that replacement and pays for no third generation, and so does one that arrives after a generation has completed and before its operation has settled: the lookup inside the transaction takes an operation that is pending, running, waiting or parked for the authority class that would readmit it as well as a completed one (never one being cancelled, failed or abandoned, and never an operator's park), and a completed generation whose parked operation no longer describes the installation is settled there as `long_rest.stale_configuration`, its sweep and generation left as history, so the operation is not stranded. A live fence that cannot be captured at all (the feature disabled, the recipe unresolved, the dataset unprovable) is still `LongRest.Unavailable`. The configuration value digest covers `features.longRest`, `features.covenant`, every field of every provider, `defaultModel`, `fastModel`, `integrations.embeddings` and the resolved pricing table, though the recipe names less of it: an edit to an unrelated provider or to a price still starts a new generation, which pays for its summaries and decisions again because nothing is reused across generations. A drained maintenance window (for example a Covenant erasure that closed and then reopened admission) or a retired and recovered Covenant authority inside the boot does too.

Adjudication selection keeps a private SQLite `DiscoveryCursor` separate from the paid `CommittedItemCursor`/`CommittedWorkDigest` coordinate pair. Each selection first returns or disposes one pending anchor group. With no pending group it visits at most the source-page bound of 128 leaves and evaluates candidates for at most one eligible anchor; a no-work scan commits its private cursor under the exact sweep/generation revisions and yields noncompleted progress. The candidate evaluator and frozen-source verification still visit the corpus; this limit bounds repeated skip selection per transaction, not absolute corpus work. Completed anchor groups advance the private cursor with their unchanged paid-coordinate commit, and cursor-only yields never fabricate a paid work digest. A later source mutation invalidates the generation through the existing triggers. Cursor/work/completion changes roll back on cancellation or refusal. The private cursor is absent from Core interfaces, progress DTOs and checkpoint payloads; ordinary lagging-checkpoint validation continues to prove the exact completed paid unit and anchor pair.

The hosted shell treats channel identities as coalesced wake hints and scans durable requests at startup and after each wake. A bounded cursor selects clean, never-claimed Pending/attempt-zero/checkpoint-zero rows with no generation or lease and the exact current boot/configuration stamp, and clean parked sweeps that are readmittable now: a started checkpoint, no lease, a resumable code, the current configuration value (any boot), an unspent budget and an elapsed cooldown, with the free yield and operator-retry codes exempt from the budget. Each candidate still enters the normal admitted coordinator path; a refusal advances the cursor, and a retained hint starts a fresh pass for insertions behind it. Because nothing signals a cooldown that expires or a recovery pass that parks a sweep, the worker also rescans on a timer (Parked Rescan). Protected rows never enter this automatic claim path. Disabled mode creates no lookup scope and writes nothing. Prior-boot or stale-epoch pending rows are excluded rather than rebound; generic interrupted-operation recovery retains its existing attempt/checkpoint eligibility.

A fresh request may replace an exact same-scope Failed or Abandoned reservation only after acquiring its process ownership claim and proving its terminal operation kind, recovery policy, revision, completion and released durable lease. The same immediate transaction changes the old sweep and any exactly linked active generation to Retired (phase 9), advances their revisions, and inserts a new operation/sweep under the independently current request fence. Both active-scope indices exclude Retired; it is distinct from Invalidated (phase 7), whose trigger purges source-derived evidence. Retirement preserves the terminal operation, configuration/fence/recipe, checkpoint, work, Sent/paid accounting, accepted stages, disclosures and artifacts without conferring old execution or replay authority. Retired generations refuse resumption, clean re-admission, physical-attempt preparation and publication; they cannot be encoded as resumable checkpoints or returned as completed replay. Completed request replay additionally requires the operation itself to be Completed; a late-cancelled Abandoned operation with already completed durable stages cannot block a fresh request as a replay candidate. The public sweep-store finder retains its complete-corpus evidence contract: the Running owner of a readmitted sweep (the hosted worker, or the Session shell for a protected sweep) may prove its exact current lease, checkpoint, fence and matching operation identity against that corpus to finish the final operation transition without replaying work. Request selection uses a separate internal terminal-Completed selector over the same corpus validation. Later source/label invalidation still changes phase 9 to phase 7 and runs the existing purge. Protected ReconciliationRequired/authorized-request parking continues to reserve its partition and requires its fresh eligible request; it is not a terminal replacement. Fence loss, failed exact row CAS or failed fresh insertion rolls back retirement and admission together.

Explicit request admission owns one admitted immediate SQLite transaction for the registered operation row and its exact sweep scope. Long Rest does not create or settle its operation through `ILongRunningOperationCoordinator`: the sweep store writes the operation row inside its own immediate transaction (creation through `LongRunningOperationStore.CreateWithinAsync`, retirement of a never-started or parked sweep, Atomic Readmission, and the completed-checkpoint catch-up), because the operation row has to commit atomically with the `long_rest_sweeps` row, any retired predecessor and its generation. Leases for rows that are not parked, heartbeats, checkpoints and terminal transitions go through `ILongRunningOperationStore`, and the registry descriptor and recovery handler are registered as for every kind. Exact-current identity replay remains read-only. A fresh authenticated clean request may re-admit the same prior-boot identity only with unchanged configuration value and strictly never-started Pending/attempt-zero/checkpoint-zero state, no lease, generation, work/effect or child-operation evidence, and independently proved current dataset, configuration and canonical scope. A same-boot stale epoch with that same empty execution history is retired atomically: the old operation becomes Abandoned, its sweep becomes Invalidated with the old configuration text preserved, and one new current operation/scope is inserted. Started, protected, process-claimed or otherwise unproved stale scopes refuse before writes. A parked sweep still owns its scope (Parked-Is-Active): a request never claims, resets or runs it. A clean sweep parked with a resumable code and an unspent budget, or a protected sweep parked as `long_rest.authorized_request_required`, whose stored configuration has the current value digest and either an identical stamp or a different boot, is returned unchanged with no writes, and a clean one wakes the worker. A changed value digest, or an epoch-only change inside one boot (a configuration flip back to the parked value bumps the epoch, and the generation's own fence then fails the same-boot historical validation, the rule that also retires a never-started sweep), retires the parked sweep as a terminal one (the old operation becomes Abandoned as `long_rest.stale_configuration`, its sweep and generation Retired) and creates a new one in the same transaction; worker discovery and Atomic Readmission compare the value digest only, and the two agree on every row they can both see because whichever acts first holds the process ownership claim and the revision guard. A protected sweep parked with a restart-generation code (`LongRest.StaleInput`, `LongRest.StaleFence`, `LongRest.CurrentnessLost`, `LongRest.ConfigurationChanged`, and the two retirement markers `long_rest.stale_configuration` and `long_rest.not_started`, which no run ends with but which the same table classifies the same way) is retired the same way (Abandoned under its own code, its sweep and generation Retired) and replaced in this same transaction when the request carries the live turn authority of the Session turn making it and the in-process claim is free (Fresh-Authority Retire, §10.8.2); the authority is proved before any write and again immediately before the commit. The same retire frees a protected sweep parked as `long_rest.authorized_request_required` whose captured generation can no longer resume under the live installation, by the questions a maintenance capability is created under, asked in its order and all of them over metadata and never a protected source's content: the recipe it was captured under is not the one in force (the stored recipe digest against the digest of the recipe the request carries; a code-owned version, such as the pairing arithmetic, the lexical scorer or the adjudication, moved with an upgrade, and a recipe the code no longer reads at all is judged by the stored digest alone, before anything else about the generation is parsed), the fence cannot resume it (`LongRestFenceCurrency.CanResume`: the canonical scope or the dataset moved or, inside the boot that captured it, the admission, authority or capability terms did), or a source it froze can no longer be proved at the seam depth (`VerifyFrozenMetadata`, as `ValidateRetainedSourceMetadata` asks it: the suppressed source of an earlier consolidation was erased, which removes the receipt a frozen survivor's flag rests on and invalidates no generation, because it is no leaf); no turn could ever readmit it, and it is Abandoned as `LongRest.StaleInput`. Retirement always reads only the columns of the generation's row (its identity, scope, phase and revision, which every statement that retires it is guarded by) and never parses the generation whole, on every route that reaches it: this one, a park retired as a stale configuration, and a clean or protected sweep that is already `Failed` or `Abandoned` (a clean one the worker abandoned, a protected one an operator cancelled). So a generation stored before an upgrade that moved a version, a fixed bound or the recipe preimage, which the code in force can no longer read, is still retired and replaced by the next request, and never strands the scope it holds. A park that can still resume, or whose sweep has no generation yet, is returned unchanged. Any other parked sweep (a non-resumable fault, a spent budget, or, for a request that carries no live turn authority, a protected sweep parked with a restart-generation code; a clean restart-generation fault is never parked, it is retired as above) is refused with **409** `LongRest.SweepParked` and no writes; the message names the parked operation's content-free identifier, the one `operation retry` and `operation cancel` take. The exact process ownership claim encloses reassociation/retirement through transaction disposal; a claim another executor in this process already holds makes the request, like a Session resume of that operation, answer a typed `LongRest.OperationBusy` with nothing written; canonical and independent process fences are checked before writes and immediately before commit. Failed scope insertion or fence proof rolls back the whole admission, and only committed clean admission emits a wake hint. These explicit request rules do not expand historical execution reassociation, retry reset or generic interrupted-operation recovery, and the background selector never rebinds or retires stale rows.

**Verification cost.** The path every eligible Session turn takes is read-only and its cost is counted, not assumed. A statement that proves without writing runs in a deferred transaction (`WithinReadAsync` in the sweep and attempt stores, which the completed-replay lookups and `ValidateAttemptAsync` use, and the discovery store's own deferred reads, which `DiscoverAsync` joins), so it neither waits for the writer lock nor holds anyone else's up; every write stays an immediate transaction, and the stores' one transaction helper takes the choice as a parameter so the two cannot drift into separate bodies. The completed-replay lookup reads the completed candidates of its scope newest generation first (insertion watermark, then operation), narrows to the exact partition inside the query when the caller names one and leaves the whole-scope form conservative, and proves the cheap set-based questions - an eligible source with no leaf, a disposition still open - before the pass over the generation's leaves, so a generation the corpus has outgrown never pays for it. It returns the first generation that proves out, pages by keyset and never caps how many candidates it examines, because a candidate it never reached is a false miss and a miss starts a paid re-sweep. The protected partition probe builds its projection once per call, answering the ambiguity count and the next digest from one pass, and builds it not at all when no kind-6 label exists and no stored version carries a sensitivity (a superset test: it can only decline to short-circuit, so a sensitive version with no label still refuses). Both halves of that test are index probes, the label by the kind-6 expression index and the version by the partial index of sensitive versions (§16.2), so it costs the same however many versions are stored; `LongRestPartitionProbeTests` shows it from the virtual-machine steps SQLite takes for the statement, which are the same over 6 stored versions and over 160. The label comparisons are the loose, spelling-insensitive ones on purpose, so a mis-spelled protected label still counts as protected; the expression indexes in §16.2 make them searches without changing what they match. `LongRestVerificationCounters` records, for the async flow of an open `Measure` scope and nowhere else, the full and metadata leaf reads, the per-leaf corpus passes, the rotating scrub windows, the set-based passes, lexical-lane verifications, protected-partition passes and read and writer transactions; outside a scope it is a null check. Every Long Rest store counts the transaction it begins, where it begins it (`LongRestVerificationCounters.Transaction`), so "nothing on the idle path takes the writer lock" is a count over the whole of the Long Rest and not over two of its stores; a test reads the folder so that a store added later cannot open a transaction uncounted or count it under the wrong lock (`BeginTransaction(deferred: x)` must be followed by `Transaction(deferred: x)`, and a call that names no `deferred`, the provider's own `BeginTransactionAsync` among them, begins `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and must count as a writer; receipt inspection, which only reads, begins deferred), a test runs the apply and the inspection under SQLite's own trace and holds the counters to the trace, and the idle-turn budget also reads SQLite's own count of `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, which no store can under-report. `LongRestIdentityIndexPlanTests` pins the plan of the statements production executes (the SQL constants and the installed trigger bodies, not a restatement) as `SEARCH ... USING INDEX`, the set read of a seam as one walk of the leaves in key order with every other table reached by key, and the cleanup body of `long_rest_node_label_delete` and the partition early-out as index searches; `LongRestSweepStoreTests` proves the lookups answer while another connection holds the writer lock and that writes still take it, and that a scope retaining five completed generations (three outgrown, one of another partition, one current) is answered with one corpus pass; `LongRestPartitionProbeTests` proves the single pass, the early-out and the spelling and sensitive-version refusals; and `LongRestVerificationBudgetTests` asserts, from the counters and the SQLite statement trace, that an idle turn over 150 memories pays exactly one corpus pass, reads no leaf in full and takes no writer lock, and that the statement trace of a turn over 30 memories and over 150 is the same list of statements run the same number of times; and `LongRestSweepStoreTests` asserts from the same trace that a seam over a generation the sweep has acted on costs two statements and five more for each receipt it proves (eight for a protected receipt), at two corpus sizes and for decisions that consolidated different numbers of leaves (The cost of a seam). `LongRestScaleProbe`, opt-in with `ARCANUM_LONG_REST_SCALE_PROBE=1`, asserts the same budget at 1,000 and 3,000 memories and bounds one unit of an open sweep at a stated multiple of the corpus. None of them asserts time, which is written to the test output as a diagnostic only.

**The cost of a seam.** Adopting a completed generation's answer is a seam, so every leaf is re-proved, and the cost of that is counted in statements as well as in leaves. A seam over metadata (the completed-replay lookup, the resume entry of a protected sweep, the fence reader's stored validation) is one statement however many leaves there are. `FrozenMetadataCorpusSql` joins the generation's leaves to the live rows they describe: the version, claim, head and memory by key, the label by its exact key in a protected partition, the version's dependencies and incoming dependencies as arrays of at most seventeen elements, and the snapshot columns the point read of a version selects, which are defined once (`SagaLongRestService.SnapshotColumns`) and decoded once (`SnapshotFrom`), as the label columns are (`ArtifactSensitivityLedger.LabelColumnList` and `Materialize`). The comparison the per-leaf read makes runs on each row as it is read: the live rows must exist, the snapshot they make with the flags the leaf was frozen with and the label must be the stored manifests byte for byte, and the digest the generation froze must be the digest of that leaf recomputed from them. Nothing is cached and nothing is skipped. An idle turn takes the same statements over any number of memories (29 in the scale probe's installation of three protected partitions: the lookups, the probe and their transactions), and the scale probe holds that list identical at 30, 1,000 and 3,000 memories. The digest is a hash, which SQLite cannot compute, so the comparison runs on the row as it arrives and is not a clause of the statement; the statement's own work is a lookup by key for each join, which the plan pin holds to. A leaf the sweep itself consolidated, or produced, no longer has the flags it was frozen with, and the applied receipts that explain the difference must be proved in full, as the per-leaf read does. The statement carries those receipts in the leaf's row, found by key: the receipt that suppressed the version (a version has at most one suppression, its primary key) and the receipts that name it their survivor, up to sixteen in all. The decision (every present causer of a newly set flag must be proved, the flags the causers explain must be the flags the leaf has) is the one body the point read and the set read share (`VerifyOwnProjectionAsync` pages the receipts when it is not handed them), made from the row with no statement of its own, and the proofs run once the statement has been read through, once for each receipt however many leaves its decision consolidated, because the proof is a function of the receipt and the generation alone. A proof is a hash over the receipt's inputs, which SQLite cannot compute, and it reads no leaf content, so it stays a handful of statements for each receipt.
