A seam over a generation the sweep has acted on therefore costs the set-based question and the corpus statement (two statements) plus one proof for each distinct receipt it has to prove (five statements for a clean receipt, eight for a protected one), whatever the corpus holds and however many leaves each decision consolidated; `LongRestSweepStoreTests` pins that formula from SQLite's own statement trace, over a corpus of six memories whose decision consolidated six leaves and one of forty whose decision consolidated sixteen, and a second decision costs exactly one more proof. Two kinds of leaf are handed to the per-leaf read instead, which decides them, because the row cannot: a protected leaf whose label the exact-spelling join does not find (the join is made only for a memory id that is a Guid in D form, because it keys on the memory id in upper case and the point read on the upper case D form of the Guid it parses, one key only for a D-form id; capture refuses any other spelling and the hash that binds a leaf refuses it too, but the equivalence of the two reads must not rest on that), and a leaf that more than sixteen receipts touch (a truncated list is never the basis of a verdict). A label stored in another spelling is found by the loose comparison and refused by the exact point read, and the point read decides it. A step still reads the leaves of its window, and a unit its inputs, one by one, which is a bounded number whatever the corpus holds, and the per-leaf read is the reference the set read is held to. `LongRestMetadataCorpusEquivalenceTests` runs every row of the mutation matrix, clean and protected, on a leaf the next unit uses and on one it does not, with the triggers that watch the corpus removed so that the generation survives the mutation and both reads have leaves to compare, and adds the stored-side changes the matrix leaves to the full recompute (a stored digest, a manifest reformatted or given another key, a label's JSON, spelling and owner): on every corpus the two reads give one verdict, and the same kind of exception where the corpus has one fault (the set read takes a leaf's own columns, then its live rows, then its label, in the order the point read does, so a corpus with several faults is refused by the same exception in practice, though the contract is the verdict). The comparison of a stored manifest is the one place the two reads compare in different languages, and it is held to the storage class: the per-leaf read compares inside SQLite, where a BLOB is unequal to every TEXT value whatever its bytes, and the column is TEXT only by affinity, which a BLOB escapes, so the statement hands the set read an empty string, which no manifest equals, for a stored manifest that is not TEXT, and the comparison of the bytes decoded from a TEXT value is then the comparison SQLite makes (the serializer writes ASCII); the matrix includes a manifest stored as a BLOB, clean and protected, and the trailing-NUL forms that the same reasoning covers. A second set changes a plain corpus with dependencies and a corrected memory one column at a time, on either side of the comparison. The attribution question inside the set-based statement is one pass over the generation's leaves and not four: each term probes the suppressions or the receipts by the leaf's version and reads the leaf's manifest only for a leaf the probe found a row for, and the two terms that ask whether a frozen flag still has its row read every leaf's flags from one parse of its manifest, so that its cost over every step is about half of what the four passes cost. `LongRestAttributionQuestionTests` keeps the four-pass statement as an oracle and holds both to the rule in each of the 48 states of two frozen flags and the rows that set them.

**Seams and Steps.** A generation freezes the leaves a sweep rests on, and the question every gate asks is whether they still hold. The answer comes at one of two depths, and a gate names its depth: `LongRestVerificationDepth` is a parameter of `ValidateGenerationAsync` (the fence reader behind every `EnsureCurrent`), `ValidateSweepGenerationAsync` and `RequireGenerationAsync` (the sweep store) and `ValidateAttemptSourceMetadataAsync` (the attempt store), and it has no default in any of them, so a new gate cannot inherit the cheap depth by omission. A **Step** is every `EnsureCurrent`, every sweep-store read and commit, every attempt-store operation and every fold read, and it performs no corpus pass. It re-proves the generation row, the fence, the claim, lease, capability, label, epoch and configuration facts in full; asks one set-based statement of every leaf (the metadata anti-join, with attribution asked in both directions: every receipt or suppression that sets a consolidated or transformation-output flag on a leaf of this generation must be the receipt of one of its own committed work items, unless the leaf was frozen with the flag set, and every leaf frozen with a flag must still have the row that sets it, a suppression of its version for the consolidated flag and an applied receipt that kept its version for the output flag); re-proves the leaves the step is about to act on (in full through `inputs` of `ValidateGenerationAsync` and at every sweep-store read, and by metadata at the attempt gate, which holds no capability). The leaves a step acts on are the leaves its request derives from, not the leaves the request lists: an adjudication's inputs, and for a fold every leaf under its children however deep (`LongRestHierarchyWork.Leaves`, read in the transaction that plans the fold), because the summary derives from all of them and so does the embedding of the summary, while a request lists only the first few of each child. A fold at layer 3 or above has children that stand for hundreds of leaves, and each gate in front of its summary's send and its embedding's send re-proves them all. `EnsureCurrentAsync`, the wrapper behind every such gate, takes its depth and its inputs as required parameters, as the stores do, so that a gate added later cannot be silently cheap by leaving them out; a gate that acts on no leaf, the claim heartbeat or the check that precedes publish, says so with an empty set, while the paid door itself refuses a request that names none, because a send with no leaf to prove would have every gate in front of it prove nothing about it; and re-proves in full one rotating window of `ScrubWindowLeaves` (32) leaves. The windows tile the leaves in identity order and the sum of the sweep's revision and the generation's own picks the window, with no schema change: in discovery the sweep's revision advances by one per committed unit, so a leaf goes unproved for no more than ceil(leaves / 32) units; while the hierarchy is built the generation's revision advances irregularly, the window is a sample, and publish is the bound. A **Seam** re-proves every leaf, once, in full where the caller holds the authority to read content: publish; the completion verify that precedes `AdvanceDiscoveryAsync(complete: true)` in the transaction that completes the sweep; the resume entry (`StartOrResumeAsync` on a retained generation, `ReadmitCleanAsync`, interrupted-send settlement, and the first unit of a protected run, which is the first thing that holds the capability and so re-proves the protected corpus in full before anything is sent); capability issuance; and completed-replay adoption. A clean resume proves every leaf in full; a protected resume proves every leaf's metadata, because resuming carries no capability to read content with, and the first unit under the capability supplies the rest. A seam that proves metadata alone does it in one statement over the generation's leaves (The cost of a seam). A seam that refuses a retained generation is a stale generation, not a storage fault: a clean sweep is retired for a fresh request to replace, and a protected one is refused by the first unit under its capability and stays parked for its own authority class, whose next authorized request meets the same refusal.

The reason a Step may skip the corpus pass is a property of what it does with the corpus, and the trigger-coverage argument says exactly which mechanism refuses which mutation. Nothing a step sends or applies is taken on trust: a request is built from the unit's own leaves, each of which is read in full in the transaction that queues or resolves it and again, in full, by every `EnsureCurrent` that stands between it and the send, and canonical application re-reads its inputs in its own transaction. What a step does not re-read is a leaf the unit does not act on, so a divergence there can only change which neighbours are offered, never what is disclosed or changed, and the discovery scan that offers them reads every leaf in full before it counts one. A unit acts on a leaf when its request derives from it, and a fold's request derives from every leaf under its children (a request lists only the first few of each), so those are re-proved too. The classes, and what refuses each before a send, are:

| Mutation class | Refused by the next Step because |
| --- | --- |
| A memory's text, a correction (new version and head), retirement, pin, owner Session, an embedding, attachment provenance, a dependency, a kind-6 label, a tracked source's deletion or epoch (the matrix mutates a member of each class, and both the update and the delete of attachment provenance, a head's move and its delete, and an embedding's update and delete) | A `long_rest_*` trigger advances the source's `MutationEpoch` in the writing transaction, `long_rest_sources_mutated` and `long_rest_sources_deleted` flip every generation that froze it to phase 7, and `long_rest_generation_invalidate` deletes its leaves, nodes and work. The row every step reads first is gone (**trigger**). |
| A label's partition digest, an owner binding, scope, embedding width, an epoch that differs from the leaf's | The metadata anti-join compares them for every leaf at every step (**anti-join**). |
| A foreign consolidation or a foreign transformation output | No trigger can tell it from the sweep's own application, so the attribution question refuses any receipt the generation's own work items do not own (**attribution**). |
| An ordinary erasure of a memory an earlier consolidation suppressed: a delete, a Saga or Session retention prune, a Covenant purge | An ordinary operation, not a bypass. The erasure plan removes the consolidation's receipt and suppression with their source, so a survivor frozen as a transformation output stops being one without anything having written the survivor, and nothing advances its epoch because no trigger watches a row that only disappears. The reverse attribution question refuses a leaf frozen with a flag whose row is gone, at every step and without a read of the leaf (**attribution**). Where the source is a protected memory the route is the Covenant erasure kernel, and the attempt gate, which holds no capability, refuses it by the same question. |
| The generation row, its phase, its fence; the dataset, configuration, authority, capability, claim, lease | Read and compared first at every step (**generation row**, **fence**). |
| A forest row (node, edge, summary, summary vector) | Not read by a leaf pass at either depth. Hierarchy reads and the publish proof verify it while the forest is built, and the discovery scan reads every summary's whole subtree in full before the next anchor's candidates are offered (**scan**). |
| An FTS row | Not verified at either depth. It can only add or remove an offered neighbour, and a hit is re-read in full before it counts (**hit verification**). |
| The unit's own records (its queued inputs) | The attempt gate and the next read compare them leaf by leaf with the live corpus (**unit**). |
| A write-guarded row (`annal_versions`, `artifact_sensitivity`, a leaf row) changed with its guard bypassed | Nothing sees it until a seam, unless it is a frozen flag no row explains, which the anti-join refuses (**anti-join**). A leaf the unit acts on, or a leaf any fold under way derives its text from, is re-proved by the step; any other is reached by the window within ceil(leaves / 32) revisions and by the next seam (**seam**). |
| The Covenant erasure kernel, the FK-off embedding reset, restore sanitation and factory reset | Each deletes the generation's rows itself, in the statements that remove the sources, so the generation row is absent (**generation row**). A factory reset is refused while the sweep's operation is active, so that operation is ended first. |
| A table rebuild, which drops the table's triggers and restores them later | A rebuild runs with the host not serving, so a sweep meets the changed table only at a resume entry, which is a seam: a clean sweep is refused and replaced, a protected one is refused by the first unit under its capability (**seam**). |

The argument holds while the triggers exist, and that premise is a property of the installed schema rather than of the sweep. The matrix therefore does not rest on it: `LongRestMutationMatrixTests` mutates a corpus of 40 leaves, larger than one window so that a leaf can sit outside it, between two units, once on a leaf the next unit acts on and once on a leaf it does not, for a clean and a protected sweep, by every route in the table, and requires that the next step's verdict equal the full recompute's wherever a send could follow. A row names the mechanism that refuses it and the test proves the name: a trigger row is refused on a leaf outside the window, so only the trigger can have done it; a seam row is the single place a step may admit what a seam refuses, and the test then shows that the full recompute refuses it now, that the window reaches it within the bound at the fence reader and, where the divergence is visible to metadata, at the attempt gate, and that a unit that meets it sends nothing built from it. A negative control drops the trigger that watches a memory's text, changes a leaf outside the window, shows that the steps that do not scan admit it and that the completion seam refuses it, which states the exposure window as a test. A row that nothing refuses is a failure of the design and is closed by a trigger or a step check, never exempted; the attribution question is the step check that closed the foreign consolidation row, and its reverse direction is the one that closed the row an ordinary erasure of a consolidated source opens (the matrix drives it through `SagaMemoryStore.DeleteAsync`, a Saga retention prune and, for a protected source, the Covenant erasure kernel, on a leaf the next unit acts on and on one it does not, and again while the sweep is parked and readmitted). The same oracle runs in the middle of the hierarchy build, on 300 memories whose forest is three layers deep with a top fold whose children each stand for more leaves than a request lists: at each of three points (before the unit that reads the top fold, before its summary's send, before its embedding's send) a row is applied to a leaf under the fold that its request does not list and that no window reaches, and the unit must send nothing built from it, and nothing may publish on it. The metadata recompute is deliberately blind to a leaf's plaintext, because it holds no capability, so a text change that bypassed its trigger is reached only by the fence reader's window, the entry seam, publish and completion. `LongRestStepSeamCounterTests` asserts from the counters that a step makes no corpus pass and reads only its window and its inputs, that each seam makes exactly one, that publish is the one unit of the build to make a pass (with the first unit of a protected run), and that a unit that scans the corpus for an anchor reads a bounded multiple of it. Readmission of a clean sweep after a same-boot abort proves the corpus twice, before and after its work is adopted, in one immediate transaction. Counts only; none of these asserts time.

Focused production fixtures combine the real gate/runtime, native stores, durable claim/disclosure/attempt accounting, coordinator and counting SDK transport. They cover actual Boot A→B summary and adjudication reuse, clean/protected direct duplicate dispatch, interrupted canonical/checkpoint replay, journal-await fence loss, paid refusal accounting, independent heartbeats, latest cancellation, bounded source debt and partition replay. Closed recovery, hosted producer, derived-output and tracked/embedded catalog inventories include this path.

#### 21.16.4 Paid-unit admission and disposition

**One layout, one budget.** A recipe carries `ProviderInputUtf8Bytes`: the strict UTF-8 bytes one chat request (system prompt, user prompt, schema, schema name and schema description) may take, from 4,096 to 32,768. `LongRestRecipeResolver` derives it from the chat provider's `contextWindowLimit`, clamped as the context-budget check clamps it: `floor((window - 2,048 reserved answer tokens - 16 framing tokens) * 100 / 115)`, capped at 32,768. A 128,000-token window therefore keeps the 32,768-byte budget and the default 8,192-token window yields 5,328 bytes. The divisor is the shared token estimator's worst case and not a typical ratio: a model it does not know is counted at one token per byte, no tokenizer yields more tokens than bytes, and the estimator adds a 15% margin on top. A pinning test fills a request to exactly the budget and holds it against the real estimator, for an unknown-model profile and for the verified OpenAI profile, at windows from 6,775 to 131,072 tokens; a budget derived from two bytes per token fails it for every unknown model. `LongRestPromptLayout` (Core) is the single description of those bytes: the fixed prompts and schemas, the `Observation <place>` summary block, the `Memory <place>` adjudication block (two digits and the text, 12 bytes of overhead; the fixed instructions of an adjudication are about 2,300 bytes), the order the blocks are listed in and the size of each. `RenderChat`, the hierarchy planner (`LongRestHierarchy.PlanPage`) and the adjudication packer all measure that layout, and a payload carries the budget it was built with, so a fold or pack the planner admits always renders within the budget. The budget is part of the recipe digest, and `LongRestDiscoveryHash.Recipe` accepts exactly 4,096 to 32,768. The 32,768-byte bound on one captured source stays as the allocation guard.

**Packing.** `ReadNextWorkAsync` loads the exact leaves of every discovered neighbour and `LongRestGroupPacker.Pack(anchor, neighbours, budget, floor)` (Core, pure and deterministic) turns them into the units the sweep decides, in this order. (1) **Exact First.** Every neighbour byte-identical to the anchor goes to duplicate-only packs of at most fifteen, of any size: a pack of nothing but exact duplicates is committed locally with no request (`CommitExactDuplicatesAsync`), so the budget does not decide it and the envelope does not count it. (2) **Clique packs.** The other nominees are paired with the anchor by the Pairing Gate (§21.16.1) or counted `unpaired` and dropped. The paired ones, nearest first (cosine, then memory id), are placed first-fit into the first open pack that has room (sixteen memories and the byte budget) and in which the nominee is paired, at the anchor's floor, with every member beside the anchor (a member of identical content is exempt); otherwise the nominee opens a new pack while fewer than `MaximumPacksPerAnchor` (3) exist, and otherwise it is counted `incohesive` (it fitted a pack by size and failed only on cohesion) or `pack_limit`. An equivalence folds every member into one survivor, and a nominee close to the anchor is not thereby close to another nominee, so every pack is a clique under one calibrated predicate and the survivor the policy chooses is close to every memory it replaces. (3) **Pair Fallback.** For every member of a clique pack of three or more, in clique-pack order, the packer also queues the unit `[anchor, member]`, at most `PairFallbackLimit` (15) per anchor. Under the whole-unit rule a model that asserts three of four paraphrases loses the clique; the pair units recover those folds with plain two-memory units whose receipt equals the unit's inputs, so no proof changes. If the clique is applied, the memories of its pair units are consolidated and the existing disposal finishes them with no request; if the clique decides NoChange, the pairs are asked, and set-level reuse (below) makes the pair (a, b) and (b, a) one question. The cost is bounded: an anchor whose clique is refused pays for at most fifteen more requests, and a store of templated sentences pays more than a varied one. The work item index stays two digits: at most three duplicate packs, three cliques and fifteen pairs. A neighbour that cannot fit a request with its anchor even alone is skipped and counted `oversize`, unless it is byte-identical to the anchor. `arcanum.long_rest.sweep.skipped_candidates{reason}` counts the skipped neighbours as `oversize`, `unpaired`, `incohesive` or `pack_limit` and never carries an identity or content. It, like `arcanum.long_rest.sweep.reused_decisions`, is published only after the transaction that counted it has committed, so a busy retry or a rollback counts nothing twice and nothing that did not happen. A duplicate-only pack costs nothing, so the envelope does not count it: an anchor whose paid packs are full still consolidates its oversize exact duplicates, and nothing about them is skipped. When every neighbour fits and is paired, the packs are exactly the groups discovery formed. An anchor with no pack is passed over like an anchor with no neighbours. A fold cannot skip a child either, because every leaf must appear in the forest once, but it need not summarize it: a child that cannot fit a summary request even alone is carried into the forest unsummarized as a one-child group (§21.16.1), so one oversize memory never stops a sweep and never holds back the summaries of the memories around it. Whether the budget can hold anything at all is the recipe's concern, not the planner's: the smallest budget (4,096 bytes) holds a fold of two small children and an adjudication of an anchor with one neighbour.

**What is guaranteed.** Whatever the model answers and whatever an injected memory says: (G1) every applied set is byte-identical or pairwise at least as close as the anchor's Background Floor, which is checked when the unit is packed and again at the mutation point; (G2) an `EquivalentObservations` fold never joins memories whose sets of digit-bearing tokens differ (§21.16.2: the set, not the order, so rearranged values are not caught); (G3) no fold happens unless the model asserts sameness for every pair of the unit. A fold across topics therefore needs three failures at once on the same pair: the embedding model places two memories of different topics at paraphrase distance, the model asserts that they state the same fact, and their numbers agree. G1 is geometric, so it holds only as far as the embedding model separates topics. On `qwen3-embedding:8b` the closest cross-topic pair of the qualification's labelled corpus (cosine 0.566) is more than 0.09 under every anchor's floor (0.66 to 0.74) and the weakest true pair (0.815) clears it, so G1 alone excludes every cross-topic fold there and a model that agrees to everything folds nothing wrong. On `embeddinggemma` the closest cross-topic pair (0.753) is closer than the most distant paraphrase (0.710), no gate on one scalar can separate them, and G2 and G3 carry the rest. The qualification measures the separation for each embedding model (§13.8). What no gate can do is tell apart minimal pairs built on one template (a dentist and a manager who share a first name, one service on several ports): there safety rests on the model's assertion for every pair and on Number Agreement, which refuses a token that one memory lacks but not a value rearranged between two memories.

**Reasoning off when declared.** For an adjudication request only, when the resolved chat model's entry declares reasoning (a `reasoning` block under its provider `models` entry), the request carries the typed effort `None` (`ChatOptions.Reasoning`, which the provider client sends as `reasoning_effort: "none"`); any other model keeps the provider default, and a summary always does. No configuration key is added. The effort is part of the chat payload digest (grammar v2: a final integer, 0 for the model's own default and 1 for none), so a model that declares reasoning and one that does not are different requests. It exists because the answer is a few short member verdicts under a closed schema, and a reasoning model given the fixed 2,048-token answer reservation can spend it on thought and be cut off before the verdicts, which is an invalid paid answer that parks the sweep; with reasoning off the same model answered in seconds where it took minutes.

**Work identity and the floor.** An anchor unit's work identity carries the floor it was queued under (`PairingFloorPermille`, 500 to 1000 for an adjudication unit and 0 for every other kind of work: a column of `long_rest_work_items` whose CHECK says exactly that). `LongRestDiscoveryHash.Work` hashes it under the domain `Arcanum.LongRest.Work.v2`, so resolving a unit or reading an accepted adjudication re-binds it, and a floor changed in the table is another unit and is refused.

**Set-level decision reuse.** A request names no anchor, so its text is a function of the set of memories alone. Adjudication memories are listed in ordinal `MemoryId` order, whatever order the pack holds them in, and summary children are labelled `Observation 01` to `Observation 16` by their place in the fold, never by a node identity one generation drew at random. The work's source digest is likewise a digest of the set, binding each member's exact policy state, so the same set in the same recipe is the same request whichever member it was found from: k memories that name one another form k identical sets. Before `ReadNextWorkAsync` queues a pack it looks, inside the same generation and therefore the same scope, protected partition and capability window, for a finished unit with this source digest and recipe digest whose accepted decision is NoChange. If there is one it queues nothing, counts `arcanum.long_rest.sweep.reused_decisions` (no identity or content), and an anchor all of whose packs are decided is passed over like an anchor with no neighbours. Only NoChange is reused: an applied decision consolidates its members and so changes the digest of every set that held them, and an exact-duplicate pack was never adjudicated. A set that differs by one member, or by one member's pin, retirement, consolidation or any other bound fact, is a different set. Nothing is reused across generations: a successor asks again. The recipe binds `AdjudicationRecipeVersion` (2), the version of the adjudication request text: the system prompt, the member-verdict schema, the memory block shape (`Memory 01` and the text) and the ordering rule. A test pins a digest of that text to the version, so a decision made under another wording is never offered as the answer to a new question.

**Deferred protected-turn diagnosis.** The live preparer preserves its existing refusal condition and `LongRest.Unavailable` code. Its message names the operation GUID, exact recognized fault-policy code or fixed `Unknown`/`Incomplete`, and `arcanum operation show <id>`. Transient guidance waits for the condition to clear and then requires a fresh eligible Session request; protected work has no clean-worker cooldown/failure budget. A restart-generation reason requires fresh validation, and authorized-request-required never suggests that operation retry creates authority. Needs-operator or unknown paid outcomes are inspected before another attempt. No stored cursor, source, arbitrary reason or private content enters this message, and no transition/readmission behavior changes.

**Content-free Long Rest diagnosis.** `LongRestProviderFailure` reads `ClientResultException.Status` or `HttpRequestException.StatusCode`, never exception text. A known failure status is retained in a fixed remedy message: 401/403 credential/access checks, 404 model/endpoint checks, 400/413/422 model capability/request-limit checks, 429 rate-limit/quota checks, and 408/5xx availability/service checks. Unknown status remains unknown. Transient/rejected/unreachable classification and the possibly-served unknown-usage budget are unchanged. The executor emits one Warning per refused physical call with bounded configured provider/model labels (128 characters, control characters replaced), nullable HTTP status, operation ID and stable error code. The factory owns the corresponding credential-resolution Warning, with operation ID when invoked by the provider; local resolution failure is `LongRest.CredentialUnavailable` (NeedsOperator, HTTP 409), never reachability advice. Caller cancellation propagates without a failure Warning. The coordinator records a Debug park event with operation ID and code, avoiding a duplicate Warning. No raw exception, provider body, prompt, source, credential, endpoint or host path is logged. Settlement/release failures, whether exceptions or failed Results, emit distinct fixed recovery event codes (`long_rest.settlement_failed`, `long_rest.release_unsent_failed`) while preserving the original refusal/cancellation and retained attempt. Claim/worker heartbeat faults emit `long_rest.claim_heartbeat_failed` / `long_rest.worker_heartbeat_failed` before cancelling dispatch; the original heartbeat is still joined before its scope or admission exits. These diagnostic events grant no replay or authority.

**Admit-then-Prepare.** The refusals that follow from the request itself happen before any provider-effect row or accounting run exists. In the paid door the request is rendered and hashed, its token estimate is taken and `ModelCallExecutor.CheckLongRestWindow` compares it with the provider's window (a chat request against the clamped window; an embedding input against the window when one is set) before `PrepareAttemptAsync`, and a refusal is `LongRest.ModelContextTooSmall`; the executor applies the same rule again as its last gate before any SDK object exists. Such a refused unit leaves no effect row and no accounting run. Two refusals only the provider layer can see come after the attempt is prepared: the daily budget reservation (which also opens an accounting run, completed as failed) and the provider credential. Neither may leave the attempt behind, because a `Prepared` row cannot be certified as not sent by a same-boot abort and `ReadmitCleanAsync` refuses any Prepared, Disclosed or Sent effect, a rule that is unchanged. So when the provider call ends, by refusal, failure or cancellation, before the physical send was recorded, the frame that owns the attempt withdraws it inside the external-effect group it still holds (`ILongRestAttemptStore.ReleaseUnsentAttemptAsync`, best effort, like the in-frame settlement). A unit that had never sent returns to having no effect row at all. A unit whose earlier attempts did send (a summary already paid, now its embedding) keeps their counters and the withdrawn attempt becomes the failed shape of a send that never left the process: failed, `LongRest.ProviderUnreachable`, no completion evidence, no failure charged to the Unknown-Usage Cap (§10.8.2). Only the exact current `Prepared` attempt without a disclosure receipt can be withdrawn; a disclosed or sent attempt is left to the reboot settlement. So a same-boot drained abort followed by a clean readmission is stopped only by a genuinely unsettled send, never by a local refusal, and the paid work of the generation is not lost to one.

**Embedding-Bounded Summary.** A recipe carries `SummaryUtf8Bytes`, the most one summary may take, from 1,024 to 8,192 bytes, and `LongRestRecipeResolver` derives it from the embedding provider's `contextWindowLimit` with the arithmetic the embedding window gate uses: `floor((window - 16 framing tokens) * 100 / 115)`, capped at the code-owned 8,192, with the window clamped as the context-budget check clamps one and the full 8,192 kept for a window that is unset (zero or less), which the admission does not check. The default 8,192-token window yields 7,109 bytes, a 2,048-token window (the context length Ollama's `embeddinggemma` reports) yields 1,766, the smallest window a recipe may have (1,194 tokens, `MinimumEmbeddingWindowTokens`, below which the recipe stays unresolved with its reason) yields the smallest bound, 1,024, and 9,437 tokens or more keep 8,192. The floor is a usefulness floor on the bound and not the size of a chat answer: `MinimumSummaryUtf8Bytes` is 1,024 bytes (at least 1,000, so the bound sentence stays four digits) and `MinimumEmbeddingWindowTokens` is derived from it with the arithmetic the bound uses read the other way, `ceil(1,024 * 115 / 100) + 16` framing tokens. The summary request states the bound, so an answer is never asked to be larger than the embedding window holds, and the 2,048-token answer reservation that sets the chat window floor sets none for the embedding window. A summary of exactly that size, charged at the estimator's worst case (a model it does not know is counted at one token per byte, no tokenizer yields more, and the 15% margin comes on top) with its framing, always fits the window, so the embedding of an answer that respects the bound is never refused. A pinning test checks the bound against an independent search for the largest fitting size at every window from the floor to 40,000 tokens, and against the real estimator, for an unknown model and the verified OpenAI profile, at every boundary and a stride across 1,194 to 32,768 tokens, including that one byte more is charged past the window. A 2,048-token embedding window is pinned end to end: the resolver binds 1,766 bytes, the request states them, and every summary size from one byte to the bound passes the estimator and the window gate.

The summary request states the bound. `LongRestPromptLayout.SummarySystemPromptFor` appends 'The summary must not exceed N bytes of UTF-8 text; omit detail rather than exceed it.' to the instruction, with N always four digits so `FixedBytes` needs no bound. The request's maximum output tokens are not derived from the bound: they stay the fixed 2,048-token answer reservation at every bound, which the chat input budget, the call's admission and the executor's last gate all read. A byte bound cannot prove a token count (a byte-level tokenizer needs from a fraction of a token to a whole token per byte, and identifier-, path- and timestamp-dense text takes about one token per two bytes), so a cap computed from it would cut off an answer that is within the bound, and a cut-off answer is invalid JSON, a paid `LongRest.InvalidOutput` that needs an operator. The cap is the recipe's single fixed answer reservation, so the bound adds no new way for an in-bound answer to fail; an answer that needs more than 2,048 tokens is cut off by the provider's own limit. The bound is part of the recipe digest (`LongRestDiscoveryHash.Recipe` accepts exactly 1,024 to 8,192) and the exact system prompt is part of the payload digest, so a different bound is a different recipe and a different request. The recipe goldens for every bound, the 8,192-byte one included, come from an independent script; a change of the embedding window is a configuration change and so starts a new generation whatever it does to the bound (§10.8.2); only the recipe, and its golden digests, is the same for every embedding window from 9,437 tokens up.

The embedding window gate remains the last guard for a model that ignores the bound. An answer up to the code-owned 8,192 bytes is still accepted and paid, and when its embedding would not fit the window `ModelCallExecutor.CheckLongRestWindow` refuses it locally with `LongRest.ModelContextTooSmall` before an effect row or an accounting run exists, and `arcanum.long_rest.summary.embedding_window_refused` counts the case (no identity or content). The refused summary stays accepted within its generation, so a readmission of the same generation reuses it and does not pay again; raising the embedding window changes the configuration and starts a new generation, which asks for the summary and pays for it again. A model that respects the bound never reaches the gate, so what remains is the model's behavior and not the configuration's. The minimum is a usefulness floor on the summary bound rather than a worst case: a minimum at the worst case for an 8,192-byte summary would refuse the default 8,192-token window, and one sized to a full 2,048-token answer would refuse the common 2,048-token embedding models, which the stated bound already serves.

Maintenance refusal is classified from the same lease's locked revocation obligation, recorded when admission closes, even before cancellation callbacks notify the worker. A direct entry refused by maintenance and a refused physical-send group both propagate the narrow maintenance-deferred outcome without terminal reconciliation; caller cancellation and unrelated worker/authority failures retain their existing handling.

The atomic acceptance overloads carry the expected worker owner. Before any new Accepted completion or artifact write, and again before commit, their existing transaction proves the durable Running lease, exact owner, unexpired lease and decoded checkpoint's scope, generation and committed cursor association. This is the same proof used by live worker validation. Exact retained artifact replay remains read-only and does not require a newly live worker; known-usage Invalid compensation remains a metadata-only exact Sent CAS.

One `LongRestSweep` work lease is minted at a root and passed by value to every use (Carried Admission): no object stores a work lease or an external-effect group. The hosted worker acquires the lease synchronously and hands it to `ILongRestAdmittedSweep.ResumeAdmittedAsync(operationId, lease, ct)`, an Infrastructure-internal port with no capability parameter that the coordinator implements and DI exposes as a forwarding alias (as for `IDataRetentionHostedSweep`). The owned run passes the same lease to `ILongRestAdmittedMaintenance.ProcessAdmittedAsync(operationId, workerOwner, capability, lease, ct)`, the internal port the API `LongRestMaintenance` implements, so the lease crosses the Core/API seam without appearing on the public Core `ILongRestMaintenance` contract. Fold, adjudication and the paid door take the lease as a parameter, and each physical send independently wins one external-effect group on that very parameter; the local function that runs before a send and the heartbeats capture no lease. Both admitted entries apply the Admission Kind Guard: a missing lease is an `ArgumentNullException`, and a lease whose kind is not `LongRestSweep` is an `ArgumentException`, before any work. The drained-maintenance pre-check passes the same lease formal to the facts reader and stores, and the reader forwards only a `LongRestSweep` lease to the gate. Maintenance closing delays that lease's revocation only through the winning paid unit; host cancellation, borrowed protected authority, worker/claim loss and live configuration/source checks remain effective. The group is released before a subsequent summary, embedding or adjudication send. Claim and worker heartbeats remain owned through disposition and are joined before their scopes unwind.

For a valid response, the owning discovery/sweep transaction completes the exact Sent attempt as Accepted and retains its exact artifact together: summary evidence without cursor advancement, the complete embedding fold with node/vector/edges/label/FTS/unit/cursor, or immutable adjudication evidence. Provider I/O and normal billing precede that transaction. Canonical adjudication application is a separately revalidated continuation and may remain pending after the paid artifact commits. Known observed usage whose acceptance fails may complete only the unchanged exact Sent attempt as Invalid without projection. An SDK call that ends with no result and no cancellation is settled in-frame as unknown usage, never as zero usage and never as an estimate (see Unknown-Usage Settlement and Cap in §10.8.2); a cancelled attempt, or one whose settlement write was refused, remains unresolved `Sent` for the reboot settlement. Independent billing is not authority to reconstruct an absent result. Accepted completion is immutable and cannot be downgraded or billed again by compensation.

The Session request path, `ILongRestSweepCoordinator.ResumeAsync` (called only by the Campaign Rollup turn preparer, which supplies the capability), is the one self-admitting shell. It checks caller cancellation, synchronously acquires its own `LongRestSweep` lease, retains it with `await using`, and awaits the private capability-bearing core that owns linked cancellation, process ownership and the joined sweep. A refused acquisition rethrows the caller's cancellation if it was requested, and otherwise throws the narrow maintenance-deferred outcome before any operation row is read or written. The hosted worker never uses the shell: its port calls the same core with a null capability under the worker's own lease, which stays owned by the worker. The core awaits its lease cleanup before the entry point returns.

`LongRestMaintenance` has no entry shell. `ProcessAdmittedAsync` applies the Admission Kind Guard and checks caller cancellation, links the lease's maintenance revocation, and borrows a lease that stays owned by its caller; it neither disposes nor stores it. Its individual physical groups still own their own joined effect lifetimes.

Two architecture tests and one inventory fixture keep that spine single, and each has a synthetic twin that proves it catches what it names. `AuthorityCarrierBanTests` reads every production compilation semantically and refuses anything outside the admission gate's own types that keeps, captures or lends a gate-minted handle. A type holds a handle through its type arguments, its base types, the interfaces it implements, its type-parameter constraints, its tuple elements or its anonymous members, so a field, property or implicit primary-constructor field of such a type keeps the lease or the group. A store of one into a member typed as a supertype (`object`, `IAsyncDisposable`, a type parameter), an array element, an indexer, a `ref` or `out` location or a ref-returning call keeps it too, as does a closure, local function or event subscriber that captures one (the `this` of a lease implementation included), a delegate bound to one as its receiver, and a service registration of one. A member named `Bind` is refused when it takes one, when a delegate-typed field, property or event of that name takes one, and when any call to a member of that name is handed one. A callee, member or type is judged by its declaration and not by what a call site closed it over: a lease passed to a formal of type `T` is followed into the callee, and a store into a field of type `T` that a caller closed over the lease is a store of it. The handle is followed through locals, copies, conditionals, tuples, array literals, patterns, `foreach` and deconstruction variables, element reads of a container it was written into, return values (async, iterator and local-function returns included) and the authored callees it is passed to: every override and every interface implementation in the analysed source of a virtual or interface member, and the primary-constructor base arguments and positional record properties of a type. Another project reaches a callee through a retargeting layer (every project reference of the production compilations is one), so the formal a callee is read with is found through the syntax that declares it and not through the symbol the call site sees; the cross-compilation self-test builds its two compilations with separate platform references so that the layer is really there, and fails if it is not. A handle given to a callee the scan cannot read (anything declared outside the analysed source, an interface member nothing implements, a delegate invocation, a call bound at run time, an indexer's accessors) is a finding, apart from the null guard and the reference comparison. This is what backs the hosted-producer inventory's documented limits on a handle written to instance storage and read back by a closed key, on a static alias through a local or a reference, and on a delegate that carries it: production is not allowed to contain those shapes. Every disposable handle interface that the gate or a work lease returns is classified (`Every_disposable_handle_the_gate_mints_is_banned_reviewed_or_excluded_with_a_reason`): the work lease and the group are banned; the request lease, the closing owner and the exclusive closed lease are a separate reviewed family that may be kept only where an exact, fully qualified census names the holder (the request scope, the erasure closure and slot, and the closed-period authority); the ordinary open ticket and the expired-lease adoption interlock are excluded with a stated reason. The work lease and the group may not be kept anywhere, with no exception: the reviewed census names no work lease and no group, and a closure over one is a finding wherever it is, a delegate that a busy retry awaits where it invokes it included (`busy-retry-delegate-capture-of-a-lease`). The two Long Rest store methods that attest their lease on every busy-retry attempt, `LongRestDiscoveryStore.ReadmitCleanAsync` and `ReconcileCompletedCheckpointAsync`, therefore write the attempt loop themselves around their own lease parameter with the retry cursor of §16.2, and the cursor holds nothing of the attempt (`retry-cursor-loop-around-the-lease-parameter`). A retry overload that took the lease as a state argument would only move it into a delegate invocation that the ban must refuse as well. `AdmittedEntryCensusTests` pins, by exact interface symbol and through every implementation of it wherever it is declared (a nested class included; a call by the concrete type, a call through another interface the same method satisfies, a method group, an explicit implementation, a method the implementer inherits from a base class that does not implement the interface, and a generic interface the implementer closes all count), who may call each door. It shares its matcher with the Lease-Handoff chain pin (`HostedGrimoireProducerInventory.MethodReferencesTo`), which is the one definition of a door in the test suite: a door is a method, the interface slots it implements, the methods that implement a slot (the method a class runs for a slot, declared by it or inherited from a base class, and a slot of a generic interface matched on its open definition), the other interface members the same implementation satisfies, the overrides in both directions and every name that binds to any of them, in a call, a lambda, a local function or a method group, never a name inside `nameof`, and it is identified by its documentation identity so that a symbol seen through another compilation's retargeting layer is the same method. A pin on a door that no compilation declares is refused instead of matching nothing. The census and the chain pin each keep only the rendering of a reference they report (qualified member names for one, owner and member with a reference mark for the other). The doors are: `ILongRestAdmittedSweep.ResumeAdmittedAsync` only from the worker's `RunOneAsync`; the coordinator's private core only from the Session shell and that port; `ILongRestAdmittedMaintenance.ProcessAdmittedAsync` only from the owned run; `ILongRestSweepCoordinator.ResumeAsync` only from the Campaign Rollup turn preparer; atomic readmission only from the core; and a `LongRestSweep` lease only from the worker's pending lookup, the worker's `RunOneAsync` and the Session shell (a mint whose kind is not a constant, and a mint passed on as a method group, is reported as a possible one). The inventory itself pins the Ambient Holder Refusal (`AmbientHolderIsRefused`). The demand is exact: an instance property or field whose declared type is `IGrimoireWorkLease`, declared in authored source, read through a member access or a conditional access in the member's own body (a lambda or local function of it is a member of its own), under an ordinary hosted root. A member that reads one has no Work from its caller and is granted no Effect, so its sends say `HOSTED_SITE_WORK_FRONTIER_MISSING` and `HOSTED_SITE_EFFECT_FRONTIER_MISSING`, and a group begun on that lease is `HOSTED_ADMISSION_RECEIVER_MISMATCH`, while the same chain on its lease formal is granted in full. The refusal is of the read: it does not depend on what the holder is called or on how it came by its lease, and nothing lifts it. The rows cover a binder named `Bind`, a binder named anything else, no binder, a property setter, a constructor capture, a public field and a conditional access, each with the second send on its own lease formal granted in full, and a mutation that keys the demand on a binder name again fails the property rows. No member is exempt, a recovery handler included (`AmbientHolderIsRefusedInARecoveryHandler`): a handler that reads a holder's lease takes no Work and no Effect from its shell, and a group it begins on that lease also carries the receiver mismatch, while the unmodified recovery matrix is the granted twin. The demand does not read a lease that comes out of an object some other way: a simple name inside the holder itself, a property pattern, a method's return, a slot whose type is a class that implements the interface, or a lambda body keep the member's Work. The Lease Receiver Proof refuses any group begun on the value they read, so the send under such a group holds no Effect and the discovery is refused (`AmbientHolderLeftToTheReceiverProofIsStillRefusedAtItsGroup`). The Carrier Ban still keeps a holder out of production; the refusal is what the checker says about one that is written anyway. The production lane's Long Rest hosted-root test (`ActualLongRestHostedRootRetainsPhysicalDispatchCapsules`) reads the shared production discovery and requires the `RunOneAsync` acquisition to be kind 17 and its own Work, the admitted maintenance to be the one declared Lease-Handoff Root of the worker's service with its `admission` formal, that formal's own Work row to admit kind 17, exactly one handoff-binding row at the owned run's awaited call to tie that formal to the acquisition, the lease to reach the paid door's group receiver as a parameter, and the group and the chat and embedding sends to carry the bound formal's Work and the group. It refuses a frontier, escape, receiver, handoff, budget or callback diagnostic under either root, and an unanalysed caller of the handoff root anywhere. It lets no diagnostic of any code pass, under either root or anywhere in the discovery, and `ReviewedCapsuleManifestExactlyMatchesProductionDiscovery` requires the same of the whole discovery, and a regeneration of the manifest it compares with is reviewed by the Diff Row Classifier (Manifest Regeneration Protocol, §13.1). The Pure Park Handler is pinned the same way: a constructor with no parameters and no field, no name written in its body, no member or type the compiler binds for it (an enumerator, an awaiter, an operator, the type of any expression) from Infrastructure or the API but its own checkpoint decoder, an additional root that traversed cleanly and holds no site of any kind, and no Long Rest row among the recovery effect contracts, with the chat and embedding callees of the paid door required to be discovered under the hosted root so that the absence of recovery effects is not a vacuous result.

Runtime recovery classifies both Long Rest checkpoint versions as DB-only and binds nothing: the Pure Park Handler only decodes the checkpoint and parks the row (§10.8.2), so recovery acquires no `LongRestSweep` lease, owns no group and cannot be refused by maintenance. A clean sweep is readmitted by the hosted worker, which mints the kind-17 lease itself; a lease of any other kind cannot adopt a clean sweep. If maintenance closes while the worker holds the sweep, the coordinator parks the row best-effort as `long_rest.maintenance_deferred` (a protected sweep as `long_rest.authorized_request_required`) with a non-cancellable write and rethrows the narrow maintenance-deferred outcome; when even that write is refused, the lease expiry and `long_rest.interrupted` are the fallback. A sweep that has not yet saved its first checkpoint is not parked at all: it keeps its lease, recovery abandons it as `long_rest.not_started` when that lapses, and the next request replaces it. Maintenance cancellation escapes terminal settlement. Historical readmission keeps its genuine boot-change rule with unchanged recipe, configuration value and frozen source/dataset/scope facts. Same-boot continuation has the separate, freshly attested lease below; a changed stored admission integer cannot supply it.

The bounded current physical effect stores `OriginalWorkJson`: source-generated, content-free `LongRestStoredWork` JSON of at most 14336 UTF8 bytes (six escape bytes per maximum identity byte plus 8192 bytes of fixed coordinate/fence allowance). Actual Prepare captures it alongside the original physical WorkDigest and replaces it only on the next exact physical Prepare, retaining cumulative accounting. Disclosure, Sent, completion, interrupted-transport settlement, adoption and ordinary reads preserve its bytes. The reader separately authenticates the original Work by exact hash and canonical JSON round-trip, refusing malformed, duplicate, unknown, missing or noncanonical fields before physical transition. Projected current Attempt.Work remains distinct. Terminal Invalid/Failed association validates every stable coordinate, source and recipe plus the existing genuine-boot rule or exact stored same-boot executable association; it never waives the original effect digest or reconstructs a provider result. The unpublished v18 head and v17→v18 table definition agree on the bounded NOT NULL field without a synthetic default or effect backfill. The transition's source pin continues to authenticate published v17; the v18 head fingerprint is computed from the current catalog.

#### 21.16.5 Drained clean continuation and completed checkpoint reconciliation

A fully drained, nondestructive maintenance abort records a constant-space live gate interval, broken by any undrained or destructive edge. A live classified work lease may present itself as evidence that its previous admission is in that interval. The independent facts reader's actual gate attests the presented lease and the previous and current admission generations at each use, under its own lock: the lease must be the gate's own concrete lease (a wrapper, or a lease minted by another gate, refuses even with equal counters), still registered, with the gate Ordinary, the scope unreleased, no pending obligation and an uncancelled revocation token, its generation equal to the gate's and to the current admission, and the previous generation at or above the interval floor and below the current one. The attestation is an abstract gate member returning a bool; no proof object exists, so nothing is stored, persisted in the checkpoint or returned as request authority, and authority cannot outlive the lease because every later attestation re-checks it. The gate predicate carries no work-kind clause. The attestation and the lease's revocation getter are abstract, and the lease contract has no default member while the gate contract's only default is a pure forward to an abstract wait (the exact set is pinned by reflection): the hosted-producer checker walks lifetime on a default interface body while traversing the DI-bound override for effects, so a default slot could keep an acquired Work across a disposing override, and abstractness is the guard. The guard is not the gate's and the lease's alone: reflection pins those two contracts, and the `CheckerLimitPinTests` pin `No_interface_slot_that_takes_an_authority_handle_has_a_default_body` holds every other interface slot of the product that takes or returns a lease or a group (a type that holds one included, and an accessor as much as a method) to be abstract, because the lifetime walk resolves a call to the body it finds on the slot and consults the DI-bound override only when there is none. The Lease-Handoff slots, `ILongRestAdmittedMaintenance.ProcessAdmittedAsync` and `ILongRestAdmittedSweep.ResumeAdmittedAsync`, rest on it: a body on either would be walked in place of the declared root, and the root's Formal Preservation would never be asked whether the caller's lease outlives the call. Which kinds may carry a clean sweep across such an abort is Long Rest policy, decided by the facts reader before it consults the gate: only a Long Rest sweep lease, the one the hosted worker or the Session shell minted (recovery runs no sweep, so no recovery lease ever presents itself). An adoption reads its previous admission once from the transactionally reloaded generation row and every validation, including the one after the fence was replaced, attests that original previous admission. Clean active adoption owns one immediate admitted transaction, proves the exact current full same-boot configuration stamp, canonical scope/path, dataset, runtime/capability, worker/deadline/checkpoint, frozen source/owner/label and immutable artifact/physical associations, then updates only generation admission/revision and proved fold or pending-anchor unit digests. Prepared/Disclosed/Sent, protected debt, changed semantic facts and pending anchors needing unproved own-projection refresh refuse. Finished Kind3 receipt WorkDigest and sweep CommittedWorkDigest remain historical. Retained artifact reads may follow that exact stored executable association later without retaining or inventing live permission. Original terminal provenance makes repeated adoption constant space per unit; it does not enumerate the admission interval.

A completed generation uses a separate reconciliation facet. With the same actual-gate attestation of the presented lease, live facts and worker proof, both generation and sweep must already be Completed, with no pending or unsettled work, exact ownership/recipe/partition, the current canonical corpus and its owning receipt/source proof, and authenticated retained hierarchy artifacts. The facet catches up only the operation ledger checkpoint in that same immediate transaction, using exact Running owner, unexpired deadline, checkpoint version, old payload and ledger revision CAS, with repeated attestations and proofs before the write and commit. It preserves every generation, sweep, unit, input, receipt, effect, artifact and billing byte; it does not enter maintenance or provider execution. Coordinator returns the historical completion directly, skipping generic checkpoint persistence and active adoption. The coordinator that owns the run settles the operation with a latest-revision terminal compare-and-swap, and a `Cancelling` row settles `Abandoned` as `long_rest.cancelled` even when the cancellation arrives after the facet returned. If maintenance revokes the lease first, the coordinator parks the row as `long_rest.maintenance_deferred`, retaining the reconciled checkpoint, and the hosted worker readmits it.

#### 21.16.6 Counterfactual credit and explainable Saga ranking

The existing default-off `Arcanum:Features:LongRest` gate also enables policy version 1 for Saga recall. With it off, the managed search retains raw cosine scores, thresholds and ordinal identifier ties; no age, origin or usefulness modifier, dormancy exclusion or additional temporal filter participates. The declaration route remains independently available. Ranking performs no provider work and has no public tuning keys.

**Evidence is measured benefit plus exact committed exposure.** `SagaUseCoordinate` preserves the current memory, claim, version, hash format and digest through actual ledger admission. The successful final provider branch replaces the turn writer's admitted set; a compact `saga_committed_uses` companion is inserted in the same immediate transaction as the native assistant finalization. Partial/interrupted, discarded, imported/forked, replayed, stale, erased, protected and incorrectly owned sources produce no successful-use proof. One turn retains at most 50 coordinates, bounded by the Saga result clamp. The table is jointly owned by the actual assistant Entry, finalization, Saga row and immutable Annals claim/version. Source erasure explicitly removes it even on an FK-disabled connection; retention/reset inventories include it and restore removes its authority. Existing source history and content remain untouched.

The reader derives bounded aggregates from retained canonical counterfactual reports (§20.6), never from retrieval or admission frequency. It validates registration, source manifest, evaluator decision and report digest on the same read snapshot. Only a supported completed experiment containing exactly one clean Saga intervention and no dependency closure can supply item-level evidence. Current dataset, exact current source/hash/origin/scope/validity and canonical owner identities must still agree; stale/cancelled/interrupted/insufficient/multi-source/dependency-only/damaged evidence gives no credit. Future reports and exposure before source creation are refused. At most the canonical 1,024 retained evaluations are considered. Deleting an evaluation or source immediately removes its effect, without a second usefulness ledger. A completed native response alone proves exposure, not usefulness. A report's measurement concerns its frozen declared workload/model/options/evaluator; applying its bounded signal to recall is not a claim of universal causal benefit.

**Reuse only a proved unchanged read cut.** Saga listing, inspection and recall own a deferred read snapshot. They may reuse one immutable, content-free evidence dictionary per native SQLite handle, held weakly and bounded by the retained-evaluation quota; no source text or retained report bodies are cached. The cache also binds the current dataset generation. Before beginning, after a table read pins the snapshot, and after successful commit, the reader compares the main schema cookie, external-commit data version and local total-write count. Reuse requires identical stamps and a cut already proved committed; any concurrent commit, local write, failure or cancellation prevents publication. Caller-owned transactions, including raw SQL transactions, never consume or publish a cached cut. Any database write conservatively invalidates reuse, including report/use changes, source edits, sensitivity, Annals heads, owner bindings, erasure and consolidation. There is no shared cache across physical connections or installations. Within an unchanged database, the cut is valid from its requested instant up to but excluding the next future retained-report completion, source validity/recording boundary or matching use finalization. Source/use expiry follows the validated canonical version IDs, not the separate relational evaluation-source projections. Exact boundary equality and backward clock movement rebuild it. Age/dormancy/scoring still use each call's exact clock instant. A malformed optional boundary disables reuse rather than breaking recall. This saves report validation and source rehashing on repeated reads through a retained connection; a new connection or any intervening database write pays the full validation cost.

**Versioned formula and bounds.** Raw cosine must first clear the configured similarity threshold. Every eligible candidate is scored before streaming top-K selection, and the response's similarity remains raw cosine. The additive score is `similarity + usefulness + recency + origin`: usefulness is 0.01 per net benefit minus harm report, capped to [-0.04,+0.04], with positive credit requiring retained successful exact use; recency decreases linearly from 0 to -0.05 over 180 days and remains capped; operator-stated origin adds +0.09. Total modifiers are bounded [-0.09,+0.13], so they cannot reverse a raw-similarity gap greater than 0.22. Equal final scores use ascending ordinal memory identity, independent of storage order and accelerator availability. At equal raw similarity the worst scored operator statement retains +0.05, above an inferred statement's maximum +0.04.

**Dormancy is a projection.** A version becomes dormant at 365 days since its recorded/creation instant or its latest corroborated measured benefit. Successful exposure, retrieval/admission counts and no-effect reports do not refresh age; future timestamps do not refresh it. Pinned and operator-stated versions are exempt from age penalties and dormancy. Claimless legacy rows retain neutral treatment without invented origin or history. Retirement, exact-current-source consolidation and valid-time interval checks remain separate eligibility rules; validity is inclusive-from/exclusive-to, and a pin does not overrule an explicit validity end. Existing pin release of consolidation is preserved. Dormancy makes no canonical write, removes no embedding and deletes no content; a later pin, correction, eligible measured benefit or explicit gate opt-out can make the retained memory recallable again.

**One policy for selection and inspection.** `SagaRankingReader` captures one clock instant and bounded evidence cut. Managed unscoped, generic-scoped and Campaign-scoped Saga searches use it before K; hydration, next-turn eligibility, listing/detail/review/search and `memory explain` consume the same metadata and pure policy. Inspection retains dormant rows and reports `Dormant` or `OutsideValidity` rather than confusing them with deletion, retirement or a missing embedding. Explanation emits policy version, each component, evidence class/counts, dormancy and exemptions with no source text, digest or version coordinate. It omits protected identities entirely. `--similarity` is an explicit reference cosine (default 0), never an embedding/provider query or a claim about an unseen next prompt; `--saga-id` selects one identity, otherwise the newest 50 clean in-scope metadata rows are returned with `hasMore`.

**Aggregate inspection without protected classification.** `memory status` keeps its legacy retained-store counts and adds an optional clean-only Saga census: memory and current-version counts, exact consolidated/superseded versions, dormant versions, and versions with positive, negative or uncorroborated benefit. The full metadata scan is scope-bound and intersects a selected Session; it uses one snapshot/policy instant, constant-space counters and the existing bounded evidence cut, rather than sampling the explanation page. Missing Annals versions are not invented. Protected current versions and normalized sensitivity-labelled identities are excluded from this census. Disabled ranking reports neutral age/evidence classifications while exact consolidation remains independent. Plain search renders the same available evidence components as JSON. Explain carries the shared closed eligibility reason, so retirement, consolidation and dormancy remain distinguishable. Explicit retirement is authoritative in search and hydration with either gate value, including a residual embedding; feature-off scoring and ordering of live memories remain raw cosine.

Core v20 evolves the unchanged published v19 catalog to the same complete fresh catalog. Real-SQLite tests cover receipt rollback/replay/erasure/protection/ownership, exact evidence and report deletion, pre-K scoring and raw thresholds, default-off parity, pin/operator exemptions, temporal/dormancy boundaries, scalar explanation safety and source-generated API/CLI output. The pure policy also rejects nonfinite similarities and prevents malformed/overflowing counts from generating positive credit.

## 22. Structured output, cost tracking, and prompt caching

These intelligence-pipeline capabilities share the same turn infrastructure.

### 22.1 Structured output enforcement (`response_format: json_schema`)

- **Validation.** `JsonSchemaHelper` (Core `Primitives`) is an AOT-safe, reflection-free JSON Schema parser/validator built on `JsonDocument`. It supports a pragmatic subset: `object` (with `properties`, `required`, `additionalProperties:false`), `string`, `number`, `integer`, `boolean`, `array` (with `items`), `enum`. A `type` array is a union: a value satisfies it when it matches any listed type, and `null` in the array makes the value nullable. A type name outside that set matches no value, so an unknown member of a union never widens it. A `type` that is neither a string nor a non-empty array of strings is rejected by `Parse` with `StructuredOutput.SchemaInvalid` rather than read as some other type. Unsupported features (`anyOf`, `oneOf`, `allOf`, `$ref`, `pattern`, `format`, `minimum`/`maximum`, `minLength`/`maxLength`, `uniqueItems`, `multipleOf`) are ignored. `Parse` and `Validate` each take a `maxDepth` parameter (default 10, clamped 1–50 by `ArcanumSettingClamps.JsonSchemaMaxDepth`); schemas or payloads exceeding the depth are rejected with `StructuredOutput.SchemaInvalid` (HTTP 400).
- **Correction.** `StructuredOutputValidator.ValidateAndRetryAsync` validates the buffered candidate and, on failure, appends a corrective system message naming the errors and re-invokes the model while the invalid output/correction state changes. Repeating a previously seen state stops deterministically. Before another call it estimates the error-message token count (`InferenceTokenizerResolver` first, else `length/4`) and compares against the provider's `ContextWindowLimit`; if the correction would not fit, it stops and returns the best-effort result with a `context window too small for retry` warning. Strict streaming buffers answer/reasoning and uses the same buffered replacement calls; rejected streamed content is never released, and only replacement answer/reasoning survives. `PromptTurnResult.Warnings` (an `init` property defaulting to `[]`) carries warnings out to the endpoint.
- **Failure behavior.** Best-effort by default: after correction stops making progress the last response is returned with an `X-Arcanum-Structured-Output-Warning` response header and a `system_fingerprint` suffixed with `:arcanum:structured-output-warning`. A request whose `json_schema` wrapper sets `strict:true` flips this to a hard `400 StructuredOutput.ValidationFailed` on the buffered path and an `Error` event that terminates the stream on the streaming path (no `Result` or buffered answer/reasoning frame is emitted). Best-effort streaming remains post-hoc and does not request correction because output has already been released.
- **Provider-side constrained decoding.** `OpenAiRequestAugmentingHandler` augments outgoing `application/json` request bodies (streaming requests pass through unchanged — recognised by an event-stream `Accept` header or by `"stream": true` in the body, the latter being the only marker the OpenAI client actually sends): it injects `strict: true` into the `json_schema` wrapper; if the provider 400s mentioning `strict`, it inspects at most 64 KiB of the response stream and retries once without the flag. Caller cancellation propagates; a malformed or failed diagnostic read does not manufacture a retry.
- **Wiring.** `StructuredOutputValidator` is a DI singleton; `WizardIntelligenceProvider.ExecutePromptAsync` invokes it for `response_format: json_schema` requests after the tool loop terminates.

### 22.2 Cost tracking and budget enforcement (`Arcanum:Cost`)

**Enforcement state and recorded spend are separate.** A daily cap applies only while `Arcanum:Cost:Budget:Enabled` is true and the effective `Arcanum:Cost:Budget:DailyLimitUsd` is positive. An enabled zero limit retains the no-cap behavior, but configuration validation logs a warning naming both keys; the offline doctor `configuration.budget_enforcement` check and the host's `Budget` health component report Degraded with the remedy. Disabled enforcement is intentional, not a health fault. This warning does not refuse startup or make health return 503. `GET /api/budget` always reads committed local cost plus outstanding reservations and delegated cost, retaining the unpriced delegated count, and returns `enforced` independently of `enabled`. `remainingUsd` and `spentPercent` apply only when enforced; otherwise their wire values are zero placeholders. The CLI and Forge Treasury keep recorded spend visible, show the missing-limit remedy, and hide cap metrics when enforcement is inactive.

Authoritative composition is **current-call reservation → per-call context budget → reconcile**. `ITurnRunWriter`, `IBudgetReservationService`, and the count-free provider-I/O boundary `IModelCallExecutor` are the enforcement seams. Reservations are never multiplied by an assumed model-call or tool-round count, and their database transaction is never held across provider I/O. Outstanding spend includes current-period `Reserved` rows and all `UncertainPaid` rows, including earlier periods. Core schema version 22 adds `IX_BudgetReservations_Status` alongside the period/status index so both branches use indexed searches without scanning settled reservation history. Fresh installs and the atomic version-21 transition receive the same index; USD subtraction and accumulation remain exact managed decimal operations.

- **Pricing.** `ModelPricingEntry` (`InputPer1M`, `OutputPer1M`, `CachedPer1M`, nullable `ReasoningPer1M` USD) is keyed by model name in `Arcanum:Cost:Pricing:ModelPricing`, with `DefaultPricing` (default free) as the fallback. `CostCalculator` clamps cached input to the prompt-token count, prices non-cached input at `InputPer1M` and cached input at `CachedPer1M`; the default cached rate is zero, but a configured nonzero rate has always been charged. Reasoning tokens are a completion subset priced at `ReasoningPer1M` (falling back to output) without double billing. Configuration rejects rates outside 0–1,000,000 USD per million tokens; runtime arithmetic also clamps rates and saturates accumulated cost. Each `BillableOperations` row snapshots the applicable rates and token counts (ledger keys include provider/model/operation).
- **Billable boundary.** Every operation that invokes a token-producing provider is billable: chat/model rounds, embeddings, Spell routing, Lexicon/Saga extraction, and structured-output corrections. Model listings, non-inference health probes, `POST /api/providers/test`, and `POST /api/intelligence/mana` are the closed non-billable set (`NonBillableSurfaces`). `POST /api/intelligence/context/inspect` is not in it: it never performs the main response inference, but with retrieval enabled it makes real auxiliary provider calls, and they are not all accounted alike. Every embedding it makes (the shared query embedding, and the semantic Spell router's prompt embedding and, on a catalog cache miss, its Spell-catalog embedding) goes through `WeaveService.EmbedBatchAsync`. The preview publishes no turn accounting, so each of those calls opens, reserves, settles, and closes its own short `embedding` run (surface `embedding`) and records one `embedding` billable operation per provider batch, exactly as an embedding made outside a turn does. The preview therefore does write run rows and ledger rows; what it never writes is the turn run of a model answer. The model-backed auxiliary calls, LLM Spell routing (`routing`, reached only when semantic routing is off or falls back) and Lexicon entity extraction (`lexicon`), have no accounting handle to record into, so `TryRecordAuxiliaryUsageAsync` reports them in the response and writes no ledger row. Every call is listed in the response's `auxiliaryCalls`, with provider-reported tokens where the provider returns them (an embedding reports none). `noRetrieval` makes the preview spend-free.
- **Headless-call tool posture.** A background call that reads stored corpus text must have nothing a hostile excerpt could talk it into calling. Tapestry cluster summaries (§21.11) therefore send `DisableAllTools` — no tool is advertised or invoked, where `DisableMcpTools` alone would leave the hub-native tools (web read/search among them, when web browsing is on) in the set — and cap the response at twice `MaxSummaryTokens`, the allowance the context-fit estimate reserves, because reasoning counts against the same limit. The cap is also the most one summary can bill. The Campaign Logger and Saga extraction read stored transcript text on the same unattended basis — an Entry can hold a fetched page or a tool result — so they send `DisableAllTools` too.
- **Usage authority.** Each provider call maps `InputTokenCount`, `OutputTokenCount`, `CachedInputTokenCount`, and `ReasoningTokenCount` independently. Cached tokens remain a prompt subset; reasoning remains a completion subset. If `TotalTokenCount` is present, that provider value is authoritative even when it disagrees with the subsets (including zero). Only a missing total is derived as clamped prompt + completion. Missing usage leaves the pre-call estimate intact; reported input is retained as the original signed `long` with validity and signed `reported - estimated` variance. Invalid negative input is exposed as inconsistent and omitted from the nonnegative reported-token histogram rather than rewritten. Neither reconciliation nor later telemetry rewrites the historical estimate or provider-reported value. Multi-round/tool/correction usage is accumulated call by call without adding either subset again.
- **Missing usage.** A provider call with no usage payload contributes no `BillableOperations` row and no calculated cost. Arcanum does not fabricate billable token counts from the admission estimate. The converse holds for a streamed round that ends abnormally: whether the caller cancelled or the provider failed or timed out mid-stream, whatever usage the provider had already reported in that round is recorded on `CancellationToken.None`, so a round that billed reconciles its reservation rather than releasing it as unspent.
- **Durable operation ordering.** Every completed provider call with reported usage is persisted as its own `BillableOperations` row before its cost enters the in-memory accumulator and before guardrails, structured-output checks, tool-loop finalization, or other post-processing can fail. Corrections and tool continuations therefore remain billable without a duplicate final aggregate row. Routing and extraction provider I/O remains request-cancelable, but once either call completes with usage, its ledger write uses `CancellationToken.None` so a cancellation at the provider/accounting boundary cannot release the reservation as unspent. A durable-write failure marks accounting failed, propagates the failure, and leaves the reservation conservatively outstanding rather than releasing or reconciling unverifiable spend. Session projections, success metrics, and final success audit records remain success-only.
